english: Why do my mature plantain trees fall over easily when the wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui ni eda lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ tswa amɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees easily blow over if microscopic soil worms called nematodes weaken their shallow root system. Propping heavy fruiting trees with strong wooden poles prevents them from falling during windstorms.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛji akɛ sũ mli ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ ha shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ gbɔjɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ wo tsei ni wa amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛkagbee shi yɛ ahum ni tswaa lɛ mli.

english: Why does my field yield less maize every year even though I plant the same seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo daa afi lɛ? He ni miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same piece of land every season drains the soil of specific nutrients. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts returns essential nutrients back into the soil naturally.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi kome yɛ he kome daa be lɛ, ebaaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ baaha niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop in the middle of the day even when the soil is damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: In the hot afternoon sun, plants lose water through their leaves faster than roots can draw it up, causing temporarily drooping leaves. As long as the plants recover by evening, this midday wilting is a normal heat defense mechanism.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli. Shii abɔ ni tso lɛ baaná hewalɛ yɛ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ, hulutsoo be mli ni egboɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ latsaa he.

english: Why are my vegetable nursery seedlings growing tall, thin, and falling over?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ miida, amɛmiifee mlɛo ni amɛmiiho lɛ?

english: Seedlings grow tall and weak when they are searching for sunlight in heavy shade. Moving the nursery bed to an area with partial or full sunlight encourages stems to grow thick and strong.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ daraa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ kɛji amɛmiitao hulu la yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ́ ajie gbekɛbii akwɛmɔ saatso lɛ kɛtee he ko ni hulu lɛ fã ko loo hulu lɛ fɛɛ yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa.

english: Can I just collect seeds from crops I buy at the local market and plant them on my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mabua dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli jara nɔ lɛ anaa ni madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Market crops are often hybrids or may carry hidden diseases. Planting certified, genuine seeds from a trusted source ensures your crops grow strong and give you a high yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee ekome loo ekolɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ yɛ amɛhe. Dumɔwui diɛŋtsɛ ni yɔɔ he odaseyeli ni jɛ he ko ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaha onibii lɛ adara waa ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: How do I know if the seeds I bought are good quality before I plant them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ dumɔwui ni miheɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ dani miduɔ?

english: Genuine, high-quality seeds are usually clean, undamaged, uniform in size, and free from insects or decay, which helps ensure they sprout evenly and healthily.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui diɛŋtsɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ he tse, efiteee, ni amɛdalɛ tamɔ amɛhe. ni kooloi bibii loo ŋmeii ko bɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Why is it better to raise seeds in a nursery first instead of planting them straight into the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ mli klɛŋklɛŋ moŋ fe ni aaadu yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Raising seedlings in a nursery protects young plants from heavy rains, hot sun, and pests, allowing them to build strong root systems before moving to the main field.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akwɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baabu amɛhe kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he. Hulu ni mli edɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni mli wa dani aduɔ amɛ kɛyaa saatso wulu lɛ nɔ.

english: What proper steps should I follow when nursing seedlings so they don't die after transplanting?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii esa akɛ mafee kɛ́ mikwɛ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ koni amɛkagboi yɛ be mli ni ajie amɛ awo he kroko lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Seedlings need steady shade, carefully controlled watering, proper seed tray spacing, and a gradual exposure to sunlight before being transplanted into the main soil.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ hia hulutsoo ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni akudɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Dumɔwui atrɛi lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa kɛ hulu la ni akɛwoɔ mli fiofio dani adu awo shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ.

english: Does it matter how far apart I plant my trees in the forest area?
ga: Te abaadu tsei lɛ yɛ koo lɛ kpokpaa lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ?

english: Proper spacing ensures that each tree gets enough sunlight, ground water, and soil nutrients without competing with surrounding trees for survival.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ tsei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ abɔ akaŋ koni ehi shi

english: Why do some of my farm trees grow very tall and thin without producing good fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ kwɔlɔ ni amɛhe tseee aahu akɛ amɛwooo yibii kpakpai lɛ?

english: When trees are planted too close together without proper placement, they stretch upwards competing for sunlight, which wastes their energy instead of growing thick trunks and fruits.
ga: Beni adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ni akɛwooo he ni sa. Tsei baagbala amɛhe koni amɛye hulu la lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ tsei kɛ aduawai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ.

english: Is there a specific way I should position my trees when planting them among existing forest trees?
ga: Ani gbɛ pɔtɛɛ ko yɛ ni esa akɛ matsɔ nɔ matsɔ tso ko nɔ beni miduɔ yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ koo ko ni yɔɔ momo lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Trees should be placed where they will receive adequate light and space, ensuring they are deliberately aligned rather than randomly placed so they don't choke each other.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ tsei awo he ko ni kane kɛ he ko ni sa yɔɔ. Ajɛ yiŋtoo mli ato tsei lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ bɔni afee ni akakɛ amɛ awo he ko kɛkɛ. Koni tsei akatswa amɛhe

english: Can I plant my seeds at any time of the year as long as I put them in the ground?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu midumɔwui lɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli be fɛɛ be, kɛji akɛ mikɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Seeds need the right soil moisture and temperature to germinate. Planting at the wrong time of year can cause seeds to dry out, rot, or fail to grow well.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ dɔlɛ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛ́ adu yɛ afi lɛ mli be ni esaaa mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ agbi, amɛgboi, loo amɛkwɛ̃ŋ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I just throw seeds into small holes without proper soil preparation?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ bu bibii lɛ amli kɛkɛ? Ni asaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Proper planting requires loosening the soil and digging the right depth so the roots can spread easily and receive enough air and water to take root.
ga: Dumɔ ni sa biɔ ni ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni atsa kɛyashɛ he ko ni sa koni shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo. ni amɛnáa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛwo shishifãi.

english: What is the correct way to handle delicate seedlings when moving them into the soil?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni ja ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ dumɔwui ni waaa lɛ ahe nii kɛ́ adu amɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: You must carefully dig out the seedling with its soil intact around the roots and place it gently into a wet, properly sized hole to prevent root shock.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ sũ abɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe jogbaŋŋ ni okɛwo bu ko ni mli efɔ ni dalɛ sa mli blɛoo koni shishifãi lɛ akatswa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is essential for healthy plant growth. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or planting legumes in the soil beforehand helps restore their green color and vigor.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ ni mli wa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ dani adu lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee amɛhe ŋmɔŋ kɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas together with my maize help my soil stay fertile?
ga: Te cowpea ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni efee tɛŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This acts as a natural fertilizer, feeding the soil and improving the growth of nearby maize.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni eha ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground during heavy rain seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need well-drained soil because standing water starves the roots of air and encourages fungal rot. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain off easily.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu ni ekã shi lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ shishifãi lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni ewo ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ahe hewalɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies. Controlling these pests early with neem oil spray keeps the leaves flat so they can produce full-sized peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛtsɔ neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, afeɔ baai lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni anyɛ afee chili ni dalɛ fɛɛ.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to create food for the tubers growing underground. Lifting the leaves up on wooden stakes ensures maximum sunlight exposure while keeping leaves away from soil diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Kɛ́ awó baai lɛ anɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ, ehaa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ he babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, steal water, food, and sunlight from the main plantain tree. Leaving only one or two strong suckers ensures the main tree gets enough energy to bear large, heavy bunches.
ga: Tsoi loo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ nu, niyenii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ náa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo niji agboi ni tsii.

english: Why is it better to start my pepper seeds in a sheltered nursery before moving them to the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaaje pepper dumɔwui ashishi yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe mli dani ajie amɛ kɛya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young pepper seeds are delicate and vulnerable to intense heat, heavy rains, and weeds. Raising them in a protected nursery gives them a strong, healthy root system before they face main field conditions.
ga: Baby pepper dumɔwui lɛ waaa ni dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ jwɛi baanyɛ afite amɛ oya. Kɛ́ atsɔse amɛ yɛ he ko ni abuɔ he lɛ, ebaaha amɛná shishifãi ni mli wa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ dani amɛkɛ ŋmɔ mli shihilɛi titrii akpee.

english: Why are my cocoa trees dropping all their flowers without producing any cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛjieee cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers when stressed by prolonged dry weather, nutrient shortages, or insect damage. Proper shading, mulching to retain soil moisture, and pest management prevent flower drop and encourage pod growth.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ hao amɛ. niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa loo kooloi bibii fiteɔ, ehaa hulutsoo, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akwɛmɔ Etsiɔ fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ naa ni ehaa pod lɛ daa.

english: Why are the bottoms of my tomatoes turning black and soft before they get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This soft black spots are known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant during fruit formation. Watering the tomato plants regularly keeps a steady flow of calcium moving from the soil into the developing fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ he diŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo nɛɛ akɛ blossom end rot. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ tsei amli yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ aduawai lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo o-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ daa lɛ, ebaaha calcium lɛ aya nɔ ajɛ sũ lɛ mli kɛya aduawai ni miida lɛ amli.

english: How do groundnut plants produce their nuts underneath the soil after flowering above ground?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei tsei woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii beni amɛwo fɔfɔi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Once groundnut flowers are pollinated above ground, the plant sends long stem-like tubes called pegs downward into the soil. These pegs push underground, where they safely expand into groundnut pods.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii fɔfɔi lɛ shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ tsuɔ ŋmeii kakadaji ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ pegs lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Akɛ nɛkɛ pin nɛɛ kudɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi. he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shweshweeshwe ni amɛtsɔ ŋmei ŋmeii

english: Why do experienced farmers plant plantains on the same field with young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ duɔ kookoo dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni amɛduɔ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and easily scorched by harsh sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and produce broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, protecting young cocoa from direct sun and keeping the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa, ni hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shãa amɛ oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Can plantain plants help keep moisture in the ground for my cocoa farm?
ga: Ani dumɔwui baanyɛ aye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛha mi kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, plantains create shade that slows down water evaporation from the soil. Their thick foliage and leaf mulch help retain ground moisture, which helps young cocoa roots survive dry periods.
ga: Hɛɛ, plantains haa hulutsoo baa ni haa nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo. Baai ni mli tse kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Enɛ haa kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: When should I start removing plantain trees from my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mabɔi dumɔwui ajiemɔ kɛjɛ kookoo ŋmɔ mli?

english: You should trim or remove plantain trees after about three to four years, once the cocoa trees grow strong enough to form their own thick canopy and no longer need heavy shade.
ga: Esa akɛ ofolɔ loo ojie dumɔwui lɛ yɛ aaafee afii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ kookoo tso lɛ da waa bɔ ni sa ni efee ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli wa yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehe ni ehe ehiaaa dɔŋŋ akɛ eyɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni tsii lɛ,.

english: If cocoa seedlings receive too much sun, their leaves will turn yellow, dry out at the edges, or look scorched, and the plant's overall growth will slow down drastically.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ ná hulu la babaoo lɛ Baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ, ebaagbi yɛ eshishigbɛ, loo ebaafee tamɔ nɔ ni eshã. ni tso lɛ dalɛ fɛɛ baafee mlɛo waa.

english: Why do plantain plants grow much faster than cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui daa oya fe kookoo tsei lɛ?

english: Plantains are fast-growing herbaceous plants that focus energy on quick leaf and stem production, whereas cocoa is a woody tree that takes longer to establish deep roots and strong branches.
ga: Plantains ji tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ tsuɔ baai kɛ amɛshishifãi ni feɔ oya lɛ ahe nii. Cocoa, yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, eji tso ni yeɔ afii babaoo ni eheɔ be babaoo dani efeɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ niji ni wa.

english: Do mature cocoa trees need as much shade as young seedlings do?
ga: Kookoo tso ni eda lɛ he miihia hulutsoo kɛ agbɛnɛ hu hulutsoo. Kɛ dumɔwui bibii loo daabi?

english: No, while young seedlings need heavy shade to survive, mature cocoa trees need more controlled sunlight to flower heavily and produce good pods, though light shade is still helpful.
ga: Dabi, eyɛ mli akɛ tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulutsoo ni tsii koni amɛhi shi moŋ. Shi cacao tsei ni eda lɛ he miihia ni akudɔ hulu la babaoo koni amɛwo fɔfɔi babaoo ni amɛwo ŋmeii kpakpai. Sɛɛnamɔi yɛ hulutsoo be mli po lolo.

english: Should I rely more on traditional farming methods from elders or advice from agricultural officers?
ga: Ani esa akɛ wɔkɛ wɔhe afɔ̃ blema okwaayeli gbɛi ni jɛ onukpai adɛŋ loo ŋaawoo ni jɛ okwaayeli he onukpai adɛŋ lɛ nɔ babaoo?

english: Combining both is best. Traditional knowledge from experienced local elders provides practical wisdom specific to your area, while agricultural officers offer modern techniques to prevent diseases and increase yield.
ga: Enyɔ lɛ ni akɛaafee ekome lɛ ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ. Kusum nilee ni jɛ onukpai ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ adɛŋ lɛ kɛ nilee ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii ni kɔɔ he pɔtɛɛ ni oyɔɔ lɛ he haa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, okwaayeli he onukpai lɛ kɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋaai ni akɛtsiɔ helai anaa ni akɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ba.

english: Is it safe to plant food crops like plantain alongside main cash crops like cocoa?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ abaadu niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains yɛ shika ŋmɔshi nibii wuji tamɔ kookoo masɛi?

english: Yes, intercropping food crops like plantain with young cocoa is safe and beneficial because food crops provide shade for the cocoa and give you food or income while waiting for cocoa to mature.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii ni akɛfutuɔ nii tamɔ plantains kɛ cocoa bibii ni akɛfee ekome lɛ dumɔ yɛ shweshweeshwe ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, niyenii tsei haa kookoo lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhaa bo niyenii loo shika be mli ni omɛɛɔ kookoo lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: How can I protect my cocoa seedlings from dying during the hot Harmattan season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-kookoo tsei lɛ ahe koni amɛkagboi yɛ Harmattan hulutsoo be mli?

english: You can protect seedlings by ensuring adequate shade from nurse plants like plantains and applying dry leaves around the base of the stems as mulch to cover the ground and trap soil moisture.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu dumɔwui ahe kɛtsɔ hulutsoo ni sa ni oooha amɛ kɛjɛ tsei bibii tamɔ plantains ahe kɛtsɔ baai ni egbi ni okɛbaabɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ shishi ji ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni akɛmɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: What are the signs that my cocoa field needs better soil nutrients?
ga: Mɛni ji okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni hi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Signs of low soil nutrients include pale green or yellowing leaves, slow stem growth, small pod sizes, and trees shedding leaves prematurely.
ga: Okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa lɛ ekomɛi ji baai eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ, tsei ni daraa blɛoo, kɛ tsei bibii. ni tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ oya

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow and curl up during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔleɔ ehe yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants curl their leaves to protect themselves from intense sunlight and slow down water loss. If the leaves turn yellow, it means the heat or lack of nutrients is stressing the plant's ability to produce food.
ga: Abele tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ nu ni hoɔ blɛoo lɛ he. Kɛji baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dɔlɛ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ miiha tso lɛ nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛbaatsu nii lɛ miihao.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods when the forest shade around them is too thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ beni koo ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli ewo ŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Cocoa lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ?

english: Cocoa trees need a balanced amount of light. While young cocoa needs shade, mature trees need enough direct sunlight filtering through to make energy for flowering and pod production.
ga: La ni ja he miihia kokoo tsei. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kookoo bibioo he miihia hulutsoo. Tsei ni edara lɛ taoɔ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha hewalɛ aha fɔfɔi kɛ pod feemɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers without growing peppers during hot spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni eduuu pepper yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, pepper plants shed their flowers to conserve energy and water, protecting the main stem until weather conditions improve.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he. Buu tsɔne wulu lɛ he kɛyashi kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does strong wind affect my plantain trees, and why do their leaves split so easily?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ saa mi plantain lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ? Ni mɛni hewɔ baai lɛ fãa oya lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves split naturally in strong winds so wind can pass through without uprooting the whole tree, though heavy winds can still dry out the plant and soil faster.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa nɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli ni ejieee tsei lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baaha tsei kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya moŋ.

english: Why do cassava plants drop their leaves during dry seasons and still survive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli shi ehiɔ shi lolo lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry periods to reduce water consumption. It rests and stores energy in its underground roots until rain returns to trigger new leaf growth.
ga: Akɛ ŋmei baa shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ koni akɛba nu ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ shi. Ebaajɔɔ ehe ni ekɛ hewalɛ ato eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba koni eha baai heei akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt in the afternoon even though I water them every morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ? Nu ni oooha daa leebi?

english: In intense midday heat, tomatoes lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can draw it from the soil, causing temporary wilting until the air cools down.
ga: Yɛ shwane gbi lɛ mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Tomatoi shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ tomato lɛ atsu nii yɛ be kukuoo mli kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: How does covering the soil with dry grass around my vegetable crops help them grow better?
ga: Mulching shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ jwɛi ni egbi ni ebɔle he lɛ Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni mi tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ?

english: Mulching with dry grass acts as a protective shield that keeps the soil cool, prevents water from evaporating quickly, and maintains steady moisture for the crop roots.
ga: Mulch ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekaho oya ni eha tso shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i daa

english: Why do the leaves on my cowpea plants turn pale green and stop growing after heavy continuous rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni ekpaa dalɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Excessive water fills the tiny air pockets in the soil, suffocating the roots so they cannot draw up nutrients needed to keep the leaves dark green and healthy.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛnyɛŋ amɛjie niyenii ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni eyɛ hewalɛ.

english: What happens to my crops if I put too much fertilizer on them at once?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo mli shikome?

english: Applying too much fertilizer creates high salt levels in the soil that burn the crop roots, causing leaf tips to dry up and potentially killing the plant.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ŋmei babaoo aya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ashã. Enɛ haa baai lɛ ashishigbɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni ebaanyɛ efite tso lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with small yields if I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo ni yibiiwoo fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When planted too close, crops compete heavily for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, causing them to stretch upward for light rather than growing broad leaves and big fruit.
ga: Kɛji adu he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná hulu la ni faaa, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni eŋmɛ gbɛ ni la lɛ abote mli. Mohu ɔ, nyɛ hyɛɔ baai nɛ a mi wa kɛ yiblii nguahi.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn and dry up easily under direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow quickly and provide living shade, protecting the young cocoa plants until they are strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛhaa hulutsoo. Buu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains flood the soil and water sits for too long, the roots drown because they cannot breathe, causing them to rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hoɔ ni nu lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu, ni no baaha amɛgboi.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground toward the sun, preventing leaves from rotting and helping tubers grow larger.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni efɔ lɛ, ni ekwɛɔ hulu lɛ hiɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa bulb lɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build strong, green leaves. Adding organic manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ eŋɔli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which takes nitrogen from the air and traps it in the soil through their roots. This naturally fertilizes the soil for crops planted in the next season.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why does putting dried cow or chicken manure on my land help my crops stay healthy during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo tsina ŋmei ni egbi ni mikɛfataa mishikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Animal manure feeds plants essential nutrients and improves the soil structure, helping the soil act like a sponge that holds onto moisture longer when rain is scarce.
ga: Koolooi ashishifã ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii feɔ fɛo. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ sponji, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ.

english: What causes small caterpillars to eat ragged holes in the middle of my maize leaves so fast?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ buji ni etse amɛhe lɛ? Oya yɛ ŋmãa baa ko teŋ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which hide in the inner funnel of the maize plant where it is soft and moist, eating the new leaves rapidly before they unfold.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ he ni amɛhe yɔɔ blɛoo ni amɛhe edɔ lɛ. Ye baai heei oya dani amɛje kpo.

english: Tomatoes shed their blossoms when temperature or water stress is too high. High heat damages the pollen inside the flower, causing the plant to drop the flower instead of growing a fruit.
ga: Tomato baakwɛ fɔfɔi kɛji hulutsoo loo nu mli haomɔ fa tsɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ kpataa fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɛ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to stay small and thin even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa beni nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa po lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal fertilizer, water, and sunlight away from your crops. Even with good rainfall, the weeds swallow up the food before your crops can reach it.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ miinɛ moŋ, shi ehi. Jwɛi lɛ po yeɔ niyenii lɛ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baashɛ.

english: Dig a small hole about hand-deep and squeeze a handful of soil. If it forms a soft ball that stays together without water dripping out, the ground has enough moisture for seeds to germinate safely.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ bu bibioo ko ni miihe ashɛ onine mlibotemɔ he. No sɛɛ lɛ, shwiemɔ sũ fioo ko kɛjɛ mli. Kɛji efee bɔɔlu ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni hiɔ shi ekome ni nu shwieee shi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: As a young person in Ghana looking to start farming, which fast-growing crop can give me a quick harvest and income?
ga: Ákɛ oblanyo fioo ni yɔɔ Ghana ni miisumɔ ni ebɔi okwaayeli. Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni daa oya baanyɛ aha maná yibii kɛ shika oya?

english: Vegetables like local tomatoes, pepper, and okra are fast-growing crops that can yield harvests within three to four months. They allow new farmers to generate quick cash flow compared to long-term tree crops like cocoa or oil palm.
ga: Aduawai tamɔ tomato, shito, kɛ okra ji tsei ni daa oya ni baanyɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. Enɛ haa okwaafoi heei náa shika oya kɛ akɛtoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ tamɔ kookoo loo mu tso lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers before turning into actual fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔii dani amɛbatsɔ anɔkwa yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop flowers when the weather gets too hot, when watering is inconsistent, or if there is a lack of key soil nutrients like phosphorus. Regular morning watering and using mulch keep the soil cool and moist so flowers turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛji nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ daa Aloo kɛji akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ fɔsfɔs bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, nu ni oooha daa leebi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. koni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ tomato

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants curl up during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miihoso yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a plant's natural defense to conserve water and protect itself from extreme heat. Watering the roots early in the morning helps the plant stay strong and hydrated throughout the intense afternoon sun.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ nu leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa edɔɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni naa wa lɛ mli.

english: If I plant my tomato seeds very close together, will I get more crops from my farm?
ga: Kɛ midu tomato dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ Ani maná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting too close forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak plants and tiny fruits. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to branch out, stay healthy, and produce a larger total harvest.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tso lɛ atswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ aduawai bibii baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ niji baaje kpo. Hiɛ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ofee nibii babaoo ni jɛɔ mli baa

english: What causes the bottom of my growing tomatoes to turn black and rotten before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni haa tomato ni midu lɛ shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani ekwɛ̃ɔ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium reaching the fruit, usually due to irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the plant absorb calcium smoothly from the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. ni calcium ni faaa lɛ kɛbaa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛjieɔ calcium kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomatoes split open while they are still ripening on the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomatoi lɛ mli gbalaa be mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ lolo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes split when they take in too much water too fast after a long dry spell, causing the inside to grow faster than the skin can stretch. Giving crops a steady, even water supply prevents this sudden swelling.
ga: Tomato fiteɔ kɛji akɛ aha lɛ nu babaoo oya tsɔ, ni egbiɔ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa mligbɛ lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tso lɛ nɔ daa kɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ trukaa fũu nɛɛ akafee nɔ ko.

english: When is the best time of the year in Ghana to plant tomatoes so heavy rains do not destroy them?
ga: Mɛni ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ Ghana ni esa akɛ adu tomato koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akagbe amɛ?

english: Planting tomatoes toward the end of the main rainy season or using simple irrigation during the dry season works best. Heavy downpours during peak flowering wash away blossoms and promote fungal rot on leaves and fruit.
ga: Tomato ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ naagbee loo nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mlɛo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ fɔfɔi be mli lɛ hoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe ni ehaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ baai kɛ aduawai lɛ anɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: What kind of tomato quality do processing factories look for when buying from local farmers?
ga: Mɛɛ su tsɔne ni akɛfeɔ tomato lɛ yɔɔ kɛ́ ehe nii kɛjɛ maŋ lɛ mli okwaafoi adɛŋ?

english: Processing factories look for firm, fully ripe, disease-free tomatoes with thick flesh and rich red color. Varieties with less water and more solid pulp produce better yield when processed into pastes and sauces.
ga: Mɛi ni feɔ nibii nɛɛ taoɔ tomato ni wa, ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ, ni hela bɛ mli, ni loo lɛ mli edɔ ni eyɛ su tsuru ni mli tse. Srɔtoi ni nu faaa mli ni amɛhe wa waa lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai kɛji akɛ afee amɛ paste kɛ sauce.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes spoil so fast before I can get them sold?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya dani abaanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes spoil quickly if picked when fully red or packed in unventilated containers under hot weather. Picking them when they just start showing a pink tint (breaker stage) and keeping them in ventilated crates extends their life.
ga: Tomato baafite oya kɛji akɛ ajie lɛ beni eyɛ tɔrɔmɔɔ kwraa loo akɛto tsɛnsii ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli mli yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. Picking be mli ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛjieɔ pinki su kpo kɛkɛ. (distance breaker) ni akɛwo adeka ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ baaha ewala sɛɛ atsɛ.

english: How should I pack my harvested vegetables so they don't get crushed on the way to market or processing centers?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ mawo mi-aduawai ni mikpa lɛ amli koni amɛkakumɔ yɛ gbɛ ni yaa jara nɔ loo he ni atsuɔ nii yɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: Avoid overpacking fresh produce into heavy sacks; instead, use shallow, rigid plastic or wooden crates lined with paper or leaves. Stacking sturdy crates prevents the weight of top layers from crushing the bottom fruit.
ga: Tsi ohe kɛjɛ nibii heei babaoo ni oookɛwo kotokui ni tsii amli lɛ he. Kɛ plastic loo tso adeka ni mli ekwɔɔɔ atsu nii. Nɔ ni wa ni akɛ wolo loo baai ebɔ he moŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ adekai ni wa to he lɛ, ebaatsi ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ muji lɛ naa koni ekakumɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to measure and space out my maize seeds instead of just scattering them on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ masusu mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ni majara mli moŋ fe ni magbɛ amɛ ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When maize crops are spaced correctly, each plant gets enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients without competing with its neighbors, which leads to bigger cobs and higher yields.
ga: Kɛ́ oodu ŋmãa lɛ, ha gbɛ ni sa kɛjɛ oteŋ. Tso fɛɛ tso baaná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ekɛ ekutsoŋbii lɛ akaŋ akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my yam vines need high soil mounds to grow well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow underground and need loose, deep soil to expand. High mounds protect the tubers from hard soil and excess water logging, allowing them to grow large and healthy.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni ehe hiaa shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli tse koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ buɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa kɛ nu ni fa fe nine ni ahiɔ mli lɛ he. Ha amɛdara ni amɛhe awa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under strong sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide canopy shade and retain soil moisture, protecting the cocoa plants during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ haa hɔɔŋ ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tso lɛ he yɛ eshishijee afii lɛ amli

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, which naturally restores nutrients that heavy feeder crops like maize took away.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni tsei ni yeɔ kooloi wuji, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ jieɔ lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Maize leaves curl inward during intense heat to reduce the amount of leaf surface exposed to the sun, which helps the plant conserve internal water and avoid drying out.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli koni ekɛba baa lɛ hiɛ ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ nu toɔ emli, ni ehaaa baai lɛ agbi.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during prolonged dry spells to lower their need for water and survive drought conditions, after which fresh leaves will grow back when the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli koni amɛha amɛ nu he hiamɔ nii aba shi ni amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ shihilɛi amli. No sɛɛ lɛ, baai heei baakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when temperatures get too high or when there is inconsistent watering, which prevents proper pollination and fruit formation.
ga: Tomatoi baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu lɛ haaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ pollination ni sa kɛ aduawai ni baa lɛ naa.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow plenty of leaves but very few pods when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ baa babaoo shi ŋmɔtɔ fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli beni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo lɛ?

english: Excessive water and soil nutrients cause cowpea plants to focus all their energy on leaf and stem growth rather than producing flowers and seed pods.
ga: Nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni fa fe nine lɛ haa cowpea tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai kɛ amɛshishifãi ni miida lɛ ahe nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔii kɛ dumɔwui ŋmɔji

english: Why do weeds make my crops look weak and pale green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow quickly and steal light, water, and essential soil nutrients away from your main crops, leaving your crops malnourished.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ onibii titrii lɛ amli. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, niyenii ni oduɔ lɛ baaná niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: How can I tell underground cassava roots are fully mature and ready for harvest?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa amɛ?

english: Cassava is typically ready when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, the base of the stem hardens into wood, and the ground around the root base starts to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. Tso lɛ shishigbɛ wa ni etsɔɔ tso. ni he ni ebɔle shishitoo lɛ he lɛ bɔi fãmɔ

english: How does putting chicken manure on my maize field help the crop grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ?

english: Chicken manure is rich in nitrogen and organic matter, which enriches the soil and helps your maize grow strong stalks, greener leaves, and larger cobs.
ga: Nitrogen kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɛ tsina ŋmɔ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa o-abele lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii ni wa, baai eŋɔli, kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot withstand direct, harsh sunlight. Leaving or planting shade trees protects them from heat, keeps the soil moist, and prevents leaf burn during their early years.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui nyɛɛɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ ni oooshi loo odu lɛ baaye abua ni abu ohe kɛjɛ latsaa he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa baa lɛ shãaa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli

english: Cassava naturally sheds its leaves during long dry spells to reduce water loss and protect its root tubers. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh green leaves.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni ebu eshishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tsei lɛ baakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Wait until the soil has received two or three good rains so it is deeply moist. Planting in dry soil can cause seeds to spoil before they can sprout.
ga: Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ kpakpa enyɔ loo etɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ waa. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ agbo dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Planting plantains too close together forces them to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stems and smaller bunches of fruit.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo kɛ aduawai bibii.

english: What causes holes in my young maize leaves and leaves caterpillar droppings inside the leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli kɛ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ baa lɛ mli lɛ baa?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm pest. They feed on tender leaves inside the plant's funnel, so checking your farm early and using recommended treatments saves the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Fall Armyworm lɛ. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra. Ni kɛ akɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafite.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slowly and produce a poor harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo ni amɛmiiwo yibii kpakpai lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital sunlight, water, and soil nutrients away from your crops. Clearing weeds early leaves all the soil nutrients available for your crops to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ahi shi koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: This condition, known as blossom-end rot, is caused by uneven watering and a lack of calcium uptake. Keeping soil moisture consistent prevents the fruit bottoms from rotting.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be kɛ calcium ni anáaa lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ baatsi aduawai lɛ ashishi lɛ naa koni ekafite.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Regular watering and balanced fertilizer help flowers set fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo mli. Nu ni akɛhaa fɔfɔi lɛ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains specific soil nutrients and allows maize pests and diseases to build up in the soil. Rotating with legumes like cowpeas restores soil fertility.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa tsake lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I test my farm soil before I start planting my seeds for the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maka shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ makwɛ dani mabɔi dumɔwui kɛha be lɛ?

english: Testing your soil before planting gives you vital information about what nutrients are missing and whether the soil is too acidic. Taking time to check your soil first prevents you from wasting expensive seeds and fertilizer on land that is not ready.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa ni afeɔ dani aduɔ nii lɛ baaha ale nibii ni he hiaa ni kɔɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni elaaje lɛ he kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ acid tsɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ be kwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ebaatsi bo gbɛ koni okafite dumɔwui kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni asaaa nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cowpea seeds rot in the ground instead of sprouting after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea dumɔwui lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛakwɛ̃ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds need air as well as moisture to sprout. When heavy rain leaves soil waterlogged, the seeds drown and soil fungi attack them before they can emerge. Planting in well-drained soil or raised beds protects the seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui he hiaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ fɛ̃i dani amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui lɛ baagbee nu mli ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baatutua amɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ loo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu dumɔwui lɛ ahe.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are a signal that the plants are starving for nitrogen. Heavy rains often wash nitrogen out of the topsoil, so applying a small dose of nitrogen fertilizer like Urea helps the plants regain their green color and grow strong.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fioo tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná amɛhe ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: If I add double the recommended fertilizer to my pepper plants, will they produce yield twice as fast?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛwo mi-pepper tsei lɛ amli lɛ toi enyɔ lɛ, Ani amɛbaawo yibii oya fe tsutsu lɛ shii enyɔ?

english: No, putting too much fertilizer will burn the roots and damage the crop. It is always better to adjust the dosage down to the exact recommended amount so the plant can safely absorb the nutrients without getting damaged.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli fe nine lɛ, ebaashã shishifãi lɛ ni efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsake tsofa lɛ mli tsofa lɛ mli bɔ ni sa koni tso lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shweshweeshwe ni nɔ ko nɔ ko akafite.

english: How can I tell if my young cocoa trees are getting damaged by too much sunlight?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ efite mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Crops communicate their stress through their foliage. If young cocoa leaves start scorching, curling up, or turning brown at the edges, it means the sun is too severe and you need to plant plantains or shade trees to shield them.
ga: Tsei kɛ nɔnyɛɛ haa kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Kɛji akɛ kookoo baai bibii lɛ bɔi shãa, amɛkpokpo, loo amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ amɛnaagbɛ lɛ No tsɔɔ akɛ hulu la lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Ni ehe miihia ni odu dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ.

english: Dropping leaves is a natural survival trick cassava uses during drought to save water. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout new green leaves and continue building its roots under the ground.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ gbɛ ni ŋmei kɛtsuɔ nii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni ekɛbu nu he. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baawo baai heei ni eŋɔli ni ebaaya nɔ ekwɛ̃ shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: I sprayed pesticide on my tomato farm, but the insects are still moving hours later. Did the chemical fail?
ga: Mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieɔ mitato ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ. Shi ŋmeii lɛ miitsi amɛhe lolo yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai komɛi asɛɛ. Ani tsofai lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii?

english: Many modern farm chemicals do not kill pests instantly upon contact; they require time to absorb into the pest's body. You must wait a day or two to see full results before deciding to spray more chemicals.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsofai babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ egbeee tsɛŋemɔ helai amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ amɛhe. Be he miihia amɛ dani amɛbote tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli. Esa akɛ omɛ gbi kome loo gbii enyɔ koni ona bɔ ni ebaatsu nii eha lɛ fɛɛ dani okpɛ oyiŋ akɛ obaashwie tsofai babaoo nɔ.

english: Why do diseases spread so fast through my farm after a windy day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ gbi ni kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The wind carries invisible fungal spores and tiny insect pests from infected plants to healthy ones across long distances. Knowing this helps you inspect your crop downwind right after stormy weather.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni anaaa kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛjɛɔ tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli kɛyaa he ko ni jɛkɛ. Enɛ ni ooole lɛ baaye abua bo ni okwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli yɛ ahum ni tswaa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to cut off the small side shoots on my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nitsulɔ ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ wo mi ŋaa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? yɛ tomato tso lɛ nɔ

english: Pruning small side shoots, called suckers, stops the plant from wasting food on extra leaves. This allows the plant to focus its energy on growing bigger, healthier fruits.
ga: ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots Enɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafite niyenii kɛjɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I harvest my cocoa pods as soon as they start showing a little yellow color?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikpaa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ kɛji amɛje shishi amɛfee ŋmɔŋ fioo pɛ?

english: Cocoa beans inside the pod need extra time to fully ripen and mature. Plucking pods too early leaves you with small, flat beans that give poor quality chocolate and bring less money at sale time.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ pod lɛ mli lɛ biɔ be kroko dani amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ ogbala ŋmeii lɛ oya tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ahi ohe. No haa onáa tsokolate ni hi jogbaŋŋ, ni shika hu baa shi yɛ jarayeli be mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when the sun is very bright?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains or cassava around them creates living shade that protects the young cocoa plants and keeps moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni aduɔ yɛ jɛmɛ he fɛɛ he. Ehaa hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ baa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Yellow leaves usually show that the maize plant is hungry for nitrogen, a vital nutrient in the soil. Applying animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer like Urea helps the leaves turn dark green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ nitrogen tamɔ urea tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why is it bad if I plant maize on the exact same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific plant nutrients from the soil and allows pests that attack maize to multiply. Rotating maize with crops like groundnuts or beans restores soil fertility and breaks the pest cycle.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ lɛ haa tso pɔtɛɛ ko mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ koni amɛshwere. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei tsakeɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni efoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ lɛ mli.

english: Cassava roots rot when they sit in soaked, waterlogged soil for too long because the roots cannot breathe. Planting your cassava on raised earth mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji amɛtara shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up toward the sunshine to make energy. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet ground to prevent diseases and helps the plant produce much bigger tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɛya ŋwɛi kɛya hulu la lɛ he koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni nu yɔɔ lɛ koni helai akabote mli ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ewo ŋmeii wuji babaoo.

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from the leaves. Spraying early with neem oil extract or recommended insect treatments protects the leaves so they can expand normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Ni akɛ neem fɔ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ nɔ mra Aloo, tsofa ni akɛwoɔ kooloi amli lɛ baaye abua ni abu baai lɛ ahe koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã bɔ ni sa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or lack of soil nutrients. Giving your tomato plants regular water and mulching the soil keeps them cool and helps flowers stay on to turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ hao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa waa mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni oooha o-tomato tsei lɛ daa ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo mli lɛ baaye abua ni amɛha amɛhe afee fɛ̃i ni eye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ aya hiɛ kɛyashi amɛbaatsɔ aduawai.

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into plant food in the soil, which helps neighboring maize grow without buying as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni etsakeɔ lɛ efeɔ tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmãa ni yɔɔ afã lɛ daa ni ehe ehiaaa ni ehe tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli.

english: Why are weeds taking away the strength of my crop plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miihe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahewalɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal soil food, groundwater, and sunlight away from your crops. Clearing weeds early when crops are young ensures your crops get all the nutrients they need to grow big.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ onibii amli lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Beni tsei lɛ darako lɛ enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni otsei lɛ naa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara.

english: Why do I see small caterpillars eating the inside of my maize stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are usually Fall Armyworms or stem borers that hatch from eggs laid by small moths. Catching them early and applying neem solution or appropriate treatments into the center of the plant stops them before they destroy the whole crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, loo stem borers ni jɛɔ ŋmeii bibii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ amli lɛ amli. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ neem tsofa loo tsofa ni sa tsu nii yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ baatsi amɛnaa dani amɛbaafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle strong, direct sunlight because their foliage burns easily and their roots dry out. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a canopy that protects the young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya ni amɛshishifãi lɛ hu gbɛ́ɔ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why should I measure spacing between my crops instead of planting as many seeds as possible close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu gbɛ ni kã miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ he? Mohu ɔ, du dumɔwu ɔmɛ ngɛ he nɛ a kɛ a he maa su bɔ nɛ o ma nyɛ.

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak plants and small yields. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room and food to grow healthy and produce big fruits.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ waa ni ewo yibii wuji.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and strong. Adding compost, manure, or a nitrogen fertilizer can help bring back their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do experienced vegetable farmers cover the ground around their crops with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ ni duɔ aduawai lɛ kɛ jwɛi haa he ni amɛduɔ nii yɛ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or palm leaves, called mulching, keeps the soil moist by stopping water from evaporating in the sun. It also keeps the roots cool and blocks weeds from taking over your farm.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmei tsei baaha nɔ Atsɛɔ lɛ mulching. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i kɛtsɔ nu ni ehaaa efo yɛ hulu la lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ hu feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Should I apply fertilizer to my crops right before a heavy rainstorm comes?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani ahum aba?

english: No, you should not apply fertilizer right before heavy rainfall because the strong flowing water will wash the fertilizer away before the plant roots can drink it. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist after a gentle rain.
ga: Dabi, esaaa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa baa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu ni hoɔ waa lɛ baaho ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anu. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ.

english: What causes tiny holes and chewed edges on my corn leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Kɛ ŋmeii ni ashɛre yɛ mi-abele baai lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: Small holes and chewed edges are usually caused by caterpillar pests like the Fall Armyworm that hide in the center funnel of the corn plant. Checking your field early and using safe bio-pesticides or neem extract can stop them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni emɔ amɛ, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni atsɔ mli lɛ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe loo neem mli nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ akpa amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant tomatoes on the exact same plot of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ makwɛ tomato yɛ he kome daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same land every season drains the specific nutrients that crop needs and allows soil pests and diseases to multiply. Alternating with crops like beans or cassava helps break disease cycles and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tsei lɛ lɛ hoɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ babaoo. Nibii ni aduɔ ni tsakeɔ amɛhe tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekpaa hela lɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi.

english: How do I know when my cassava stems underground are ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cassava tsei lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 8 to 12 months after planting, depending on the variety. You can tell it is maturing when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Edamɔ henɔi lɛ anɔ Obaanyɛ ona akɛ baai lɛ edara kɛji baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why should I pinch off the extra side branches growing on my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Removing small extra side shoots allows the plant to send its energy and nutrients directly into growing bigger, healthier tomatoes instead of wasting energy on useless extra leaf branches.
ga: ŋmeii bibii ni ajieɔ lɛ He ni yɔɔ kpo lɛ haa tso lɛ tsɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛyaa tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: Why do I need to dig up weeds and turn the soil over before I plant my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo jwɛi lɛ ni matsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Turning over the soil loosens it so young roots can easily spread and find water, while removing weeds ensures wild plants do not steal sunlight, space, and food from your crop seeds when they sprout.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa egbɔjɔɔ bɔni afee ni shishifãi bibii lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛna nu oya. Yɛ be mli ni jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa koo mli tsei lɛ ejuuu hulu la, ŋwɛi kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ odumɔwui lɛ amli beni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen or that the soil is waterlogged, which prevents the roots from breathing and taking up nutrients from the earth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ amu ni amɛkaŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: How do I know if my cassava leaves are curling because of a disease or just because of the hot sun?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ hela hewɔ loo hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ pɛ hewɔ ni ŋmeii baai lɛ miihoso lɛ?

english: If leaves curl and show light yellow mosaic patches or sticky spots underneath, it is caused by disease or whiteflies. If they only wilt during the hottest part of the afternoon and recover by night, the plant is simply responding to heat.
ga: Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛyɛ mosaic ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shishi. Etsɔɔ akɛ hela loo ŋmeii yɛŋ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kɛji akɛ amɛgboi yɛ shwane mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ pɛ mli ni amɛhe wa amɛ gbɛkɛ. Tso lɛ baaha hetoo yɛ latsaa lɛ pɛ he.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot survive direct harsh sunlight and hot dry winds. They need shade from taller trees or plantains to protect their delicate leaves and keep the surrounding soil cool and moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji loo plantains adɛŋ koni ebu amɛbaai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe ni eha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ.

english: Is it safe for me to sow my seeds immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is risky because the first rain is often followed by a long dry spell. If seeds germinate and the rain stops, the tender roots will quickly dry out and die in the hot soil.
ga: Oshara yɛ ejaakɛ bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ ni nugbɔ lɛ kpa Shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I mix animal manure into the soil weeks before planting instead of applying fresh manure right when I put the seeds in?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli otsii komɛi dani madu lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mikɛ ŋmeii hee baafata he amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ woɔ mli lɛ.

english: Fresh manure releases intense heat and strong gas as it breaks down, which can burn young plant roots. Allowing it to decompose in the soil first makes the nutrients safe and ready for the plant to use.
ga: Manɔ hee jieɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli wa beni efiteɔ lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tsei bibii ashishifãi ashã. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni efite yɛ sũ lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ehaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni tsei baanyɛ amɛkɛtsu nii.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller yields when I plant many seeds close together to save space?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni mikɛha he ko akafee nɔ ko lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing plants compete against each other for light, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin stalks and very small cobs or tubers.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii bibii waa baa.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience high heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of key nutrients like phosphorus in the soil.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ ni jɛ la ni mli wa mli lɛ he. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa loo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases that feed on that specific crop to build up in the field.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔji amli.

english: Weeds have strong root systems that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients faster than your crops can, leaving your plants undernourished.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe bɔ ni otsei lɛ baanyɛ afee. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ otsei lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers start to rot quickly after I store them in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ bɔi fitemɔ oya beni mikɛto ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot quickly if they are bruised during harvest, stored in places with poor airflow, or exposed to excessive heat and moisture in the storage area.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. Okɛto he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ. loo hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni fa fe nine yɛ hei ni akɛ nibii toɔ lɛ

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is a key food maize needs to stay green and build big cobs. When the plant lacks nitrogen, it takes whatever nutrient is left from the older bottom leaves to feed the young top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni abele ahi shi eŋɔli ni efee ŋmeii wuji. Kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen Ebaajie niyenii ni eshwɛ kɛjɛ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli ni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ.

english: Crops cannot eat solid fertilizer dry; it must dissolve in water so the roots can drink it in. If you apply fertilizer to dry soil under full sun, it can burn your crop roots or blow away before helping the plant.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nyɛŋ aye ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa ni egbi. Esa akɛ atsɔ nu mli koni shishifãi lɛ anu. Kɛji akɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ wo hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tso shishifãi baanyɛ ashã loo kɔɔyɔɔ atswa amɛ dani abaanyɛ ahere tso lɛ yiwala.

english: How do I know which way is up when I am sticking cassava stems into the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole gbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei nine wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Look closely at the small leaf nodes or buds along the stem. These little bumps should always point upwards toward the sky, because if you plant the stem upside down, the shoots struggle to grow and your harvest will be very small.
ga: Kwɛmɔ baai bibii ni ebɔle ehe loo ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Esa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi be fɛɛ be. Ejaakɛ kɛ́ odu tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ewa akɛ obaakwɛ̃ ni okpamɔ lɛ baafee bibioo kwraa.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under bright sunlight. Plantains grow fast with wide leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving the young cocoa plants the cool shade and moisture they need to survive their first two years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Groundnut flowers bloom above ground, but the actual nuts grow underground. After pollination, the plant naturally bends its stems downward to push the developing seed pods deep into the warm soil where they can safely mature.
ga: Peanut fɔfɔii fɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ, shi ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. after pollination Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛyaa shi koni amɛkɛtsi dumɔwui ni miiya hiɛ lɛ amli kɛya shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do I have to erect tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mato tso kakadaŋŋ ko koni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally like to climb high so their leaves can spread out and catch full sunlight to make food. Keeping the leaves off the damp ground also prevents leaves from rotting and helps the tubers underground grow much larger.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, sweet potato wain tsei sumɔɔ ni amɛkwɔ kɛya shɔŋŋ koni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo ni amɛkɛhoo amɛ niyenii lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ koni ekafite, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants crinkling and curling up into tight balls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe ni efee bɔɔlu ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites that hide under the leaves and drain the plant's juices. These insects can also spread plant viruses that make the new leaves grow out deformed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ekɛ ehe teeɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni ejieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ koolooi nɛɛ baanyɛ amɛgbɛ tsei amli helai ni haa baai heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ fiteɔ lɛ hu amɛshwã.

english: Why do insects flock to my cowpea field as soon as the flowers appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii baa mi-cowpea ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji fɔfɔi lɛ je kpo pɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers produce a sweet nectar that attracts pests like thrips and pod borers. Protecting the plant during the flowering stage is critical, because if insects damage the flowers, they fall off before forming seed pods.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ woɔ nu ni gbalaa kooloi tamɔ thrips kɛ pod borers. Tsei ahe ni abuɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia waa. Ejaakɛ kɛji kooloi bibii kpata fɔfɔi ahiɛ lɛ Fɔfɔi hu shwieɔ shi dani dumɔwui akutsei baa.

english: If too many shoots grow around one plantain stem, they compete for water, light, and soil nutrients. Removing extra shoots leaves only two or three strong stems, which guarantees larger and heavier plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ tso kome Nakai ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ baajɛ mli aba. Enɛ maa nɔ mi akɛ plantain lɛ baafee agbo ni etsii.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomato fruits turning soft and black before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ediŋŋ dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This soft black bottom is called blossom-end rot, caused when the plant cannot pull enough calcium from the soil, often due to irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the plant transport calcium properly to the fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ shishigbɛ diŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo nɛɛ akɛ blossom end rot. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ calcium lɛ yaa aduawai lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot handle direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees to protect their leaves and maintain moisture in the soil until they grow stronger.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo koni amɛbu amɛbaai lɛ ahe ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi amɛhe baawa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate that the maize lacks nitrogen in the soil. Maize needs a lot of food to grow, and without enough nutrients, it pulls nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to support new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Niyenii babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃. ni ebɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa Abɛi hu baajie nitrogen kɛjɛ shishigbɛ baai momoi lɛ amli koni eye ebua dalɛ hee ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ.

english: What causes small holes in my young maize leaves with powdery dirt left inside the leaf funnels?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi gbekɛ lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmãa baa ni muji eshwɛ yɛ baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It hides inside the central shoot of the maize plant during the day and eats the young leaves, which can destroy the plant if not treated early.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ekɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni eyeɔ baai bibii, ni baanyɛ agbe tso lɛ kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ oya.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the soil when heavy rains fall for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long because the roots cannot breathe. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines up off the ground with tall sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu sweet potato wain tsei ni tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yam vines need sunlight on their leaves to make the food that grows big tubers underground. Staking raises the leaves toward the sun and prevents fungal diseases that spread on wet ground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛ́ amɛmiikwɛ bulb agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baaha baai lɛ akwɛ hulu lɛ hiɛ ni ebaatsi fungal helai anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa hei ni nu yɔɔ lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when weather temperatures become too hot or when the soil suddenly shifts from very dry to very wet, which stresses the plant and stops pollination.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ ni amɛkpaa pollination.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap, or by a leaf curl virus spread by whiteflies that damages leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ leaf curl hela ko ni ŋmeii yɛŋ ni fiteɔ baa lɛ dalɛ nɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: If too many shoots grow around the main tree, they all fight for the same water and soil nutrients. Removing extra shoots leaves only two or three, ensuring big and heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii komɛi miikwɛ̃ yɛ Tsei wuji babaoo tsɔ Tsei wuji fɛɛ wuɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛha nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ, ŋmeii 2 loo 3 pɛ baa, ni no haa aduawai wuji ni tsii baa.

english: How does planting cowpea or groundnuts help make my soil better for next season's crop?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ aha be ni baa lɛ mli dumɔ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant dies, that stored nitrogen remains in the soil to feed the next crop, like maize.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ niyenii.

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry spell before the main rainy season starts. Seeds planted too early may sprout but will wither and die if continuous rains do not follow immediately.
