ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi. Dumɔwui ni adu mra tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ shi amɛbaagbi ni amɛgboi kɛji nugbɔ ni yaa nɔ enɛɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen. Maize needs nitrogen to build green leaves, so when the soil lacks this nutrient, the plant moves what little it has from old bottom leaves to feed the new top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ekɛ baai eŋɔli aba. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii bɛ lɛ Tso lɛ jieɔ nɔ fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my groundnut plants look healthy above ground, but produce empty shells with no nuts inside when I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ejie ŋmei ni nɔ ko bɛ mli ni ŋmei ko bɛ mli beni mikpa lɛ lɛ.

english: Empty groundnut pods, often called 'pops,' happen when the soil lacks calcium. Groundnut pods absorb calcium directly from the surrounding soil to fill out the seeds, so poor soil calcium leaves the pods hollow.
ga: Peanut pods ni bɛ nɔ ko, ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ lɛ ‘pops’ lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ calcium. Peanut pods lɛ shwieɔ calcium kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛwo dumɔwui lɛ amli ekoŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, calcium ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ afee ŋmeii.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with weak stems when I plant them very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ be mli ni miduɔ amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they shade one another and compete for sunlight. The plants respond by stretching rapidly upward to reach the light, making their stems thin, tall, and easily broken.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la. Tso lɛ haa hetoo kɛtsɔ oyaiyeli ni ekɛbaashɛ la lɛ he lɛ nɔ. Ehaa tso lɛ mli tsɔne lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ekwɛɔ ni efoɔ oya.

english: Excessive flower drop in cocoa is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like mirids (capsids), extreme moisture stress, or lack of insect pollinators like midges. Protecting pollinators and controlling pests keeps the flowers attached.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mirids (capsids) lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ kookoo nɔ fe nine lɛ baa. Haomɔ ni jɛɔ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo mli baa. aloo fɔfɔi ni haa fɔfɔi tamɔ midges lɛ bɛ, fɔfɔi ahebuu kɛ kooloi ni gbeɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe nitsumɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɔ shi.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling tightly upward and stopping the fruit from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ miiho kɛmiiya ŋwɛi ni amɛmiikpa aduawai lɛ adalɛ?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is commonly caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. When infected, the plant concentrates its energy on defending itself rather than expanding leaves or growing large fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Kɛji hela lɛ emɔmɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ maa amɛhebuu nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a gblɛɛɔ a ba ɔmɛ a mi loo a woɔ yiblii nguahi.

english: Why are the leaf tips of my swamp rice turning brown and drying up during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi Nong Khao baai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Browning leaf tips in swamp rice can be caused by fungal diseases like rice blast or by too much iron in waterlogged soil (iron toxicity), both of which prevent the plant from taking up water properly.
ga: Fungal helai tamɔ rice blight baanyɛ aha baa ni yɔɔ peat rice mli lɛ ashishifãi ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ aba. aloo dade babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ tsɔ. (iron toxicity) Enɛɛmɛi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ tsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaŋɔ nu jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants shed their flower buds and small fruits during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ aduawai yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry air cause pepper plants to drop buds and fruits to save moisture and stay alive. Without enough water, the plant cuts off supply to non-essential parts like flowers.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ haa pepper tsei lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛwoɔ aduawai koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛhi shi. Kɛji nu faaa lɛ Nitsumɔhe lɛ baafo nibii ni he ehiaaa tamɔ fɔfɔii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily at the root whenever a strong wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees easily blow over if microscopic worms (nematodes) or stem borers have damaged their root system underground. Weak roots cannot anchor the heavy stem and fruit bunches against high winds.
ga: Ewaaa akɛ ŋmeii bibii shwieɔ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ. (Nematodes) loo ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ. Shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ tsei ni tsii lɛ kɛ aduawai akui lɛ anɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he.

english: Why are my cassava roots remaining thin and woody instead of swelling into big tubers after a year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ tsei yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee bulbs wuji yɛ afi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots fail to swell when the soil is too hard and compacted, or when the plant lacks potassium. Hard soil physical boundaries stop the roots from expanding wide.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa tsɔ ni ebɔle ehe. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ potassium Shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ husui ni yɔɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why do my stored yams rot and go soft quickly inside the barn shortly after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ fiteɔ oya ni efeɔ blɛoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpaa ŋmɔ lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam rot in storage usually starts from small cuts or bruises made during harvest. Fungi and bacteria enter through these hidden wounds, especially if the storage barn is warm and lacks fresh airflow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni akɛtoɔ ŋmeii ahe lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni baa yɛ kpamɔ be mli. Fungus kɛ bacteria boteɔ pilamɔi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ nɛɛ amli. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛji akɛ shĩa lɛ mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ jɛmɛ.

english: How can I make an old farm land that has been left to bush rich enough for planting crops again?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ momo ni jwɛi eshi lɛ afee nɔ ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ?

english: You can clear the vegetation, leave the cut weeds to decompose naturally as organic mulch, and plant soil-building leguminous crops like cowpeas or cover crops to restore vital nutrients to the soil.
ga: Obaanyɛ ojie tsei lɛ kɛjɛ jɛmɛ. Ha jwɛi ni afo lɛ afite yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli. ni adu ŋmeii ni maa shikpɔŋ tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it helpful to stop farming on a piece of land for a few years when crops stop yielding well?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ baaba he akɛ aaakpa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ okwaayeli afii fioo komɛi beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekpa ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai awomɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, leaving land to rest or fallow allows the soil to naturally regenerate its organic matter and nutrients through falling leaves and natural root activity, making it fertile again for future planting.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ejɔɔ ehe loo efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ tswaa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛtsɔ baai ni egbee shi kɛ adebɔɔ mli shishifãi anitsumɔ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ kɛha okwaayeli wɔsɛɛ.

english: How do I know if my farmland has recovered and is healthy enough to support crops like plantains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ ehiɛ edɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains?

english: Healthy, recovered soil usually has a dark rich color, stays moist without waterlogging, crumbles easily in your hands, and contains visible organisms like earthworms.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni asaa lɛ fɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kwɛmɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni nu akahiɛ mli. Efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli ni bɔɔ nii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni abaanyɛ ana, tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii yɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my plantain shoots turning yellow and drying up early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi oya lɛ?

english: This is often caused by leaf spot diseases like Black Sigatoka or soil-borne fungi like Panama disease, which prevent the leaves from catching sunlight and feeding the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji baa lɛ he helai tamɔ Black Sigatoka loo sũ mli ŋmeii tamɔ Panama hela, ni haaa baa lɛ aná hulu la ni ekɛ niyenii aha tsei lɛ.

english: How can I choose healthy plantain suckers so I do not bring disease to my clear farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ koni hela akaba miŋmɔ ni mli tse lɛ mli?

english: Select vigorous 'sword suckers' with narrow leaves, make sure the bulb at the bottom is firm and white without dark spots, and peel off the outer roots to check for hidden pests like stem borers or nematodes.
ga: Halamɔ ‘Sword Bud’ ni wa ni eyɛ baai bibii. Kwɛmɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ afee shiŋŋ yɛ shishigbɛ ni amɛfee futafuta ni ŋmeii diji ko bɛ he. ni ojie shishifãi ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ koni okwɛ kɛji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ tamɔ stem borers loo nematodes yɛ mli.

english: How do plant diseases manage to get onto a newly cleared farm field?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ akwɛ tsei ahe helai anɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ hee ni ajie lɛ nɔ?

english: Diseases can enter new farms through infected planting materials like sick suckers, contaminated farm tools like cutlasses, wind, running water, or pests moving from unkept neighboring farms.
ga: Helai baanyɛ abote ŋmɔji heei amli. Abaanyɛ ana kɛtsɔ dumɔ nibii ni hela emɔ amɛ tamɔ suckers ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ nɔ. Okwaafoi anitsumɔ nibii ni mli ewo muji tamɔ tsɔnei ni akɛfoɔ nii, kɔɔyɔɔ, nu ni hoɔ, loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ ni asaaa amɛhe lɛ amli.

english: What measures can I take to protect my newly prepared farm from getting plant diseases?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛi manyɛ matsɔ nɔ mabu miŋmɔ hee ni misaa lɛ he kɛjɛ tsei ahe helai ahe?

english: Always use certified disease-free suckers or seeds, clean your cutlasses and boots with water and soap before working, and maintain proper spacing so air flows easily between your plants.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, okɛ ŋmeii loo dumɔwui ni atsɔɔ akɛ hela bɛ mli lɛ atsu nii. Okɛ samla kɛ nu atsumɔ dade kɛ bɔɔtu lɛ he dani otsu nii. Ni ha gbɛ ni sa ahi shi bɔni afee ni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ oya.

english: What should I do immediately if I spot a diseased plantain tree in my farm?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji mina dumɔwui ni hela emɔ amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Uproot the entire sick plant right away, remove it from the farm, and chop it up to burn or bury it so that wind and insects cannot carry the sickness to surrounding healthy plants.
ga: Jiemɔ tsei fɛɛ ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ mli ni afoɔ mli koni ashã loo afu. Enɛ baatsi kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkaŋɔ helai kɛya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do unwanted weeds keep growing back so quickly on my farm after I clear the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ataooo lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mijie he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds stay dormant in the dirt for years and germinate rapidly once clearing exposes the ground to sunlight and rainwater, requiring regular weeding until your main crops grow enough shade to suppress them.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii babaoo ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulu la kɛ nugbɔ nɛ. Enɛ biɔ ni ajie jwɛi lɛ daa kɛyashi oŋmɔshi nii titri lɛ baaná hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baatsi enaa.

english: Can planting different types of crops together help protect my farm from being ruined by diseases?
ga: Tsei srɔtoi ni aduɔ Kɛ wɔfee ekome lɛ, ani wɔbaanyɛ wɔye wɔbua ni wɔbu miŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ helai ni baafite lɛ he?

english: Yes, mixing different crops creates natural barriers because most diseases only attack specific plant families, making it difficult for sickness to spread across your whole field.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi ni akɛfutuɔ lɛ kɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii baa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, helai babaoo tutuaa tsei aweku kome pɛ. Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ helai baagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔji lɛ amli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my crops inside the greenhouse look weak and wilted even when I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mi-greenhouse lɛ mli lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛgboi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: High heat and trapped humidity inside a greenhouse stress plants heavily. Without fans or proper vents to clear hot air, plants cannot breathe or move water properly through their roots, causing them to wilt despite wet soil.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli lɛ kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa baa tsei lɛ anɔ. Kɛji akɛ fan loo tsɔne ni sa ni akɛjieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ bɛ lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ amu loo ekɛ nu atsɔ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po.

english: Does the height of a greenhouse structure make any real difference to how hot my plants get?
ga: Ani bɔ ni greenhouse lɛ nɔ kwɔ ha lɛ haa mi tsei lɛ mli dɔɔ waa?

english: Yes, taller structures allow hot air to rise far above the crop leaves, naturally keeping the plant level cooler and helping control excess humidity without immediately needing expensive cooling equipment.
ga: Hɛɛ, bɔ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ aha lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ babaoo hoɔ yɛ tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Ehaa tso lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekwɛɔ hulutsoo ni fa fe nine lɛ nɔ ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ nibii ni jara wa ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ atsu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why is air movement so important for vegetable crops growing in enclosed spaces?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ he hiaa aduawai ni aduɔ yɛ hei ni afo mli lɛ?

english: Moving air cools the leaf surfaces and removes trapped moisture around the plants. Good airflow prevents dangerous humidity build-up that encourages fungal diseases and molds.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ haa baai lɛ anɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ejieɔ nu ni emɔ tso lɛ he lɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ tsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni woɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe hewalɛ lɛ naa.

english: How can I reduce high moisture around my plants if I cannot afford electricity or fans?
ga: Mibaajie hulutsoo ni fa babaoo ni ebɔle he lɛ shi. Te tso baanyɛ afee tɛŋŋ Ni kɛji minyɛɛɛ mahe srawa hewalɛ loo fan?

english: You can improve natural airflow by opening side vents, building taller structures so heat escapes upward, and leaving enough space between plants so wind can blow freely through them.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ aya hiɛ kɛtsɔ sɛɛgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ ni ooogbele lɛ nɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ tsũ ko ni kwɔ fe tsutsu lɛ koni hulutsoo aya ŋwɛi. Ni oshi gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli oya.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without turning into fruit when the weather becomes too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, crops get stressed and drop their blossoms to preserve water and energy. Keeping the crop area shaded or cooled helps flowers stay on the stem and form fruit.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Kɛ́ aha he ni aduɔ nii lɛ yɛ hulutsoo loo fɛ̃i lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Can excessive heat harm my crops even if there is plenty of water in the soil?
ga: Ani dɔlɛ ni fe nine baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui eyɛ mli akɛ nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Yes, extreme heat can bake the plant leaves and stop internal growth processes like photosynthesis. Even with wet roots, a plant suffering from extreme heat will shut down to protect itself.
ga: Hɛɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa baanyɛ ashã tso baai ni ekpa mligbɛ dalɛ nifeemɔi tamɔ fotosintɛsis. Kɛji akɛ shishifãi lɛ mli efɔ po Tsei ni hulutsoo ni naa wa waa baa amɛnɔ lɛ hu ŋmɛɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe.

english: Why do the leaves on my crops stay wet until late morning, and is that bad for them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ mli efɔ kɛyashiɔ leebi lɛ? Ni ani eyeɔ nakai tsei lɛ awui?

english: Leaves stay wet when morning air is very humid and there is no breeze to dry them off. Water sitting on leaves for hours invites fungal diseases like blight and mildew to attack your crop.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ leebi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. ni kɔɔyɔɔ ko bɛ ni baaha egbi. Nu ni ta baai anɔ ŋmɛlɛtswai babaoo lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ blight kɛ mildew tutuaa onibii.

english: Why do foreign seed varieties brought from overseas struggle to grow well in our open local fields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ maŋsɛɛ dumɔwui ni akɛbaajɛ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ wɔ maŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔji ni mli tse lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Foreign seeds are usually bred for cooler climates or specific greenhouse setups. In open Ghanaian heat, they get stressed easily unless grown in controlled environments that mimic their home conditions.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, afɔɔ maŋsɛɛ dumɔwui kɛha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli ejɔ loo yɛ ŋmɔji pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli. Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli edɔ tamɔ Ghana lɛ mli lɛ Amɛnáa haomɔ oya. Ja atsɔse amɛ yɛ shihilɛ ko ni akudɔɔ ni kaseɔ amɛshia shihilɛi lɛ amli.

english: What is the main benefit of growing crops under a protective cover instead of out in the open field?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi titrii ni yɔɔ tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ shishi moŋ fe ni akwɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he?

english: Protective structures allow you to control heat, humidity, rain damage, and pests. This controlled environment protects delicate crops from harsh weather and produces higher yields.
ga: Tsumaa ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni oyeɔ dɔlɛ, fɛ̃i, kɛ nugbɔ ni fiteɔ nii anɔ. kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui Nɛkɛ shihilɛ ni akudɔɔ nɛɛ buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai ahe, ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo baa.

english: Why does trapped humidity inside a farming shade make diseases spread faster among my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni emɔ okwaayeli he hulutsoo be mli lɛ haa helai gbɛɔ eshwaa miŋmɔshi nibii amli oya lɛ?

english: Fungi and bacteria thrive in warm, calm, moist air. When humidity gets trapped around leaves without air movement, disease spores multiply rapidly and spread from plant to plant.
ga: Fungi kɛ bacteria yeɔ omanye yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ, ni yɔɔ kpoo, ni mli ejɔ, be mli ni fɛ̃i ebɔle baai lɛ ahe ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ. Helai ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo oya ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants get sunburned easily because they cannot handle direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains planted beside them to block the hot sun and keep the soil cool during their first few years.
ga: Hulu shãa cacao tsei bibii lɛ oya ejaakɛ hulu la nyɛŋ ashɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to stay green and grow strong. Applying the right fertilizer early in the crop's growth helps bring back the dark green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni sa wo tso lɛ mli mra yɛ tso lɛ dalɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ená eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Extreme heat or a sudden lack of water causes tomato plants to stress and shed their flowers to save energy. Watering regularly at the soil level early in the morning helps the plants hold onto their blossoms.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ trukaa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu daa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Cassava roots cannot breathe when water sits around them for too long in soaked soil. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges lets excess water drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi nyɛɛɛ amu kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Why does putting dry grass around the base of my crops help them grow better in hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mikɛwoɔ mitsei lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass acts like a blanket over the soil. It traps moisture so it does not dry out in the heat, stops weeds from growing, and turns into food for your crops as it decays.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ koni ekagbi yɛ latsaa be mli. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ Ni ebafeɔ niyenii kɛhaa onibii beni efiteɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my seed yams refuse to sprout right after I harvest them from the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikpa amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yam tubers go into a natural resting state called dormancy immediately after harvest. They will not sprout until this sleep period naturally ends, which usually takes two to three months.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ boteɔ shihilɛ ko ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy lɛ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ. Amɛkwɛŋ kɛyashi nɛkɛ wɔɔhe be nɛɛ baagbe naa yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ nyɔji enyɔ loo etɛ.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller harvest when I plant seeds very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa kwraa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni ekɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded together, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper space ensures it gets enough food and light to produce big, healthy yields.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ ni sa lɛ, ehaa enáa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my field after harvesting maize instead of planting maize again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu ŋmãa ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the soil of the same specific nutrients. Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the ground, naturally enriching the soil for the next crop.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Koni ekɛ sɛɛnamɔ afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are small worms eating the inside leaves of my young maize plants at night?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli baai lɛ gbɛkɛ lɛ?

english: These are likely armyworms, which hide inside the plant funnel during the hot day to stay cool and come out at night to eat the tender leaves. Spraying recommended biopesticides or neem extract into the funnels early can protect your crop.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei amli ŋmeii amli yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli koni amɛhe ajɔɔ amɛ ni amɛje kpo amɛbaye baai bibii gbɛkɛ. Ni akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ afɔseɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli mra. Ebaanyɛ ebu onibii ahe.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites that suck the juices out of young leaves and spread plant viruses. Controlling these tiny pests early prevents the leaves from twisting and stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai bibii amli ni egbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ eshwaa tsei amli helai bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui Enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛɔ shishijee Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ amɛhe ni amɛkpa helai gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants turning yellow and curling up suddenly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ trukaa ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and yellowing are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the leaf juices, or spreading a virus. Spraying organic neem seed extract or appropriate insect control early stops them from destroying your entire harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu loo helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ ŋmɔŋ. Organic neem dumɔwui ni ajieɔ loo kooloi akudɔmɔ ni sa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra. Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite onibii fɛɛ.

english: How do I stop armyworms from eating my maize crop before they destroy the whole farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi cutworms lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye mi-ŋmãa lɛ dani amɛfite miŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Fall armyworms hide inside the central funnel (whorl) of young maize plants. You can crush them manually or apply recommended natural or chemical treatments directly into the whorl early in the morning or late evening when the worms are most active.
ga: Fall flukes lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi (rings) lɛ amli. Obaanyɛ okɛ onine atsɔ mli loo okɛ adebɔɔ mli loo tsofa gbɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ, be mli ni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ tsuɔ nii waa lɛ atsu nii.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high, when water supply is irregular, or when there is poor pollination. Keeping the soil evenly moist and planting windbreaks nearby helps protect the blossoms so they can form fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni pollination lɛ ehiii Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔŋ tsɔne ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my cassava plants have very leafy tops, but the roots underneath stay tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium, the plant spends all its energy growing leaves instead of tubers. Adding wood ash or a potassium-rich fertilizer encourages the roots to swell into large cassava tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa Tsei kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ baai yɛ bulbs najiaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ tso mli sũ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni potassium eyi mli obɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmei agboi.

english: What causes my young maize leaves to turn purple during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-baby corn baai lɛ feɔ purple yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Purple leaves on young maize indicate a phosphorus deficiency, often because cold or waterlogged soil prevents roots from absorbing nutrients. Improving soil drainage and applying phosphorus fertilizer helps the crop recover.
ga: Baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs faaa. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni haa ebaa lɛ nakai ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ aná niyenii kpakpai. Shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ ni afeɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ fɔsfɔs ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Legumes like cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for maize. They also cover the soil surface, retaining moisture and stopping weeds from invading your field.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmãa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oooha lolo Kwɛmɔ ni hulutsoo ahi shi ni otsi jwɛi anaa koni amɛkabote oyale lɛ mli.

english: How does putting dry grass or cocoa pods around the base of my crops help them grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi loo kookoo ŋmeii ni mikɛwoɔ mitsei lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Covering soil with organic material (mulching) acts like a blanket, keeping the ground cool and retaining moisture under strong sunlight. It reduces how often you need to water and stops weed seeds from sprouting.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli (mulch) ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Enɛ baaha shii abɔ ni esa akɛ okɛ nu awo mli lɛ aba shi, ni ebaatsi jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃.

english: Why do my newly transplanted oil palm seedlings wither and die after a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tsei ni adu ehee lɛ gboɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Transplant shock occurs when roots are damaged or when seedlings are planted during harsh, hot sun. Planting at the beginning of the rainy season and providing temporary shade keeps the root system cool until it establishes.
ga: Transplant shock baa kɛji shishifãi lɛ efite loo kɛ́ adu dumɔwui yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ́ adu mra yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli ni aha hulutsoo be kukuoo ko lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i kɛyashi ebaatswa shi.

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and carry heavy bunches near the top. Propping them up with sturdy, forked wooden poles (Y-sticks) supports the weight and prevents winds from snapping the plants before harvest.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ kui ni fa babaoo ni bɛŋkɛɔ ŋwɛigbɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ (Y-shaped bars) fi amɛsɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsɔne ni tsiimɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ, ni ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekafo tso lɛ mli dani akpa ŋmaa lɛ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my yam tubers so they don't rot?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ? koni ekafite

english: Yams are ready for main harvest when the vines and leaves turn yellow and dry up naturally. Harvesting at this point ensures full tuber development and longer storage life without rotting prematurely.
ga: Sweet potatoes efee klalo kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ titri lɛ beni wain tsei kɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ. Nikpamɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ehiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni efiteee oya.

english: This usually happens when the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the plant food maize needs to grow strong and stay dark green. The maize plant naturally pulls nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the younger top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ faaa. Enɛ ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni etsɔ hewalɛ ni efee ŋmɔtɔ. Abɛi gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛhaa ŋwɛi baa bibii lɛ.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips sucking the juice out of the leaves, or by a virus carried by insects. These pests stop the leaves from expanding and reduce your crop yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ mites loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni kooloi bibii kɛbaa lɛ anɔ Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ tsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã ni ehaa onibii ni oduɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, usually caused by extremely hot daytime temperatures or inconsistent watering. The plant saves energy by dropping the flowers until growing conditions improve.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ he. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ waa yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo nu ni akɛhaa yɛ be fɛɛ mli. Tsei buɔ hewalɛ he kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛjieɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyashi be mli ni amɛdalɛ shihilɛi lɛ baafee nɔ ni hi.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. Planting tall crops like plantains nearby provides living shade and holds moisture in the air, protecting the cocoa until its roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baaha hulutsoo aba ni ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ mli waa.

english: Why do I get tiny, weak cobs of maize when I plant three or four seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmãa ni bɛ hewalɛ nɔ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui etɛ loo ejwɛ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for water, light, and soil nutrients. Because no single plant gets enough food, all the plants remain thin and produce small cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei lɛ eko kwraa enaaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. No hewɔ lɛ tsei fɛɛ yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ bibii ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Weeds are naturally adapted to the soil and weather, allowing them to steal water and fertilizer faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds early gives your planted crop room to eat and grow without competition.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛjuɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe tsei ni aduɔ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaaha o-grow room lɛ aye nii ni eda ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts have helpful bacteria on their roots that trap nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. When the crop season ends, this extra nitrogen acts as free food for the next crop you plant.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ helatsɛmɛi ahe nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ dumɔ be lɛ ba naagbee Nitrogen ni fa fe nine nɛɛ baatsu nii akɛ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ.

english: Plantain roots do not go deep into the ground; instead, they spread sideways near the topsoil. When heavy bunches of fruit grow at the top, the plant becomes top-heavy and soft wet soil easily loses its grip on the shallow roots.
ga: Plantain shishifãi eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Mohu ɔ, a gbɛ a he kɛ ya he nɛ ngɛ zugba a yi mi ɔ he. Kɛ aduawai babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ ŋwɛi Tso lɛ bafeɔ nɔ ni tsii ni efeɔ blɛoo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ baafite.

english: You can tell yams are ready when the leaves and vines above ground turn yellow and start to dry up. This sign shows that the vine has stopped growing and has transferred all its stored energy into the tuber below.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ko efee klalo kɛ́ baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛbɔi ŋmɔtɔ. Okadi nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ wain tso lɛ ekpa dalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛto lɛ etee bulb ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Why do cassava roots spoil quickly in the ground if heavy rain falls after the leaves drop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa beni baai lɛ egbee shi lɛ?

english: When cassava plants drop their leaves, they stop actively taking up water. Heavy rains soak the soil and cut off air to the roots, causing fungal rot to spread through the mature cassava underground.
ga: Kɛji cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ fite lɛ Ebaakpa nu numɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyiɔ ni efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yaa shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmei shishifãi ni eda lɛ fɛɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees turn yellow and fall off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa leaves are sensitive to heat and dry winds. When the weather gets too hot, the tree drops its leaves to save water and protect itself from drying out completely.
ga: Cocoa baai nuɔ dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi he waa. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbi kwraa.

english: Is it harmful if I scrub or scrape the outer bark and leaves of my cocoa tree while cleaning around it?
ga: Ani ebaaye mi awui kɛji mikɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmeii kɛ kookoo baai lɛ shwie shi loo mikɛshwie shi yɛ be mli ni miitsumɔ he ni ebɔle he lɛ?

english: Yes, scraping the tree damages its protective outer layer. Wounding the bark or leaves leaves the tree open to attacks from insect pests and fungal infections.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni ajieɔ lɛ fiteɔ kponɔgbɛ fã ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ. Pilamɔi ni baa tso lɛ yibii loo baai lɛ anɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ mlɛo koni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ atutua lɛ.

english: Why do I need to trim extra branches and leaves from my adult cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ niji kɛ baai krokomɛi ni jɛ cacao tso ni eda lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Trimming lets sunlight and air flow through the branches, which dries up excess moisture and prevents damp-loving diseases from harming your pods.
ga: Nibii ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tsei lɛ aniji amli. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ agbi. Ni tsi helai ni ŋmɔtɔ ni yeɔ o-pods lɛ awui lɛ kɛbaa lɛ naa.

english: Why must I rinse my chemical spraying container three times with clean water after use?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ nu ni mli tse afɔ spray tsɛnsi lɛ he shii etɛ kɛji mikɛtsu nii?

english: Rinsing three times ensures all leftover chemical liquid is completely removed so it does not spoil your next batch or burn your crop leaves.
ga: Nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli shii etɛ lɛ haa ajieɔ tsofa mli nu ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ kwraa. No hewɔ lɛ, efiteee o-batch ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ loo eshãŋ tso lɛ baai lɛ.

english: Do I need to wash my harvested cocoa pods in water before breaking them open?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mafolɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ amli yɛ nu mli dani magbele?

english: No, washing pods adds unnecessary moisture that can encourage molds to grow on the fresh beans during the drying and fermentation process.
ga: Dabi, ŋmeii lɛ ahe ni afɔɔ he lɛ haa ŋmeii ni he ehiaaa baa ni baanyɛ awo ŋmeii ni shwereɔ yɛ kɔfi ŋmeii heei anɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ be mli ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do fresh cocoa beans need to be covered with banana leaves right after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ akɛ banana baai aha kookoo yibii heei ahe kɛji akpa amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Wrapping fresh wet cocoa beans in thick plantain or banana leaves keeps them warm so they ferment properly, which develops the chocolate flavor and brown color.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ plantain loo banana baai ni mli edɔ wo kookoo ŋmeii heei ni efɔ lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛdɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baaha efee tsokolate ŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why should I leave fallen cocoa leaves on the ground instead of sweeping them off my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi kookoo baai ni egbee shi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ moŋ fe ni mafolɔ amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fallen leaves act as a natural blanket that keeps the soil cool and moist, while slowly breaking down to feed valuable nutrients back to the tree roots.
ga: Baai ni egbee shi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, fiofio lɛ Efiteɔ koni ekɛ niyenii ni jara wa aku sɛɛ aba tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do some of my cocoa pods turn dark black and soft while still growing on the branch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa yɛ nine lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in excess moisture and wet weather, spreading quickly from pod to pod if not removed.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Fuŋ ko ni shwereɔ yɛ fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ pod mli kɛyaa pod mli kɛji ajieee.

english: Why do my crops look weak and pale right after heavy rainfall when they have plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ, be mli ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ lɛ?

english: Too much water fills up all the air spaces in the soil, which suffocates the roots and temporarily prevents them from taking up plant food.
ga: Nu babaoo eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ hei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa amɛye tso lɛ niyenii yɛ be kukuoo mli.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa crop is hungry for fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: If your cocoa trees grow very slowly, have pale or yellowish leaves, and produce few flowers or pods, the soil is likely running out of nutrients.
ga: Kɛji o-cocoa tso lɛ miida blɛoo waa lɛ Eyɛ baai ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔŋ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi loo ŋmɔtɔ fioo lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees need time to build strong roots and mature trunks that can hold heavy pods. During the first few years, the tree uses all its energy to grow sturdy branches and leaves rather than making fruit.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia be koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa kɛ tsei ni eda ni baanyɛ aye abua ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ. Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ niji kɛ baai ni wa moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii.

english: Why do some cocoa farms produce many bags of cocoa while a neighboring farm gets very little?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji komɛi feɔ kookoo kotokui babaoo yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ nine shɛɛɛ nɔ fioo ko pɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa yield depends heavily on tree age, soil fertility, pruning, and pest control. Even next-door farms will have different yields if one farmer manages shade better and keeps the trees free of diseased pods.
ga: Cocoa yibiiwoo damɔ afii ni tso lɛ eye lɛ nɔ. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ ji nɔ ni wa waa Okwaafoi ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ po baanyɛ ajie yibii sɔrɔtoi kɛji okwaafoi lɛ kwɛ amɛ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛha amɛtsei lɛ amli tsɛŋemɔ helai akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why do cocoa trees planted too close together produce fewer pods per tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei ni adu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɛ tso kome mli lɛ?

english: When cocoa trees are planted too tightly, their roots compete for soil nutrients and water, while their upper leaves block sunlight from each other, leaving the trees weak and unable to support many flowers.
ga: Kɛji adu kookoo tsei waa tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. yɛ be mli ni amɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ekwɛ fɔfɔi babaoo nɔ.

english: A cocoa tree produces thousands of flowers, but it naturally drops up to 90% of them. The tree naturally decides how many pods it can feed based on how much water, food, and sunlight it is receiving.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔii akpei abɔ. Shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔii ni fa fe 90% baagbee shi. Tso lɛ damɔ nu, niyenii, kɛ hulu la ni enine shɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ ekpɛɔ eyiŋ yɛ ŋmeii enyiɛ ni ebaaye lɛ he.

english: Why does my cocoa farm yield a smaller crop in the middle of the year and a larger crop toward the end of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo yɛ afi lɛ teŋgbɛ, ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo yɛ afi lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowering is triggered by seasonal rain and temperature changes. The smaller rainy season leads to the minor harvest, while the major rainy season causes heavy flowering for the main harvest season.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be mli kɛ dɔlɛ tsakemɔi kɛ kookoo fɔfɔi baa. Nugbɔshiimɔ be bibioo lɛ kɛ kpamɔ bibioo baa. Yɛ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ kɛ fɔfɔi babaoo baa yɛ kpamɔɔ be titri lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do cocoa trees grown under shade trees look healthier than those growing in full sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni kookoo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yɛ hewalɛ fe tsei ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally grow best under forest canopies. Shade trees shield young cocoa leaves from harsh sunlight, keep the soil moist, and prevent the trees from drying out during hot periods.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ kooi lɛ ashishi. Tsei ni haa hulu kpɛɔ lɛ buɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni otsi tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and dry up when there is heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Excessive wet weather creates high humidity that allows fungal diseases like Black Pod to spread quickly. The fungus infects the pod surface, causing the cocoa inside to rot and turn black.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ fe nine lɛ kɛ hulutsoo babaoo baa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya. Fungus lɛ yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ. Enɛ haa kookoo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ fiteɔ ni etsɔɔ ediŋŋ.

english: Why do crops with dry leaves spread around their base survive better during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni baai ni egbi egbɛ eshwa amɛshishigbɛ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Covering the soil around plant roots with dry leaves is called mulching. It acts like a protective blanket that traps water in the ground and shields the soil from hot sunlight.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ baai ni egbi shwieɔ tso shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni buɔ mɔ he ni ŋmɛɔ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: Why is it bad to let unwanted water sprouts or suckers grow at the base of my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji nɔ fɔŋ akɛ mahã cacao ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni ataooo lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ mi cacao tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Water sprouts, or chupons, draw food and water away from the main trunk. Removing them ensures the tree directs all its nutrients toward growing healthy pods on the main branches.
ga: Tsei bibii, loo chupons lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ he. Amɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ kudɔɔ niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛyaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji wuji lɛ anɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: How can I tell if my crop leaves are turning yellow because of poor soil or because of plant pests?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mitso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ahewɔ?

english: Lack of nutrients in the soil usually causes an even yellowing across many older leaves, whereas pest damage usually leaves small spots, holes, or chewed edges on young leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ momo. Mɛi babaoo ji ŋmɔŋ ni tamɔ amɛhe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ haa ŋmeii bibii, bu, loo ŋmeii ni ashɛreɔ yɛ baai bibii lɛ anɔ baa.

english: Why should I plant my vegetables on raised beds instead of flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu aduawai yɛ saatsoi ni awó nɔ nɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Raised beds improve soil drainage, prevent heavy rains from washing away young roots, and make it easier for plant roots to spread and grow quickly.
ga: Saji ni awo nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Etsiɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ shishifãi bibii lɛ. ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ tsei shishifãi lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛdara oya

english: Why does my soil feel tired and weak after I pull out an entire harvest from my crop bed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ etɔ lɛ ni egbɔjɔ beni mijie ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Uprooting whole plants removes nutrients from the ground, so you need to mix in compost or manure before planting again to restore the soil's strength.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie tso muu lɛ fɛɛ shishifãi lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afutu mli dani odu ekoŋŋ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi ekoŋŋ.

english: Are there fast crops I can grow that take only about a month to harvest?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi yɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni heɔ aaafee nyɔŋ kome pɛ dani akpaa?

english: Yes, short-duration leafy vegetables and some root crops mature in around 40 days, allowing you to harvest and sell them quickly for fast income.
ga: Hɛɛ, aduawai kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ be kukuoo mli lɛ ekomɛi daa yɛ aaafee gbii 40 mli, ni no haa onyɛɔ okpaa amɛ oya ni ohɔ̃ɔ koni onine ashɛ shika nɔ oya.

english: How long should I keep seedling crops on a nursery bed before moving them?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ makɛ midumɔwui lɛ ahi ŋmɔ mli dani mikɛwo he kroko?

english: Most vegetable seedlings stay on a nursery bed for around 30 to 40 days until they are strong enough to survive being transplanted into the main field.
ga: Aduawai amli dumɔwui babaoo baata ŋmɔ mli saatsoi anɔ gbii 30 kɛyashi 40 kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu amɛ awo saatso wulu lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to uproot the entire crop all at once instead of picking leaves little by little?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ shikome moŋ fe ni mafolɔ baai lɛ ekomekomei lɛ?

english: Certain crops mature all at the same time, so pulling up the whole plant allows you to harvest at peak freshness and immediately prepare the bed for the next crop.
ga: Tsei komɛi daa yɛ be kome mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛtsɔ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ ni oootsi lɛ nɔ lɛ, obaanyɛ okpa nii yɛ be mli ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni osaa ŋmɔ lɛ kɛha dumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: What should I do with my garden bed immediately after clear-harvesting all my plants?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee abɔɔ mli saatso lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni akpa tsei lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Once a bed is completely harvested, you should clear the leftover roots, add fresh organic matter, and turn the soil over so it is ready for immediate replanting.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akpa saatsoi lɛ agbe naa lɛ Esa akɛ ojie shishifãi ni eshwɛ lɛ. kɛ nibii heei ni wala yɔɔ mli afata he ni amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, otsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee klalo kɛha dumɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Should I plant the same crop on the same bed right after harvesting it?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ saatso kome nɔ beni akpa ŋmaa lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: It is better to rotate crops because planting the same crop repeatedly on the same bed drains specific nutrients and allows pests to build up in the soil.
ga: Ehi akɛ aaatsake ŋmɔshi nibii ejaakɛ aduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shii abɔ. Yɛ saatso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni haa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: How can my family coordinate better when one person grows the crops and another sells them at the market?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni miweku lɛ afee ekome jogbaŋŋ beni mɔ kome duɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mɔ kroko lɛ hɔ̃ɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Agreeing on clear harvest dates allows the seller to arrange transportation and buyer demand in advance, preventing harvested crops from spoiling before sale.
ga: Nikpamɔ gbi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni akpɛlɛɔ nɔ lɛ haa mɛi ni hɔ̃ɔ nii lɛ toɔ nibii ni akɛbaatsu nii kɛ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ ahiamɔ nii ahe gbɛjianɔ kɛtsɔ hiɛ. Enɛ ji koni tsei ni akpa lɛ akafite dani ahɔ̃ɔ.

english: What quick-growing crops can I plant to avoid hunger in my home while waiting for my long-term crops to mature?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya manyɛ madu koni hɔmɔ akaye mi yɛ mishia lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Planting fast 40-day vegetables alongside long-term staples gives your household a quick source of food and cash while waiting for crops like cassava or corn.
ga: Kɛ́ okwɛ aduawai yɛ gbii 40 hiɛdɔɔ mli kɛfata niyenii ni heɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaha oweku lɛ aná niyenii kɛ shika oya yɛ be mli ni amɛmɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa.

english: How can I ensure I have vegetables to sell continuously instead of all at one time?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana nɔmimaa akɛ maná aduawai ni yaa nɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli moŋ fe fɛɛ shikome?

english: By planting new beds every two weeks—a practice called staggered planting—you ensure a constant cycle where one bed is ready for harvest as another is just starting.
ga: Saa hee ni aduɔ daa otsii enyɔ, nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ staggered planting. Enɛ baaha saatso kome afee klalo kɛha kpamɔ yɛ be mli ni ekroko lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛkɛ.

english: Why should I plant my groundnuts on ridges instead of on flat land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii anɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting groundnuts on ridges keeps the soil loose and soft, which makes it much easier for the plant's flowering stems to push into the ground and form pods. It also allows excess rain to drain away so the roots do not sit in standing water and rot.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii anɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee blɛoo. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛha tso lɛ fɔfɔi tsei lɛ akɛ amɛaatsi amɛhe kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛfee ŋmeii. Ehaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ hu hoɔ koni shishifãi lɛ akabote nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli ni amɛkagbo.

english: How do I know if my soil is loose enough for cowpeas to grow well without buying expensive tests?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ etse bɔ ni sa ni tsina ŋmei baanyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni miheee kaa he nibii ni jara wa?

english: You can test your soil by taking a handful of moist dirt and squeezing it into a ball. If it holds its shape slightly but easily crumbles apart when you gently poke it, your soil is loose enough for cowpea roots and water to move freely.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka shikpɔŋ okwɛ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni oooŋɔ ni okɛmiifee bɔɔlu lɛ nɔ. Kɛji ehiɛ egbɛhe lɛ mli fioo shi egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ okɛ ohe wo mli blɛoo. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ etse bɔ ni sa ni baaha cowpea shishifãi kɛ nu lɛ aya nɔ oya.

english: Why do groundnut flowers bend down and bury themselves in the dirt after they bloom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are unique because their pods grow underground. After the flower is pollinated above ground, a special stem called a 'peg' grows downward into the soil to safely form the groundnut pod beneath the dirt where it is protected from heat.
ga: Eyɛ srɔto kwraa akɛ ŋmeii yɛ ejaakɛ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Beni atswa fɔfɔi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ, tsei krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ ‘pegs’ lɛ daa kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛfee ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shweshweeshwe. ni abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he lɛ

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly like small tubes during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ jwɛi bibii lɛ? Yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Maize leaves roll up to protect themselves from intense sunlight and prevent water from evaporating out of the plant. It is the crop's natural way of saving water during the hottest parts of the day.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa baai shwieɔ shi koni ebu he kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he, ni ekɛtsi nu ni jɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ naa. Eji tso adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ nu toɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni edɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why are my groundnut leaves turning pale yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your groundnuts are lacking essential plant nutrients like nitrogen or iron, or the soil is too dry or flooded. Improving soil drainage and adding organic manure can help your leaves turn healthy and green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-peanuts lɛ bɛ tso mli niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen loo dade. aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ ni ooofee lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua obaai lɛ ni amɛfee hewalɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are there small ragged holes on my young maize leaves with tiny green droppings inside the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? ni etse ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the leaves and eats the growing plant. Catching them early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extracts directly into the center of the leaves helps protect your crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai amli ni amɛyeɔ tsei ni miida lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ omɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ awo tso lɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start to turn black and rot underground when we get heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air to stay healthy. When heavy rains flood the field and water sits in the soil for days, the roots suffocate, allowing harmful fungi in the waterlogged soil to rot the tubers.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia cassava shishifãi koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ eyi ŋmɔji amli ni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli gbii babaoo. Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha bulbs lɛ agbo.

english: Why do my tomato fruits get dark, flat spots on the bottom side before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: Dark spots on the bottom of tomatoes are usually caused by a condition called blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil due to irregular watering.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shihilɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ baa. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do extension officers tell me that planting beans or groundnuts this season will help my maize crop next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension agent lɛ miikɛɛ mi akɛ, kɛ́ midu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua mi ni madu ŋmei yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have beneficial bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the ground. When you harvest them, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil as free fertilizer for your next maize crop.
ga: Muawai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii amli yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji okpa amɛ Nakai nitrogen ni emɔ lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha o-abele ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How can I tell the exact right time to harvest my groundnuts so they do not rot in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmeii koni amɛkafite yɛ sũ lɛ mli?

english: You can check by pulling up a few sample plants and opening the pods. If the inside lining of the shell has turned dark brown or black with dark veins, your groundnuts are mature and ready for harvest.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ enɛ kɛtsɔ tsei fioo komɛi ni oootsi kɛya ŋwɛi ni ogbele ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Kɛji akɛ mligbɛ ŋmei lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ ni eyɛ fãji ni tsuɔ waa Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-peanuts lɛ ekwɛ̃ ni esa akɛ akpa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my corn plants turning yellow in a 'V' shape starting from the tip?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ‘V’ su mli, ni amɛjeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing that forms a 'V' shape starting at the tip of lower leaves is a sign that your soil is low in nitrogen, a vital nutrient corn needs to stay green and produce good cobs.
ga: Yellow ni feɔ ‘V’ su ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ anaa lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Esa akɛ ŋmãa ni niyenii ni he hiaa yɔɔ mli lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni ewo ŋmãa kpakpa.

english: Why do people advise me to plant groundnuts on my plot before planting maize the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmei yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans have special root nodules that catch nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, leaving free fertilizer behind for the next crop like maize.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ashiɔ ahaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ.

english: When maize seeds are planted too close, the plants compete with each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients, causing them to stretch tall for light instead of developing thick stems and large cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛmɔ la. Mohu ɔ, e ngɛ tso nɛ mi wa kɛ tso agbo.

english: Staking yam vines lifts the leaves off the damp ground so they can catch full sunlight to make food for the tuber while reducing the risk of fungal diseases from wet soil.
ga: Staking sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni ekɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo aha bulb lɛ niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ ni mli efɔ mli baa lɛ baa shi.

english: How do I know which part of the cassava stem is best to cut for planting my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmei tso lɛ fã ni sa jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaakwɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: The middle portion of a mature, healthy cassava stem is best because it contains plenty of stored energy and strong buds that sprout faster and healthier than the soft top or woody bottom.
ga: Kasava tso ni eda ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ teŋgbɛ fã lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ eyɛ hewalɛ babaoo ni ato kɛ ŋmeii ni mli wa ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni eyɛ hewalɛ fe casava tso ni yɔɔ blɛoo loo shishigbɛ fã ni tso yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Which kind of plantain sucker should I dig up from an old farm to start my new field?
ga: Mɛɛ dumɔwui esa akɛ mafo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ momo lɛ mli koni mikɛje ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: Choose 'sword' suckers, which are young shoots with narrow, spear-like leaves and a broad base, because they have strong food reserves and establish much faster than suckers with broad leaves.
ga: Halamɔ ‘klante’ tsei, ni ji tsei bibii ni baai lɛ mli tse, tamɔ akpɔlɔi, ni amɛshishi lɛ mli kwɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛyɛ niyenii ni mli wa ni amɛtoɔ, ni amɛbuaa amɛhe naa oya fe ŋmeii ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves dry up and burn when there is no shade over them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa be mli ni hulutsoo be ko bɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct, harsh sunlight, which dries out their leaves faster than their small roots can take up water from the soil.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa waa he tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ baaha baai lɛ agbi oya fe shishifãi bibii lɛ. ni baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves droop in the middle of the afternoon even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ leebi moŋ?

english: In intense afternoon sun, pepper leaves lose water through evaporation faster than the roots can suck it up, so the plant wilts temporarily to protect itself from losing more water.
ga: Yɛ shwane hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ, Pepper baai lɛ laajeɔ nu yɛ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ lɛ hewɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo akafite amɛ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop without forming fruit when the weather becomes too hot or when the soil goes from extremely dry to very wet, which shocks the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ waa nɔ. ni haa tso lɛ he feɔ gbeyei lɛ

english: Why are there ragged holes and dark powder inside the top leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji ni etse kɛ powda ni tsuɔ diŋ yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Ragged holes and dark powder (frass) inside the leaf funnel are typical signs of caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm, which hide inside the plant and chew the new growing leaves.
ga: Buji ni etse kɛ powda ni mli edɔ (frass) ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji okadii ni afɔɔ naa yɛ ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei amli ni amɛyeɔ baai heei ni miida lɛ ahe.

english: Cocoa flowers must be pollinated by tiny insects or by hand within a short window after opening. If pollination does not happen in time, the flower dies and falls off the tree naturally.
ga: Esa akɛ kooloi bibii awo kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ amli. aloo kɛtsɔ nine nɔ yɛ samflɛ kuku ko mli yɛ be mli ni agbele sɛɛ kɛji akɛ pollination baaa yɛ be naa. Fɔfɔi lɛ baagboi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛbaagbee shi kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: How does hand pollinating my cocoa trees help me get a bigger harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ cacao tsei ni akɛ niji shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni maná ŋmaa babaoo?

english: Natural insects often miss many flowers on a cocoa tree. When you manually transfer pollen from one flower to another using tools, almost every flower you treat can turn into a healthy cocoa pod.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, adebɔɔ mli kooloi bibii lɛ kwɛɔ fɔfɔi babaoo ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ onine tsɔ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛtee ekroko mli kɛtsɔ dɛŋdade ko nɔ lɛ, Nɔ ni miihe ashɛ fɔfɔi fɛɛ ni okwɛɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct heat and sunlight. They require shade trees or fast-growing companion crops like plantains to shelter their leaves and keep the soil moist while their roots develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo loo tsei ni fata amɛhe ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛbu baai lɛ ahe ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why are my older cocoa trees producing small pods even though the leaves look green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei ni edara lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ tamɔ eŋɔli po

english: As cocoa trees age, they draw heavy amounts of specific nutrients like potassium and phosphorus out of the ground. Even if leaves look fine, depleted soil reduces the tree's ability to grow large, healthy pods.
ga: Kɛji kookoo tso lɛ da Amɛyeɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ potassium kɛ phosphorus. Nibii babaoo je kpo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ moŋ Shi shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛmɔ ni ekɛbaafee ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa lɛ baa shi.

english: What causes the pods on my cocoa tree to turn dark brown and rot during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that thrives in cold, wet weather. Water droplets spread the fungal spores from the soil and infected leaves onto healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Nu mli nui ni hoɔ lɛ gbɛɔ fungal spores kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why should I cut branches off my cocoa tree if I want it to give me more fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo niji kɛji miisumɔ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unnecessary foliage so air and sunlight can reach the trunk where flowers grow. It prevents disease-causing dampness and directs the tree's energy into pod growth instead of leaf growth.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei ni he ehiaaa lɛ. Bɔni afee ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la anyɛ ayashɛ tsei ni fɔfɔii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ hela baa lɛ naa, ni etsɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ gbɛ kɛyaa pod dalɛ nɔ moŋ fe baai dalɛ.

english: Why do cocoa flowers grow directly on the thick trunk instead of at the tips of the small branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei ni mli tse nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei niji bibii lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce flowers on their trunk and heavy limbs so that the tree can safely support the weight of heavy, fully grown pods without snapping thin outer branches.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ tsei kɛ amɛhe nibii ni tsii anɔ. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ akwɛ ŋmeii ni tsii ni eda lɛ anɔ shweshweeshwe ni efoŋ kponɔgbɛ niji bibii lɛ.

english: Why are insect pests like mirids attacking my cocoa crop more during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ mirids lɛ tutuaa mi-kokoo tsei lɛ shii abɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Mirids multiply quickly in hot, dry conditions and feed on young shoots and pods. Trees that are stressed by heat or lack of shade have weaker natural defenses against insect damage.
ga: Mirids fɔɔ oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. ni amɛyeɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii Tsei ni latsaa haa amɛhaoɔ loo amɛbɛ hulutsoo lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii babaoo ni buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ oshara waa lɛ ahe nibii ni fiteɔ amɛ lɛ ahe.

english: How does clearing weeds under my cocoa trees help the cocoa pods grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your cocoa trees for water and nutrients in the dirt. Clearing weeds ensures your trees get full access to soil moisture and fertilizer, while also removing hiding spots for pests.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ o-cacao tsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ooojie lɛ haa otsei lɛ náa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ hei ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ kɛyaa.

english: How can I tell if a cocoa pod is fully ripe and ready to pick from the tree?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni esa akɛ ajie kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: A ripe cocoa pod changes color, turning from green to bright yellow, or from dark red to orange-yellow. Tapping a ripe pod also makes a hollow sound because the seeds inside loosen from the inner pod wall.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su. Tsakemɔ kɛjɛ eŋɔli kɛya ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse loo kɛjɛ etsuru ni mli edɔ kɛya ŋmɔŋ-ŋɔli. Kɛ́ atswa pod ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ hu, ehaa gbee ni mli ewo muji baa ejaakɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ jeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ pod lɛ mli gbogboi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize plants yield much less food when I plant seeds saved from last year's harvest instead of buying fresh seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ woɔ niyenii fioo kwraa beni miduɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooohe dumɔwui heei

english: Saved seeds from hybrid crops lose their vigor and genetic strength over generations, resulting in smaller yields and weaker plants. Buying fresh certified seeds ensures uniform, strong growth and better resistance to local diseases.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ fiteɔ fɔmɔ su mli hewalɛ kɛ hewalɛ yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni tsei lɛ hu baa shi. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ ahemɔ haa amɛdaraa be fɛɛ be, ni amɛhe wa, ni amɛnyɛɔ amɛshiɔ helai ni baa maŋ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it better to raise tomato seeds in a small nursery bed first or plant them straight into my main farm field?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu tomato dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ bibioo ko mli? dani loo adu yɛ miŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ

english: Starting tiny seeds like tomatoes in a protected nursery bed allows you to give them special care, water, and protection from pests while they are weak. You can then transplant only the strongest, healthiest seedlings into your main farm field.
ga: Kɛ́ obɔi dumɔwui bibii, tamɔ tomatoi yɛ he ko ni abuɔ he lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ, ohaa amɛ nu, ni obuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛhe yɔɔ oshara lolo lɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ dumɔwui ni he wa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ aya oŋmɔ titri lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants turning yellow and curling up into little cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiifee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf yellowing and curling are usually signs that tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies are sucking the sap from the leaves, or that the soil is missing key nutrients like nitrogen. Protecting the plants early stops insects from spreading viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛŋ miimu nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ. aloo etsɔɔ akɛ niyenii titrii tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ahe ni abuɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni kooloi akagbɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why do the blossoms on my tomato plants fall off without turning into actual tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Flowers drop off when the plant experiences stress, such as extreme heat, irregular watering, or having too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to focus on growing green leaves instead of setting fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na nɔnyɛɛ tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ. aloo nitrogen fertilizer babaoo yɛ Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama baai eŋɔli ni amɛkwɛɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why do my cowpea leaves droop and look dead during the hot afternoon sun, but bounce back looking healthy every morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cowpea baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ mli lɛ? Shi obaaku osɛɛ kɛ hewalɛ daa leebi?

english: Plants fold or droop their leaves in the heat of the afternoon to conserve water and protect themselves from burning. As long as they recover by morning, the plant is managing stress, but it indicates the soil is getting dry.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ loo amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane latsaa ni naa wa lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ shãa he. Shii abɔ ni amɛhe baajɔ amɛ leebi lɛ Tsei baatsu nɔnyɛɛ he nii. Shi etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ miibɔi gbimɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die whenever I clear all the large shade trees from the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ be fɛɛ be ni majie tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to direct, harsh sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or large forest trees to create a cool cover and keep the air humid until the young cocoa roots are deep enough to handle full heat.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa waa he tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo, tamɔ tsei bibii loo koo mli tsei wuji, koni amɛfee he ko ni mli ejɔ ni amɛha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ mli baawo mli bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ latsaa lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow small and twisted instead of long, big, and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ, agbo ni eja lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, soft soil to expand properly. If the soil is packed hard or filled with stones, the root cannot push downward easily, causing the tuber to grow bent and small. Building high, soft mounds solves this problem.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni egbɛ eshwa jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ Anyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ashwie shi mlɛo. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ bibioo. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni afee lɛ tsuɔ naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why does putting chemical fertilizer directly against the stem of my crop cause the plant to dry up and die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mi tsei lɛ ashishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa amɛgbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ lɛ?

english: Fertilizers contain concentrated salts that draw water out of plant roots and stems if placed too close, effectively burning the plant. Fertilizer should always be applied a few inches away from the stem in wet soil.
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ nu ni baajie nu kɛjɛ tsei ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi amli kɛji akɛ akɛwo amɛhe tsɔ. Ebaashã tsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi inchii fioo komɛi.

english: Why do weeds make my maize plants stay short and weak even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛhe waaa eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crop for plant food, sunlight, and root space. Even with plenty of rain, weeds will consume the soil nutrients before your maize roots can reach them.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha tsei niyenii, hulu la kɛ shishifãi ahe gbɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ, shi Jwɛi hu yeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ dani ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe.

english: Why do small beetles bore tiny holes through my harvested beans after I put them in storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ bu bibii kɛtsɔɔ mi ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ amli beni mikɛwo nibii ni akɛtoɔ lɛ kotoku lɛ mli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weevil insects often lay microscopic eggs on bean pods while they are still in the field. If the beans are not thoroughly sun-dried and stored in airtight containers or treated bags, the eggs hatch inside storage and eat the grain.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ amɛwui bibii ni anaa lɛ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo lɛ. Kɛji akɛ hulu lɛ shɛɛɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe lɛ, ha amɛgbi ni okɛto tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo kotoku ko ni akɛ tsofa ewo mli momo lɛ mli. Wɔlɔi lɛ fɔɔ yɛ tsɛnsi lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ dumɔwui lɛ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my crops instead of just waiting for a traditional day?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ makpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ otsi lɛ mli gbi kome kɛkɛ?

english: Crops give clear physical signs when they are mature, such as leaves turning yellow or seeds hardening. Relying on crop maturity signs rather than fixed calendar days ensures your harvest reaches full size without spoiling.
ga: Tsei baaha gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ beni amɛdaraa lɛ, tamɔ baai ni baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo dumɔwui ni wa. Kɛ́ okɛ ohe fɔ̃ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ he okadii lɛ anɔ moŋ fe kalanda gbi pɔtɛɛ ko lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni okpamɔ lɛ ashɛ egbɛfaŋnɔ ni efiteee lɛ he.

english: Will my maize keep growing bigger if I leave it in the field past its normal harvest time?
ga: Mi ŋmãa lɛ miiya hiɛ waa. Kɛji mishi yɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛho kpamɔɔ be ni sa lɛ he?

english: No, once maize reaches full maturity, it stops growing and begins to dry out. Leaving it in the field too long exposes the cobs to insects, birds, and mold without adding any extra weight.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Ebaakpa shweremɔ ni ebɔi ŋmɔlɔ. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii, okpoi kɛ ŋmeii aba ŋmeii lɛ anɔ ni ekɛ muji ko fataaa he.

english: What standard methods should I use so that my harvested maize does not rot?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛi ni ato he gbɛjianɔ esa akɛ mikɛtsu nii koni mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ akafite?

english: To stop maize from rotting, harvest on a dry day, shell the cobs when properly dry, and spread the grains in the sun until they are completely hard before storing them in clean, dry bags elevated off the ground.
ga: Bɔni afee ni ŋmãa lɛ akafite Kpamɔ yɛ gbi ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Kpɔ̃ɔ ŋmei lɛ kɛji egbi jogbaŋŋ. ni okɛ dumɔwui lɛ agbɛ ashwã koni amɛgbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kwraa dani okɛwo kotokui ni he tse ni egbi amli ni okɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my harvested yams spoil so easily, and how does using crates help protect them?
