ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya lɛ? Ni te adeka ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni abu ŋmeii ahe aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Yam tubers have delicate skins that bruise easily during transport, letting rot in. Packing yams carefully in sturdy crates prevents physical damage and allows air circulation, keeping them fresh much longer.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ yɛ hewolo ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ akɛmiiya he kroko. ni eha egbo Kɛ́ okɛ sweet potato wo adeka ni mli wa mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaatsi gbɔmɔtsoŋ fitemɔ naa ni ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Ehaa amɛfeɔ ehee be babaoo.

english: How do I tell if my farmland is ready for planting or if I need to change my preparation method?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ efee klalo kɛha dumɔ? Aloo ehe miihia ni matsake gbɛ ni mitsɔɔ nɔ misaa mihe lɛ?

english: Land is ready when the soil is properly cleared, loose, and adequately moist. If your soil remains hard or packed, you should change your method to deep tilling or constructing ridges to aid root growth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa. Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ wa lolo loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Esa akɛ otsake gbɛ ni otsɔɔ nɔ otsuɔ nii lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ nɔ loo ofee ŋmeii ni baawo shishifãi lɛ adalɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Should I plant the same crop on my field every season, or is it better for me to change crops?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa be loo ehi akɛ matsake ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: It is best to change (rotate) your crops each season. Alternating crops like maize with legumes improves soil fertility, breaks pest cycles, and leads to better overall yields.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsake (otsake) oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa afi. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yaa hiɛ. Gbalamɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ ni ekɛ nibii ni anáa lɛ fɛɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa

english: How can I tell if the rain situation is reliable enough for me to start planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ shihilɛ lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi dumɔwui?

english: Wait until the rainy season is fully established with consistent, deep-soaking rains over several days. Planting after just one light early rain can cause seeds to germinate and then dry up and die.
ga: Mɛɛ ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba. kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ gbii babaoo Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ Shikome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgbi ni amɛgboi.

english: What basic materials and inputs should I distribute to my farm workers for planting maize and yams?
ga: Mɛɛ shishijee nibii kɛ saji esa akɛ magbala mi ŋmɔ mli nitsulɔi ni duɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: You should supply certified, high-germination maize seeds, healthy seed yam tubers, balanced fertilizers, and sturdy handling containers like crates to protect the crop during harvest.
ga: Esa akɛ oyahe ŋmãa dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ni awo he odaseyeli. Sweet potato tubers ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja kɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni wa tamɔ adekai ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: What visual signs show that my maize seeds are healthy enough to plant?
ga: Okadii ni anaa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu.

english: Good planting seeds are whole, smooth, completely dry, and free from insect holes or discolorations. Healthy seeds ensure fast germination and strong seedling growth.
ga: Dumɔwui kpakpai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛgbi kwraa, ni amɛbɛ kooloi amli ŋmeii loo amɛhe su ni tsakeɔ. Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ haa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya ni dumɔwui ni he wa hu daa.

english: How can I estimate the amount of maize yield I will get so I can plan for the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masusu mi-ŋmãa yibiiwoo lɛ he koni mato mijarayeli he gbɛjianɔ?

english: You can estimate yield by counting mature cobs in a small sample area of your field and multiplying that by your total plot size. Good field management helps ensure your actual harvest matches your financial expectations.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu yibiiwoo lɛ he akɔntaa kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni eda lɛ ni oookane yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli nɔkwɛmɔnɔ bibioo ko mli lɛ nɔ, ni okɛ oŋmɔ lɛ dalɛ fɛɛ abɔ he. Gbɛjianɔtoo kpakpa yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni okpamɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ ashɛ shika he gbɛkpamɔi ni oyɔɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I plant them in an open field without any plantain trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni dumɔwui bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very delicate and burn easily under harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains alongside them creates living shade and keeps the soil moist, giving the young cocoa trees the protection they need to survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa kwraa, ni hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa hulutsoo ni wala yɔɔ mli baa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa cacao tsei bibii lɛ náa hebuu koni amɛhi shi yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Will I get a bigger harvest if I plant my maize seeds very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni ekɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ?

english: Planting seeds too close together makes the plants compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak stalks and small maize cobs, whereas proper spacing gives each plant enough room to grow large and productive cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmãa bibii baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmãa wuji ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient for leaf growth. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer will help restore the green color and make the plant grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ akwɛ̃ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni ewo tsei lɛ adalɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Why do people advise me to plant groundnuts or beans on the same field after harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have special roots that grab nitrogen from the air and put it back into the ground. Planting them rejuvenates tired soil naturally, helping the next crop you plant grow better without buying as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Tsei nɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni etɔ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ye obua ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohé tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli.

english: Why do my crops refuse to grow well on land where the top layer of soil was scraped away or heavily dug up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ loo atsa shi waa lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: The top layer of dirt, called topsoil, holds almost all the dark organic matter and nutrients crops need to feed on. When the topsoil is gone, only hard, infertile subsoil remains, which makes it very difficult for crop roots to find food or breathe.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ akɛ topsoil. Ekɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni he hiaa tsei lɛ ateŋ babaoo toɔ. Kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ etee Shikpɔŋ shishi shikpɔŋ ni wa ni wooo yibii pɛ baashwɛ. Enɛ haa ewaa waa kɛhaa tsei shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaana niyenii loo amɛmu.

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry spells as a natural way to save water and protect themselves from heat. They are not dead; once the rains return, the stems will quickly shoot out fresh leaves and continue growing underground tubers.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Eji adebɔɔ gbɛ ni oootsɔ nɔ okɛ nu ato ni obu ohe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Amɛ gboko lolo. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ tso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei oya ni ebaaya nɔ ekwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii.

english: How can I tell if my crops are drooping because they need water or because a disease is attacking them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho ejaakɛ nu he miihia amɛ loo helai miitutua amɛ?

english: If crops are just thirsty, they will look limp during the hot afternoon but perk up on their own in the cool early morning or after watering. If a plant remains wilted in wet soil or during cold hours, a disease is likely attacking its roots or stems.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kumai miiye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛkɛ Amɛbaafee tamɔ mɛi ni egbɔjɔ yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Shi amɛbaakwɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ leebi maŋkpa ni hulu lɛ miitso loo beni awo amɛ nu sɛɛ. Kɛji tso lɛ tee nɔ egbo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ loo yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ Hela lɛ hu sumɔɔ ni etutua eshishifãi loo eshishifãi lɛ.

english: Why should I pluck off some of the extra side branches and lower leaves from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe niji ni yɔɔ afã kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Removing small side shoots allows the tomato plant to send its water and food energy directly into making bigger, healthier fruits rather than spending that energy growing extra useless leaves and stems.
ga: Nibii bibii ni ajieɔ lɛ Enɛ haa tomato tso lɛ tsɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii hewalɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Mohu ɔ, moo ngɔ jamɛ a he wami ɔ kɛ wo tsohi kɛ tsohi nɛ a he be se nami kpahi.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and becoming hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Curled, hard pepper leaves are usually a sign that tiny insects like aphids or mites are hiding underneath and sucking out the plant's sap. Spraying the leaves with soapy water or appropriate pest control stops the insects and allows new leaves to grow normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ baa ni ebɔle ehe ni wa lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ koolooi bibii, tamɔ aphids loo mites, kɛ amɛhe ewo shishi ni amɛmiinu tso lɛ nu lɛ. Ni akɛ nu ni mli edɔ loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ baashwie baai lɛ anɔ. Ehaa kooloi bibii lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe ni ehaa baa heei daa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do the seeds I save from my own harvest yield smaller crops than the fresh seed packets I buy from the agricultural officer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mibua naa kɛjɛɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ mli lɛ woɔ yibii bibii fe dumɔwui heei ni miheɔ kɛjɛɔ okwaayeli he onukpai lɛ adɛŋ lɛ?

english: Many commercial seeds are special hybrids bred for high yields in their first planting. Seeds saved from those harvested crops lose their special strength in the next generation, producing weaker plants with smaller yields compared to fresh commercial seed.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛheɔ jara lɛ ji dumɔwui krɛdɛɛi ni atsɔse amɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwui lɛ amli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ nakai tsei ni akpaa lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ amɛhewalɛ krɛdɛɛ lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni akɛheɔ jara lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my mangoes look ripe and red on the outside, but when I open them, they are full of tiny worms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ekwɛ̃ ni eyɛ tɔrɔmɔɔ yɛ kponɔgbɛ shi kɛ́ agbele lɛ, ŋmeii bibii eyi mli obɔ lɛ?

english: Fruit flies bore tiny holes into the skin of ripening fruit to lay their eggs inside. When these eggs hatch into maggots, they eat the fruit flesh from the inside out, causing internal rotting while the outside still looks colorful.
ga: Yibii amli ŋmeii lɛ woɔ bu bibii. Eboteɔ aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ahewolo mli koni ewo wɔji yɛ mli. Kɛ́ wuji nɛɛ fɔ lɛ, amɛbatsɔmɔɔ ŋmeii. Ebaaye aduawai lɛ loo lɛ kɛjɛ emli kɛya kponɔgbɛ. Enɛ haa emli lɛ fiteɔ yɛ be mli ni kponɔgbɛ lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do insects attack my fruits mostly when they are almost ready for harvest instead of when they are young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi aduawai lɛ babaoo beni eshwɛ fioo ni amɛbaakpa lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatutua amɛ beni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ

english: As fruits ripen, they become softer and produce strong sweet scents and sugars. Pests like fruit flies are attracted to these smells and find soft, ripe skin much easier to pierce and lay eggs in.
ga: Beni aduawai lɛ shwereɔ lɛ, efeɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni sugar babaoo yɔɔ mli. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ gbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ aduawai amli ŋmeii. Ni ana akɛ hewolo ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni egbɔ lɛ mliboteɔ mli ni ewoɔ ŋmeii lɛ waaa kwraa.

english: I noticed sticky patches on my ripening fruits before tiny holes appeared on them. What is causing this?
ga: Miyɔse okadii komɛi ni ŋmɛɔ shi. Yɛ aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ nɔ dani bu bibii jeɔ kpo lɛ, mɛni kɛ enɛ baa?

english: Insects like fruit flies often rub against or secret sticky fluids on the fruit skin while searching for the softest spot to puncture and deposit their eggs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii, tamɔ aduawai amli ŋmeii, shwieɔ loo amɛhiɛɔ nu ni mli tse yɛ aduawai lɛ anɔ. yɛ be mli ni etaoɔ he ni egbɔjɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ koni ebote mli ni efɔ bii lɛ.

english: How do small flies put worms deep inside a mango without destroying the whole skin?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei bibioo ko aŋɔ etsɛŋemɔ helai awo mango mli ni efiteee ŋmei lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Female fruit flies have a needle-like body part called an ovipositor that acts like a syringe. It pierces a microscopic hole through the skin to lay eggs directly into the flesh without tearing the rest of the fruit.
ga: Fruit ŋmeii yei yɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ fã ko ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ lɛ ovipositor ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli. Amɛfoɔ bu bibii bibii kɛtsɔɔ hewolo lɛ mli koni amɛkɛ ŋmeii awo loo lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛgbalaaa aduawai ni eshwɛ lɛ amli.

english: If I pick my mangoes while they are still green, will that stop insects from laying eggs inside them?
ga: Kɛji okpa mango be mli ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ, Ani kooloi bibii baanyɛ akpa ŋmeii ni amɛwoɔ yɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yes, harvesting mature green fruits early prevents fruit flies from attacking, as flies prefer softer, fully ripening fruit. Green mature mangoes can safely complete their ripening off the tree.
ga: Hɛɛ, aduawai eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃ mra lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ aduawai amli ŋmeii ni baatutua bo lɛ anaa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii sumɔɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni ekwɛ̃ kwraa. Abaanyɛ ajie mango eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃ kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do some of my fruits change color to red or yellow much earlier than expected while still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yibii lɛ ekomɛi miitsɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ loo ŋmɔŋ mra fe bɔ ni mikpaa gbɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Early color changes are often a stress response caused by insect attack. When pests pierce the skin, the wound causes the fruit to produce ethylene gas, making it turn color prematurely.
ga: Mra be mli su tsakemɔ Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni jɛɔ haomɔ ni kooloi ni tutuaa mɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ mli baa ji enɛ. Kɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai bote hewolo lɛ mli lɛ Pilamɔ lɛ haa aduawai lɛ jieɔ ethylene gas. ni ekɛ su tsakeɔ oya baa.

english: How can I tell if fruit rot on my farm is caused by insect eggs or by rain and bad weather?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ ŋmeii akui ji nɔ ni kɛ aduawai ni fiteɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa? loo nugbɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni ehiii kɛbaa

english: Insect rot usually starts with tiny puncture marks, sticky spots, and worms inside the flesh, whereas weather-related rot usually begins as soft, moldy patches spreading across the outer skin surface.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fitemɔ jeɔ shishi kɛ ŋmeii bibii, ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi, kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ loo lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ mli baa lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ hei bibii. ŋmɔtɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hewolo lɛ kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ fɛɛ mli

english: What simple step can I take to prevent flies from laying eggs in my tree fruits near harvest time?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mafee nɔ ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo Koni ŋmeii akawo mitso lɛ yibii lɛ amli beni kpamɔɔ be lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ lɛ?

english: Covering young fruits with protective bags or placing commercial pheromone traps around the farm traps and kills adult flies before they can land on the fruit to lay eggs.
ga: Ŋmɛɛ kotoku lɛ mli koni obu aduawai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ahe loo okɛ jarayeli pheromone tsɔne ko abɔle he. ŋmɔ mli tsɔne ni egbeɔ ŋmeii ni eda lɛ dani amɛkpɛtɛɔ aduawai ahe koni amɛwo ŋmeii.

english: Why is it bad to leave fallen, rotten mangoes lying on the ground under my trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ mashi mango ni egbo ni egbo lɛ yɛ mitso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Fallen fruit contains insect eggs and larvae that feed, enter the soil, and hatch into hundreds of new adult flies that will fly back up to attack your remaining crop.
ga: Yibii ni egbee shi lɛ amli kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni taoɔ niyenii, amɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni amɛfɔ̃ɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii onukpai ohai abɔ ni kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbatutuaa onibii ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: Is it safe to harvest and sell fruits that have tiny pinpoint holes on their skin?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ abaakpa aduawai ni bu bibii yɔɔ hewolo lɛ mli lɛ ni ahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Fruits with tiny holes likely have pest eggs inside that will quickly hatch and rot the flesh during transport, making them unsafe to store or sell to buyers.
ga: aduawai ni bu bibii yɔɔ mli Bei pii lɛ, kooloi awui yɛ mli. Enɛ baafo oya ni ebaagbo yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa lɛ. Enɛ haaa efee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe akɛ abaato loo ahɔ̃ɔ aha mɛi ni heɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow from the center line down to the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ teŋgbɛ line lɛ nɔ kɛmiiya ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ?

english: When maize leaves turn yellow in a V-shape starting from the tip, it is usually a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen is the main food crop plants need to stay green, grow tall, and build strong stalks.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ, ni amɛfeɔ V su ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli, amɛdara, ni amɛma tsei ahewalɛ.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts or cowpeas on my farm helps improve the soil for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special leaves and roots that pull nitrogen directly from the air and trap it in the soil, acts like a natural fertilizer for future crops like maize or cassava.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ baai kɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn small and woody when I harvest them during a very dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛfeɔ tsei beni mikpaa amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants store extra energy and water in their roots. During long dry periods, the plant uses up the stored starch in its roots to keep itself alive, which leaves the tubers thin, dry, and tough.
ga: Cassava tsei kɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu ni fa fe nine toɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ Tsei kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ato yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ mlɛo, amɛgbiɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do young cocoa trees wither and die if I clear away all the big trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to direct heat and strong sunlight. Big forest trees provide shade and keep the air humid, protecting delicate young cocoa leaves from scorching while their roots grow deep.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ hulu la ni naa wa he waa. Tsei wuji ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ haa hulutsoo baa, ni amɛhaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli fɛ̃ɔ. Ebuɔ kookoo baai bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe koni amɛkashã be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when the bunches start growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ tsei lɛ aniji je shishi amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Plantain roots grow shallow in the upper soil rather than deep into the ground. As the fruit bunch grows heavy, it makes the plant top-heavy, so strong winds can easily pull the shallow roots out of the soft soil unless supported with wooden props.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋwɛi fã lɛ mli fioo moŋ fe ni amɛaakwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ aduawai akuu lɛ bafee tsiimɔ Ehaa tso lɛ tsiimɔ waa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ. Ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ nɔ oya ja akɛ tsei ni akɛfiɔ he lɛ tsu nii.

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunlight to manufacture energy for growing large tubers underground. Staking lifts the foliage off the damp ground, exposing leaves to full sun and keeping them safe from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la babaoo koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Ha baai lɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo. ni amɛkwɛ shweshweeshwe shihilɛ nɔ kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their blossoms without forming fruit when the weather becomes very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni amɛwooo yibii be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and damages the pollen inside the flowers. When pollen dies from high temperatures, the flower fails to set fruit and drops off the stem to save energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni efiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛji pollen gbo yɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa hewɔ lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ wooo yibii ni amɛbaagbee shi kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why can crops like sorghum and millet survive long dry spells much better than my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ fe mi ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Sorghum and millet have extensive, deep root systems that seek out water far beneath the surface, and their leaves can roll up tight to prevent water from evaporating into the hot air during a drought.
ga: Sorghum kɛ millet yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli kwɔ ni taoɔ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi. Ni amɛbaai lɛ baanyɛ abɔle amɛhe shi jogbaŋŋ koni nu akatsɔ la ni mli edɔ lɛ mli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling tightly upwards and looking crinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe kɛmiiya ŋwɛi ni amɛmiifee tamɔ nɔ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies hiding underneath the leaves, or by a virus these insects transmit while feeding on the sap.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa beni amɛyeɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when the soil stays soaked with rain for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ? Ani nugbɔ enɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ?

english: Roots need air to breathe just like the upper plant. Excessively wet soil fills up all air spaces with water, smothering the roots and allowing rot-causing fungal germs to multiply rapidly.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he hiaa shishifãi koni amɛmu tamɔ bɔ ni tsei feɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni edɔ tsɔ lɛ baayi kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ. Ekɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ lɛ feɔ babaoo oya.

english: How deep should I put my maize seeds into the ground when sowing?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu?

english: Plant your maize seeds about 3 to 5 centimeters deep, which is about the length of your thumb till the first joint. If you plant too shallow, birds will eat the seeds or the sun will dry them out, but if you plant too deep, the seed will run out of energy before reaching the surface.
ga: Dumɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ aaafee sɛntimitai 3 kɛyashi 5, ni ji aaafee oshishifa lɛ mlilɛɛmɔ kɛyashi klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ. Kɛji odu he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ Okpoi baaye dumɔwui lɛ loo hulu la baaha amɛgbi. Shi kɛji odu mli tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ ahewalɛ sɛɛ foɔ dani amɛshɛɔ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ.

english: Can I grow crops successfully on sandy soil near the coast?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ ŋã shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ ŋshɔ lɛ naa lɛ nɔ yɛ omanyeyeli mli?

english: Yes, but sandy soil loses water and plant food very fast because it does not hold moisture well. Mixing organic matter like compost, dry leaves, or animal manure into sandy soil helps it hold onto water and nutrients so your crops can feed properly.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛ tsei aniyenii oya waa ejaakɛ ehiɛɛɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, baai ni egbi, loo ŋmɔshi nibii futu ŋãi amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ehiɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ mli bɔni afee ni otsei lɛ anyɛ aye niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do extension officers recommend planting beans or groundnuts together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension agent lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ adu ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legume crops like beans and groundnuts have special roots that grab nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil. Planting them with maize feeds the soil naturally, helping your maize grow stronger without buying as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ye obua o-abele lɛ ni ehiɛ wa ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohe tsofa-kɛ-ŋma babaoo.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean your crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is a main nutrient plants need to stay green. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer like Urea gives the plant energy to turn green again and produce big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ ni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my tomato leaves droop in the hot afternoon heat even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ miiho yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji mikɛ nu wo nɔ leebi po.

english: In intense heat, tomato plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it from the ground. As long as they stand tall again in the cool evening, it is normal, but covering the soil with dry grass helps keep the ground cool and moist.
ga: yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shii abɔ ni amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ ekoŋŋ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ mli lɛ, no lɛ ehi. Shi kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ.

english: How do weeds hurt my cassava plants if the cassava is already taller than the weeds?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aye mi-cassava tsei lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ? Be mli ni ŋmei lɛ ekwɛ fe jwɛi lɛ momo?

english: Even if cassava plants are tall, weeds under them steal water, nutrients, and underground space. Clearing weeds early gives the cassava roots full access to plant food so the tubers can grow thick and heavy.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmei tso lɛ kɛlɛ moŋ Shi jwɛi ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ juɔ nu, niyenii kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi he. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ naa tsei niyenii kwraa. Bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant peppers on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop in the same spot lets plant diseases and harmful pests build up in that soil over time. Rotating peppers with crops like maize or cassava starves out those specific pests and keeps your land healthy.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha tsei ahe helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. Chili ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni akɛtsakeɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni ejie tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eha oshikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Pepper flowers need insects like bees to visit them and carry pollen so the fruit can form. If flowers fall off, it often means there are no pollinators around or the weather is too dry; keeping flowering bushes near your farm attracts pollinators to help set fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii he miihia kooloi bibii, tamɔ ŋmeii, koni amɛbasara amɛ kɛ pollen koni amɛwo yibii. Kɛji fɔfɔi lɛ gbee shi lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bei pii lɛ, pollinators bɛ he ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ. aloo kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Kɛ́ okɛ tsei bibii ni woɔ fɔfɔii lɛ to he ko ni bɛŋkɛ oŋmɔ lɛ, ebaagbala ŋmeii ni shwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: What is eating small holes in my maize leaves and leaving dark dirt inside the stalk?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ muji ni tsuɔ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the funnel of the plant. Checking your farm early and putting wood ash, neem leaf extract, or recommended pest control inside the leaves can stop them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Okwaafoi lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra ni akɛ tso sũ Neem tso lɛ mli nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ afata he Aloo, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni akɛwoɔ baa lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ amɛnaa dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: How do government-certified seeds differ from the seeds I save from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esoro dumɔwui ni nɔyeli lɛ eŋmɛ he odase lɛ yɛ dumɔwui ni mihere kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ he?

english: Government-certified seeds are tested and selected by experts to resist local crop diseases and handle dry spells better. They germinate more evenly and usually produce much higher yields than seeds saved from previous harvests.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni nɔyeli lɛ eŋmɛ gbɛ lɛ ekwɛ ni ŋaalɔi ehala amɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo tsei ahe helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ni amɛkwɛ hulutsoo be lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ni bei pii lɛ amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni aŋmala ashwie shi kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves are usually a sign that your soil lacks nitrogen. The maize plant moves the remaining nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to feed the young, growing top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi tsei tsiɔ nitrogen ni fa fe nine kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant beans or groundnuts together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni extension agent lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ mikɛ mi-corn lɛ adu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and groundnuts have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. This naturally feeds the maize crop and keeps your land fertile.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmãa lɛ aye niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eye ebua oshikpɔŋ lɛ ni efee nɔ ni baa nii.

english: How does putting dried cow or chicken manure in my farm help my crops survive dry periods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo tsina ŋmei ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Manure acts like a sponge in the soil. It improves the soil structure so it can hold onto moisture longer after rain, keeping crop roots hydrated during dry spells.
ga: Manure tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii feɔ fɛo bɔni afee ni enyɛ ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop many of their small young pods before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii babaoo dani edaraa lɛ?

english: This is called 'cherelle wilt.' Cocoa trees naturally produce more young pods than they can feed, so the tree drops the extra ones to save energy and water for the healthy pods.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ ‘Cherelle wilting’ Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ ŋmeii bibii babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu ato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do I need to tie my yam vines to tall wooden stakes off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei fĩɔ tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for the tubers growing underground. Staking holds the leaves high up into the light and keeps them off the hot, wet ground where diseases spread.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ yaa ŋwɛi kɛyaa la lɛ mli ni ehaaa he ni edɔ ni edɔ, he ni helatsɛmɛi baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã lɛ.

english: What causes my plantain trees to easily fall over during strong wind storms?
ga: Mɛni haa mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa lɛ mli?

english: Plantain plants do not have deep taproots; their roots spread out near the surface. If the soil is too soft or pests have eaten the shallow root system, the top-heavy plant loses its balance.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Eshishifãi lɛ gbɛ eshwa he ko ni bɛŋkɛ nu lɛ hiɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ loo kɛji kooloi ni yeɔ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ yeɔ lɛ, Tsei ni tsii lɛ baafee mɛi ni nyɛɛɛ amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Curled, small leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips sucking the sap out of young shoots, or by a leaf-curl virus spread by insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ leaf curl hela ko ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot underground when rain falls continuously?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ miinɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain leaves standing water around the roots, the soil starves of oxygen, allowing fungi to attack and rot the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu kpɛtɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmei lɛ tutuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Weeds grow faster than most crops and aggressively steal nutrients, light, and root space from your crops, effectively starving them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei babaoo ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, la kɛ shishifãi ahe gbɛ kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ amli. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ yɛ gbɛ ni mɔɔ shi nɔ.

english: Why do my ripe tomatoes split open on the vine right after a sudden rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ shwereɔ niji yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ trukaa lɛ?

english: When tomato plants get a sudden heavy drink of water after a dry spell, the inside of the fruit swells faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing the skin to crack open.
ga: Beni tomato tsei lɛ nuɔ nu waa trukaa yɛ hɔmɔ be ko sɛɛ lɛ. Yibii lɛ mligbɛ fã lɛ fũuɔ oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ baanyɛ ashɛre. Enɛ haa hewolo lɛ fãa.

english: How do I know the exact right time to start planting my seeds after the first rains fall?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ maje dumɔwui ashishi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the ground has received two or three steady rains and the soil is consistently wet. Planting after just one light rain can trick seeds into sprouting, only for them to dry out and die if a dry spell follows.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ nɛɔ shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ, ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ewo ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ Mɔdɛŋbɔɔ kome pɛ baanyɛ alaka dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃. Dumɔwui lɛ pɛ baagbi ni amɛgboi kɛji hulutsoo be ko nyiɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why is it bad if I push my seeds very deep into the dirt when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji mikɛ midumɔwui lɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ waa beni miduɔ nii lɛ?

english: If seeds are buried too deep, they exhaust all their stored energy trying to push up through the heavy soil before reaching sunlight, causing them to rot or die underground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afu dumɔwui lɛ amli tsɔ lɛ, akɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii ni akɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni atsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ nɔ atsɔ ŋwɛi dani hulu la lɛ aba. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ loo amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to leave wide gaps between crops instead of planting them close together to fit more on the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ wɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔshi gbɛ ni da yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ lɛ? Mohu ɔ, mo du mɛ kɛ su he konɛ a kɛ he ɔ nɛ sa saminya.

english: Planting crops too close together makes them fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough room and resources to produce larger, healthier food.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ wuɔ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa nitsumɔhe fɛɛ nitsumɔhe náa he kɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaafee niyenii wuji ni haa mɔ he waa.

english: Is it better for my soil if I burn the cleared bush before planting, or should I clear the land without burning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ abaashã tsei bibii ni ajie lɛ dani adu loo ehi akɛ abaatsumɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ashãaa?

english: Clearing without burning is better because leaving grass and leaves on the farm allows them to rot into natural fertilizer while keeping the soil moist. Burning kills good soil organisms and leaves the land exposed to heat.
ga: Nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni ashãaa lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ kɛ́ ashi jwɛi kɛ baai yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha jwɛi kɛ baai lɛ afite akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Shãa fiteɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ wala ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dɔɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is starving for nitrogen, which is a major nutrient plants need to grow green, or the roots are sitting in too much water and cannot breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ onibii amli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ eŋɔli. Aloo shishifãi lɛ yɛ nu babaoo mli ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu.

english: Why do my crop leaves curl up or droop during the hottest part of the afternoon even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ, eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Leaf curling is the plant's natural defense against heat. It rolls its leaves to reduce water loss from evaporation during extreme sun, and it will relax once the temperature drops in the evening.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. Okɛ baai lɛ abɔ he koni nu ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ la ni hoɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ aba shi. ni ebaajɔɔ ehe kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi gbɛkɛ.

english: Weeds grow much faster than regular crops and aggressively steal the nutrients, sunlight, and root space meant for your farm crops, leaving your plants starved.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ daa lɛ, ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, hulu la, kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ waa. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye otsei lɛ.

english: Why should I plant cassava or plantain on the same field alongside my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo plantain yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plants like plantain and cassava act as living umbrellas, providing essential shade and keeping the soil cool for cocoa saplings.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains kɛ cassava tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ kɛhaa kookoo tsei lɛ.

english: How can I check if the seeds I saved from last year's harvest will actually sprout before I go ahead to plant them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ baakwɛ̃ diɛŋtsɛ dani madu amɛ?

english: You can do a simple germination test by placing 10 seeds inside a wet cloth for 3 to 5 days; if 8 or more sprout, your seeds are healthy and ready for field planting.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee shweremɔ he kaa ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Obaanyɛ ofee enɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui 10 ni okɛaawo mama ni mli efɔ mli gbii 3 kɛyashi 5 lɛ nɔ. Kɛji 8 loo nɔ ni fe nakai kwɛ̃ lɛ, no lɛ odumɔwui lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni amɛfee klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ ŋmɔ mli.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer to my crops so that heavy rains do not wash it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akashwie amɛ?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist but not during active downpours. Burying or covering the fertilizer lightly with soil right near the crop roots keeps it from washing away during future rains.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi jeee yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni akɛfuɔ loo akɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe fioo yɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ baaye abua ni nu akafɔ̃ lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ wɔsɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Can I still plant cocoa on land that was previously dug up for illegal mining (galamsey)?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ kookoo lolo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsutsu lɛ atsa kɛha shika tsuru ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ (galamsey) lɛ nɔ?

english: Mining strips away the fertile topsoil and leaves behind harmful chemicals or heavy metals. Before planting cocoa on such land, the soil must be tested, restored with fresh organic matter, and treated so young plants can survive.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ jieɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ni eshiɔ tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo dade ni tsii. Dani abaadu kookoo yɛ he ni awie he lɛ Esa akɛ aka shikpɔŋ lɛ akwɛ. Kɛ nibii heei ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba. kɛ tsamɔ koni tsei bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: What kind of soil is best for starting a new cocoa farm in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ hi fe fɛɛ kɛha kookoo ŋmɔ hee shishijee yɛ Ghana?

english: Cocoa grows best in deep, well-draining soils rich in organic matter that can hold water without becoming soggy or waterlogged during heavy rains.
ga: Cocoa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɛ mli ni baanyɛ ahi nu mli ni ehaaa efee ŋmɔtɔ loo nu ewo mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: How do I know if my farm soil has lost the nutrients needed for a good cocoa harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miifite niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛkpa kookoo kpakpa lɛ?

english: If leaves turn yellow, young trees grow very slowly, or the harvest drops significantly year after year, your soil is likely depleted of key nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium.
ga: Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ, tsei bibii lɛ daaa blɛoo waa, loo ŋmaa lɛ baa shi waa afi fɛɛ afi. Ekolɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, fɔsfɔs, kɛ potasium hu efo oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. They need partial shade from food crops like plantains or shade trees to keep them cool and moist while their roots develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be ko kɛjɛ niyenii tsei tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Koni tso lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Cassava grows heavy roots that aggressively suck water and nutrients out of the soil, competing with young cocoa trees and slowing down their growth.
ga: Cassava kwɛ̃ɔ shishifãi ni tsii ni kɛ yiwalɛ shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ekɛ kookoo tsei bibii yeɔ akaŋ ni ehaa edalɛ baa shi.

english: Why do many of the small cocoa pods on my trees shrivel up and turn black before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ Tsei babaoo ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbo ni amɛmiitsɔ ediŋŋ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: This is often due to a natural process called 'cherelle wilt,' where the tree sheds extra pods it cannot feed, or it can be caused by insect damage and lack of water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ ‘cherelle wilt’ ni tsei shwieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni anyɛɛɛ aha amɛ niyenii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Aloo ebaanyɛ ejɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii kɛ nu ni faaa yɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot when there is continuous heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ ni naa wa miinɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Excess rain and high humidity encourage the spread of the Black Pod fungal disease. The fungus thrives in wet conditions and quickly jumps from pod to pod.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo woɔ blackpod fungal hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ he hewalɛ. Fung lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ mli ni efoɔ oya kɛjɛɔ pod mli kɛyaa pod mli.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to cut off extra side branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nitsulɔ ni kwɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ wo mi ŋaa akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo tso lɛ he lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy so sunlight and fresh air can flow through. This keeps the tree dry, reduces fungal diseases, and helps energy go into making big pods.
ga: Kpojiemɔ lɛ gbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ mli egbiɔ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hewalɛ ni ekɛfeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai wuji.

english: Why does leaving overgrown weeds around my cocoa trees reduce my crop yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine ni mishiɔ mikoo tsei lɛ ahe lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Weeds act like theft in the farm—they steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight that your cocoa trees need to produce healthy flowers and pods.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli, ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa o-cacao tsei lɛ koni amɛkwɛ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: My old cocoa trees are producing very few pods compared to ten years ago; why is this happening?
ga: Mi cacao tso momo lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ kɛ akɛto afii nyɔŋma ni eho nɛ lɛ he. Mɛni he je nɛ e baa jã a?

english: As cocoa trees age past 20 to 30 years, their natural pod production slows down. Old trees may need pruning, heavy soil feeding, or gradual replanting with improved young varieties.
ga: Beni cacao tsei hiɔ shi fe afii 20 kɛyashi 30 lɛ, adebɔɔ mli pod ni afeɔ lɛ baa shi. Ekolɛ tsei ni edara lɛ he baahia ni afolɔ amɛ. Ha shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ niyenii loo okɛ ŋmeii bibii ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ adu ekoŋŋ fiofio.

english: I am moving my farming activities from the Eastern Region to the Western Region; can I plant the exact same tree crops I used to grow back home?
ga: Mijie mi okwaayeli nitsumɔi lɛ kɛmiijɛ bokagbɛ kpokpaa lɛ nɔ kɛmiiya anaigbɛ kpokpaa lɛ nɔ. Ani manyɛ makwɛ tsei ni miyɔɔ yɛ shia lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: While both regions are in the forest zone, the Western Region generally receives higher and more continuous rainfall. Crops like cocoa, oil palm, and rubber thrive extremely well there, but crops that require a long dry spell to mature or fruit might not perform as expected.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ kpokpai enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ yɛ koo lɛ mli moŋ. Shi yɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ, anaigbɛ kpokpaa lɛ baaná nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo ni ebaaya nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ kookoo, mu kɛ rɔba kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ waa. Shi ekolɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni biɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani amɛshwereɔ loo amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ tsuuu nii bɔ ni akpaa gbɛ lɛ.

english: I recently acquired land in the Western Region around Mpohor Wassa East; which tree crops grow best in this area?
ga: Etsɛko tsɔ ni mihe shikpɔŋ yɛ anaigbɛ kpokpaa ni bɔle Mpohorwassa Bokagbɛ lɛ nɔ. Mɛɛ tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nɛkɛ he nɛɛ?

english: Mpohor Wassa East has high rainfall and rich forest soils. Tree crops like cocoa, oil palm, rubber, and citrus thrive very well in this soil and climate.
ga: Mpohor Wassa Bokagbɛ ji he ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ, ni koo mli shikpɔŋ lɛ hu eyi obɔ kɛ nibii babaoo. Tsei tamɔ kookoo, mu, rɔba kɛ citrus kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ nɛɛ nɔ.

english: I have land around the Nkwanta area; what kind of economic trees grow well in that climate?
ga: Miyɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ Ung Kwang Ta kpokpaa lɛ nɔ. Mɛɛ shika helɛtemɔ tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nakai kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ lɛ mli?

english: The Nkwanta area lies in a transition zone with a distinct dry season. Hardy trees like cashew, mango, and teak do very well there, alongside staple crops like yam and cassava.
ga: Nkwanta kpokpaa lɛ yɛ tsakemɔ he ko ni hulutsoo be ni yɔɔ faŋŋ yɔɔ mli. Tsei ni wa tamɔ cashew, mango, kɛ teak tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa. kɛfata ŋmɔshi nibii titrii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: How can I tell if a specific section of my land is not good for planting tree crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hei komɛi ni yɔɔ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ ehiii kɛha tsei akwɛmɔ?

english: Land that stays flooded or waterlogged for weeks, ground with heavy rocks, or shallow soil over hard rock is unsuitable. Tree roots need deep, loose soil so they can breathe and push downward easily.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ loo nu eyi nɔ otsii babaoo. Shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ tɛi ni tsii. loo shikpɔŋ ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni yɔɔ tɛ ni wa nɔ lɛ esaaa. Tso shishifãi lɛ hia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli tse bɔni afee ni amɛmu ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛya shi oya.

english: Should I plant the exact same tree crops on both the high ground and the low swampy parts of my farm?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli hei ni yɔɔ gɔŋji kɛ ŋshɔkpɔi ni yɔɔ ŋshɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ?

english: No, different parts of your land suit different crops. Lowland swampy areas suit crops that can handle wet soils like sugarcane or oil palm, while cocoa and citrus prefer well-draining higher ground or slopes to prevent root rot.
ga: Dabi, oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hei srɔtoi lɛ sa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi. He ni jwɛi yɔɔ lɛ hi kɛha tsei ni baanyɛ atsu shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ he nii, tamɔ shɛ̃ loo mu tso. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, kookoo kɛ citrus sumɔɔ hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo hei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ koni shishifãi lɛ akafite.

english: How do I know which part of my farm will give me the best tree yield before I start planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male miŋmɔ lɛ fã ni baawo tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ dani mabɔi dumɔ?

english: Look at the soil color, depth, and natural weeds. Dark, soft, crumbly topsoil with deep ground cover indicates high fertility where tree roots will grow strong and produce good harvests.
ga: Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ su, emlibotemɔ, kɛ adebɔɔ mli jwɛi. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni egbɛ eshwa, ni mli kwɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo. Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baakwɛ̃ waa ni ebaawo yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do some trees grow very fast on my neighbor's farm but grow slowly on my land in the same village?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi daa oya waa yɛ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ mli shi amɛdaraa fiofio yɛ mishikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ akrowa kome mli lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Even within the same village, soil depth, water drainage, past farm land use, and shade levels can vary. Trees on deeper, more fertile soil with good moisture control will naturally grow much faster.
ga: Yɛ akrowa kome mli po lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ, nu ni hoɔ, ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ baanyɛ afee srɔtoi. Tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni baa nii babaoo ni nu yɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: What will happen to my tree crop if I plant it in a place where the climate or soil does not support it?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi loo shikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii yɛ lɛ?

english: The tree will show signs of distress such as yellowing leaves, stunted growth, lack of flowers or fruits, and high vulnerability to pests and diseases, often dying before reaching maturity.
ga: Tso lɛ baajie haomɔ he okadii akpo, tamɔ baai ni miifee ŋmɔŋ kɛ dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ. Fɔfɔi loo aduawai ni bɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ oshara waa akɛ kooloi kɛ helai baanyɛ aba amɛnɔ. ni bei pii lɛ amɛgboiɔ dani amɛshɛɔ dalɛ ni yeɔ emuu lɛ he

english: Why do trees like oil palm and rubber need regions with high rainfall to yield well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei tamɔ oil palm kɛ rɔba he hiaa hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai lɛ?

english: Oil palm fruits and rubber latex require continuous high amounts of water to produce their oils and liquids. In drier regions, these trees struggle to produce good yields.
ga: Mu tso yibii kɛ latɛs biɔ nu ni akɛhaa be fɛɛ be koni aná mu kɛ nu. yɛ hei ni nu bɛ Tsei nɛɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ waa koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Can getting too much rain in an area harm my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo yɛ he ko lɛ baaye mi-kokoo tsei lɛ awui?

english: Yes, excessive rain combined with constant shade creates high humidity, which encourages fungal diseases like black pod rot and rots tree roots if the water does not drain away.
ga: Hɛɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be fɛɛ be fata he lɛ kɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa baa. Enɛ woɔ ŋmeii helai tamɔ black pod rot kɛ tso shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ he hewalɛ kɛji akɛ ajieee nu lɛ kɛjɛɛɛ mli.

english: Cassava naturally sheds its leaves during long dry spells to save water and protect itself from drying out. As long as the main stem stays green inside, the plant is alive and will sprout fresh leaves as soon as the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ hulutsoo be mli. Shii abɔ ni tso titri lɛ ji eŋɔli lolo yɛ emli lɛ. Tso lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo ni ebaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii heei kɛji nugbɔ nɛ ekoŋŋ pɛ.

english: Pepper plants often drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme sun heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients. Giving them steady moisture and light shade during the hottest part of the day helps the flowers stay on and form fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli lɛ miigba amɛnaa. Kɛ́ hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be fɛɛ be yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Tomato leaves curl inward as a natural shield to reduce water loss from direct sunlight. Placing mulch around the base of the plant keeps the roots cool and damp, which helps the leaves relax.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa mli koni efee adebɔɔ mli tsɔne ni haa nu ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fiteɔ lɛ baa shi. Mulching ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ jɔɔ amɛhe

english: Yam vines are naturally designed to climb upward so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight to build food for the growing tuber underground. Lifting the leaves off the damp ground also prevents soil diseases from rotting the plant.
ga: Afee sweet potato wain tsei lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛkwɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛkɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu, eyeɔ ebuaa ni helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ akafite tso lɛ.

english: How do I know if my soil is ready for me to plant maize after the first rain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛha ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Your soil is ready when it is moist but not muddy. Scoop up a handful of soil and squeeze it; if it forms a soft ball that easily crumbles when touched, it has the right balance of moisture and air for seeds to sprout safely.
ga: Oshikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ edɔ shi ebɛ muji. Kpɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ ni okɛ nine shɛɔ nɔ lɛ ni okɛmimɔ mli; Kɛji efee bɔɔlu ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni fãa oya kɛji akɛ eshɛ he lɛ, hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni sa baafee nɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my plantain suckers grow very thin and weak when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ahe tseee ni amɛhe waaa lɛ, kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots compete fiercely underground for soil nutrients and water, while their leaves fight for sun. Spacing them properly allows each plant to get full nourishment and grow thick, healthy stems.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ mli lɛ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa hulu la he akaŋ lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ nɔ, ni eyɛ tso lɛ shishi ni mli wa ni mli wa.

english: Why do some of my crop seeds rot underground instead of growing into shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Seeds rot when buried too deep in heavy, waterlogged soil where they cannot get air to breathe. Planting seeds at a shallow depth in loose soil helps them get the warmth and oxygen needed to break out of their shell.
ga: Dumɔwui fiteɔ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ aahu akɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu. Dumɔwui lɛ ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ekwɔɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji nɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛje amɛhe kɛjɛ amɛmli.

english: Why should I clear weeds around my crops before I put fertilizer down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Nibii ni aduɔ dani awoɔ ŋmɔshi nii?

english: Weeds have aggressive roots that drink up water and fertilizer much faster than your crops can. Clearing the weeds first ensures all the nutrients go directly into feeding your crops instead of feeding the weeds.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni baanu nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe otsei lɛ. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ aya onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha jwɛi lɛ niyenii

english: What causes small holes in my young maize leaves when the plants are still short?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa bibioo lɛ baai lɛ anɔ beni tsei lɛ yɔɔ kuku lolo lɛ?

english: Small holes in young leaves are usually caused by early caterpillar pests like fall armyworm that feed on delicate foliage. Checking the central whorl of the plant early lets you catch them before they damage the growing point of the stalk.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mra be mli ŋmeii tamɔ fall armyworms ni yeɔ baai ni mli tse lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ baai bibii amli lɛ baa. Tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua bo ni omɔ amɛ dani amɛfite he ni tso lɛ shishifã lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why do small insects appear in my stored corn even when I keep the room clean and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miije kpo yɛ mi-abele ni mikɛto lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa mitsu lɛ mli tseɔ ni mifeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ.

english: Weevils often lay tiny, invisible eggs inside the corn grains while the crop is still standing in the field. Drying your harvested corn thoroughly under the sun and storing it in sealed, airtight bags prevents those eggs from hatching into destructive bugs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii fɔɔ wɔji bibii. ni anyɛɛɛ ana yɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ amli be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ damɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo Kɛ́ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ agbi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu shishi ni akɛto kotokui ni akɛ vacuum tsiɔ mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaatsi nakai ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui.

english: Young cocoa plants are very delicate and burn easily in harsh sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or bananas grown beside them to provide shade, cool air, and moist soil while their roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa kwraa, ni hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shãa oya. Amɛmiisumɔ ni adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo banana yɛ amɛmasɛi. Amɛhaa hulutsoo, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ, kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa waa lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the tip usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is essential food for plant growth. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore the green color and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei lɛ adalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves have ragged holes with small green caterpillars hiding inside the center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Ani okɛ ohe ewo teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworms feeding on the young leaves inside the plant whorl. Early field checks and spraying approved treatments or neem extracts into the plant center will protect your harvest.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworms ni yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli lɛ. Gbɛjegbɛ nɔ kwɛmɔ mra Ni tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo neem mli nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ ni oooshwie tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with lots of leaves but give me small, thin tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: When cassava receives too much nitrogen or is planted too close together, it puts all its energy into leaf and stem growth instead of storing energy in the underground roots.
ga: Beni ŋmei lɛ nine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ loo adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ehe tsɔ. Ebaakɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ awo baai kɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ hewalɛ baato shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi amli lɛ

english: Why do the bottoms of my young green tomatoes develop dark, rotten spots before ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition, called blossom-end rot, happens when the plant lacks calcium, often caused by uneven watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the plant transport calcium into the fruit.
ga: Shihilɛ nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ calcium. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ calcium woɔ aduawai lɛ amli.

english: Leaf curling is caused by tiny pests like aphids or thrips sucking nutrients from the leaves, or by a virus carried by whiteflies. Controlling these insects early prevents leaf leaf curling and stunted growth.
ga: Kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛji kɛbaa lɛ anɔ. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ naa.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves into sunlight so they can manufacture maximum food for the tubers below, while keeping the leaves off damp ground to avoid fungal diseases.
ga: Staking haa sweet potato baai lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ hulu la mli koni eha niyenii babaoo aba kɛha bulbs ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akamɔ bo.

english: Why should I prune away extra young shoots growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ plantain tso titri lɛ.

english: Too many young shoots (suckers) compete with the main plant for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Removing excess suckers leaves all the food for the main stem, producing bigger bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei bibii babaoo (tsei) kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, eshiɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ kɛhaa tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ. Feemɔ kuu agbo.

english: Why is it harmful for my field if I plant maize on the exact same plot every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be lɛ, eyeɔ miŋmɔ lɛ awui lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously strips the soil of specific nutrients and allows pests and soil diseases to build up. Alternating crops keeps the soil balanced and healthier.
ga: Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ akaná niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi, ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni akɛtsakeɔ amɛhe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts improve the soil for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have friendly bacteria on their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for the crops planted next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ naanyobɔɔ mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa tsei ni abaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why are my small cocoa pods drying up and turning shriveled on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii No hewɔ lɛ minɔ lɛ egbi ni egbo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Small cocoa pods often shrivel due to insect damage like capsid attacks, or through a natural self-thinning process called cherelle wilt when the tree lacks enough nutrients or water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii tamɔ capsid tutuamɔ hewɔ. loo etsɔ adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni haa tso lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni atsɛɔ lɛ Cherel withers lɛ mli Kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: How do pests cause cocoa pods to shrivel up before they are ripe?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛshwereɔ?

english: Insects like mirids and capsids bite into the young pod to suck its juices, injecting saliva that kills the surrounding tissue and causes the pod to dry up and shrivel.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ mirids kɛ capsids shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii amli koni amɛnu nu lɛ. Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ fãji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboɔ

english: If I see shriveled pods on my cocoa tree, does it mean pests are definitely on my farm?
ga: Kɛ mina ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo yɛ cacao tso nɔ lɛ Ani enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Not always. While insects do cause shriveling, harsh weather, lack of rain, or fungal diseases like black pod can also cause pods to dry up without pests being involved.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be, eyɛ mli akɛ kooloi bibii baaha amɛgbo moŋ. Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni ehiii, nugbɔ ni nɛɛɛ, loo ŋmeii helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji baanyɛ aha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni ŋmeii kɛ amɛhe wooo mli.

english: Is it helpful to spray pest-killing chemicals like 'Global' directly on cocoa pods that have already shriveled?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ aaafɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi tamɔ ‘Global’ lɛ ashwie kookoo ŋmeii ni egbo lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: No, spraying pods that are already dead or shriveled will not save them. You should spray to protect the healthy green pods and leaves from future insect attacks.
ga: Dabi, ŋmeii ni egbo loo ni egbo lɛ ni oooshwie nɔ lɛ hereŋ amɛyiwala. Esa akɛ okɛ tsofa afɔ nɔ koni obu ŋmeii lɛ kɛ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni baatutua amɛ wɔsɛɛ lɛ ahe.

english: What should I check on my farm before applying a chemical to kill pests?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ makwɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ atsu nii?

english: You should check if the damage is truly caused by insects rather than bad weather or disease, check which crop leaves or fruits are affected, and make sure you have the right chemical for that specific pest.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii kɛ nɔ ni efite lɛ ba diɛŋtsɛ, shi jeee kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ loo hela ni ehiii. Kwɛmɔ tsei lɛ baai loo amɛyibii ni enaa he sɛɛ. Ni kwɛmɔ ni oná tsofai ni sa kɛha nakai tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ.

english: Why did the pesticide I sprayed fail to stop my cocoa pods from drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni mikɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsĩ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi lɛ?

english: Pesticides fail if they are applied at the wrong time, if the wrong chemical was selected, or if the pod drying was caused by disease or dry weather rather than insect pests.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ tsuuu nii kɛji akɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ be ni esaaa mli. Kɛji ohala tsofa ni ejaaa Aloo kɛji akɛ hela loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ baa moŋ fe ŋmeii.

english: How do I know if a chemical like 'Global' is safe to use on my food crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tsofa ko tamɔ ‘Global’ lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛbaatsu nii yɛ mi niyenii ni miduɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Always consult an extension officer or read the product label to ensure the chemical is approved for your specific crop and that you follow the recommended dosage and waiting period before harvesting.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, bi extension official loo kanemɔ nibii ni aŋmala nɔ lɛ koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ akpɛlɛ tsofa ko nɔ kɛha onibii pɔtɛɛ. Ni onyiɛɔ tsofa ni akɛhaa lɛ kɛ be ni akɛbaamɛ dani akpaa nii lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young oil palm trees starting to shrivel and dry out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ miibɔi shwiemɔ ni amɛmiigbi lɛ?

english: Oil palm leaves shrivel mainly when leaf-eating caterpillars or beetles attack them, or when the roots cannot get enough water during extended dry seasons.
ga: Mu tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ titri kɛji ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ tutua amɛ. aloo be mli ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ mli lɛ.

english: Can I use the same pest-killing chemical for both my cocoa trees and my oil palms?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsofa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii yɛ kookoo kɛ mu tsei fɛɛ anɔ?

english: Not always. Cocoa and oil palm face different insect pests and have different sensitivities, so you must confirm if a chemical is approved for both crops before spraying.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be. Cocoa kɛ oil palm kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai srɔtoi kpeɔ ni amɛnuɔ he amɛhaa srɔtoi. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ oma nɔ mi akɛ akpɛlɛ tsofa ko nɔ kɛha tsei srɔtoi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ dani okɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ nɔ.

english: How does pest damage on oil palm leaves affect the fruit yield later on?
ga: Te tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ oil palm baai lɛ saa sɛɛ mli aduawai ni baa lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: When pests damage or shrivel oil palm leaves, the tree loses its ability to make food from sunlight, leading to smaller fruit bunches and lower palm oil yield.
ga: Beni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fiteɔ loo amɛhaa oil palm baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛfee niyenii kɛjɛ hulu la mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, aduawai ni ekpɛtɛ amɛhe lɛ feɔ bibii ni ŋmei fɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle full sun. Their leaves scorch when exposed to direct heat, so planting temporary shade crops like plantains alongside them keeps the air moist and shields them until they mature.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Amɛbaai lɛ baashã kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ odu tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains yɛ masɛi Enɛ baaye abua ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: Why do my pepper plants look wilted in the afternoon even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbo yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: On very hot afternoons, pepper leaves release moisture into the air faster than roots can draw it from the ground. This temporary wilting is a self-defense reaction to conserve water, and the leaves usually stand back up when temperatures cool in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Pepper baai lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ be kukuoo mli shwiemɔ nɛɛ ji nɔ ko ni akɛbuɔ mɔ he koni akɛbu nu he. Ni baai lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛte shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: High heat and inconsistent watering cause heat stress in tomatoes, which prevents proper pollination. When pollination fails, the plant sheds its flowers instead of spending energy to form fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni eyaaa nɔ lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa tomato mli. Enɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa lɛ naa. Beni pollination lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii Tso lɛ fɔfɔii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛbaawo yibii lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why is my maize crop turning light green and yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ miitsɔ eŋɔli ni mli tse kɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves in maize are a clear sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Maize requires nitrogen to produce chlorophyll for growth, so adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure restores the healthy green color.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ mli lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ekɛfee klorofil kɛha dalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in small nodules on their roots. When the plant dies, this trapped nitrogen breaks down into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi bibii amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nɛkɛ nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ nɛɛ fiteɔ kɛboteɔ sũ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi.

english: Does it matter which direction I insert my cassava stem cuttings into the dirt?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmei niji awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, planting cassava stems upside down forces the buds to grow downwards first before curving back up toward the sun. This wastes the plant's stored energy and results in weak growth and smaller tubers.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmei ni akwɛ̃ɔ ni tsɔɔ shishi lɛ nyɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ klɛŋklɛŋ kɛya shikpɔŋ, ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba hulu lɛ he. Enɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni tso lɛ eto lɛ. ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei lɛ adalɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii.

english: It is safer to wait for steady rainfall rather than planting after the very first rain. Early rains are often followed by dry spells that can scorch germinating seeds beneath the dry soil surface.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe fe dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔi ni baanyɛ aha dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ashã yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ shishi lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines on tall wooden poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ sweet potato wain tso awo tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are natural climbing vines that need to lift their foliage high into the sunlight to produce energy for large tubers. Staking also keeps leaves off the wet soil, preventing fungal leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni shwieɔ shi ni ehe hiaa ni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛnɔ bɔni afee ni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha amɛ bulb agboi lɛ. Staking hu buɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ he koni ekɛtsi baai helai ni ji fungal lɛ anaa.

english: What is eating ragged holes in the leaves of my young corn and hiding in the center funnel?
ga: Mɛni ji bu ni ekpɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli lɛ yeli ni ekɛ ehe ewo ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide deep inside the leaf whorl during the day to feed on growing tissue. Applying neem oil or approved insecticides into the central whorl early prevents severe crop loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛye ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛwoɔ teŋgbɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli mra. Ebaaye ebua ni akafite ŋmɔshi nibii ni naa wa waa.

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants adapted to absorb water and soil nutrients much more aggressively than farm crops. Clearing weeds early prevents them from stealing vital light and nutrients from young crop seedlings.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju la ni he hiaa waa kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui bibii amli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees look weak and dry when there are no big shade trees left around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛgbi yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ eshwɛɛɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees need partial shade to protect them from excessive sunlight and dry winds. Without shade trees, the hot sun dries out the soil and stresses the cocoa plants, making them weak and more vulnerable to diseases and insect attacks.
ga: Cacao tsei biɔ hulutsoo be fioo koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ fe nine kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa amɛgbiɔ lɛ he. Kɛji tsei ni baaha hulutsoo be lɛ bɛ lɛ Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ ni ehaa kookoo tso lɛ haoɔ. Enɛ haa kookoo tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni helai kɛ kooloi nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛ.

english: Which trees are good to plant inside my cocoa farm to provide shade without harming my crop?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei sa akɛ adu yɛ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛ hulutsoo aha ni efiteee miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Trees like Ofram, Framo, or Gliricidia are good because they grow tall to provide a high canopy without competing heavily with cocoa roots for nutrients. Avoid trees that attract pests or drop heavy branches that can break young cocoa trees.
ga: Tsei tamɔ Ofram, Framo loo Gliricidia hi ejaakɛ amɛdaraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni kɛlɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii babaoo kɛjɛ kookoo shishifãi lɛ amli. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei ni gbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo tsei niji ni tsii ni baanyɛ akumɔ kookoo tso lɛ he.

english: How do I know if a dangerous disease like Swollen Shoot has entered my cocoa farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji helai ni yɔɔ oshara tamɔ ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ ebote mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Look out for leaves with red veins or yellow patterns, swollen stems or roots, and small or deformed cocoa pods. If trees start shedding leaves and dying from the top down, leaving empty patches in your farm, it is a strong sign of Swollen Shoot disease.
ga: Taomɔ baai ni yɔɔ fãji tsuji loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi. Tso loo shishifãi ni efuu kɛ kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ ji bibii loo efite. Kɛji tso lɛ bɔi baai lɛ shwiemɔ ni egbo kɛjɛ ŋwɛi kɛtee shishi He ko ni bɛ nɔ ko babaoo eshwɛ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. No ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ efuu.
