english: What causes small, young cocoa pods to turn black and rot right on the tree?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that grows quickly in wet, humid conditions with excessive shade. Keeping the farm clean, pruning extra branches, and letting sunlight into the farm helps keep pods dry and prevents the rot.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji ŋmei ni daa oya yɛ hei ni efɔ kɛ hulutsoo fe nine. Gbɛ ni aaaha ŋmɔ lɛ mli atse lɛ Nibii krokomɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli Ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ kɛboteɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaaa amɛfite.

english: Why do some areas of my cocoa farm suddenly lose all their leaves while nearby trees look green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli hei komɛi efo amɛhe baai fɛɛ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ feɔ eŋɔli lɛ?

english: Diseases often attack trees in clusters and spread through insects like mealybugs or through touching roots. As the infected trees die off, they create gaps in the farm's canopy where trees stripped of their leaves can no longer grow properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela nɛɛ tutuaa tsei ni efee kui ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ mealybugs loo kɛtsɔ shishifãi ni akɛkpeɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ gboi Amɛfeɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Tsei ni bɛ baai lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ dɔŋŋ.

english: Why does the government extension team insist on cutting down sick cocoa trees instead of spraying them with medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nɔyeli kui ni tsiɔ nibii anaa lɛ maa nɔ mi akɛ esa akɛ afolɔ kookoo tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaawo amɛ tsofa lɛ?

english: Viruses like Cocoa Swollen Shoot live deep inside the plant's sap where chemical sprays cannot reach. Cutting down the infected tree and its immediate neighbors is the only proven way to stop the virus from spreading to the rest of your farm.
ga: Virus tamɔ Cocoa Swollen Shoot hiɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. ni tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ kɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ pɛ ji gbɛ ni ana he odaseyeli ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hela lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa hei krokomɛi. ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ

english: How do government spraying programs help protect my cocoa trees from pests?
ga: Te nɔyeli lɛ gbɛjianɔtoo ko ni akɛshwieɔ tsofa nɔ lɛ baanyɛ abu mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Government mass spraying programs help treat large areas at the same time to kill pests like capsids and control fungal diseases. Treating entire communities together prevents pests from flying from an untreated neighbor's farm onto your crop.
ga: Nɔyeli lɛ gbɛjianɔtoo ni akɛshwieɔ tsofai babaoo nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsaa hei wuji yɛ be kome mli koni egbe tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ capsids ni ekɛkudɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli lɛ. Akutso muu lɛ fɛɛ ni ooofee ekome kɛtsu nii lɛ baatsi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkajɛ okutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ ni atsako lɛ mli kɛba oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ.

english: Can I plant new cocoa seedlings right away in a spot where a diseased cocoa tree was cut down?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu kookoo dumɔwui heei yɛ he ni afo kookoo tso ni hela emɔ lɛ yɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: It is best to wait a few months after removing all infected roots and stumps. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains first prepares the soil and creates a safe, shaded environment before introducing fresh cocoa seedlings.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi beni ojie shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii fɛɛ ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ sɛɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ saa shikpɔŋ lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ni ehaa shihilɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli baa. Dani abaadu kookoo dumɔwui heei

english: How often should I walk through my farm to inspect my cocoa trees?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mayakwɛ kookoo tsei lɛ?

english: You should inspect your farm at least once a week. Regular inspections help you catch early signs of diseases, pest infestations, or fallen shade branches before the problem spreads across your entire farm.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, esa akɛ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli shikome yɛ otsi mli. Kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ona hela, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, loo tsei niji ni egbee shi lɛ ahe okadi mra dani naagba lɛ agbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do tall weeds around my cocoa trunks make my trees produce fewer pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kakadaji babaoo ebɔle he lɛ? Cocoa tsei lɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ.

english: Tall weeds steal water and nutrients from the soil that your cocoa trees need to produce pods. They also trap excess moisture around the base of the trunk, creating an environment where fungal diseases thrive.
ga: Jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni he hiaa cacao tso lɛ koni ekɛfee eshishifãi lɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ hu shwieɔ tso lɛ shishi, ni ehaa shihilɛ ko ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ aya hiɛ yɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Look closely at the small nodes or buds on the stem where new growth will happen. Make sure these buds are pointing upward toward the sky before pushing the stem into the ground, otherwise the plant will struggle to grow.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni ŋmeii heei baakwɛ̃ yɛ lɛ. Kwɛmɔ akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ miitsɔɔ ŋwɛi dani okɛ tso lɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ. Kɛ jeee nakai lɛ, tso lɛ baaná naagba akɛ ebaada.

english: Why do we need to build high soil mounds to plant yams instead of planting them on flat land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni wɔma gɔji ni kwɔlɔ koni wɔkɛdu sweet potatoes yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni wɔbaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Mounds loosen the soil, making it easy for yam tubers to grow big and long underground without fighting hard dirt, while also protecting the seed yam from rotting in waterlogged soil.
ga: Gɔji lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛdara yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛkɛ muji ni mli wa lɛ akpee. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ ahe koni amɛkafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, which is a vital nutrient they need to grow, or that too much water is sitting around their roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara loo nu babaoo ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings die when they get full sunlight all day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tsei lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ hulu lɛ ye amɛnɔ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that dry out easily under harsh, direct sun. They need shade from taller plants like plantains or shade trees to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. koni ehi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the heat becomes too intense, when the soil dries out completely, or when bad weather stops insects from pollinating the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji la lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa Aloo be mli ni kɔɔyɔŋ fɔŋ tsiɔ kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves and sucking away the plant's juices.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ pepper tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ.

english: Why do extra shoots keep growing at the base of my plantain tree, and should I remove them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi yaa nɔ amɛdaraa lɛ? Yɛ mi plantain lɛ shishi Ni ani esa akɛ majie kɛjɛ mli?

english: These extra shoots are called suckers, and they steal water and nutrients from the main tree. Removing most of them helps the main tree produce larger, healthier plantain bunches.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi nɛɛ akɛ suckers ni amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso wulu lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie emli babaoo lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso titri lɛ ni ewo plantain tsei wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops produce much smaller fruits and smaller cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii bibii kwraa kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and nutrients in the soil, effectively starving your plants before they can produce full-sized crops.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye otsei lɛ dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains the soil of specific nutrients maize needs and allows pests and diseases that attack maize to build up in the soil.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baaná niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ kɛjɛ abɛi lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas help make my soil better for other crops later?
ga: Te ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehi aha tsei krokomɛi yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that naturally pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, leaving behind richer soil for the next crop you plant.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛjieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Shi shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ adumɔ.

english: Why do the seeds I get from the agricultural officers yield more corn than the seeds I save from my own harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni minine shɛɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ okwaayeli he onukpai adɛŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa babaoo fe dumɔwui ni mibuaa naa kɛjɛɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds provided by agricultural authorities are specially bred and processed for high performance, resisting common diseases and producing larger ears of corn compared to traditional saved seeds that lose their vigor over time.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni okwaayeli nitsumɔhei kɛhaa lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ ni atsuɔ he nii koni ená hewalɛ babaoo. Enyɛɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ naa lɛ anaa ni ehaa ŋmãa toi wuji kɛ akɛto blema dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ahe, ni hewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Is it safe for me to stop using my traditional local seeds and switch completely to new seed varieties?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ makpa akutseiaŋ dumɔwui ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni matsake kɛya henɔi heei anɔ kwraa?

english: Yes, switching to certified varieties recommended by agricultural officers is safe and beneficial because these seeds have been thoroughly tested to ensure higher yields and better consistency in local conditions.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsakemɔ kɛmiiya henɔi ni yɔɔ odaseyeli ni okwaayeli he onukpai lɛ jieɔ yi lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, akaa dumɔwui nɛɛ akwɛɔ jogbaŋŋ koni ana akɛ amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli.

english: How do improved corn seeds behave differently in the field compared to traditional seeds?
ga: Te ŋmãa dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ lɛ feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa tɛŋŋ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ kɛ akɛto blema dumɔwui ahe?

english: Improved corn varieties tend to grow more uniformly, reach maturity at the same time, and produce heavier, well-filled cobs, making harvesting predictable and yielding far more produce per acre.
ga: Abɛi henɔi ni atsake amɛ lɛ fɔɔ shweremɔ ni yaa hiɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. shwereɔ yɛ be kome too mli ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni tsii ni eyi obɔ fe ŋmeii lɛ Enɛ haa anáa ŋmaa ni anyɛɔ atsɔɔ hiɛ atsɔɔ mli ni anáa yibii babaoo yɛ acre kome mli.

english: Why do my traditional corn plants yield less even when I give them good care?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi blema ŋmãa tsei lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo eyɛ mli akɛ mikwɛɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ moŋ lɛ?

english: Traditional seeds often lack genetic resistance to modern pests and climate stresses, meaning their natural yield potential is much lower than improved certified seeds, regardless of how well you tend to them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, blema dumɔwui bɛ hewalɛ ni teɔ shi ewoɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he haomɔi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛ adebɔɔ mli yibiiwoo ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo lɛ baa shi kwraa fe dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ. Bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni obaakwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ oha.

english: What benefit do I get by getting my seeds through official agricultural channels instead of saving my own?
ga: Mɛɛ sɛɛnamɔi maná kɛjɛ midumɔwui lɛ ni mikɛbaatsɔ okwaayeli gbɛi ni maŋ lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni bo diɛŋtsɛ obaabua dumɔwui lɛ anaa lɛ

english: Official channels provide certified seeds that have been properly cleaned, treated, and tested using modern machinery, guaranteeing higher germination rates and protection against seed-borne diseases.
ga: Gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajaa dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni akɛ tsɔnei ni yɔɔ ŋmɛnɛ lɛ tsuɔ he nii jogbaŋŋ, atsuɔ he nii ni akaa amɛ akwɛɔ lɛ. Ehaa dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ni etsiɔ helai ni jɛɔ dumɔwui amli baa lɛ anaa.

english: Why do seeds from the agricultural extension office look better and sprout faster than seeds from the open market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni jɛ Agricultural Extension Office lɛ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya fe dumɔwui ni jɛ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds from agricultural authorities undergo strict quality control and mechanical processing to ensure that only the healthiest, fully developed seeds are selected and treated for planting.
ga: Dumɔwui ni jɛ okwaayeli nitsumɔhei lɛ amli lɛ tsɔɔ bɔ ni amɛhi ha lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ, ni akɛ tsɔne tsuɔ nii koni ana akɛ ahala dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ pɛ ni atsuɔ he nii koni akɛdu.

english: Why should I spend money to buy new seeds from officers every season instead of using corn left in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafite shika koni mahe dumɔwui heei kɛjɛ nitsulɔi lɛ adɛŋ daa afi lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni okɛ ŋmãa ni eshwɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baatsu nii?

english: Buying fresh certified seed each season is a profitable investment because the high yield and healthy harvest from certified seeds far outweigh the small cost of purchasing them compared to low-yielding barn seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli hemɔ daa be mli lɛ ji shikawoo ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, yibiiwoo ni fa kɛ ŋmaa ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni jɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli mli lɛ feɔ shika fioo ni akɛheɔ kɛ akɛto ŋmɔ mli dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii fioo lɛ ahe.

english: Do improved corn seeds require special machinery or modern tools to grow properly?
ga: Ani ŋmãa dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ biɔ tsɔnei krɛdɛɛi loo ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ nibii koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: While improved seeds can be planted manually, using modern equipment for land preparation and sowing helps them establish deep roots and achieve the highest possible yield.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ abaanyɛ akwɛ dumɔwui ni atsake lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe moŋ. Shi kɛ akɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ nibii ni akɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ dumɔ nii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛná shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo fe fɛɛ.

english: Why do almost all the seeds given to us by agricultural authorities sprout, while many of my traditional seeds fail to come up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ dumɔwui fɛɛ ni okwaayeli nitsumɔhei kɛhaa wɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni mishishijee dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ babaoo nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Government-supplied seeds go through proper screening and sorting machines that remove damaged or dead seeds, ensuring almost every seed you plant successfully germinates.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ dumɔwui ni nɔyeli lɛ kɛhaa lɛ awo tsɔne ni akɛhalaa dumɔwui lɛ amli ni ajie dumɔwui fɛɛ ni efite loo egbo lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baaha nɔ ni miihe ashɛ dumɔwui fɛɛ ni odu lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I save the corn harvested from my new high-yielding crop to plant again next year?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ ŋmãa ni akpa kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii heei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ afi ni baa lɛ?

english: It is best not to replant harvested grain from improved varieties, as the second-generation crop will lose its high yield behavior and will not perform as well as freshly certified seed.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu dumɔwui ni akpa momo kɛjɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli. Enɛ ji akɛ, tsei ni ji yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ baafite amɛ yibiiwoo ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ he subaŋ lɛ, ni amɛtsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ tamɔ dumɔwui heei ni awo amɛ he odase lɛ.

english: Why do groundnut plants produce flowers above the ground, but the nuts develop underneath the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii woɔ fɔfɔi yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii daa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Once the groundnut flower is pollinated, it grows a long stem called a peg that bends downward and pushes itself into the soil. The nut then grows safely underground where it is protected from sunlight and heat.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ shwie shi lɛ Eyɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ peg ni shwieɔ shi kɛyaa shi ni ekɛ ehe woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ baakwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Abuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ he.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or soybeans make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei loo soybeans ni miduɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and soybeans belong to a crop family that feeds special soil bacteria. These bacteria trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the plant roots, leaving natural fertilizer in the soil for future crops.
ga: Peanuts kɛ soybeans fata tsei aweku ko ni feɔ sũ mli helai krɛdɛɛi lɛ ahe. Muawai nɛɛ mɔɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ tsei shishifãi amli. Kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my soybean plants turning yellow and falling off when the pods are brown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi soybean tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf loss at this stage is a natural behavior showing that the plant is mature. It drops its leaves to focus all remaining moisture and energy on drying the seed pods for harvest.
ga: Baai ni laajeɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli subaŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ edara. Amɛshwieɔ baai lɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama ŋmɔtɔ ni eshwɛ kɛ hewalɛ nɔ yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ agbimɔ mli kɛha kpamɔ.

english: How do I know that my groundnuts are ripe and ready to pull out of the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-peanuts lɛ ekwɛ̃ ni esa akɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: You can dig up a few sample plants and crack open the pods. If the inside wall of the shell has dark brown or black veins and the seeds are full and firmly wrapped in their skins, the crop is ready.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ tsei fioo komɛi ni ji nɔkwɛmɔnii lɛ atsu nii ni ogbele ŋmeii lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mli gbogbo lɛ yɛ ŋshɔŋlooi ni tsuɔ loo ediŋŋ. ni dumɔwui lɛ eyi obɔ ni akɛwo ŋmei mli jogbaŋŋ. Etsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛ.

english: Rolling up leaves is a defense reaction. The plant minimizes the surface area exposed to direct sunlight to conserve internal water when the weather is extremely hot and dry.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji nɔ ko ni akɛbuɔ mɔ he. Tso lɛ haa he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baa shi koni ekɛbu nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ he kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni edɔ waa.

english: Why do my crops look like they are wilting even when the soil has plenty of water from recent rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: When the ground holds too much water for too long, air cannot reach the roots. This causes root distress or decay, which prevents the roots from taking up water to send to the leaves.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ naa amanehulu loo amɛgboiɔ, ni no haaa shishifãi lɛ aŋɔ nu ni amɛkɛyashɛ baai lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my bean plants producing a lot of leafy vines but very few flowers and pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean tso lɛ miiwo wain tsei ni baai babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ? Shi fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ.

english: When soil has excessive nitrogen, the plant puts all its growth energy into making green leaves instead of transitioning into the flowering and pod-forming stages.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛdaraa lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli. Mohu ɔ, e tsakeɔ kɛ yaa fɔfɔi kɛ pod peemi be ɔ mi.

english: This yellowing behavior happens when the crop lacks nitrogen. The plant moves nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to feed the younger leaves at the top.
ga: Nɛkɛ subaŋ ni ji ŋmɔŋ nɛɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai bibii lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my mature cassava roots start to rot if I leave them in the wet ground during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni eda lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ he ko ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots are living plant organs that need soil air to remain healthy. Waterlogged soil cuts off oxygen, causing the starch inside the mature roots to spoil and rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ji gbɔmɔtso mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni he hiaa kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishifãi ni eda lɛ amli lɛ fiteɔ ni efiteɔ.

english: Why do groundnuts turn moldy quickly if I harvest them when the air is damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛji mikpa amɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested groundnuts have high moisture levels. If they cannot dry quickly under clear sun, fungus grows on the shell and seeds, producing harmful poisons that make them unsafe to eat.
ga: Peanuts ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo. Kɛji enyɛɛɛ egbi oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ yibii kɛ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ. Ekɛ tsofai fɔji ni yɔɔ oshara ni haaa efee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe akɛ ayeɔ lɛ baa.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually show that the soil has run out of nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to stay green. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps keep the leaves green so the corn ears can grow full.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli lɛ efo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi eŋɔli bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atoi lɛ anyɛ adara.

english: Why does my land produce smaller yields every time I plant on the same plot without letting it rest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo be fɛɛ be ni madu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni mihaaa ejɔɔ ehe lɛ?

english: Soil is like a food store; every crop you harvest takes nutrients out of the ground. If you plant year after year without adding manure or leaving the land to rest, the soil becomes hungry and exhausted, causing crop yields to drop.
ga: Shikpɔŋ tamɔ niyenii atoohe. Nibii fɛɛ ni okpaa lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji odu nii afi fɛɛ afi ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli loo ohaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe lɛ, Hɔmɔ baaye shikpɔŋ lɛ ni egbɔjɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni baa shi.

english: How do crops like cowpea or groundnuts make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii aha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha mi ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have friendly bacteria in their roots that take nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil. When the plants die, that trapped nitrogen stays in the earth to feed whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ naanyobɔɔ mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Eheɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ tsei gboi lɛ, nitrogen ni emɔ mli lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: Young cocoa plants have weak root systems and soft leaves that lose water very fast in harsh dry winds. Planting shade crops like plantains near them and covering the soil around their roots with dry leaves keeps them cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ baai bibii, ni nu fiteɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni mli egbi lɛ mli. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ Ni akɛ baai ni egbi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ.

english: Why do I need to clear tall bushes and tie my yam vines onto wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo jwɛi kakadaji ni mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei akpɛtɛ tsei ahe lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make energy that builds big tubers underground. Lifting the vines up on stakes helps the leaves catch maximum sunlight and prevents them from rotting on the damp ground.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi tsɔnei wuji baa lɛ aba. Wein tsei lɛ ni awoɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni aaanyɛ. ni ehaaa efite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ.

english: When too many suckers grow around one plantain stem, they all fight for the same water and soil food. Leaving only one or two strong suckers allows the main tree to focus its energy on producing a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ ehe Plantain kome Amɛyeɔ akaŋ kɛhaa nu kɛ shikpɔŋ niyenii hu. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ ajwɛŋmɔ ama tso agbo ni tsii ni eeefee lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the soil when we get too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ wɔná nugbɔ babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air pockets in the dirt to stay alive. When heavy rain leaves standing water on the field for too long, the roots suffocate and drown, allowing fungi to enter and rot the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu lɛ hiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Shishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛbaagboi yɛ nu mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ boteɔ mli ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: When weather temperatures get extremely high or soil moisture bounces between too dry and too wet, tomato plants get stressed. The heat damages the pollen inside the blossoms, causing the flowers to drop off before forming tomatoes.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi tsɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni edɔ tsɔ teŋ. Tomato tsei lɛ baaná haomɔ. Dɔlɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ tomatoi.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites that hide under the leaves and suck out the plant's juice, or from sicknesses carried by these pests. Spraying with neem water or proper insecticides stops these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛmuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ kɛ baa lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛbaa lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ neem nu loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi nɛɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi kooloi nɛɛ akpa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slowly and look weak even when rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ daa blɛoo ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive competitors that drink up the water and eat up the soil nutrients meant for your crops. Removing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food, water, and sunlight they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi ji akaŋshilɔi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni baanu nu ni amɛye niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ mli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants wither and die when exposed to strong sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and sensitive roots that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains beside them creates a cool canopy that protects the cocoa trees while they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ lateral plantains lɛ adumɔ Ehaa shade ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ kookoo tso lɛ he beni edara lɛ baa.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting my crops during the rainy season in Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli yɛ Ghana?

english: It is best to wait until the rainfall becomes steady for at least two to three consecutive weeks. Planting too early after a single rain can cause seeds to rot or dry out if a dry spell follows.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi kɛ hoo lɛ, nugbɔ nɛɔ daa otsii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu mra tsɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome sɛɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ agbo loo amɛgbi kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛ sɛɛ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant growth. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer will help restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ, ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Is it safe for me to grow cassava and maize together on the same land?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ abaadu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, growing cassava and maize together works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested early, leaving space and sunlight for the slow-growing cassava to mature later.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni akpaa lɛ mra. Shi he ko kɛ hulu la koni ŋmei ni daa blɛoo lɛ akwɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: What is causing small holes in the leaves of my vegetables and how can I stop it?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ aduawai ahe baai amli lɛ baa ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa amɛ?

english: Small holes in leaves are typically caused by insect pests like caterpillars or beetles feeding on your crop. Spraying a mixture of organic neem leaf solution or safe recommended pesticides can repel these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ neem baa mli nu ni akɛfutu mli loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he lɛ shwie nɔ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshwie kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Cassava root rot usually happens when water sits in heavy soil without proper drainage. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away and keeps the roots healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji nu ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ adu yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ewajeɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce small bunches of fruit instead of big ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii bibii lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ebaajɛ mli aba lɛ?

english: Small plantain bunches often result from nutrient-poor soil or having too many stems growing from one plant. Cutting away extra suckers and keeping only two or three strong stems per mat allows the plant to send more energy into making bigger fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantains bibii jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ bɛ mli loo tso kome mli tsei babaoo tsɔ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ amli ni akɛ tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahi shi yɛ mat kome nɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ aduawai wuji.

english: Should I save seeds from my previous harvest to plant, or buy fresh certified seeds?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ kpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu loo mahe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli?

english: While saving seeds is cheaper, certified seeds from local agricultural dealers yield more, grow stronger roots, and resist local diseases better than seeds saved over multiple seasons.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ dumɔwui ni abua naa lɛ jara waaa moŋ, Shi dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ maŋ lɛ mli okwaayeli jarayelɔi adɛŋ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo. Eyɛ shishifãi ni mli wa fe no. ni amɛnyɛɔ amɛshiɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ anaa fe dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ be babaoo lɛ.

english: How can I keep my vegetable farm moist during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu ahi shi yɛ harmattan be ni nu lɛ mli egbi lɛ mli?

english: Covering the soil around your crops with dried grass or leaves (mulching) slows down water evaporation and keeps the soil cool and moist for longer periods.
ga: Mulching around Kɛ okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ha oŋmɔshi nibii ahe (mulching) lɛ baaye abua ni nu lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ be kakadaŋŋ

english: Why do weeds grow faster and stronger than my main crops on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya ni amɛhe wa fe miŋmɔshi nibii titrii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to quickly soak up water, sunlight, and soil nutrients faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds early in the growing season prevents them from stealing food from your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛgbala nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow mainly when the soil lacks nitrogen or when excessive rain floods the field and starves the roots of air. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ babaoo kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ babaoo ni eha ŋmɔji lɛ eyi obɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa shishifãi lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do experienced farmers recommend planting groundnuts or beans together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ adu ŋmãa loo ŋmãa?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and beans gather natural nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. This acts as a natural fertilizer that nourishes the nearby maize crop and improves the soil for future seasons.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Buaa adebɔɔ mli nitrogen naa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ hewalɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Why does my cassava crop lose almost all its leaves during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is cassava's natural defense mechanism to save water during hot, dry weather. The stem and underground roots remain alive, and fresh leaves will quickly sprout once the rains return.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ kɛha ŋmei koni ekɛbu nu he yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ, ni egbi lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ shishi tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo. Ni baai heei baakwɛ̃ oya kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when there is a lack of water. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering and light shading during extreme heat helps save the blossoms.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni nu efo mli lɛ Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do I need to tie my yam vines onto tall wooden sticks instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei fĩɔ tsei kakadaji ahe lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking yam vines lifts the leaves into the sunlight so the plant can make maximum food. When yam leaves get plenty of direct light, the plant directs that energy underground to grow big, heavy tubers.
ga: Staking sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu la nɔ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ awo niyenii babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Kɛji akɛ sweet potato baai lɛ shɛ la tɛ̃ɛ he lɛ Tsei kudɔɔ nakai hewalɛ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni ekɛfee bulbs agboi ni tsii.

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, steal water and nutrients from the main stem. Removing all but one or two strong shoots ensures the main plantain tree gets enough nourishment to produce a large, heavy bunch of fruit.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei loo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, no haa ŋmeii titri lɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo yibii wuji ni tsii.

english: Does it make a difference which direction I point a cassava stem when planting it in the soil?
ga: Beni aduɔ ŋmei yɛ mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ? Ani srɔtofeemɔ ko yɛ mli?

english: Yes, the small growth buds on the stem must point upward toward the sky. If you plant the stem upside down, the shoots struggle to grow upward, which weakens the plant and leads to poor root production.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji odu tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaawa akɛ tso lɛ baakwɛ̃. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaaa shishifãi lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the small green pods on my cocoa tree turning black and drying up during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is black pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, wet conditions. Clearing weeds and pruning dense overhead shade branches allows sunlight and airflow to dry out the trees and prevent the disease.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni efɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Tsei ni eyi obɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni yɔɔ amɛyiteŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛ amɛhe ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli koni tsei lɛ agbi ni helai akamɔ amɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids that attack young leaves. Controlling these insects early with neem oil spray or recommended treatments helps the leaves expand properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni tutuaa baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ mra Kɛ akɛ neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo tsofa kroko ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baa lɛ mli alɛɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell when a pod on my cocoa tree is mature enough to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa?

english: Ripe cocoa pods clearly change color. Unripe green pods turn bright yellow when ready, while reddish or purple pods change to an orange or yellow-orange color, indicating the beans inside are fully developed.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su yɛ faŋŋ mli. Pods eŋɔlii ni eshɛko lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛji amɛfee klalo. yɛ be mli ni pods tsuru loo purple tsakeɔ kɛfeɔ akutu loo ŋmɔŋ-akutu. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa.

english: Why is it bad if I harvest foliage or fruits from my trees before they fully mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji mikpa tso ko baai loo aduawai dani eda kwraa lɛ?

english: Harvesting too early strips the plant of the energy it needs to build strong roots and branches, which reduces the overall yield and lifespan of the crop.
ga: Kɛ́ akpa tso lɛ mra tsɔ lɛ, ehaaa tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni eshishifãi kɛ eniji ni wa akwɛ̃. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni anáa kɛ wala be ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my cassava plants need fertilizer even if their leaves look green and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ?

english: Green leaves mean the plant is growing above ground, but fertilizer provides specific nutrients like potassium that encourage energy to move downward into developing thick, heavy tubers.
ga: Baai eŋɔli tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miida yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii haa niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ potassium, ni woɔ hewalɛ hewalɛ koni eya shi kɛyashɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa ni tsii lɛ ahe.

english: Heavy rains flood the soil and push out oxygen, which suffocates the roots and stops them from taking up nitrogen, causing the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ ni ekɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ jeɔ kpo. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa amɛŋɔ nitrogen. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why should I plant plantain next to my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantain yɛ mi-kooko dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily in direct sunlight, so fast-growing plantains provide essential temporary shade and keep the soil moist while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni shwereɔ oya lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa yɛ be kukuoo mli, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Staking lifts the leaves into the sunlight and away from damp soil diseases, allowing the plant to capture more energy and produce much larger tubers.
ga: Staking baaha baai lɛ ashɛ hulu la he ni helai akashɛ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ emɔɔ hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛ bulbs ni da fe tsutsu lɛ baa.

english: Why do I need to cut off some of the lower leaves and stems from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe baai kɛ amɛshishigbɛ fãi lɛ ekomɛi?

english: Pruning removes unnecessary foliage so the plant can direct its water and nutrients straight into growing bigger, healthier tomatoes instead of extra leaves.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ewoɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli koni ekwɛ tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ moŋ fe ni ekɛ baai krokomɛi baatsu nii.

english: Why do weeds lower my harvest even if I apply fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that steal water and fertilizer faster than your crops can absorb them, effectively starving your crop.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe bɔ ni otsei lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ onibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites that drain the plant's nourishment; applying neem oil or appropriate sprays stops them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ mli niyenii mli hewalɛi lɛ hoɔ Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo spray ni sa wo mli lɛ, ebaakpa enɛ.

english: Extreme heat or dry soil causes stress that makes the plant drop its blossoms to save water, which can be prevented by mulching to retain soil moisture.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ kɛ haomɔ ni haa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi baa koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Abaanyɛ atsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ sũ ni akɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli koni sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the seeds I saved from last year's maize yield smaller ears this year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mijie kɛjɛ nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ bafee bibioo afi nɛɛ?

english: Saved seeds from hybrid crops lose their high-yielding strength in the next generation, so buying fresh certified seeds ensures strong, uniform yields every season.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ ahemɔ baaha yibiiwoo ni mli wa ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ aba daa be mli.

english: Why do weeds keep coming back on my farm even after I spray chemical weed killers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ yaa nɔ amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi moŋ.

english: Weeds often grow back quickly if the spray only kills the leaves above ground while leaving the roots alive, or if weed seeds buried in the soil germinate after rain. Using a systemic herbicide that penetrates down to the roots and combining spraying with manual clearing gives longer-lasting control.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ fɔɔ daa oya kɛji akɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ gbe baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ pɛ yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi lɛ. Aloo kɛji akɛ jwɛi dumɔwui ni afu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Kɛ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni boteɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ tsu nii ni akɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ kɛ nine ni akɛjieɔ jwɛi lɛ fata he lɛ, ehaa nɔyeli lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do insects return to attack my crops just a few days after I spray them with pesticides?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ ku amɛsɛɛ amɛbatutua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ wo mihe lɛ?

english: Insects return quickly if the spray did not destroy their eggs hidden under leaves, or if the pests have built up resistance to the same chemical being used repeatedly. Rotating different types of sprays and applying them at the right growth stage destroys the entire insect life cycle.
ga: Kplukai lɛ baaku amɛsɛɛ oya kɛji akɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ efiteee ŋmeii ni akɛtee baai lɛ ashishi lɛ. aloo kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ tswa tsofa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii shii abɔ lɛ he hewalɛ. Spray rotation henɔi srɔtoi ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ dalɛ be ni sa mli lɛ baafite kooloi ashihilɛ fɛɛ.

english: How can I tell whether my crop leaves are being eaten by pests or damaged by a plant disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai eye mitso lɛ baai lɛ?

english: Pests usually leave physical signs like ragged holes, bitten edges, or visible insects on the leaves. Plant diseases, on the other hand, usually appear as discolored yellow spots, powdery patches, or soft rots without any visible bugs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ shĩɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii, tamɔ bu ni etse, ŋmeii ni emɔ, loo kooloi bibii ni anaa yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, tsei ahe helai jeɔ kpo akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni etsake su, ŋmɔtɔ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ, loo ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni kooloi bibii ni anaaa bɛ mli.

english: How do I choose the correct spray product to protect my crops from damage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala tsofa ni sa ni akɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ koni ekafite?

english: Different crop problems require specific solutions: insecticides kill bugs, fungicides stop fungal rot, and herbicides kill weeds. Identifying the exact problem on your leaves with an extension officer ensures you buy the correct treatment instead of wasting money on the wrong product.
ga: Naagbai srɔtoi ni kɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ biɔ tsabaa pɔtɛɛ, tamɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi. Tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ. kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi gbeɔ jwɛi Saji pɔtɛɛ ni kɔɔ ogbɛfaa kɛ o-extension agent lɛ he lɛ ni oooyɔse lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni ohe tsofa ni sa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite shika yɛ nibii ni ejaaa lɛ ahe lɛ

english: Can applying too much pesticide or chemical spray harm my crops instead of helping them?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui moŋ fe ni eeeye ebua amɛ?

english: Yes, using too much chemical or mixing a spray too strong can burn leaves, stunt plant growth, and ruin the soil. Always follow recommended mixing ratios carefully so the chemical protects the crop without damaging it.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo tsofa ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni mli wa tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ ashã. ehaa tsei lɛ adalɛ baa shi ni ebaanyɛ efite shikpɔŋ lɛ Nyiɛmɔ bɔ ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ jogbaŋŋ be fɛɛ be. Bɔni afee ni tsofai lɛ abu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe ni efiteee amɛ.

english: What is the best time of day for me to spray chemical products on my crop field?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai afɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: The best time to spray is early in the morning or late in the afternoon when temperatures are cool and the wind is calm. Spraying during hot sunlight causes the chemical liquid to evaporate into the air before it can work on the plants.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔse tsofa lɛ ji leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli. Enɛ ji be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hu efee kpoo. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa lɛ shwie hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa tsofa lɛ mli nu lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani abaanyɛ akɛwo tsei anɔ.

english: Will heavy rain wash away the medicine I just sprayed on my crops?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baatsumɔ tsofa ni mikɛshwie miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ amrɔ nɛɛ?

english: Yes, if rain falls shortly after spraying, it washes the product off the leaves before the plant or pest can absorb it. Try to spray when no rain is expected for at least 4 to 6 hours so the chemical has enough time to take effect.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji nugbɔ nɛ beni afɔ lɛ nɔ etsɛɛɛ lɛ No sɛɛ lɛ, nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ shwieɔ nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ahe yɛ baai lɛ anɔ dani tsei loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Bɔɔmɔdɛŋ ni okɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ nɔ be mli ni akpaaa gbɛ akɛ nugbɔ baanɛ kɛ hoo lɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 4 kɛyashi 6 koni eha tsofai lɛ be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛtsu nii.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that crops lack essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or that the soil is holding too much water around the roots. Adding proper fertilizer or improving soil drainage helps bring back the healthy green color.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo yɛ eshishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo mli loo aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ekwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do some plants on my farm stay very short while others right next to them grow tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi hiɔ shi be kukuoo yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi ni yɔɔ amɛmasɛi lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Uneven growth happens when soil nutrients, water, or sunlight are not spread equally across the field, or when hidden soil pests attack the roots of specific plants. Testing and preparing your soil evenly across the field promotes uniform growth.
ga: Dalɛ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee lɛ baa kɛji akɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, loo hulu la mli lɛ ejaaa ŋmɔ mli pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli. aloo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ tutua tsei komɛi ashishifãi lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni akaa ni asaa he pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ baaye abua ni eha shweremɔ po aya hiɛ.

english: Why are my crops producing flowers but dropping them before any fruit or pods develop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi shi egbeeɔ shi dani aduawai loo ŋmeii baa lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off prematurely when plants suffer from water stress during dry spells, lack essential nutrients needed for fruiting, or when insects damage the delicate parts of the flower. Keeping soil moist and managing pests during flowering ensures good fruit set.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli. Niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha yibiiwoo loo be mli ni kooloi bibii fiteɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni bɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ fɔfɔii akwɛmɔ be mli lɛ haa aduawai kpakpai baa.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to grow strong and green. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or compost will help the leaves turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni etsɔ hewalɛ ni efee ŋmɔŋ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I turn my extra maize into Tom Brown cereal so it doesn't spoil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsɔ ŋmãa ni fa lɛ matsɔ Tom Brown ŋmãa koni ekafee yaka?

english: To make Tom Brown, clean and roast dried maize together with soybeans or groundnuts, then mill them into fine flour. Roasting removes moisture, allowing the flour to stay fresh for months so you can sell it for a higher price.
ga: Kɛji ooofee Tom Brown lɛ, ŋmãa ni ashã ni he tse ni egbi kɛfata soybeans loo ŋmãa he. No sɛɛ lɛ, shwie nɔ ni etsɔ powda kpakpa. Ashãa yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ hiɔ shi nyɔji babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ lɛ yɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ.

english: Why are some of my maize cobs half-empty with missing kernels?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii lɛ ekomɛi amli fã efee efolo ni amɛmli ŋmeii lɛ bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Half-empty cobs happen when hot, dry weather damages the silks during flowering, preventing proper pollination. Giving maize enough water when the cobs start forming helps ensure full rows of grain.
ga: Cobs ni fã efee efolo lɛ baa kɛji shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ fite siliki lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi be mli. Enɛ haaa amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee pollination jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ afɔ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ nu bɔ ni sa beni ŋmãa lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa yiɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli.

english: Tomatoes rot quickly because they contain lots of water and naturally release a gas that makes them over-ripen fast. Keeping them in a cool, shaded place or processing excess harvest into tomato paste prevents them from rotting.
ga: Tomato fiteɔ oya ejaakɛ nu babaoo yɛ mli ni ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa tomato shwereɔ oya tsɔ lɛ kpo. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ wo he ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli loo okɛ nɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ tsu nii ni okɛfee tomato puree lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets extremely hot or when the plant experiences drought. The plant drops its flowers to save water and protect itself from stress.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na hɔmɔ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ haomɔi ahe.

english: Why do the skins of my tomatoes crack open while they are still on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato hewoloi lɛ mli gbalaa be mli ni miyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Tomato skins split when there is a sudden influx of water—like heavy rain after a dry period. The inside of the tomato expands faster than the skin can stretch, causing it to crack.
ga: Tomato hewoloi lɛ tswaa kɛji nu ko ba trukaa, tamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ. Tomato lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. kɛ mligbalamɔ baa

english: Why does rice need so much water in the field compared to my maize crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu babaoo he hiaa ŋmãa yɛ miŋmɔ mli kɛ akɛto miŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Rice plants naturally adapted to thrive in flooded soil, which helps block weeds and keeps nutrients available, whereas maize roots will rot if left standing in water for too long.
ga: Omɔ tsei lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni etsĩɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa ni ehaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ hiɔ shi. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ baafite kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: Why does my stored rice smell bad and turn moldy inside the sack?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ he ŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ kotokui lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Rice turns moldy if it is bagged before it is completely dry. Moisture trapped inside the bag causes mold to grow, so you must sun-dry the rice grains until they are hard before storing them.
ga: Omɔ baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛji akɛ awo kotoku mli dani egbi kwraa. Moisture trapped inside the bag causes mold. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ogbi ŋmãa lɛ mli kɛyashi ebaawa dani okɛto.

english: Is it better to sell my raw crops right after harvest or process them into new food products?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mahɔ̃ɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛkpaa lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ loo mafee amɛ niyenii heei?

english: Processing raw crops like maize into Tom Brown or tomatoes into paste extends their shelf life and protects you from low market prices during harvest time, allowing you to earn more profit.
ga: Nibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ tamɔ ŋmãa ni afee lɛ Tom Brown loo tomato puree lɛ haa amɛshihilɛ yaa hiɛ ni ebuɔ ohe kɛjɛɔ jara ni baa shi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be mli lɛ he. Help you earn more profits.

english: Why does planting maize in the same field every year give me a smaller yield each time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ woɔ yibii fioo be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Maize eats up specific soil nutrients very quickly. Planting it on the same spot every season drains the soil, so alternating with crops like cowpeas or groundnuts returns natural strength to your farm.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ oya. Kɛ́ adu nii yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa be lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu atsɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmei tsake ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha oŋmɔ lɛ mli adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains on the same land where I just planted my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni midu kookoo tsei bibii amrɔ nɛɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because direct, strong sunlight can burn their leaves and kill them. Plantain trees grow very fast and produce large leaves that protect the young cocoa from harsh sun while keeping the soil moist during their early years.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã ni egbe baai lɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do I have to put tall wooden sticks in the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsei lɛ awo ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ nɛkɛ? Okɛwo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high off the ground to catch enough sunlight to make food. Staking keeps the leaves off damp soil where they might rot and helps the leaves capture maximum light, which results in larger yam tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya shɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha nihoomɔ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akabote shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ yɛ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi yɛ lɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ la babaoo Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ wuji.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to build healthy green leaves. Applying fertilizer or well-rotted manure restores nitrogen and turns the leaves green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: How does planting beans or groundnuts in my field help make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts naturally capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When you plant maize on that land in the next season, the maize feeds on that leftover nitrogen to grow strong without requiring as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji odu ŋmãa yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ ŋmãa baaye nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ waa ni tsofai babaoo he ehiaaa.

english: Cassava is usually ready 9 to 12 months after planting. You will see the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem will begin to crack open as the tubers swell underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu. Obaakwɛ akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ baabɔi fãmɔ be mli ni tuber lɛ mli fũuɔ lɛ.

english: What is making the leaves of my pepper plants curl up tightly and stop growing properly?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are typically caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids. Controlling these insects early with proper sprays prevents them from spreading viruses that stunt the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛji akɛ afɔse amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, abaanyɛ atsĩ amɛnaa koni amɛkagbɛ helai ni tsiɔ tsei anaa lɛ agbɛfaŋ.

english: What are the small caterpillars eating holes in the middle of my maize leaves, and why are they dangerous?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ bu yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ? Ni mɛni hewɔ eyɛ oshara lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, which attack the central growing tip of the maize plant. If they destroy this central area, the plant cannot develop healthy ears of corn, leading to massive yield losses.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni tutuaa ŋmei tsei ni daraa yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ashishifãi lɛ. Kɛji akɛ akpata nɛkɛ he ni mɛi fɛɛ yɔɔ nɛɛ hiɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ afee ŋmãa toi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii babaoo ni afeɔ lɛ ni laajeɔ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the weather gets too hot or when the plant does not get consistent water. Keeping the soil evenly moist and planting at the right time helps flowers stay attached and form fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ nu daa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ dumɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil food directly from your crops. When weeds grow close to your plants, your crops become weak and hungry, producing smaller yields.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ jwɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ otsei lɛ ahe lɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni hɔmɔ baaye bo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ fioo.

english: If seeds are buried too deep, they run out of stored food energy before their sprouts reach the surface, causing them to die underground or emerge very weak.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afu dumɔwui lɛ amli tsɔ Niyenii hewalɛ ni ato lɛ baaho dani dumɔwui lɛ baaje kpo. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi loo amɛgbɔjɔɔ waa.

english: If I do not have an irrigation system on my farm, how can I make sure my crops still get enough water?
ga: Kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ bɛ nu shwiemɔ gbɛjianɔtoo Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nu ni fa lolo?

english: You can plan your planting calendar around the natural rainy season so that the heaviest rains fall right when your crops need water the most.
ga: Obaanyɛ oto oŋmɔshi nibii ahe kalanda lɛ he gbɛjianɔ yɛ adebɔɔ mli nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli bɔni afee ni nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa fe fɛɛ lɛ aba yɛ be mli ni nu he hiaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Is it possible to get a very good yield without buying expensive watering equipment for my crops?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ maná yibii kpakpai waa ni aheee nu ni jara wa kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yes, rain-fed farming can produce great yields if you align your planting dates so that natural rainfall meets the crop's peak water demand.
ga: Hɛɛ, okwaayeli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha yibii kpakpai aba kɛji oto gbii ni okɛbaadu nii lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ bɔni afee ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ kɛ nu ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɔɔ lɛ akpã gbee.

english: What should I do if I am relying on rainwater and the rains come later than expected?
ga: Kɛ ehe bahia ni okɛ ohe afɔ̃ nugbɔ nu nɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ sɛɛ fe bɔ ni okpaa gbɛ lɛ, mɛni esa akɛ ofee?

english: Delay your planting until the rains actually start so your seeds do not dry up in the soil, ensuring they receive steady water through their early months of growth.
ga: Tsɔ dumɔ lɛ sɛɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaje shishi diɛŋtsɛ. Bɔni afee ni odumɔwui lɛ akagbi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kwɛmɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ aná nu daa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ ni amɛdaraa lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why is getting good rainfall around the third month of planting so important for my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ kpakpa ni nɛɔ yɛ nyɔŋ ni ji 3 ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ mli lɛ he hiaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Around the third month, many crops enter a critical development stage where adequate water is essential to transition from leaf growth to flowering and fruiting.
ga: Aaafee nyɔŋ ni ji etɛ lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo miibote shihilɛi ni he hiaa waa amli. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa he miihia kɛha tsakemɔ ni jɛɔ baa lɛ dalɛ mli kɛyaa fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo mli.

english: What happens to my crops if they face dry weather during their key growth stage?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji amɛna shihilɛi ni mli egbi yɛ amɛdalɛ be ni he hiaa waa lɛ mli?

english: If crops lack water during their critical growth period, their development slows down, leading to stunted plants and lower overall harvest yield.
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu yɛ edalɛ be ni he hiaa waa lɛ mli lɛ, Nɔyaa lɛ baafee mlɛo. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ shwereɔ ni nibii fɛɛ ni afeɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: How do I know when my crops have reached the stage where missing water will harm them the most?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛ he ni nu ni bɛ lɛ baaye lɛ awui fe fɛɛ lɛ?

english: This usually happens when the plant finishes growing leaves and starts developing flowers, pods, or tubers, which is when its demand for water peaks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tso ko baai lɛ fɛɛ kwɛ̃ ni ebɔi fɔfɔi, ŋmeii, loo ŋmeii, ni no ji be mli ni nu he hiaa fe fɛɛ.

english: How do I time my planting so that my crops are ready for market in October and November?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mato be ni mikɛduɔ nii koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee klalo kɛha jara yɛ October kɛ November mli?

english: Check how many months your crop takes to mature, then count backward from October or November to set your planting month at the start of the rainy season.
ga: Kwɛmɔ nyɔji enyiɛ eheɔ dani otso lɛ shwereɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, kanemɔ sɛɛ kɛjɛ October loo November mli koni ona nyɔŋ ni aduɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ mli beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do many farmers in Ghana aim to harvest their crops around October and November?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi babaoo ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ kɛ amɛhiɛ fɔ̃ɔ nɔ akɛ amɛbaakpa amɛnibii yɛ October kɛ November teŋ lɛ?

english: October and November fall at the end of the major rainfall period, offering ideal harvesting conditions and high demand as traders buy produce for the end-of-year season.
ga: October kɛ November baa shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni naa wa lɛ naagbee gbɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmaakpamɔ shihilɛi ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ nibii ni ataoɔ babaoo baa be mli ni jarayelɔi heɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ afi lɛ naagbee lɛ.

english: How does matching my crop's growth period with local rainfall make my farm more profitable?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii adalɛ be kɛ maŋ lɛ mli nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ afee ekome lɛ aha miŋmɔ lɛ aná sɛɛnamɔ babaoo?

english: It reduces water stress on your crops without added irrigation costs, helping you produce high-quality produce right when market prices are favorable.
ga: Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu he haomɔ ni baa onibii anɔ lɛ baa shi ni ekɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ he nyɔmɔwoo eyaaa hiɛ. Ehaa okɛ nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ tsuɔ nii yɛ be mli ni jarayeli jara lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: What does it mean to plan my farming activities so that harvest time becomes 'business time'?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni tsɔɔ akɛ mato mi okwaayeli nitsumɔi lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ koni kpamɔ be lɛ afee ‘jarayeli be’?

english: It means deliberately choosing planting dates so your crops mature during peak market demand when buyers are ready to pay good prices for fresh harvest.
ga: Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ ohala gbi ni okɛbaadu nii yɛ jwɛŋmɔ mli koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ be mli ni jara lɛ taoɔ nii babaoo lɛ. Beni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaawo nyɔmɔ kpakpa kɛha ŋmaa hee ni akpaa lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plant is lacking nitrogen, a vital nutrient it needs to grow strong, or that too much water around the roots is preventing the plant from taking in food from the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kɛha shweremɔ kpakpa loo nu ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Shishifãi babaoo tsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekaná niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my soil become hard and crusty after growing maize on the same plot for a few years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ beni midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli afii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the soil's organic matter and natural nutrients. Adding compost, animal manure, or rotating with beans helps keep the soil soft and rich.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ baaha nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ atsɔ mli be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmeii ni akɛtsakeɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ ni ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry spells to save water. The plant goes into a resting state while keeping its tubers safe and growing under the ground until the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Tsei lɛ baabote shihilɛ ni mli wa mli yɛ be mli ni amɛhaa bulb lɛ hiɔ shi shweshweeshwe ni amɛdaraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Tomatoes shed their flowers when temperatures get too high or when rainfall is unpredictable. When the plant experiences heat stress or drought, it drops flowers to save its energy.
ga: Tomato fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Kɛ tsei kɛ dɔlɛ haomɔ loo hɔmɔ kpe lɛ Fɔfɔi baagbee shi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato.

english: Planting too many seeds in one hole forces the crops to fight each other for water, sunlight, and nutrients, resulting in weak stalks and very small corn cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni aduɔ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ ehe awo nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa baa.

english: Why should I clear weeds from around my young cocoa trees while they are small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Cocoa tsei lɛ darako yɛ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ.

english: Weeds grow faster than young trees and steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Keeping the base of young cocoa clear gives the tree the strength to grow tall quickly.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei bibii ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ oha kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ mli tse lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni ekwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why do nursery farmers cover newly sown pepper seeds with palm fronds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni kwɛɔ tsei anɔ lɛ kɛ ŋmei baa haa ŋmɔtɔ dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Palm fronds protect fragile seeds from scorching sun heat and heavy rain drops, keeping the soil moist so the seeds can sprout safely.
ga: Palm baai buɔ dumɔwui ni waaa lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fũɔ bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do some farmers cut off lower branches from pepper plants after they start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi shwieɔ amɛ pepper tsei lɛ aniji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ beni amɛdu amɛ amɛgbe naa lɛ?

english: Removing lower, unproductive branches helps the plant direct its energy into producing bigger pepper fruits and improves airflow to prevent fungal diseases.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni wooo yibii lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni etsɔɔ ehewalɛ nɔ koni ekɛwo pepper yibii wuji. ni eha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ koni akaye tsɛŋemɔ hela.

english: Excessive rain and high dampness create the perfect condition for black pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads from pod to pod through splashing raindrops.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha black pod hela lɛ baa. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ pod mli kɛyaa pod mli kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know when my yam tubers are mature and ready for harvesting under the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Yams tell you they are ready when their above-ground leaves and vines turn yellow and dry up completely, showing that the plant has finished storing energy in the tuber.
ga: Sweet potato kɛɛ bo akɛ efee klalo beni baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi kwraa lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe hewalɛ ni ekɛtoɔ eyitso lɛ naa.

english: How do I know when it is safe to start planting my seeds when the rains keep changing?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ehi akɛ mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ tsakeɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Relying purely on unpredictable weather can lead to seed loss. Wait until the soil receives consistent rain for a few consecutive days and stays moist at root depth before sowing your seeds.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ he fɔ̃ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni bɛ faŋŋ nɔ pɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ afite. Mɛɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be gbii fioo komɛi ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ, ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli dani odu dumɔwui.

english: Why does rice need so much water to grow compared to maize or cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa biɔ nu babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ kɛ akɛto ŋmãa loo ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Rice plants naturally thrive in shallow water or very wet soil because their roots are adapted to pull nutrients from waterlogged earth, which also prevents weeds from choking the young plants.
ga: Omɔ tsei daa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ nu ni mli ekɔɔɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni efɔ waa nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ etsake amɛhe koni amɛjie niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni jwɛi akatutua tsei bibii lɛ.

english: How can I harvest more bags of rice from my small plot of farm land?
ga: Makpa ŋmãa kotokui babaoo kɛjɛ ŋmɔ bibioo ko mli. Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná minɔ lɛ?

english: You can increase your harvest by using certified high-yield seeds, transplanting seedlings in straight rows with correct spacing, and applying nitrogen fertilizer at the key growth stages.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha onibii lɛ aya hiɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni awoɔ yibii babaoo ni awo he odaseyeli akɛ oootsu nii lɛ nɔ. Tsi dumɔwui lɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja kɛ gbɛ ni sa. ni okɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii yɛ dalɛ bei ni he hiaa lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves mean the plant cannot absorb nutrients properly, which happens if the soil is too dry, too waterlogged, or if the soil is acidic enough to lock nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baaba mli kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ fa tsɔ. aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli eyi kɛ acid bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ ahiɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ mli

english: Why are pests like armyworms attacking my farm more frequently these days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi tamɔ cutworms tutuaa miŋmɔ lɛ shii abɔ yɛ nɛkɛ gbii nɛɛ amli lɛ?

english: Irregular rain and hot weather create ideal conditions for pests to reproduce rapidly, while weakened, thirsty plants have fewer natural defenses to fight off infestation.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa koni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ afɔ oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni kumai yeɔ amɛ lɛ bɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni buɔ amɛhe ni amɛkɛwuɔ amɛshiɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ.

english: Why do my rice plants fall over to the ground just when the heads are becoming heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ beni bulb lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɔjɔɔ lɛ?

english: This is called lodging, which happens when plants get too much nitrogen fertilizer, making them grow too tall and weak to hold up the heavy grain heads when strong wind blows.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ abobaahe. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ shɔŋŋ tsɔ ni amɛhe waaa tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛfi dumɔwui ayitsei ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ miitswa.

english: Which food crops can survive best in my farm if the rains stop early this season?
ga: Mɛɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii baahi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa yɛ be nɛɛ shishijee mli?

english: Crops like cassava, millet, and sorghum handle drought well because they have deep roots or natural water-saving features that keep them alive long after the rain stops.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmei, kɛ ŋmei nyɛɔ amɛkpeɔ hɔmɔ naa jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ amɛyɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo adebɔɔ mli nibii ni haa nu baa shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why does my harvested grain spoil or rot so quickly inside my storehouse?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ miifite loo miifite oya yɛ mitoohe lɛ?

english: Spoilage happens when grain is stored before it is completely dry, because trapped moisture creates a warm environment where mold grows and storage insects quickly multiply.
ga: Nɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji akɛ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ to dani amɛgbi kwraa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu ni mli edɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ lɛ mli dɔɔ. Fuji lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ nitoohe lɛ baafa oya.

english: What is the benefit of buying distributed certified seeds instead of using seeds from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni agbɛ ashwã ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ ahemɔ he yɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mikpamɔ ni mikpa nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ mli lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Certified seeds are specially bred to resist diseases, mature faster, and produce uniform crops, whereas seeds saved year after year lose their vitality and give lower yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai, amɛshwere oya ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa nɔ daa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why does my farm yield fewer crops every year even though I plant the same size of field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi lɛ? Nɔ ni midu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Plants take nutrients out of the earth every season. Without crop rotation, organic manure, or fallow resting periods, the soil becomes exhausted and loses its ability to feed new plants.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ bɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ tsei heei anɔ dɔŋŋ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient plants need to grow green and strong. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or well-rotted animal manure helps restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Amɛji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛ su lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.
