english: Why does my farm soil become hard like dry clay, and how does that affect my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ? Ni te enɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Hard, compacted soil prevents roots from spreading deeply to reach water and nutrients, which stunts plant growth. Adding compost or animal manure softens the soil and helps it hold moisture much better during dry spells.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã shɔŋŋ koni amɛyashɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ahe. ni haa tsei nyɛɛɛ ada Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee blɛoo ni eye ebua lɛ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests to multiply in the ground. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts returns nitrogen to the soil naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Enɛ baaha nitrogen lɛ aku esɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why should I plant my crops in straight rows instead of scattering seeds all over the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting in straight rows gives every crop adequate space, sunlight, and airflow. It also makes weeding, applying fertilizer, and harvesting much easier without stepping on or damaging your plants.
ga: Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa, hulu la, kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsɔɔ mli. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akpamɔ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa ni okɛ ohe wooo otsei lɛ anɔ loo ofiteee amɛ.

english: Why do young cocoa trees wither and die when I clear all the big trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because it burns their delicate leaves and dries out their roots. Leaving taller shade trees or interplanting fast-growing plantain provides the shade they need to survive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Enɛ baashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbi. Kɛ́ amɛshi tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ loo amɛdu plantain ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ amɛhe lɛ, ebaaha amɛná hulutsoo ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: How do I know the right distance to keep between cassava stems when planting?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale gbɛ ni sa ni kã ŋmei tsei ateŋ kɛha dumɔ?

english: Spacing cassava stems about one meter apart ensures the tubers under the ground have enough room to expand into large roots without competing with neighboring plants for water and nutrients.
ga: Kasava tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji aaafee mita kome, ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã kɛyatsɔ shishifãi wuji ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛkɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha nu kɛ niyenii.

english: Why are small green worms eating the leaves and centers of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miiye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai kɛ amɛteŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: These worms are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that destroys maize leaves. Checking your farm early and applying recommended natural sprays like neem leaf extract or approved pesticides can stop them before they cause heavy damage.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ ni fiteɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra Ni okɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa tamɔ neem baa mli nu loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii. Ebaanyɛ ekpa ŋmɔji dani amɛfite nii waa.

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil remains too wet and waterlogged, or when fungal diseases attack underground. Planting on raised soil ridges or mounds helps excess rainwater drain away from the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ baagboi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ lolo ni nu eyi mli obɔ. aloo beni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa lɛ tutuaa shikpɔŋ shishi Dumɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when temperatures become extremely high, when watering is inconsistent, or when there are too few bees for pollination. Consistent watering and light shade during very hot weather reduce flower drop.
ga: Tomatoi baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa. Be mli ni nu ni akɛhaa lɛ bɛ daa Aloo be mli ni ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛfee pollination. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ nɔ daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa shi.

english: How can I tell the right time to plant my seeds when rain patterns keep changing?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ tsakeɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Instead of planting strictly by calendar months, wait until the ground receives two or three consecutive days of deep rainfall so the soil stays moist enough for seeds to germinate safely.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu nii pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ kalanda nyɔŋ lɛ naa lɛ. Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ waa gbii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ ji koni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi fɛ̃i bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil around their shallow roots. Leaving larger trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantain creates a cool canopy that protects the cocoa until it gets older.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni bɔleɔ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ he eko lɛ he lɛ mli gĩɔ. Tsei wuji ni ashiɔ loo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni egbɔ.

english: When lower maize leaves turn yellow in a V-shape, it usually means the plant lacks nitrogen nutrient in the soil. The plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed new growth at the top, which shows you need to add compost or nitrogen fertilizer.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmãa baai lɛ ashishigbɛ fãi lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ, bei pii lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni ji nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛye ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni eda yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii afata he.

english: Why do some of my cassava stem cuttings rot in the soil instead of sprouting leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ekomɛi miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Cassava cuttings rot if they are planted upside down, planted in waterlogged soil, or taken from dry, dead stems. Inserting fresh stems into well-drained soil with the bud nodes pointing upward allows roots and shoots to grow properly.
ga: Kasava niji fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ ŋwɛi. Adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. aloo ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni egboi amli Kɛ́ akɛ tsei heei wo shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ mli ni ŋmeii lɛ kwɛɔ ŋwɛi lɛ, ehaa shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves up to trap sunlight, which the plant uses to manufacture food to build big tubers underground. It also keeps leaves off the damp ground, preventing diseases and pests from attacking the foliage.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛmɔ hulu la, ni tso lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii lɛ, koni ekɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ebaatsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni ekahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Koni helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tutuaa baai lɛ akabote mli.

english: This black spot is called blossom-end rot, caused by a shortage of calcium in the plant, often because the plant is not getting steady water. Watering tomatoes regularly helps them draw up calcium from the soil to form healthy fruits.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ he diŋ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔii anaagbee fitemɔ. ni calcium ni bɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni haa ebaa lɛ ji akɛ, tsei lɛ náaa nu ni yaa nɔ daa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo o-tomato lɛ nɔ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛjieɔ calcium kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛwo yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests when I plant maize on the exact same farm every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize in the same spot continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows corn-eating pests to live in the dirt. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when stressed by extreme heat, hot dry winds, or irregular watering. Providing steady water and light shade during very hot weather helps the plant hold onto flowers so they become peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli bɔni afee ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my sweet potatoes turn out thin and twisted instead of growing big and round?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ mli tsɔi ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekwɛ̃ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Sweet potatoes need loose, soft soil to push outward as they swell into large tubers. Hard or heavily compacted clay soil resists the growing tuber, forcing it to bend and stay thin.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse he miihia sweet potatoes koni ekɛtsi kɛya kponɔgbɛ be mli ni amɛshwereɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo ni mli edɔ waa lɛ baate shi awo tuberous dalɛ. ni nyɛɔ enɔ koni ebɔle ehe ni eha efee mlɛo

english: Why do green caterpillars suddenly show up and eat the central leaves of my young corn right after the rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ baa trukaa ni amɛyeɔ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ beni nugbɔ ebɔi nɛmɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Rainfall and warm weather trigger armyworm moths to lay eggs on fresh green corn leaves. Early checking of leaf centers and applying organic neem oil or safe insecticides stops caterpillars before they destroy the crop.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii fɔɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmei baa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni kpɛɔ lɛ nɔ. Kwɛmɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ mra ni akɛ organic neem fɔ loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ. Ehaa ŋmeii lɛ kpaa dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do I get smaller crops when I plant my seeds very close together in the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii anɔ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the adult plants end up fighting for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Giving each crop enough space allows its roots and leaves to spread out and produce a larger yield.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei ni eda lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ha he fɛɛ he ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ, ebaaha eshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my cocoa beans get warm and produce wet moisture when I heap them after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa yibii lɛ amli dɔɔ ni amɛjieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli ewo fɔ beni mibua amɛnaa yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: The heat and liquid come from fermentation. Microorganisms naturally break down the sweet white pulp around the beans, generating heat that kills the plant embryo inside and creates the rich flavor needed for chocolate.
ga: Dɔlɛ kɛ nu lɛ jɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ŋɔɔ ni yɔɔ futafuta ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ. adebɔɔ mli kɔfi ŋmeii Enɛ haa dɔlɛ baa ni fiteɔ tso lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ. ni ekɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni mli wa ni he hiaa kɛha tsokolate lɛ baa.

english: Why should I dry my cocoa beans on a raised wooden rack instead of drying them directly on the bare ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbi mi-kokoo yibii lɛ yɛ tso ni awo nɔ lɛ nɔ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha amɛgbi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Drying cocoa on a raised rack keeps the beans away from dirt, goats, and pests. It also allows air to flow underneath the beans, helping them dry faster and preventing mould from growing.
ga: Cocoa ni agbiɔ yɛ tsɔji ni awo nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ muji, tooi, kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai krokomɛi ahe. Eha kɔɔyɔɔ hu hoɔ yɛ kɔfe yibii lɛ ashishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa kɔfe yibii lɛ ni amɛgbiɔ oya. ni etsĩ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekakwɛ̃

english: Why do I need to turn and stir my cocoa beans regularly while they are drying on the rack?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsake ni mafolɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ amli daa be mli ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ adeka lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Stirring the beans ensures that they all dry evenly under the sun. It stops the beans on top from burning while keeping the ones underneath from staying damp and growing mould.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ebaaha amɛgbi pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ hulu lɛ shishi. Ehaa kɔfi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ shãaa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaaa kɔfi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ŋmeii akakwɛ̃.

english: How long should I leave my cocoa beans covered under plantain leaves before spreading them out to dry?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mashi kookoo ŋmeii lɛ yɛ plantain baai lɛ ashishi dani magbɛ amɛshwã koni amɛgbi?

english: Cocoa beans usually need to ferment under plantain leaves for 5 to 6 days. Leaving them for the right amount of time allows the bitterness to leave the bean and the deep brown color to develop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ehe bahiaa ni aŋɔ cocoa ŋmeii lɛ awo baai lɛ ashishi gbii 5 kɛyashi 6. Kɛ́ oshi amɛ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaajie ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ, ni ebaaha amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: What happens if rainwater touches my cocoa beans while they are drying on the rack?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji nugbɔ nu ba mi-kokoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ be mli ni amɛmiigbi yɛ shĩa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rainwater gets soaked up by the drying beans, causing internal mould to form. Mouldy cocoa beans turn black inside, lose their quality, and will be rejected by cocoa buyers.
ga: Kɔfi yibii ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ. Ha fungus ni yɔɔ Cocoa beans mli ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ baatsɔ ediŋŋ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ ni mɛi ni heɔ kookoo lɛ baakpoo.

english: How do I know that my cocoa pods are fully ripe and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-kookoo lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Ripe cocoa pods change color completely—green pods turn bright yellow, and dark red pods turn orange-yellow. Tapping a ripe pod also produces a hollow sound because the seeds have detached from the inner wall.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su kwraa. Pods eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. ni ŋmeii tsuru ni mli edɔ lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmeii-ŋmei. Kɛ́ atswa pod ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ hu, ehaa gbee ni mli ewo muji baa be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ jeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ mligbɛ gbogboi lɛ ahe lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my young cocoa trees turn yellow and drop during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have shallow roots and lose water quickly under hot sun. When water is scarce, the tree drops leaves to save moisture and prevent the whole plant from dying.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni nu lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ nu faaa Tso lɛ baashwie baai lɛ koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he ni ekɛtsi tso muu lɛ fɛɛ naa koni ekagbo.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in wet and humid weather. Removing infected pods and clearing weeds around the tree base helps reduce humidity and stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ kɛbaa. Ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ kɛ jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ajiemɔ Tso lɛ shishi haa hulutsoo baa shi ni ehaaa helai agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do some crop processors use hot water or steam on harvested produce before drying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi komɛi ni tsuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nii lɛ kɛ nu ni mli edɔ loo lasu tsuɔ nii yɛ amɛŋmɔshi nii lɛ amli dani amɛgbiɔ lɛ?

english: Hot water or steam treatment stops internal enzymes that cause rapid decay, kills surface bacteria and insect eggs, and helps lock in the natural color and quality of the crop before drying.
ga: Nu ni mli edɔ loo lasu ni akɛtsaa hela lɛ haa enzymes ni yɔɔ mli ni kɛ fitemɔ baa oya lɛ kpaa. Egbeɔ helai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi kɛ kooloi bibii amli ŋmeii. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adebɔɔ mli su kɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha lɛ ŋmɛɔ dani egbiɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings grow better when planted under banana or plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso bibioo lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ banana loo plantain tso shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are fragile and burn easily under strong sunlight. Banana and plantain trees provide soft shade and keep the air humid, giving the young cocoa the gentle environment it needs to grow strong roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Banana kɛ plantain tsei haa hulutsoo be ni mli jɔ. ni eha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli fɛ̃i ahi shi Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa shihilɛ ni mli jɔ kɛha shishifãi ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize crops produce smaller ears when I plant seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele toi lɛ feɔ bibioo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops must fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant enough space allows it to feed well and produce larger ears.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Esa akɛ Dumɔwui lɛ awuu kɛha hulu la ni faaa, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni eyeɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa toi lɛ daraa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that easily burn under direct hot sun. Leaving shade trees or planting temporary crops like plantains acts as a shield to keep the seedlings cool and moist while they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni ashiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo tsei ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in cool, wet, and damp weather. Pruning extra branches allows sunlight and fresh air to dry out the farm and reduce fungal growth.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, fɛ̃i, kɛ fɛ̃i yɔɔ. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbiɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ baa shi.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to stay green and build leaves. Adding animal manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhiɛ amɛ eŋɔli lɛ mli ni amɛfee baai. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei loo ŋmei ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmei lɛ su kɛ hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits on the field for days without draining, the roots drown and decay, which is why planting cassava on raised earth mounds helps excess water drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nu hiɔ ŋmɔ ko mli gbii babaoo ni nu bɛ mli. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛbaagboi. Enɛ hewɔ ni ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ lɛ.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, or mulching, blocks direct sunlight from drying out the soil. It traps moisture near the roots so your plants stay hydrated even on hot days.
ga: Okɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmɔshi nibii aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekagbi. Emɔɔ nu ni bɛŋkɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ. Enɛ baaha otsei lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ po nɔ.

english: Why are small worms eating holes inside the central leaves of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, pests that hide inside the whorl of the maize plant to eat soft leaves. Applying recommended biopesticides or putting clean dry ash in the central leaf whorl can clear them out.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei amli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he akɛ akɛtsu nii loo sũ ni egbi ni he tse fata tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ejie enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛ mli.

english: Yam vines need to stretch towards sunlight to gather energy to feed the tuber underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the moist ground where diseases can attack them.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ashɛ amɛhe kɛya hulu lɛ he koni amɛbua hewalɛ naa ni amɛkɛha ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. baanyɛ atutua

english: Weeds have strong roots that steal plant food and water from the soil faster than your crops can. Removing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nutrients they need.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei aniyenii kɛ nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ oya fe otsei lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant is stressed by extreme heat or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the flowers stay attached and form fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why are my young maize plants taking so long to grow big after sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tso lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani edaa beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: In the first few weeks, maize focuses its energy underground to grow strong roots before the leaves shoot up. Once the roots are established, the stalk and leaves will start growing much faster.
ga: Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, Abɛi kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni ewaje eshishifãi lɛ dani baai lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ. Kɛ shishifãi lɛ bɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛ baai lɛ baabɔi dalɛ oya kwraa.

english: Should I expect a full, large harvest the very first season I plant cassava?
ga: Ani esa akɛ makpa ŋmaa ni fa babaoo gbɛ yɛ mi klɛŋklɛŋ be ni mikɛduɔ ŋmei lɛ mli?

english: Cassava needs time to build up tubers, usually taking between 9 to 12 months to mature. Early harvests will yield small tubers, so letting the crop grow step-by-step through its full cycle gives you the best yield.
ga: Cassava heɔ be dani efeɔ yitsei. Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 dani eshɛɔ dalɛ he. Nikpamɔ mra lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ oŋmɛ tso lɛ gbɛ ni eda yɛ fãi srɔtoi amli yɛ esɛɛkuu lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha oná yibii ni hi fe fɛɛ.

english: Is it normal for my young yam vines to look weak when they first come out of the ground?
ga: Ani eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ baafee tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ beni eje kpo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ?

english: Yes, young yam sprouts are delicate at first. They need staking so the vines can climb toward sunlight, which gives the plant the energy it needs to form big tubers under the soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ waaa shishijee lɛ. Amɛbiɔ ni akɛ tsei awo mli bɔni afee ni wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya hulu la lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛfee bulb agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yellow leaves during dry months are a sign of heat stress. Young cocoa plants need protection, so planting shade crops like plantains and putting mulch around the roots helps hold moisture in the soil.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli lɛ ji hulutsoo he haomɔ he okadi. Ehe miihia ni abu kookoo tsei bibii ahe. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains kɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: What causes my watermelon leaves to curl up during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni haa watermelon baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Leaves curl up in mid-day heat to prevent water from evaporating too fast. As long as the leaves unfold again in the cooler evening, the plant is simply protecting itself from harsh weather.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni nu lɛ akafo oya tsɔ. Shii abɔ ni baai lɛ baaje kpo ekoŋŋ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be mli lɛ, Tsei lɛ miibu amɛhe kɛmiijɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa lɛ ahe kɛkɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they face sudden stress, such as extreme heat or dry soil. Keeping the soil moist and adding organic fertilizer gives the plant the strength to hold onto its flowers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe trukaa nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi. Kɛ́ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni ekɛmɔmɔ fɔfɔii.

english: How often should I walk through my farm to check on my crops during the rainy season?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni adu lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: You should inspect your farm at least two to three times a week during the rainy season. Warm and wet weather causes weeds, insects, and plant diseases to spread very quickly if you are not watching closely.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, esa akɛ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli shii enyɔ loo shii etɛ yɛ otsi mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔɔ akɛ jwɛi, kooloi bibii, kɛ tsei ahe helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya kɛji okwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I clear weeds before planting instead of waiting until after they sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mijie jwɛi dani midu yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mamɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow very fast and steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds before planting ensures your seeds get a strong, unobstructed start without fighting for survival.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya waa ni ejuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi dani odu lɛ, ehaa odumɔwui lɛ jeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ, ni nɔ ko nɔ ko tsiii amɛ gbɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛwuu koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do I need to cut off the small extra stems growing on my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Jiemɔ shweremɔ ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: Cutting off extra shoots, called suckers, allows the main plant to direct all its energy into developing bigger stems and producing large, healthy tomatoes instead of useless leaves.
ga: Nibii krokomɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ ni aaafolɔ Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ akudɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛfee tso agbo. ni amɛwo tomatoi wuji ni mli wa yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ najiaŋ.

english: How do I know if my soil is healthy enough to start growing vegetables for the first time?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi aduawai adumɔ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa?

english: Healthy soil holds moisture well, breaks apart easily in your hand without forming hard rocks, and contains dark organic matter. Adding compost or manure before planting helps give your first crop the best environment to thrive.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Efoɔ mlɛo yɛ nine mli ni efeee tɛi ni wa. ni eyɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni mli edɔ Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he dani odu lɛ, ebaaha oklɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná shihilɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni ebaanyɛ ekwɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantain trees grow very fast and have large leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing the young cocoa with shade and moisture to help it survive its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ akpɔlɔi ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa kookoo bibioo lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. The plant pulls food from its oldest bottom leaves to keep the top new leaves growing, which causes the bottom leaves to starve and turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ amli koni amɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ akwɛ̃. Enɛ haa shishigbɛ baai lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Yam plants need sunlight on their leaves to produce food for the tubers growing underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet ground so they get full sunlight and prevents diseases from spreading from the soil.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛtsi helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anaa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the soil quickly changes from very dry to very wet. Extreme heat prevents the pollen inside the flower from working, so the plant drops the flower.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ oya waa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa fɔfɔi lɛ amli pollen lɛ tsuuu nii. No hewɔ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ shwie shi.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts makes the land better for future crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmei dumɔ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii wɔsɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut roots work with tiny organisms in the earth to pull nitrogen food out of the air and put it into the soil. When you harvest the groundnuts, that natural fertilizer stays in the ground to feed the next crop you plant.
ga: Peanut shishifãi kɛ nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ feɔ ekome kɛtsuɔ nii. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ejie nitrogen nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji okpa ŋmei Nakai adebɔɔ mli ŋmei lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do I see small ragged holes in my maize leaves and caterpillars hiding inside the center shoot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii ni akɛtee ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm. Moths lay eggs inside the center of the young maize plant, and when the caterpillars hatch, they hide in the leaves and chew them while the leaves are still folded up.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni woɔ ewui yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ fɔ Ekɛ ehe teeɔ baai lɛ amli ni ekɛyeɔ nii be mli ni baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lolo lɛ.

english: How do I choose the right cassava stem cuttings to plant so they produce good roots?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei nine ni sa ni madu koni ehiɛ shishifãi kpakpai?

english: Take stem cuttings from strong, healthy cassava plants that are at least eight months old. Choose the middle part of the stem where the buds are close together and check that there is no rot or insect damage inside.
ga: Okɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmei tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni kɛ hoo lɛ eye nyɔji kpaanyɔ lɛ mli ŋmeii awo mli. Halamɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ he ni ŋmeii lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ. Ni kwɛmɔ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii bɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to grow thin and produce small harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miifee miŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni amɛmiiwo yibii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal the water, sunlight, and fertilizer from the soil before your main crops can reach them. They act like unwanted guests taking the food off your crop's plate, leaving your plants weak.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ baashɛ. Amɛfeɔ amɛnii tamɔ gbɔi ni ataooo amɛ, ni amɛjieɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii atsɛnsii amli. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, otso lɛ baagbɔjɔ.

english: Maize takes the exact same food out of the soil every season. Planting it repeatedly drains the soil completely and allows pests and diseases that attack maize to build up in the ground, causing poorer yields each year.
ga: Abele jieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Kɛ́ adu shii abɔ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔ kwraa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nibii ni afeɔ lɛ baa shi daa afi.

english: How do I know the soil is ready for sowing my seeds after the first rains start?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛha dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Wait until the rain has soaked the ground deep enough—about the length of your hand—so that the seed gets continuous moisture. Planting after just a light rain can cause seeds to sprout and then dry up if the sun comes out strong.
ga: Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa—aaafee onine lɛ kɛlɛ—koni eha dumɔwui lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ lɛ Baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji hulu la lɛ mli wa.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen nutrient in the soil, or the roots are sitting in waterlogged ground. Applying appropriate fertilizer and ensuring water can drain properly will help the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. loo shishifãi ni ta shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tsu nii ni akwɛ koni nu lɛ anyɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants droop and wilt in the afternoon heat even though I watered them early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ leebi moŋ?

english: In intense afternoon sun, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can draw it from the soil. Placing dry grass or straw mulch around the base of the plant keeps the soil cool and retains moisture longer.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo jwɛi fɔ otsei lɛ ashishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures are too high or when soil moisture fluctuates too much between wet and dry. Keeping the soil consistently moist and planting shade crops nearby during hot seasons can help fruits form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ teŋ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni odu tsei ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ bɛŋkɛ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua yɛ enɛ mli.

english: Why do groundnut plants need soft soil around them once they finish producing flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni bɔle amɛhe lɛ he hiaa ŋmei tsei lɛ? Beni agbe fɔfɔi lɛ agbe naa lɛ

english: Groundnut flowers bloom above ground, but once pollinated, the plant grows pegs downwards into the soil where the nuts actually form. Soft, loose soil makes it easy for these pegs to push underground and mature into healthy pods.
ga: Peanut fɔfɔii fɔ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi kɛ́ afee pollination lɛ, akɛ tsei lɛ fĩɔ shikpɔŋ ni ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni etse ehe lɛ haa ewaa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ baatsi amɛhe kɛya shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, overly damp conditions. Pruning extra shade tree branches to let in sunlight and quickly removing infected pods stops the rot from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ tsɔ. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ shade lɛ koni hulu la abote mli ni ejie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii akagbɛ ashwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why are my ginger roots soft and rotten under the dirt before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ginger shishifãi lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Soft, rotten ginger roots are caused by waterlogging and fungal infection in heavy soils. Planting ginger on raised soil beds allows excess water to run off, keeping the underground roots healthy and dry.
ga: Nu ni hoɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ ni tsii mli lɛ kɛ ginger shishifãi fiteɔ baa. Ginger ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ baaha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. Ha shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ awa ni amɛgbi.

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots start turning dark and spoiling just two days after digging them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbo yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ ni mikɛfo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots begin a natural deterioration process immediately after harvest due to damage and air exposure. Processing fresh cassava into gari or flour right after harvesting preserves its value and prevents spoilage loss.
ga: Cassava shishifãi jeɔ adebɔɔ mli fitemɔ gbɛjianɔtoo shishi amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ yɛ fitemɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ afee ŋmei hee ni afee lɛ gari loo ashikishaŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ehaa sɛɛnamɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ hiɔ shi, ni ehaaa efite.

english: Why do my stored yam tubers start sprouting buds in the barn before I am ready to plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mifee klalo akɛ madu amɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers naturally wake up from dormancy as temperatures rise in the storage season. Storing yams in a well-ventilated, shaded barn with good airflow keeps the tubers cool and delays unwanted early sprouting.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ teɔ shi kɛjɛɔ wɔɔhe mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ sweet potato to ŋmɔ ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmeii lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ mra ni ataooo lɛ asɛɛ afo.

english: Why does my stored maize turn into fine powder and get eaten up by tiny insects after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikɛto lɛ tsɔɔ powda kpakpa kɛ kooloi bibii lɛ? Ani obaaye fɛɛ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli?

english: Weevils attack maize when the grain is stored while still containing moisture. Sun-drying your maize until the grains are hard and crack crisp between your teeth prevents insects from breeding inside the stored crop.
ga: Weevils tutuaa ŋmãa kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa lɛ to ni edɔ lolo. Abɛi ni agbiɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ haaa kooloi bibii afɔ yɛ tsei ni ato lɛ amli.

english: Plantain leaves dry up to protect the plant during hot periods or as a reaction to leaf spot diseases. Removing dead leaves with a clean knife and spreading organic mulch around the stem helps the plant retain water and grow strong.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ koni amɛkɛbu tso lɛ he yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli loo akɛ nɔ ni jɛɔ baa mli ŋmɔtɔ hela mli baa. Okɛ tsɔne ni mli tse ajie baai ni egboi lɛ ni okɛ organic mulch awo amɛhe. Tsoi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtoɔ nu ni amɛdaraa hewalɛ.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow even though I gave them water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni mikɛ nu wo amɛmli po lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is essential for healthy green growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea at the right growth stage helps plants regain their deep green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea wo tso lɛ mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ená su ni mli kwɔ ni eda waa.

english: Fertilizer is best applied when the soil is moist and crops are actively growing, usually two to three weeks after seedlings emerge, so the roots can absorb the nutrients efficiently without burning.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni tso lɛ miida waa, bei pii lɛ, otsii 2-3 sɛɛ beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛshãaa.

english: Excess leafy growth with small tubers happens when there is too much nitrogen in the soil and not enough potassium. Potassium is the key nutrient that feeds root and tuber expansion.
ga: Baai ni yaa hiɛ fe nine ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ baa kɛji nitrogen babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Potassium ji niyenii titri ni yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ.

english: How do I know if the rains have settled enough for me to start planting my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa ni mikɛje dumɔwui adumɔ shishi?

english: Wait until the soil stays consistently moist for several days after two or three major rains. Planting during early, scattered rains can cause seeds to sprout and then dry up and die.
ga: Mɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ gbii komɛi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni adu mra be mli ni nugbɔ enɛ egbɛ eshwã lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgbi ni amɛgboi.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough food and room to grow thick stalks and produce bigger yields.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: What is eating small holes in my young corn leaves, and how will it affect my harvest?
ga: Buji bibii ni ayeɔ Mɛni yɔɔ mi gbekɛ ŋmãa baa lɛ nɔ? Ni te ebaasa mikpamɔ lɛ he eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Small ragged holes in corn leaves are often caused by fall armyworms. If left untreated, they destroy the crop's growing center, drastically reducing your grain yield or killing the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni egbee shi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii baai amli lɛ baa. Kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ Ebaakpata tso lɛ dalɛ he lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui ni baa lɛ baa shi kwraa loo tso lɛ gboɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my crops and choke them during the early weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛtsiɔ amɛnaa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to pull water and nutrients from the soil much faster than crops. Clearing weeds within the first 3 to 4 weeks prevents them from stealing essential food from your young plants.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛjie nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe tsei. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii 3 kɛyashi 4 lɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ otsei bibii lɛ amli.

english: Why am I getting smaller harvests from my farm every year even though I plant the same crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɛɛ yibiiwoo nɔ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ moŋ?

english: Planting the exact same crop on the same plot every season strips the soil of the same specific nutrients over time. Rotating crops with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome yɛ be ni sa mli. Nibii ni aduɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei fata he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do seeds I saved from my last harvest perform worse than a new batch bought from an agro-dealer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mihere kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui heei ni ahe kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ?

english: Commercial hybrid seeds are specially bred for strong growth and disease resistance, but seeds saved from those crops lose those strong traits in the next generation. Buying a fresh batch ensures uniform growth and higher yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ jarayeli dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛdara waa ni amɛnyɛ amɛshi helai. Shi dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ nakai ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baafite nakai sui ni mli wa lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Batch heei ahemɔ haa dalɛ yaa nɔ daa kɛ sɛɛnamɔi babaoo.

english: How does writing down the dates I apply fertilizer help my crops perform better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ gbi ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ ŋmalamɔ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ?

english: Keeping simple application records helps you feed your crops at the exact growth stage they need it most, preventing wasted fertilizer and helping you see which feeding schedule gives you the biggest harvest.
ga: Nibii ni aŋmala ashwie shi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ haa onyɛɔ oyeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa yɛ he ni ehe hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ. Tsi ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni afiteɔ lɛ naa. ni eyeɔ ebua bo ni ona niyenii hamɔ he gbɛjianɔtoo ni woɔ yibii fe fɛɛ.

english: Why does my cassava crop take almost a whole year to harvest when corn takes only three months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ heɔ afi lɛ mli be babaoo kɛkpaa lɛ? Be mli ni ŋmãa heɔ nyɔji etɛ pɛ?

english: Cassava stores its energy underground in thick tuber roots, which takes many months to grow fully, whereas corn puts its energy into growing fast above the ground to produce grains quickly.
ga: Cassava kɛ hewalɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ tuber shishifãi ni mli tse mli. Eheɔ nyɔji babaoo dani edaa kwraa. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛwo dumɔwui oya.

english: How long does it take for a pineapple plant to bear fruit, and can I plant the green top crown?
ga: Be enyiɛ ŋmei tso baawo yibii? Ni ani abaanyɛ akwɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli?

english: Pineapple is a slow-growing plant that usually takes 18 to 24 months to yield fruit. You can plant the green top crown in the soil, and it will root and grow into a brand new pineapple plant.
ga: Anana ji tso ko ni daa blɛoo ni bei pii lɛ eheɔ nyɔji 18 kɛyashi 24 dani ewoɔ yibii. Obaanyɛ okɛ akekere ni ji ŋmɔ lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni ebaawo shishifãi ni eda ni etsɔ ŋmei tso hee ni abɔ.

english: If I plant my corn seeds too close to each other, why do the stalks grow tall and thin without big cobs?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni ŋmeii wuji bɛ mli lɛ?

english: When corn is planted too close together, the plants compete for light, water, and nutrients. They stretch upward to reach sunlight instead of putting energy into making thick stems and large cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛmɔ hulu la lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛma tsei bibii ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my cucumber plants spread all over the ground instead of standing up straight like corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi kukumba tsei lɛ miigbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaadamɔ shi jaŋŋ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Cucumber plants are weak-stemmed vines that naturally crawl along the soil. You can lift them off the wet ground by giving them sticks or a trellis to climb up.
ga: Kukumba tsei ji wain tsei ni amɛshishifãi yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛfoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Obaanyɛ owó amɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ tso loo ŋtayaa ni ooohã amɛ koni amɛkwɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do people say that planting groundnuts makes the soil better for maize in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmeii ni adu lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmeii ni baaba yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which pulls nitrogen gas from the air and stores it in the soil. This leaves behind natural fertilizer that helps corn grow better afterward.
ga: Peanuts fata legume weku lɛ he, ni amɛgbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young corn plants turning pale yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the corn plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to stay green and build strong stems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa tso lɛ. Eji niyenii titri ni esa akɛ tso lɛ ahi eŋɔli lɛ mli ni etswa shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why do my okra pods get hard and woody if I do not pick them quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra ŋmɔji lɛ mli wa ni eyɛ tsei kɛji mijieee amɛ oya lɛ?

english: Okra pods are meant to be harvested while young and soft. If left on the stalk too long, the plant works on maturing the seeds inside, which makes the pod outer skin tough and fibrous.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ abaakpa okra ŋmeii lɛ beni amɛji gbekɛbii lolo ni amɛhe yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ tso lɛ shishi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Tso lɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ akwɛ̃. Enɛ haa pod lɛ kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa ni eyɛ tsɔne.

english: Why do my okra flowers sometimes drop off the plant without turning into okra pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ mi okra fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni efeee okra ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Okra flowers drop when the plant experiences stress, such as sudden hot dry weather, lack of water, or shade, which prevents the flower from forming fruit.
ga: Roselle fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na haomɔi, tamɔ hulutsoo ni mli egbi trukaa, nu ni bɛ, loo hulutsoo, ni haaa fɔfɔi lɛ awo yibii.

english: How do groundnuts manage to produce nuts under the soil when the flowers are above ground?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii feɔ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi be mli ni fɔfɔi lɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: After the groundnut flower opens above ground and is fertilized, it grows a small stem called a peg that pushes downward into the soil, where the nut develops safely underground.
ga: Beni ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ ekwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni awo mli ŋmei sɛɛ lɛ, Ebaaná ŋmei bibioo ko. Atsɛɔ lɛ peg ni ashɛɔ awoɔ shikpɔŋ. Biɛ ji he ni ŋmeii lɛ daa shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Can I just cut cassava stems into small sticks and plant them directly in the soil to grow new cassava?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafolɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ amli mafee tsei bibii? No sɛɛ lɛ, ani manyɛ madu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ koni makwɛ ŋmei hee?

english: Yes, cassava grows from stem cuttings. As long as you cut a healthy stem with buds and plant it right-side up in moist soil, it will sprout roots below and leaves above.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii amli. Shii abɔ ni obaafo tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmei ni okɛdu lɛ hiɛ kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, eshishifãi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishi ni baai lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi.

english: Is it better for me to spray chemical pesticides on my maize early in the morning or in the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mafɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ anɔ yɛ ŋmãa nɔ leebi loo shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: It is best to spray early in the morning when the air is cool and wind is calm. High afternoon heat causes chemical sprays to evaporate too fast or burn crop leaves, wasting your money and reducing the chemical's effectiveness.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ leebi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hu efee kpoo. Gbi gbɛkɛ mli dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ loo eshãa tsei ahe baai. Efiteɔ shika ni ehaa tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why does spraying chemical weedicide sometimes make my crops stop growing alongside the weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni mikɛshwieɔ shi lɛ haaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ kɛfataa jwɛi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Non-selective weedicides or spray drift can accidentally land on crop leaves and roots, causing chemical stress. Using a protective spray shield or choosing crop-safe selective herbicides protects your main crop while killing the weeds.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni halaaa loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ baanyɛ agbee tsei lɛ ahe baai kɛ shishifãi anɔ yɛ oshara mli. cause chemical stress Kɛ okɛ tsofai ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ tsu nii loo tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni halaa ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaye abua ni ebu oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni ejieɔ jwɛi lɛ kɛyaa.

english: Why are the leaves of my young cocoa trees turning brown and falling off during the harmattan?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ harmatta beaŋ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that lose water rapidly during the dry harmattan wind. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains around young cocoa protects them from direct harsh sunlight and dry winds.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nu fiteɔ oya yɛ harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ he.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep dropping off the plants without producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant suffers from heat stress or extreme dry soil. Keeping the soil consistently watered and cool helps the flowers stay on the plant long enough to turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ dɔlɛ loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔ ni afɔ nɔ nu daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛtsɔ tomato.

english: Why do my garden eggs look small and taste bitter even when I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Small, bitter garden eggs are usually caused by low soil nutrients or leaving the fruits on the branch for too long. Adding organic manure to the soil and picking fruits while they are young keeps them tender and large.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sũ mli niyenii ni faaa loo aduawai ni ashiɔ yɛ tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii bibii ni ŋɔɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni okɛ aduawai ni ajieɔ beni amɛji bibii lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee blɛoo ni efee agbo.

english: Why do my young maize leaves turn yellow or purple when the crop is still short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa lolo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves mean the plant lacks nitrogen for growth, while purple leaves show a lack of phosphorus in the soil. Applying the right fertilizer early gives the plants the nutrients required to grow dark green and strong.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃. yɛ be mli ni baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa baatsu nii mra Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants curl up and turn pale during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava leaves curl and yellow under dry stress, often aggravated by small pests like green mites sucking sap. Maintaining good soil moisture and applying organic controls early prevents leaf damage.
ga: Cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔlɔ he haomɔ shishi. ni bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu lɛ gbaa amɛnaa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kpakpa ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akudɔɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra. Eyeɔ ebuaa koni akafite baai lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my plantain leaves are drying up because of disease or just lack of rain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi plantain baai lɛ egbi yɛ hela loo nugbɔ ni enɛɛɛ kɛkɛ hewɔ?

english: If lack of rain is the issue, the leaves simply droop and wilt during heat. If it is a disease like Black Sigatoka, you will notice distinct dark brown spots or yellow streaks forming on the lower leaves before they dry up.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ, baai lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛbaagbi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be lɛ he. Kɛji hela ko tamɔ Black Sigatoka ji lɛ, obaana ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse yɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ dani amɛgbi.

english: Why should I space my cassava stems far apart instead of planting them close together to get more yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbala ŋmeii lɛ amli? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni onine ashɛ yibii babaoo nɔ lɛ.

english: Planting cassava stems too close makes them fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil food. Giving each stem enough space allows the roots room beneath the soil to swell into thick, heavy cassava tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ekɛ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ abɔ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha shishifã ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ mli lɛ atsɔ ŋmei shishifã ni mli wa ni tsii.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds away from the base of my pepper plants instead of leaving them to rot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mijieɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ moŋ fe ni mahã amɛgboi lɛ?

english: Weeds near pepper roots steal sunlight, water, and fertilizer meant for your crop, while also hiding harmful pests. Clearing them ensures all nutrients go straight to growing your pepper plants.
ga: Jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ pepper shishifãi lɛ juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa onibii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ekɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ teeɔ. Amɛhe ni ooofɔ lɛ baatsɔɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ fɛɛ kɛya o-pepper tso lɛ dalɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees take so many years before they start bearing pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani amɛjeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees spend their early years building a strong root system and sturdy trunk to support future heavy pods. They require steady care and weeding during this period before they are mature enough to produce a harvest.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii yeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ ni amɛdaraa. Koni afee shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni baaye abua pods ni tsii wɔsɛɛ. Amɛbiɔ ni akwɛ amɛ daa ni ajie jwɛi yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli dani amɛdara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa amɛ.

english: Why do I need to prune healthy-looking branches off my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ cacao tso niji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes non-producing branches so the tree can direct its energy into producing larger pods. It also opens up the canopy to let in sunlight and fresh air, which prevents fungal diseases like black pod from spreading.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni afolɔ mli lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni wooo yibii lɛ koni tso lɛ anyɛ ekɛ ehewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji. Ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hu naa ŋwɛitsu lɛ. Tsi fungal helai tamɔ black pods lɛ gbɛ koni ekagbɛ eshwa.

english: When plantains are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for water and soil nutrients, and their large leaves block each other's sunlight. Giving each sucker enough space allows it to gather the strength needed to produce large, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu plantains ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. ni amɛbaai wuji lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe hulu la lɛ naa. Kɛ́ aha sucker fɛɛ sucker he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ebuaa hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ lɛ naa koni ekɛfee bales agboi ni tsii.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow and stay small if I don't apply fertilizer every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni efeɔ bibii kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli daa be lɛ?

english: Maize grows rapidly and consumes a high amount of nutrients from the soil. Yellow leaves mean the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed to make food and grow strong stalks.
ga: Abɛi daa oya ni eyeɔ niyenii babaoo ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen. Enɛɛmɛi ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha niyenii feemɔ kɛ tsei ni wa ni kwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why does my cassava yield get smaller every time I plant on the same land without giving the soil a break?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi be fɛɛ be ni madu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ efooo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots absorb large amounts of nutrients out of the earth as they grow big. Planting cassava continuously on the same plot wears out the soil's natural fertility, leading to smaller tubers unless manure or fertilizer is added to restore the land.
ga: Cassava shishifãi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli lɛ aba shi. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii. Ja akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he koni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Weeds grow fast and aggressively rob your crops of essential soil nutrients, space, and sunlight right at root level. Clearing weeds removes this competition so your crops get all the nourishment available.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa, he ko, kɛ hulu la kɛha otsei lɛ yɛ shishifã lɛ he. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ jieɔ akaŋshii nɛɛ kɛyaa. Bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii ni yeɔ emuu.

english: Why do my diseased cocoa pods need to be picked off and removed immediately instead of left to fall on their own?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ajie kookoo ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshi lɛ koni egbee shi lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Leaving black or diseased pods on the tree allows fungal spores to spread to healthy pods through rain splashes and wind. Removing and disposing of sick pods early stops the disease from wiping out the rest of your crop.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii diji loo hela yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii amli ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli kɛtsɔ nugbɔshiimɔi kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ nɔ. Nibii ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ kɛ amɛjiemɔ mra Ebaatsi hela naa koni ekafite onibii ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper flowers fall off before any fruits start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme sun heat, lack of soil moisture, or pest damage. Keeping the plants shaded and well-watered helps the flowers stay on the stem and form peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ hao amɛ. ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fiteɔ Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ he hulutsoo ni aha lɛ nu bɔ ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ shishi ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt during the dry season even if I give them water once a week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ gboɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ shikome yɛ otsi mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes have shallow roots and lose moisture rapidly through their leaves in high heat. They require consistent, frequent soil moisture rather than occasional deep watering to stay healthy and set fruit.
ga: Tomato shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni etsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ nu lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ he miihia amɛ. Mohu ɔ, mo ha lɛ nu wawɛɛ ngɛ be kɛ be ko mi konɛ e ná he wami kpakpa nɛ e wo yiblii.

english: Why do hybrid seeds cost more and require more care than seeds I save from my own harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni akɛ tsofai ebɔ he lɛ jara wa ni ebiɔ ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specifically bred to give much higher yields and fight off common diseases, but they require precise feeding and management to reach their high potential compared to traditional saved seeds.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo ni amɛwu amɛshi helai ni afɔɔ namɔ. Shi nɛkɛ dumɔwui nɛɛ biɔ niyenii pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ nɔkwɛmɔ koni amɛshɛ amɛhewalɛ ni nɔ kwɔ he kɛ akɛto blema dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build strong green leaves. Adding well-rotted manure or a nitrogen fertilizer like urea will help them regain their deep green color and grow faster.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ eŋɔli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ni yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda oya.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas make my soil better for next season's corn?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmãa?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and store it in tiny bumps on their roots. When the crop is harvested and the roots rot, that natural fertilizer stays in the soil to feed your next crop of corn.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ amli kɛ́ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni shishifãi lɛ egbo. Nakai adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakã sũ lɛ mli koni ekɛha o-ŋma ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does my white yam variety spoil faster during storage than my yellow yam?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato yɛŋ lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ fe mi-sweet potato ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: White yam varieties have thinner skin and higher moisture content compared to yellow yams. This makes them softer, more sensitive to heat and bruising, and more prone to fungal rot if stored in a warm or unventilated area.
ga: Sweet potato henɔi yɛŋ lɛ ahewolo lɛ mli tseee ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli kɛ akɛto sweet potato ŋmɔŋ he. soften E nuɔ dɔlɛ kɛ fãji ahe waa. Ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni hulutsoo loo kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ.

english: How do I know if I am planting my cassava stem cuttings upside down?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mikɛ ŋmei niji miikwɛ ŋwɛi?

english: Look closely at the small raised nodes or bumps on the stem where leaves used to grow. These bumps should point upward toward the sky; if they point down toward the soil, the stick is upside down and will struggle to sprout roots and shoots.
ga: Taomɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii. Yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, he ni tsutsu lɛ baai lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ bɛŋkɛ Esa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ amɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ Nine lɛ baatsɔ ŋwɛi ni ebaabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekwɛ shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii.

english: Planting seeds too close together forces the crops to compete with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This results in thin, weak stalks and smaller yields, whereas proper spacing gives each plant enough space to produce large, healthy fruits or tubers.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii nibii ni yɔɔ sũ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ aduawai loo bulbs wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before the tiny cocoa pods can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani cocoa ŋmeii bibii lɛ baanyɛ afee lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop off when the plant suffers from dry weather, poor soil nutrients, or a lack of tiny insects called midges that pollinate the blossoms. Keeping shade trees alive helps keep the air moist so pollinating insects can thrive and flowers can set pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na shihilɛi ni mli egbi. Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kooloi bibii ni bɛ Atsɛɔ lɛ midge ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Tsei ni akɛhaa hulutsoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli tseɔ. Bɔni afee ni kooloi ni feɔ pollin lɛ anyɛ adara. ni fɔfɔii baanyɛ afee ŋmeii

english: What is eating small holes in the central growing leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Buji bibii ni ayeɔ Mɛni ji nɔ ni yɔɔ baa ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa gbekɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: That damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central leaf funnel of maize. Applying neem leaf extract or recommended insecticides directly into the funnel early in the morning helps clear the pest before it destroys the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmei lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu loo tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ wo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ajie ŋmeii lɛ kɛjɛ mli dani amɛfite tso lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and making the plants stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle ehe ni eha tso lɛ miikpa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in peppers is caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or thrips that carry viruses and feed on leaf sap. Controlling these insects early with neem oil or insecticidal soap protects new leaves so the plant can grow normally.
ga: Kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips kɛ chili baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni ji mɛi ni hiɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli ni amɛyeɔ jwɛi ni baa yɔɔ mli akɛ niyenii Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛbaatsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu baai heei ahe koni tso lɛ anyɛ ada jogbaŋŋ.

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves, called mulching, keeps the ground cool under the hot sun, prevents water from evaporating quickly, and stops weeds from popping up to steal nutrients from your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ baai ni egbi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya ni ehaaa jwɛi lɛ aju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ.

english: Black bottoms on tomatoes, known as blossom-end rot, happen when the plant cannot draw enough calcium from the soil, which usually occurs during irregular dry and wet spells. Consistent watering helps the plant carry calcium straight to the developing fruit.
ga: Shikpɔŋ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli, ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi be fɛɛ be. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ekɛ calcium lɛ yaa tso yibii ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves turn yellow and drop off whenever I water them heavily every single day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi be fɛɛ be ni mawo amɛ nu waa daa gbi lɛ?

english: Too much water starves plant roots of air, causing them to drown and rot. Crop roots need air in the soil to breathe, so overwatering damages the roots, causing the leaves to turn yellow and drop.
ga: Nu babaoo haa kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ tsei shishifãi lɛ amli. ni haa efoɔ nu mli ni egboɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. No hewɔ lɛ, nu babaoo ni akɛhaa lɛ baafite shishifãi lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi.

english: Is it harmful if I plant my maize seeds straight into hard, unplowed soil right after the main rains begin?
ga: Ani eyɛ oshara kɛji akɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni atsuko nɔ nii nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Hard soil makes it very difficult for soft young roots to push down and find water and food. Loosening the soil first helps roots grow deep quickly, building a strong base that keeps the plant standing in high winds.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ haa ewaa ahaa shishifãi bibii lɛ akɛ amɛaatsi amɛhe kɛya shi koni amɛyana nu kɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwie shi klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ adara oya. Ehaa shishitoo ni wa ni yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni edamɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I cut down all the big trees on my farm before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mifo tsei wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ dani midu lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to harsh sunlight and heat. They require nurse crops like plantains or shade trees to act as natural sunshades while their leaves and root systems are small and tender.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ he waa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ. Koni etsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo be mli ni baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo.

english: Why do I need to guide my yam vines onto wooden stakes instead of letting them spread on the bare ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ sweet potato wain tso lɛ awo tso nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha eda yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunlight and air circulation to manufacture starch for the tubers underground. Keeping vines elevated on stakes stops leaves from burning on hot soil and prevents rot.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ babaoo koni ekɛfee starch kɛha ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ wain tsei lɛ to tsei ni kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ, ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkashã yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ, ni ebaaha amɛkafite.

english: Why are my maize plants growing tall and thin without producing big cobs when I put many seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ daa ni efeɔ mlɛo ni ekɛ toi wuji baaa beni mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo woɔ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight with each other for light, water, and soil food. They waste all their energy stretching upward for sunlight instead of developing strong stems and full corn cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baawu koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Amɛfiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ kɛjeɔ kpo kɛyaa hulu lɛ mli moŋ fe ni amɛaama tsei ni wa kɛ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why does my cassava plant produce massive green leaves above ground but very tiny tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ hiɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen manure, cassava plants direct all their energy into leafy top growth. This leaf expansion starves the roots of energy, leaving you with small tubers at harvest time.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ shweremɔ mli yɛ ebaai lɛ anɔ. Baai ni dara lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa ohiɛɔ oyitso bibioo. yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers without producing any peppers during the peak of the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛ pepper ko baaa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses pepper plants, making them drop their flowers to save water and protect themselves from drying out. Shading the plants or mulching the soil helps keep them cool enough to hold their blossoms.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi. Kɛ́ afee tso lɛ he ŋmɔlɔ loo akɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ mli jɔɔ bɔ ni sa koni efɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do crop diseases get worse on my farm when I plant garden eggs on the exact same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe helai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli woɔ wu waa kɛ́ midu ŋmeii yɛ mibɔɔ lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Pests and soil diseases that target specific crops stay alive in the soil from one season to the next. Planting the same crop continuously gives these pests a non-stop food supply, allowing their populations to multiply.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi anɔ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ be kome mli kɛyaa be kroko mli. Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ yeɔ niyenii ni amɛkpaaa. Enɛ haa amɛyibɔ ​​yaa hiɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants turning yellow-green and curling up into twisted shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ-ŋɔli ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe kɛmiifee srɔtoi lɛ?

english: Curled, pattern-stained leaves are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies. Sick plants cannot turn sunlight into food effectively, which stunts their growth.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ mfoniri lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmei bibioo lɛ ji nɔ ni tereɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ Tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ nyɛŋ atsake hulu la lɛ amɛfee niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baatsi dalɛ naa.

english: Why do weeds kill my young crop seedlings so quickly even when there is plenty of rainfall for everything on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi gbeɔ midumɔwui bibii lɛ oya nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ kroko ni yɔɔ shia lɛ mli lɛ ená nugbɔ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than domestic crops and aggressively steal nutrients and moisture from the soil before your crop roots can reach them. They also block essential sunlight from young seedlings.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe shia tsei ni amɛkɛ ekãa juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe. Etsiɔ hulu la ni he hiaa waa lɛ hu naa kɛjɛɔ tsei bibii lɛ amli.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to build strong stems, deep roots, and big yields.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛ shishifãi ni mli wa, shishifãi ni mli kwɔ, kɛ yibiiwoo babaoo aba.

english: Seeds fail to sprout if they are planted too deep, if the soil is too dry, or if pests like ants and birds eat them before they can grow. Using good seed from certified sources and planting at the right depth helps them germinate.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. aloo kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ okpoi yeɔ amɛ dani amɛdaraa. Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui kpakpai ni jɛ hei ni ana he odaseyeli lɛ tsu nii ni adu amɛ yɛ he ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is a major food source plants need from the soil. It can also happen if heavy rains wash nutrients away or if roots are sitting in flooded soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ jɛɛhe titri Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni haa tsei lɛ loo kɛji akɛ shishifãi lɛ ewo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why is it good practice for me to plant cowpeas or beans on the same land where I grow maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?
