english: Beans and cowpeas trap nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil. When you rotate or intercrop them with maize, they naturally fertilize the ground and make your next crop grow better.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ tsinabii amɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji okɛ ŋmãa tsake loo okɛ ŋmãa du ŋmãa lɛ, ŋmãa baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmãa yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eha onibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Covering the ground, known as mulching, traps moisture in the soil so it stays wet longer, keeps the roots cool during hot Ghanaian days, and stops weeds from popping up.
ga: Ale mulching hu akɛ mulching. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ yɛ Ghana gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa.

english: Cassava plants drop leaves during hot, dry periods as a self-defense trick to save water. The plant goes quiet above ground while keeping the underground tubers safe until the rainy season comes back.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa, ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ amɛhe nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni akɛbu nu he. Tsei lɛ baafee dioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ hiɔ shi shweshweeshwe kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the heat gets too intense, when the plant doesn't get enough water, or when bees and wind fail to pollinate the blossoms properly.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji la lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Be mli ni tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Aloo be mli ni ŋmeii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do young cocoa trees need taller plants like plantains grown right next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he hiaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide living shade and moisture, acting like an umbrella to protect young cocoa until it matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Plantains ni shwereɔ oya lɛ haa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i baa. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ akpɔlɔ ni buɔ kookoo bibioo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa.

english: Weeds grow faster and are tougher than most crops. They steal the water, fertilizer, and sunlight meant for your crops, leaving your plants starved and unable to grow big fruits or grains.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei babaoo. Amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ otsei lɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo aduawai loo dumɔwui wuji.

english: Why do armyworms suddenly appear in large numbers on my maize farm right after the early rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cutworm lɛ je kpo trukaa babaoo yɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ leebi nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: The early rains trigger moths to lay thousands of eggs on fresh, soft young maize leaves. The eggs hatch quickly into hungry worms that feed heavily on the growing crop.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ haa ŋmeii woɔ wɔji akpei abɔ yɛ abɛi bibii ni yɔɔ ehee ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ anɔ. Wɔlɔi lɛ fɔɔ oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni miida lɛ waa.

english: Why shouldn't I leave dug holes open for too long before planting my seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ ashiɔ bu ni atsa lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ dani aduɔ dumɔwu lɛ?

english: Leaving dug holes exposed to direct sun dries out the moist topsoil and kills helpful soil organisms. Planting quickly or covering the holes keeps the soil moist and rich for the young roots.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi bu ko ni atsa yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaha sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni efɔ lɛ agbi ni egbe sũ mli nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. Dumɔ oya loo bu lɛ mli ni awoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shishifãi bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How deep should I dig the holes when planting cocoa seedlings on my land?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafo bu lɛ mli kɛyashɛ he ni kɛ́ midu kookoo dumɔwui yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: The hole should be about 30 centimeters deep and wide so the seedling's main root can grow straight down without bending, which keeps the plant strong and healthy.
ga: Esa akɛ bu lɛ mli afee aaafee sɛntimitai 30 kɛ elɛɛmɔ bɔni afee ni dumɔwu lɛ shishifãi titrii lɛ anyɛ ada tɛ̃ɛ kɛya shi ni amɛkuuu amɛhe. Enɛ ɔ yeɔ bua tso ɔ nɛ e waa nɛ e náa he wami.

english: Why is it important to fill every single hole I dig instead of leaving some empty?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo bu fɛɛ bu ni mifoɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mashi lɛ efolo lɛ?

english: Empty holes waste valuable land, gather standing water that can cause soil erosion, and allow weeds to grow and steal nutrients from nearby crops.
ga: Buu ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ he ko ni jara wa. Buamɔ nu ni damɔ shi ni baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ naa. ni amɛha jwɛi lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why is it bad to press the soil down too tightly when filling the hole around my seedling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ manyɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ waa tsɔ beni miiwo buji ni bɔle mi dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Packing the soil too hard prevents air and rainwater from reaching the roots, making it difficult for tender young roots to spread through the dirt.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ wo mli jogbaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ nu lɛ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ akɛ amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants turn yellow and dry up when exposed to direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves are very tender and burn easily under strong sun. They need temporary shade crops, like plantains, to shield them and keep the soil moist during their first few years.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ waa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni ebu amɛhe ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: What happens if I damage the roots of my cocoa seedling while putting it into the ground?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ kookoo dumɔwu ko shishifãi fite beni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Damaging or bending the root system causes root shock, which can make the young plant wilt, grow slowly, or die before it can establish itself.
ga: Shishifãi lɛ akpãtãmɔ loo amɛkumɔ kɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tsei bibii lɛ agbi, amɛdara blɛoo, loo amɛgboi dani amɛma shi.

english: What is the best time of day or season to plant my young seedlings into the field?
ga: Mɛni ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ gbi lɛ mli loo be mli ni esa akɛ madu mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: It is best to plant at the beginning of the rainy season, early in the morning or late in the afternoon, so the cool weather reduces heat stress on the young seedlings.
ga: Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni adu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli. Ani eji leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli? Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ lɛ haa dɔlɛ he haomɔ ni baa tsei bibii anɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Is it safe to let younger family members help with planting delicate crops like cocoa?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaaha weku lɛ mli bii ni darako lɛ aye abua ni adu tso ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ kookoo?

english: Yes, as long as an experienced person supervises them to make sure the seedlings are set upright at the correct depth and the roots are not crushed.
ga: Hɛɛ, be fɛɛ be ni mɔ ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ baatsu he nii koni ekwɛ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛyashɛ he ni sa, ni amɛshishifãi lɛ akakumɔ.

english: How long will it take after planting my cocoa before I start making money from harvesting pods?
ga: Kɛ́ odu kookoo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, be enyiɛ ebaahe dani obaaje shika ni okɛbaakpa ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ shishi?

english: Hybrid cocoa varieties usually start bearing fruit within 2 to 3 years after planting, while older traditional varieties can take 4 to 5 years before producing a full harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo henɔi ni akɛfee ekome lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ, yɛ be mli ni kusum kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahé afii 4 kɛyashi 5 dani eshɛ kpamɔ ni yeɔ emuu lɛ he.

english: Can I plant food crops like plantain alongside my cocoa to earn money while waiting for the cocoa to grow?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi koni maná shika yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ kookoo lɛ ni ekwɛ̃?

english: Yes, planting plantains with young cocoa is very beneficial because the plantains provide helpful shade while producing fruit you can sell or eat before the cocoa matures.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛnamɔ babaoo yɛ kookoo dumɔwui ni akɛ kookoo bɔɔlu duɔ lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, plantains haa hulutsoo ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ aduawai hu ni obaanyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ loo oye dani kookoo lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my crop seeds once the early rains start in April?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui kɛ́ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ yɛ April mli?

english: Do not plant immediately after the very first rain because the soil is still too hot underneath and can burn the seeds. Wait until you get two or three heavy rains close together so the soil holds enough moisture to help the seeds sprout safely.
ga: Kaadu amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lolo yɛ shishi ni ebaanyɛ eshã dumɔwui lɛ. Mɛɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa fioo komɛi aba koni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my cassava roots begin to rot underground if I leave them in the soil during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When the soil gets soaked with water for too long without draining, air cannot reach the root tubers. This causes the roots to drown and suffocate, leading to decay and rot before you can harvest them.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu hoɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛmuɔ. Ekɛ fitemɔ kɛ fitemɔ baa dani obaanyɛ okpa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves and stems. Adding a nitrogen starter fertilizer or well-rotted manure early in their growth will bring back the dark green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn lɛ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli kɛ tsei ashishifãi. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛwoɔ jwɛi lɛ mli mra lɛ baaha jwɛi lɛ aku sɛɛ afee eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or lacks water during flowering. When it gets too hot or dry, the plant sheds its flowers to save energy instead of spending it on making fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ latsaa loo nu ni bɛ mli yɛ fɔfɔii lɛ amli. Beni edɔ tsɔ loo egbi lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaafite yɛ aduawai ahe.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very delicate leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast with broad leaves, acting like giant shade umbrellas to shield the cocoa until it grows strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ hulutsoo be wulu ko ni buɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa waa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ hulutsoo be lɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii.

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need sunlight on all their leaves to produce large tubers. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground where diseases spread and lifts them toward the sun so the plant can feed its roots.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la yɛ amɛbaai lɛ fɛɛ anɔ koni amɛfee bulbs agboi. Staking haa baai lɛ shɛɛɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ni ewoɔ baai lɛ nɔ kɛyaa hulu lɛ he koni tso lɛ anyɛ aha eshishifãi lɛ niyenii.

english: What kind of nutrients do my young crops need right after sprouting to grow strong early on?
ga: Mɛɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he hiaa mi tsei bibii lɛ beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ koni amɛdara waa mra?

english: Just sprouted crops need phosphorus to build deep roots and nitrogen to grow thick stems. Giving them balanced starter nutrients early gives them the head start they need to survive dry spells and pests later.
ga: Tsei ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ he miihia fɔsfɔs koni amɛná shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. kɛ nitrogen koni eha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Ni aha amɛ niyenii ni ja ni akɛjeɔ shishi mra Enɛ haa amɛ hiɛyaa ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ hulutsoo be kɛ sɛɛ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai amli.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow a lot of leafy green vines but produce very few bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ wain tsei ni yɔɔ baai babaoo shi ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: If you give cowpeas too much nitrogen fertilizer, the plant uses all its energy making leaves instead of flowers. Cowpeas naturally make their own nitrogen from the air, so they need phosphorus instead of nitrogen to produce pods.
ga: Kɛji oha cowpea nitrogen babaoo lɛ, Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛfeɔ baai yɛ fɔfɔii najiaŋ. Cowpeas lɛ diɛŋtsɛ feɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, tsina ŋmei biɔ fɔsfɔs yɛ nitrogen najiaŋ koni ekɛfee ŋmeii.

english: Why are ragged holes appearing in the young leaves in the middle of my corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji ni mli ewo muji jeɔ kpo yɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: This is typically caused by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm hiding inside the center shoot of the corn. They feed on the tender young leaves before they open, leaving holes visible once the leaves expand.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ amɛhe ewo ŋmãa yiteŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii dani amɛgbeleɔ. Enɛ haa anaa buji lɛ beni baai lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I prune the lowest leaves off my tomato plants near the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo mi-tomato tsei ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ahe baai ni yɔɔ shishi fe fɛɛ lɛ?

english: The bottom leaves sit close to the soil where fungal diseases live. Rain drops bounce off the mud onto these low leaves and infect the plant, so removing them keeps the plant dry and disease-free.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ taraa shikpɔŋ ni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ masɛi. Nugbɔ baashwie muji nɔ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ anɔ. Enɛɛmɛi ni haa tso lɛ he tsɛŋeɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ojie amɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ agbi ni helai akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why are agricultural officers telling us to plant cocoa in straight lines instead of scattering the seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔdu kookoo yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ moŋ fe ni wɔbaadu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Planting in straight lines makes it easier to walk through the farm, clear weeds, apply fertilizers, and ensures each tree gets enough sunlight and soil nutrients without crowding its neighbors.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ aaatsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli, ajie jwɛi lɛ, awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii, ni akwɛ koni tso fɛɛ tso aná hulu la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ekɛ ekutsoŋbii lɛ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Does planting my maize in neat rows really produce a better harvest than broadcasting the seeds?
ga: Ani ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hi fe dumɔwui ni aduɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, planting maize in rows gives every seed the right amount of space to grow strong roots and catch full sunlight, which leads to bigger stalks and larger corn cobs.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa mli lɛ haa dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi ni wa akwɛ̃ ni ená hulu la ni fa babaoo. Enɛ baaha ŋmãa lɛ afee wuji ni ŋmãa lɛ hu afee wuji.

english: Why should I bother measuring distances between crops when planting instead of using my judgment?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mihe awo mli akɛ masusu gbɛ ni kã ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ lɛ he beni miduɔ nii lɛ, moŋ fe ni mikɛ mijwɛŋmɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ baatsu nii?

english: Measuring correct distances prevents crops from fighting each other for water and food in the soil, which reduces plant stress and helps stop the spread of diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ asusu he ni jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ lɛ he jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaatsi tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkawuu amɛhe kɛha nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe haomɔ baa shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekpaa helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Can I grow food crops like cassava and maize on the same land where I just planted young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni midu cacao tsei bibii amrɔ nɛɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, you can grow food crops alongside young cocoa for the first couple of years to harvest food and earn income while waiting for the cocoa to mature, as long as you leave enough space around the young trees.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu niyenii yɛ kookoo bibii ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli koni okpa niyenii ni oná shika yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ kookoo lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ. Shii abɔ ni oyɔɔ he ko ni obɔle tsei bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ ahe

english: Will planting cassava too close to my young cocoa seedlings damage the cocoa?
ga: Ani ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ tsɔ lɛ baafite ŋmei lɛ?

english: Yes, cassava grows bushy roots and tall leaves that can block sunlight and steal nutrients from young cocoa seedlings, so you must keep a safe distance between them.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ baai kakadaji ni baanyɛ atsĩ hulu la naa ni eju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ cacao tsei bibii amli. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ okwɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe nɔ yɛ cacao tsei enyɔ lɛ ateŋ.

english: Why do many farmers plant maize together with cassava on the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi babaoo duɔ ŋmãa kɛfataa ŋmãa he yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Maize grows fast and is harvested in a few months, while cassava takes longer to mature, allowing you to harvest food twice from the same plot of land without wasting space.
ga: Abɛi daa oya ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei heɔ be babaoo dani eshɛɔ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa niyenii shii enyɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni ofiteee he ko.

english: Is it possible to successfully cultivate crops like cocoa, cassava, and maize on a small piece of land?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo, ŋmei, kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ yɛ omanyeyeli mli?

english: Yes, small lands can be very productive if you organize your crops well, keep correct spacing, and combine short-term food crops with long-term crops like cocoa.
ga: Hɛɛ, kpokpaa bibioo ko baanyɛ awo yibii babaoo kɛji oto oŋmɔshi nii lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ. Ha sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ ni sa kɛ niyenii ni akwɛɔ be kukuoo mli kɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo afee ekome.

english: Can I squeeze more cocoa trees onto my small farm so I can get more cocoa pods?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mikɛ cacao babaoo awo ŋmɔ bibioo ko mli. Ani manyɛ mikɛ minɔ lɛ atsu nii koni maná kookoo ŋmɔtɔi babaoo?

english: If cocoa trees are squeezed too close together, their branches block sunlight from each other, resulting in weak trees with fewer cocoa pods than a farm with properly spaced trees.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ashɛre kookoo tsei lɛ ahe tsɔ lɛ, Amɛniji lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Enɛ haa kookoo tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ hu faaa fe ŋmɔji ni tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and turn pale yellow when they are planted close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When maize plants are crowded, they starve for sunlight and soil nutrients because they are competing with neighboring plants, causing them to grow weak stalks and yellow leaves.
ga: Beni ŋmãa tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛbɛ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ejaakɛ esa akɛ amɛkɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ abɔ akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: How do I know if the trees on my cocoa farm are too crowded?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tsei ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ebɔi tsɔ?

english: If your cocoa farm stays dark and damp inside, produces small pods, or catches black pod disease easily, it usually means the trees are planted too closely together.
ga: Kɛji akɛ o-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ mli ewo duŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli, eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii loo ŋmɔtɔ diŋ hela baanyɛ aba. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ adu tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn brown and drop off during the Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During Harmattan, dry winds and hot weather cause cocoa trees to lose water faster than their roots can take it up. The tree drops its leaves to conserve water and protect itself from dying of thirst.
ga: Yɛ harmattan beaŋ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa cacao tsei lɛ amli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛto nu ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ kumai he.

english: Why should I cut off some of the young shoots growing around the base of my plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishitoo lɛ

english: When too many shoots grow from the same root, they fight with the main stem for water, light, and nutrients. Leaving only one or two strong shoots helps the main tree produce much bigger plantain bunches.
ga: Beni ŋmeii ni jɛ shishifã kome mli lɛ fa tsɔ. Tso lɛ yibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ tso lɛ yitso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso titri lɛ ni ewo plantain jwɛi ni da kwraa.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food that builds big tubers under the ground. Staking lifts the leaves off the soil so they get sunlight and avoids diseases caused by wet ground.
ga: Sweet potato baai biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking woɔ baai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ hei ni nu yɔɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why are there small holes in my maize leaves and brown dirt inside the middle of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni muji ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar eating the young leaves inside the stalk. The brown dirt is its waste, which shows the pest is actively feeding on your maize.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ. Muji ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ji jwɛi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ o-corn lɛ miiye.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up and turning a mix of yellow and light green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni akɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse efutu mli lɛ?

english: This is Cassava Mosaic Disease, spread by tiny white insects called whiteflies. The disease damages the leaves, preventing the plant from making food and growing big roots.
ga: Hela nɛɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Kplukai bibii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Hela nɛɛ fiteɔ baai lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee niyenii, ni amɛshishifãi lɛ hu dara.

english: This is blossom-end rot, caused by irregular watering or a lack of calcium in the soil. When soil moisture changes too suddenly, the plant cannot send calcium to the fruit.
ga: Enɛ ji blossom end rot, ni nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo calcium ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsake trukaa tsɔ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ ekɛ calcium aba aduawai lɛ amli.

english: Pepper flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot, when the soil is too dry or flooded, or when there is too much nitrogen fertilizer in the soil.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ loo be mli ni nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant groundnuts or beans after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension agent lɛ woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei kɛji akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize uses up a lot of nitrogen from the soil, while groundnuts and beans have roots that put nitrogen back into the dirt, helping restore fertility naturally for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi ni haa nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ baa ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How do I know if my farm soil is tired and needs plant food or rest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ etɔ ni ehe miihia ni aye tsei niyenii loo hejɔɔmɔ?

english: Tired soil shows signs like crops growing slowly, leaves turning pale yellow early, low yields despite good rain, and soil that dries out and hardens very quickly after rainfall.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ baatsɔɔ okadii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo. Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ oya. Yibiiwoo ni baa shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi kpakpai kɛ shikpɔŋ ni gbɛ́ɔ ni ewaa oya waa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why should I cover the dirt around my crops with dry grass or dead leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo he ni ebɔle ehe lɛ he sũ? Dumɔ nibii ni jwɛi loo baai gboi yɔɔ mli.

english: Covering the soil, known as mulching, keeps the ground cool, stops water from drying up quickly in the sun, prevents weeds from growing, and turns into rich soil food as it rots.
ga: Ale mulching hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekagbi oya kɛji hulu la shɛ enɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni ebafeɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ nɔ beni efiteɔ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot withstand direct, harsh sunlight and hot temperatures. Leaving shade trees or planting plantains beside them creates a cool environment and retains soil moisture, protecting the young cocoa until it is strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ latsaa ni mli edɔ lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni ashiɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Ehaa shihilɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Buu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do I need to put wooden sticks or stakes next to my growing yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso loo tso awo emasɛi lɛ? Amɛduɔ sweet potato wain tsei

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight to manufacture food for building big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground so they catch sunlight easily and avoids diseases spread by splash-back from the soil.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji lɛ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni amɛná hulu la lɛ mlɛo. ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔ sũ ni shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ he.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of a maize plant usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps the plant stay green and grow larger ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen loo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo tsei lɛ amli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛtoi lɛ hu daraa.

english: When is the best time to put fertilizer on my crops so the heavy rain does not wash it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli? Koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akafɔ̃ tsei lɛ?

english: Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is moist but not during heavy rainfall. Covering or burying the fertilizer slightly near the plant's root zone keeps it in place so the plant can absorb it effectively.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi esaaa akɛ akɛwoɔ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ko ha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe loo afu lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hiɔ shi bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same land continuously drains specific nutrients and encourages maize pests to settle in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts returns nitrogen to the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ajieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ mli be fɛɛ be. ni owo ŋmãa mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛhi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Okɛ ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Enɛ baaha nitrogen lɛ aku esɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Cassava roots rot when excessive water remains trapped around them during heavy rains. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows extra water to drain away, keeping the roots dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu babaoo ebɔle amɛhe. yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli lɛ, ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nu babaoo hoɔ kɛyaa. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛhe wa

english: What is causing small ragged holes in the middle leaf whorls of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? Ring ko fee yɛ mi-baby corn baa lɛ teŋgbɛ.

english: Ragged holes in young maize plants are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding on tender leaves. Checking the farm early and applying appropriate control measures directly into the plant funnel stops them before severe crop damage occurs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli mra. ni okɛ gbɛi ni sa ni akɛkwɛɔ nɔ lɛ atsu nii tɛ̃ɛ yɛ tso lɛ shishi. Abaatsi ŋmɔ lɛ naa dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afite waa.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and becoming tiny and yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛji bibii ni amɛji ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Curled, small leaves on tomato plants are usually caused by a virus transmitted by tiny whiteflies. Controlling these insects early and removing infected plants prevents the disease from spreading across your entire crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ kɛbaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai bibii ni ekpɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Ni tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooojie lɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã onibii fɛɛ amli.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they suffer from high heat stress, irregular watering, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. Maintaining steady soil moisture and balanced nutrients helps the plant keep its flowers and turn them into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baawo fɔfɔi kɛji amɛna hulutsoo ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ niyenii ni sa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli ni etsakeɔ efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my plantain plants fall over so easily during heavy windstorms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ ahum be mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants fall easily if pests have damaged their roots, or if too many sucker shoots are competing for food around the main stem. Clearing unnecessary suckers strengthens the root system and anchors the plant firmly in the soil.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fite shishifãi lɛ. Aloo ŋmeii babaoo yɛ ni miitswa niyenii he akaŋ yɛ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ he. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni he ehiaaa lɛ, ewajeɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni ehaa tso lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shiŋŋ.

english: Young tree crops like cocoa have delicate leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under direct sunlight. Taller trees act like a giant protective umbrella, providing shade and keeping the soil cool and moist until the young crops are strong enough.
ga: Tsei bibii tamɔ kookoo yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai wuji, ni amɛhaa hulutsoo ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tsei bibii lɛ ahe waa bɔ ni sa.

english: How do tall trees on my farm protect my delicate food crops during heavy storms?
ga: Te tsei kakadaji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ buɔ miniyenii ni miduɔ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ ahe yɛ ahum ni naa wa waa mli lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Large canopy trees act as natural windbreaks and rain shields. They break the heavy impact of strong winds and pounding rain before it can snap stems or uproot vulnerable crops underneath them.
ga: Tsei wuji ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ he tsɔne. Amɛhaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he naagbai ni naa wa lɛ baa shi dani amɛfoɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi loo amɛjieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ.

english: How can I grow cassava and plantain for my family's fufu on the same land where I am planting cash crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ madu cassava kɛ plantains maha miweku lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ shika ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: You can intercrop by planting fast-growing food crops like cassava and plantain in the spaces between your young tree crop rows. This uses space efficiently, gives you food quickly, and provides temporary shade for your tree crops.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ tsei awo mli kɛtsɔ niyenii tsei ni daa oya tamɔ ŋmei kɛ plantains ni ooodu yɛ he ni yɔɔ odumɔ tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ kɛ he ko tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Ha bo niyenii oya ni oha otsei lɛ aná hulutsoo be kukuoo ko

english: Why should I plant different types of crops together instead of planting just one crop on my whole farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ he kome moŋ fe ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi kome yɛ miŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Mixing crops protects your livelihood. If disease or bad weather damages one crop, you can still harvest and sell the others. It also improves soil fertility and gives you food to eat while waiting for longer-term crops to mature.
ga: Nibii ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ buɔ oshihilɛ he. Kɛji hela loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni ehiii fite ŋmɔshi nibii Obaanyɛ okpa ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi hu ni ohɔ̃ɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii hu yaa hiɛ, ni ehaa onáa niyenii yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni onibii ni okɛwoɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: How can I keep getting food to eat from my land while waiting years for my main tree crops to yield harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maya nɔ maná niyenii kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ afii babaoo koni miŋmɔshi nibii titri ni yeɔ daa lɛ awo yibii?

english: By planting quick-yielding food crops like plantain, cocoyam, or cassava in between your main tree rows, you can harvest food and generate income continuously during the early years before your cash trees mature.
ga: Kɛtsɔ niyenii ni woɔ yibii oya, tamɔ plantain, cocoa, loo cassava ni aduɔ lɛ nɔ. otsoi wuji lɛ ateŋ Obaanyɛ oya nɔ okpa niyenii ni oná shika yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli. Dani oshika tso lɛ baakwɛ̃

english: Why do some of my green coconuts fall off the tree before the water inside is ready to drink?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ anuɔ lɛ?

english: Coconut trees drop young fruits early when they lack sufficient water, suffer from nutrient shortages in the soil, or are attacked by insect pests that weaken the fruit stem.
ga: Kokoo tsei shwieɔ aduawai bibii oya kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ amɛ. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa aduawai lɛ tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ lɛ tutuamɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers stay thin and tough instead of growing large and soft for making fufu?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe wa lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ agbo ni efee blɛoo kɛha flufu feemɔ?

english: Cassava roots need loose, well-drained soil and adequate moisture during their early growth stage. If the soil is too hard or compacted, the tubers cannot expand properly and remain small and fibrous.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni mli tse. Etsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. ni amɛná hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee mli Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ Tubers lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhi shi bibii ni amɛfee fiber.

english: What causes the water inside a young coconut to turn into thick dry meat as it stays longer on the tree?
ga: Mɛni haa nu ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: As a coconut matures, the tree converts the liquid water inside into solid endosperm (the white meat) to store energy for seed germination. Harvesting early yields liquid for drinking, while harvesting late gives solid meat for oil.
ga: Kɛji ŋmei lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Tso lɛ tsakeɔ nu ni ji nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ewoɔ endosperm (loo yɛŋ) ni wa mli koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato kɛha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ. Nikpamɔ mra baaha aná nu ni anuɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli wa ni eyɛ fɔ.

english: How does having a dense canopy of shade trees help stop weeds from growing on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ hulutsoo be ni mli wa yeɔ ebuaa ni ekpaa jwɛi ni shwereɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Most weeds need direct sunlight to germinate and grow rapidly. A thick umbrella of leaves from shade trees blocks sunlight from reaching the ground, naturally slowing down weed growth and saving you clearing labor.
ga: Jwɛi babaoo he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛdara oya. Tsei lɛ ahe baai ni mli tse lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ shikpɔŋ. Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ehaa jwɛi lɛ adalɛ baa shi ni ehaaa oná be ni okɛjieɔ jwɛi lɛ.

english: Why do plantain leaves droop and turn yellow during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have large broad leaves that lose water very quickly in high heat. When water in the soil is low, the plant naturally droops its leaves to reduce water loss and protect itself from drying out.
ga: Plantains yɛ baai agboi ni mli kwɔ ni kɛ́ akɛwo la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, nu lɛ fiteɔ oya waa. Kɛ nu fioo pɛ eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize farm turning yellow instead of green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen in the soil or are getting waterlogged from poor drainage, which prevents the roots from absorbing key nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu eyi mli obɔ yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ.

english: Cassava tubers rot when soil holds too much water during heavy rains or when infected by root-rot fungi, which soft-rots the roots if the land does not drain well.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ shwie nu babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa mli loo kɛji shishifãi fitemɔ hela lɛ emɔ lɛ, ni no haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieee nu jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when heat is too intense or when the plant suffers from irregular watering, causing stress that stops proper pollination.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji la lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni tso lɛ naa amanehulu yɛ nu ni afɔɔɔ lɛ daa lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ kɛ haomɔ ni haa pollination lɛ esaaa baa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when planted directly under full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and shallow roots that burn and dry out easily under harsh sunlight; they require shade plants like plantains to shelter them until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shãa oya ni egbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ plantains koni amɛha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: What causes armyworms to suddenly clear my entire corn field within a few days?
ga: Mɛni ha cutworms kpata mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ fɛɛ mli yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli?

english: Armyworms hatch quickly in large numbers during hot weather and feed rapidly on the leaf whorls of young corn, multiplying before farmers notice them.
ga: Asraafoi amli ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ oya yɛ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ Ebaalɛɛ mli dani okwaafoi lɛ baayɔse.

english: What should I do immediately when I see one of my vegetable plants looking sick?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ mina akɛ hela mɔ mitsei lɛ eko?

english: Remove and burn or bury the infected plant away from the farm right away to prevent pests or diseases from spreading to the neighboring healthy plants.
ga: Amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ojie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni oshã loo ofu amɛ yɛ he ko ni kɛ ŋmɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ koni tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai akagbɛ ashwã tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the specific nutrients that plant needs from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to live permanently in the dirt.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tso lɛ lɛ jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds very close together to fit more crops on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too closely forces the plants to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin stems and a poor overall harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛbɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei bibii kɛ ŋmaa fɛɛ ni ehiii.

english: Apply fertilizer early in the morning or late in the afternoon when the soil is moist, so heat does not scorch the plant roots.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli leebi loo shwane mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ, koni la ni tsoɔ lɛ akashã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ.

english: How do I know if the ground has enough water to plant my crops after the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ nɔ yɛ hɔmɔ sɛɛ?

english: The ground is ready when heavy rains soak deep into the root zone and the soil stays moist and easily crumbles in your hand without forming sticky mud.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa bote shishifãi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ. Ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi ni efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli ni ekɛ muji ni shwieɔ shi baaa.

english: Rice plants are uniquely adapted to grow in wet conditions, and keeping standing water in the field controls weeds while keeping the soil at a stable temperature for steady plant growth.
ga: Afee ŋmãa tsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ mli. Ni nu ni damɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ ni abaakwɛ nɔ lɛ baaye jwɛi anɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo be fɛɛ be koni tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: How long does a rice crop take from planting seeds to harvest in Ghana?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani aduɔ ŋmãa kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui amli kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ mli yɛ Ghana?

english: Most common rice varieties in Ghana take between 3 to 4 months (90 to 120 days) to fully mature and be ready for harvesting.
ga: Omɔ henɔi ni afɔɔ naa yɛ Ghana lɛ heɔ aaafee nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 (gbii 90 kɛyashi 120) dani ekwɛɔ ni efeɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ.

english: What causes my rice leaves to turn yellow early before the crop matures?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-rice baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ oya dani tso lɛ daa?

english: Yellowing leaves in young rice usually mean the plants lack nitrogen fertilizer, are choking from poor water drainage, or are suffering from insect damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii amli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii. Akpãtãa nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ loo kooloi bibii ahewɔ ni shwieɔ shi

english: Can I plant rice twice on the same field in one year?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa shii enyɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli yɛ afi kome mli?

english: Yes, if you have good irrigation during the dry season, you can harvest two crops of rice from the same land within twelve months.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ oyɛ nu kpakpa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Obaanyɛ okpa ŋmãa tsei enyɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ nyɔji nyɔŋma kɛ enyɔ mli.

english: If I expand my farm from one acre to five acres, will my crop yield increase automatically?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli shwere kɛjɛ acre kome mli kɛtee acre enumɔ Ani miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ baaya hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Increasing land size only increases yield if you maintain good seed quality, timely weeding, and sufficient fertilizer across the entire area; otherwise, crops may yield less per acre due to lack of care.
ga: Oshikpɔŋ lɛ dalɛ ni oooha eya hiɛ lɛ baaha yibiiwoo aya hiɛ pɛ kɛji akɛ ohiɛ dumɔwui kpakpai amli. Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa aha yɛ jɛmɛ fɛɛ Kɛ jeee nakai lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ awo yibii fioo yɛ acre kome mli yɛ nɔkwɛmɔ ni bɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do commercial farms with hundreds of acres get higher crop yields than my small plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jarayeli ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ acre ohai abɔ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe mishikpɔŋ bibioo lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Large commercial farms use certified seeds, mechanized land preparation, and precise fertilizer timing, allowing crops to grow strong and uniformly across the field.
ga: Jarayeli ŋmɔji wuji kɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli tsuɔ nii. Shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ kɛtsɔ tsɔnei anɔ kɛ be pɔtɛɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ Yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa waa ni amɛfeɔ ekome yɛ ŋmɔji amli.

english: Why do my crops mature unevenly when I plant a larger piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ kɛ́ midu shikpɔŋ wulu ko nɔ lɛ?

english: On larger fields, soil fertility and moisture levels vary from spot to spot, causing plants in richer areas to grow faster than those in poorer spots.
ga: yɛ he ko ni da nɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ he fɛɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ hei ni nii yɔɔ nii babaoo lɛ daraa oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ hei ni ohiafoi yɔɔ lɛ.

english: How does planting crops in straight rows help them grow better than scattering seeds?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni aduɔ lɛ?

english: Planting in straight rows ensures each plant gets adequate sunlight, water, and nutrients while making it easier to weed without damaging the crop.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ abaajie jwɛi ni efiteee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow faster than my crops when I clear a large new plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ́ mijie he ko hee ni da lɛ?

english: Clearing land exposes hidden weed seeds in the soil to sunlight and rain, allowing them to germinate quickly and compete with young crops for food and water.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa jwɛi dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ naa hulu la kɛ nugbɔ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛkɛ tsei bibii yeɔ akaŋ yɛ niyenii kɛ nu he.

english: How does clearing a large piece of land affect the nutrients my crops need?
ga: Te he ko ni da ni ajieɔ lɛ saa niyenii ni he hiaa mi tsei lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Clearing large areas can wash away the fertile topsoil during heavy rains, leaving less plant food in the soil unless organic manure or fertilizers are added back.
ga: Hei wuji ni ajieɔ lɛ baanyɛ ajie sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei aniyenii fioo pɛ eshwɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ja akɛ organic fertilizer loo fertilizer fata he ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crop seedlings need to stay in the nursery bed for up to a month before moving them to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mi dumɔwui lɛ ahi ŋmɔ mli dumɔwui lɛ amli kɛyashi nyɔŋ kome dani adu amɛ awo ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young seedlings need time in a protected nursery to build strong roots and thick stems. Keeping them in the nursery bed for about three to four weeks ensures they are mature and tough enough to survive the harsher conditions of the main open field.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ he miihia be yɛ he ko ni abuɔ he koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa kɛ ŋmeii ni mli wa. Kɛ́ akɛ amɛ wo gbekɛbii akwɛmɔhe lɛ otsii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ lɛ, ebaaha amɛdara ni amɛhe awa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ wulu ni mli tse lɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: Why should I prepare a raised nursery bed instead of planting my seeds directly into flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni awó nɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui tɛ̃ɛ yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Raised beds keep the soil loose, prevent heavy rains from washing away delicate seeds, and allow excess water to drain quickly so the root systems do not rot.
ga: Saji ni awó nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli tseɔ. Etsiɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Ni ha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ oya koni shishifãi lɛ akafite.

english: Why is it important to cover my nursery bed with dry grass right after sowing my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi aha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔhei lɛ anɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni adu lɛ?

english: Dry grass acts as a protective blanket. It keeps the soil cool and moist under the hot sun and prevents heavy rain droplets from knocking seeds out of the soil.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni edɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. ni etsĩ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekaha dumɔwui lɛ akaje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I scoop out my young seedlings from the nursery bed without snapping their delicate roots?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ majie tsei bibii kɛjɛ tsei akwɛmɔhe lɛ ni mifolɔɔɔ amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ amli?

english: Always water the nursery bed thoroughly before lifting seedlings, and scoop deep under the roots with soil attached. Pulling dry seedlings directly by the stem snaps fragile roots and damages the plant.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, ha ŋmɔ mli saatso lɛ nɔ nu jogbaŋŋ dani owó dumɔwui lɛ anɔ. ni okɛ sũ lɛ afɔ shishifãi lɛ ashishi shɔŋŋ, ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hu akpɛtɛ he Dumɔwui ni egbi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baafite shishifãi ni waaa lɛ ni ebaafite tso lɛ.

english: Why are the stems of my young seedlings snapping into small pieces so easily when I handle them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mitso lɛ shishifã lɛ fãa bibii bibii oya kɛ́ mikɛ mihe wo mli lɛ?

english: Stems become brittle and break easily if the plants are thirsty or handled during the heat of the afternoon. Handling plants in the cool morning after watering makes stems flexible and resistant to breaking.
ga: Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efoɔ oya kɛji kumai ye tso lɛ loo kɛji akɛ atsa lɛ yɛ shwane mli latsaa be mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ tsu nii yɛ leebi ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi yɛ nu ni awo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha eshishifã lɛ afee mlɛo ni enyɛŋ efo.

english: Why do my crops look weak and droopy for a few days right after I move them from the nursery to the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ gbii fioo komɛi beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: This is called transplant shock. The seedling is stressed from having its roots disturbed, but it will bounce back once the roots establish themselves in the fresh field soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ he shoofeemɔ. Dumɔwui lɛ haoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi ni gbalaa amɛnaa lɛ mli. Shi ebaaku esɛɛ kɛji shishifãi lɛ ema shi yɛ shikpɔŋ hee nɔ pɛ.

english: Why do some farmers mix broken rice husks or organic materials into the soil of their seedbeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ ŋmãa loo nibii krokomɛi ni wala yɔɔ mli futuɔ amɛ ŋmɔji lɛ amli sũ lɛ?

english: Rice husks and organic matter loosen heavy clay soil. Putting them in the bed improves air movement and makes it much easier to scoop out plants smoothly without tearing roots.
ga: Omɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ sũ ni tsii lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okɛwo saatso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ. Ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa akɛ abaajie tso lɛ mli ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni agbalaaa shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Is it better to plant my entire farm at once or split the planting into two separate batches?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ shikome loo aaaja dumɔ lɛ mli awo kui sɔrɔtoi enyɔ mli?

english: Planting in two parts a few weeks apart protects you from unpredictable weather and ensures you harvest your crops gradually rather than having everything mature all at once.
ga: Tsei ni ooodu yɛ hei enyɔ ni otsii fioo pɛ kɛ amɛhe kpaa gbee lɛ baabu ohe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ ahe. ni oye obua ni okwɛ koni okpa ŋmɔshi nibii fiofio Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha nɔ fɛɛ nɔ aho shikome.

english: How deep down under the soil should I put organic materials when preparing my plant bed?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashɛ he ni eshɛɔ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ miisaa dumɔwui?

english: Organic materials should be mixed into the top 10 to 15 centimeters of soil where young roots feed. Placing it at this depth retains moisture near the root zone without suffocating the plant.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli afutu sɛntimita 10 kɛyashi 15 awo sũ ni shishifãi bibii yeɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛwo nɛkɛ he ni mli kwɔ nɛɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi he ni bɛŋkɛ shishifã lɛ ni ehaaa tso lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why are weeds growing much faster than my crop seedlings on the nursery bed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe mi tso dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are naturally aggressive and steal water and nutrients from the soil faster than domestic crops. Clearing them early prevents them from crowding out and starving your young seedlings.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ feɔ basabasa yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe shia tsei. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkabɔle odumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe ni hɔmɔ baaye amɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, a key food crops need to grow green and strong. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like urea or adding compost fixes this issue.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni niyenii ni akɛyeɔ nii titri lɛ akwɛ̃ ni eyɛ hewalɛ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the same land where I grow my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil through their roots, acting as a natural fertilizer for maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmãa

english: Why shouldn't I spread dry fertilizer on my crop field right before a heavy downpour of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi shwieɔ midumɔi lɛ anɔ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ aba?

english: Heavy rainfall washes the fertilizer off the farm or deep into the soil beyond the reach of roots, wasting your money and labor.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔji amli ŋmɔshi nibii loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he. Ehaa ofiteɔ shika kɛ nitsumɔ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I plant them in open sunlight without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo be bɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that dry out easily in direct sun. They need shade crops like plantains to protect them until their roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ, amɛgbiɔ oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ plantains koni ebu amɛhe kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baawa.

english: Why do I need to put wooden stakes next to my yam vines as they begin to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso ama mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ masɛi beni ebɔi kwɛ̃mɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to lift their leaves up toward sunlight. Staking helps leaves catch light, giving the plant energy to make bigger yam tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ miikwɔ wain tso ko ni esa akɛ ewo ebaai lɛ anɔ koni hulu lɛ ajie ehe kpo lɛ nɔ. Staking haa baai lɛ náa la. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛduɔ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: When too many suckers grow together, they fight for the same nutrients and water. Pruning extra suckers lets the main plant produce bigger, heavier plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii lɛ fee ekome kɛdara tsɔ Amɛbaatswa akaŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo plantain tsei wuji ni tsii.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when plants face heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients, which prevents the flowers from successfully forming fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ haaa tomato fɔfɔi lɛ awo yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do small caterpillars eat the tender middle leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai bibii lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that feeds on the central funnel of maize plants. Catching them early allows you to protect the crop's main growing point.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ. Ni ooomɔ lɛ mra Ebaaha onyɛ obu hei titri ni onibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start to rot underground when the rain is too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot in water-logged soil because excess water starves the roots of air and encourages fungal rot. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps water drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ hewalɛ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Why do weeds on my farm cause my crops to grow slowly and produce small harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crops, effectively starving your plants during their growth stages.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ yeɔ ehe hɔmɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni edaa lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot tolerate direct heat and sunlight because their leaves dry out quickly. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains alongside them protects the seedlings from burning and keeps the soil moist until the cocoa is strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa, ejaakɛ baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ awo amɛhe lɛ, ebaabu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he, ni ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ mli baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed to make food and grow green. Adding poultry manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer restores their green color and boosts growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Nɔ ni ji niyenii mli hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛfee niyenii ni akɛkwɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi ashishi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ wo mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves start turning yellow and dropping off, typically around 9 to 12 months after planting. You can carefully dig up one test plant to check the tuber size before harvesting the entire farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsu kaa tso kome he nii koni okwɛ bulb lɛ dalɛ dani okpa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch enough sunlight for making food. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp soil, preventing fungal diseases and allowing the plant to direct its energy into growing big underground tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha nihoomɔ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsi fungal helai anaa ni oha tsei kɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why does my land produce fewer crops each year if I keep farming on the same spot without resting it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo daa afi kɛji mitee nɔ matsu okwaayeli yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni mikɛ mihe wooo mli lɛ?

english: Crops suck out vital minerals from the earth every single season. If you do not replace these nutrients using compost, animal manure, or chemical fertilizers, or by letting the land rest, the soil becomes tired and empty.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ shwieɔ shika tsuru ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii amli lɛ tsakeee niyenii nɛɛ najiaŋ, loo kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha ejɔɔ ehe lɛ nɔ lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ efolo.

english: Why are small worms eating holes in the middle leaves of my maize, and how do I save them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua amɛ?

english: Those are Fall Armyworms, which love to hide inside the growing center of maize plants. Checking your farm early and spraying safe biopesticides or neem water directly into the leaf centers kills them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Amɛji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe yɛ hei ni ŋmãa tsei lɛ daa lɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe loo neem nu ni oooshwie baai lɛ ateŋ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baagbe amɛ dani amɛbaafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Is it safe to plant my crops right after the very first rain of the year arrives?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ eba lɛ?

english: It is safer to wait until the rain becomes steady over two or three weeks. The very first rain is often followed by a long hot dry spell that bakes seeds in the soil before their roots can establish.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ aba shi yɛ otsii enyɔ loo etɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni mli edɔɔ ni shãa dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do weeds in my vegetable farm cause my main crops to stay small and thin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiha mi-ŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ miifee bibii ni amɛhe efee shoo lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm, stealing water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your crops. Removing weeds early gives your vegetables full access to what they need to expand.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli, ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nii lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa o-vegetables lɛ náa hegbɛ fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences stress from uneven watering or sudden hot dry weather. Keeping the soil consistently moist around the roots helps the flowers stay attached and form fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi ni edɔ trukaa lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha ebɔle he lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ Shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do experienced farmers recommend planting cowpea beans together with maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛ tsina ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa afata ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes, which means their roots pull free nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. This feeds the soil naturally, helping the neighboring maize grow stronger without needing extra bought fertilizer.
ga: Cowpea ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas ni aheee nɔ ko kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni edara waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe ŋmãa kroko kɛfata he.

english: Why do sweet potatoes harvested from rich soil taste sweeter than those grown in loose, sandy soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ nɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ fe nɔ ni adu yɛ ŋã nɔ lɛ?

english: Soil with plenty of organic matter holds onto key nutrients like potassium, which crops use to produce and store natural sugars. Sandy soil lets water and nutrients wash away quickly, resulting in less flavorful crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɔɔ nɔ lɛ toɔ niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ potassium, ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli sugars ni amɛkɛtoɔ lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii hoɔ oya. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe ŋɔɔ fioo.

english: How does adding manure or compost to my farm affect the taste and size of my vegetables?
ga: Te ŋmei loo ŋmei ni akɛwoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ saa mi-aduawai lɛ ahe fɛo kɛ amɛdalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Compost feeds the soil with balanced nutrients over time, helping crops develop stronger roots and better flavor compounds. Healthy soil nutrients translate directly into larger, more flavorful, and nutritious produce.
ga: Kompost baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni sa yɛ be ni sa mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni mli wa ni amɛnuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Atsɔɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kpakpa mli lɛ shishi kɛfeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii wuji. Eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ babaoo ni eyɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ tɛ̃ɛ

english: Can foreign crops like cabbages and carrots grow as well in Ghana as our local crops?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu maŋsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kaabe kɛ karɔt yɛ Ghana tamɔ wɔmaŋ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yes, many foreign crops can grow well in Ghana if given the right conditions, such as planting them in well-drained soil, giving them enough shade, or growing them during cooler months or in higher altitude regions.
ga: Hɛɛ, maŋsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo baanyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana kɛji akɛ aha amɛ shihilɛ ni sa, tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha hulutsoo be ni fa bɔ ni sa Loo dumɔ yɛ nyɔji ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli loo hei ni ŋwɛi ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my introduced vegetable seeds need more frequent watering than my local cassava plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni awo mi-vegetable dumɔwui ni mikɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ anɔ nu shii abɔ fe yucca tsei ni yɔɔ mimaŋ lɛ?

english: Local crops like cassava have deep root systems adapted to dry conditions, while many introduced crops have shallow roots that dry out fast in warm Ghanaian soil and need constant soil moisture.
ga: Kuu mli tsei tamɔ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni nyɛɔ amɛtsuɔ nii yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ amli. Yɛ be mli ni tsei babaoo ni akɛba jɛmɛ lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ Ghana shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ni ebiɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i be fɛɛ be lɛ.

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves to conserve water when the air and soil become hot and dry. The plant goes partially dormant above ground while keeping the edible tubers safe underground.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛhiɛ nu mli kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ ni amɛgbi. Tsei lɛ fã ko ŋmɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛhaa ŋmeii ni ayeɔ lɛ hiɔ shi shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and turn yellow during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl to protect themselves from losing too much water in intense heat, or because tiny sap-sucking pests are attacking the underside of the leaf. Shade and proper pest management help keep them flat and green.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo akafite yɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ mli. Aloo akɛni kooloi bibii shwieɔ mliki lɛ hewɔ. Etutuaa baai lɛ ashishigbɛ. Shade ni sa kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over when the bunch of fruit starts growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi beni aduawai akui lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Plantain roots grow shallow in the soil. As the fruit bunch gets heavy, the plant becomes top-heavy, so strong winds or wet, soft soil can pull the roots out unless you prop up the trunk with a strong wooden stick.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fioo. Beni aduawai akuu lɛ tsii lɛ Tso lɛ baafee tsii waa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni efɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbala shishifãi lɛ. Ja okɛ tso ni wa fiɔ tsɔne lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees drop many of their flowers before pods form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔii babaoo dani ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees produce far more flowers than they can support. If the tree experiences hot sun exposure, lack of water, or poor pollination by tiny insects, it sheds excess flowers to save energy.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ nɔ. Kɛji tso ko shɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ, nu bɛ mli, loo kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ ekɛ fɔfɔii lɛ awo mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaashwie fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine lɛ koni ekɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil, often washed away by heavy rains. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure restores their deep green color and healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. ni bei pii lɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ amɛ kɛyaa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni mli kwɔ ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why do my garden eggs become hard and bitter if I leave them on the plant too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: As garden eggs mature fully on the stem, the seeds harden and the plant produces natural bitter compounds to protect the seeds for reproduction. Harvesting them while still firm and glossy gives the best taste.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ waɔ ni tso lɛ feɔ nɔ ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe koni amɛfɔ. Nikpamɔ be mli ni eyɛ shiŋŋ lolo ni ekpɛɔ lɛ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ baa.

english: Why should I wait for the rainy season to settle fully before planting my maize instead of planting right after the very first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ omɛ ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba naagbee dani odu ŋmãa moŋ fe ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: The first rain often moistens only the surface soil. If a dry spell follows immediately after, your seeds will germinate and quickly dry out and die. Waiting for steady rainfall ensures the soil has deep moisture to support root development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ pɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛji hɔmɔ he okadii ba amrɔ nɔŋŋ Dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛgbiɔ oya ni amɛgboiɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ waa koni eye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdara.

english: Why do we plant cassava by burying pieces of stem instead of planting seeds from the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔduɔ ŋmei kɛtsɔ ŋmeii lɛ ni wɔfuɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni wɔduɔ dumɔwui kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava stem cuttings sprout faster and grow into stronger plants that produce large roots identical to the healthy mother plant. Growing cassava from actual seeds takes much longer and often results in low-yielding crops.
ga: Cassava ni afo lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya ni ebaada ni etsɔ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni shishifãi wuji yɔɔ mli tamɔ fɔlɔ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ kɛjɛɔ anɔkwa dumɔwui amli lɛ heɔ be babaoo ni bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yibiiwoo ni baa shi.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct sunlight and intense heat. They need temporary shade from larger trees or crops like plantains to protect their tender leaves from burning and to keep the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be kukuoo ko kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains adɛŋ koni ebu baai bibii ahe kɛjɛ shãa he, ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do I need to train my yam vines onto wooden sticks as they grow taller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsɔseɔ sweet potato wain tsei yɛ tsei anɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight on their leaves to make food that feeds the growing tuber underground. Lifting the vines off the wet ground on stakes keeps leaves healthy, exposed to light, and safe from rotting.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii ni haa ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ owó wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ hei ni efɔ lɛ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ yibii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ, ni la ashɛ nɔ, ni ehi shi shweshweeshwe koni ekafite.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when exposed to extreme heat or irregular watering because the plant gets stressed and tries to save energy. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tomato tsei lɛ miihao ni amɛmiitao ni amɛbu hewalɛ he. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow at the tips and dying off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛnaagbɛ ni amɛmiigboi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves on maize are a clear sign that the soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to make green leaves. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer restores their green color.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow poorly if I plant maize on the exact same spot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows pests to build up. Rotating maize with crops like groundnuts or beans restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei tsakeɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it beneficial to plant cowpeas or beans in between my rows of maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ aaadu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, which acts as a free natural fertilizer for the neighboring maize crop while covering the ground to suppress weeds.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ, ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli koni jwɛi akabote mli.

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for space, light, and soil nutrients. Even with good rain, weeds steal the food from the soil before your crop roots can reach it, stunt your crop's growth.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha he ko, la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ miinɛ moŋ, shi ehi. Jwɛi hu juɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ he. Enɛ haa onibii ni oduɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the juice out of young leaves, or passing on a virus. Controlling these insects early keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Ekɛ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ shwieɔ shi loo egbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa.

english: Why do my young maize leaves curl up and turn brown during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When the sun is very hot and there is no rain, maize leaves roll up tightly to protect themselves from losing water. If the soil stays completely dry for too long, the leaves cannot get enough moisture to survive, causing them to turn brown and die.
ga: Kɛ hulu lɛ mli edɔ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe shi shiŋŋ koni nu akafite. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ Baai lɛ naaa ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛhi shi. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ebaatsɔ blɔfo ni ebaagbo.

english: I noticed small black spots spread across my pepper leaves like a skin rash and now the leaves are dropping off. What causes this?
ga: Miyɔse he ko diŋ bibioo ko. Egbɛɔ eshwaa mi-pepper baai lɛ anɔ tamɔ hewolo nɔ tsɔi. Ni agbɛnɛ baai lɛ egbee shi. Mɛni kɛ enɛ ba?

english: Those spots are usually caused by a fungal infection that attacks leaves when moisture stays on them for too long or when splash from rain transfers dirt onto the leaves. Leaving space between plants and avoiding splashing soil onto leaves helps prevent it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni tutuaa baa lɛ kɛji ŋmɔtɔ hi baa lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɛɛ baa. Aloo beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ feɔ muji yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ oshi gbɛ yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ sũ ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Why does my cassava produce huge green leaves above the ground, but when I harvest, the tubers underneath are tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ hiɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi kɛ́ akpa Yitso ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ji bibioo?

english: This happens when the soil has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium. Nitrogen feeds leaf growth, but crops need potassium to push energy down into the ground to swell the roots into thick cassava tubers.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii ni haa baa lɛ daa. Shi tsei he miihia potassium koni ekɛ hewalɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ adara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmei ni mli tse.

english: Why do experienced cocoa farmers tell me to plant plantains on the farm at the same time I plant young cocoa shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ madu plantains yɛ eŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be kome too mli ni mikɛ kookoo bibii miidu lɛ?
