english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate direct, harsh sunlight when they are small. Plantain trees grow very quickly and have broad leaves that create protective shade and keep the air cool while the young cocoa trees get established.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ beni amɛdarako lɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo baa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: My tomato plants produce plenty of bright yellow flowers, but the flowers keep falling off without growing into tomatoes. Why is that?
ga: Mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ babaoo. Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ tomatoi. Mɛni he je nɛ e ba jã a?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences heat stress or extreme dryness. When the weather gets too hot or water is irregular, the plant drops its flowers to save energy rather than trying to feed fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo amɛhe egbi waa. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo nu lɛ ejaaa Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtao niyenii kɛha aduawai.

english: If I plant my seeds very close together so I can fit more crops on my land, why do my plants stay thin and give a smaller yield?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa koni manyɛ makwɛ tsei babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hu? Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Crops planted too close together fight with each other for light, water, and nutrients in the soil. When they are crowded, no single plant gets enough food to grow thick stems or produce large crops.
ga: Tsei ni adu yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Beni tsei ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ yɔɔ lɛ Tso ko bɛ ni nine shɛɛɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha eshishifãi ni eyi obɔ lɛ akwɛ̃ loo ewo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Why do tiny black insects appear in my stored maize bags after a few weeks even if I tie the bags tightly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii diji No hewɔ lɛ ejie ehe kpo yɛ mi-ŋmã kotoku ni mikɛto lɛ mli yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ kotoku lɛ fĩ shi shiŋŋ moŋ

english: These insects are grain weevils, and their eggs are often laid on the corn while it is still in the field. If the grain is not dried completely until it is hard before storing, the moisture lets those hidden eggs hatch and multiply inside the bag.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ ji dumɔwui amli ŋmeii. Ni bei pii lɛ, amɛwoɔ ŋmãa be mli ni eyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo lɛ. Kɛji akɛ dumɔwui lɛ egbiko kwraa ni amɛhe waaa dani akɛtoɔ lɛ, Fɛ̃i lɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ fɔɔ ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ kotoku lɛ mli.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my yam mounds with dry leaves or grass after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egboi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi sweet potato lɛ he lɛ nɔ beni midu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves creates a protective blanket called mulch. Mulch stops the hot sun from drying out the dirt, keeping the soil moist and cool so the yam roots can grow continuously.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch lɛ baa. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akagbi muji lɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Bɔni afee ni sweet potato shishifãi lɛ aya nɔ ada.

english: Why do my small nursery seedlings grow very tall and skinny, and then fall over and die before I can transplant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe ejɔ nɛkɛ lɛ? Kɛkɛ ni egbo dani akɛwo mɔ kroko mli.

english: Seedlings grow tall and weak when they do not receive enough sunlight. They stretch out desperately to find light, making their stems too thin and weak to support their own weight.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ daraa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ kɛji amɛnaaa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa. Amɛkpã amɛhe kɛ hiɛdɔɔ ni amɛyɔɔ kɛha la lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ mlɛo tsɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ egbɔjɔmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my vegetables look pale and weak even when I apply fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi-aduawai lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds have strong, fast-growing roots that steal fertilizer and water away from your crops. If weeds are not cleared first, they will consume the plant food before your vegetables can reach it.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni wa ni daa oya ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛji ojieee jwɛi lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Amɛbaaye tso niyenii lɛ dani aduawai lɛ ashɛ he.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow and drying up around the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily in direct sun. They need shade trees like plantains nearby to block harsh sunlight and keep the surrounding air and soil moist while they establish roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ koni amɛtsi hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa. ni eha kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable plants wilt in the afternoon sun even though I water them every morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa leebi moŋ?

english: During hot afternoons, water evaporates from the leaves faster than the roots can suck water up from the ground. This creates temporary water stress, but the plants usually bounce back as the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli Nu lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ kɛ nu he haomɔ baa be kukuoo ko mli. Shi tso lɛ sɛɛ foɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: Why is my maize crop turning light yellow instead of staying deep green while still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ beni eji gbekɛ lolo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, or the ground is waterlogged, which stops the roots from absorbing nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is my maize growing very tall with big leaves but taking so long to show tassels and cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai wuji shi ekɛ be babaoo jieɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ akpo lɛ?

english: When maize gets too much nitrogen fertilizer or is planted too close together, it puts all its energy into growing tall leaves and stems instead of producing tassels and cobs early.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ loo adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ehe tsɔ lɛ ŋmãa kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeŋmɛɛ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ahe oya

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting under the soil before it is even time to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani be po shɛɔ ni abaakpa lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers rot when heavy rains make the soil stay soaked in water for too long without good drainage, allowing water-loving fungi to attack the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ ta nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu kpakpa hoɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni sumɔɔ nu lɛ tutuaa shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping all their flowers without forming any small tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛwooo tomato bibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when the weather gets too hot or when watering is uneven. Extremely hot afternoons dry out the flowers before they can form fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo akɛ nu haa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Gbi gbɛkɛ ni mli edɔ waa Fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ dani amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are my stored seed yams starting to sprout in the barn before the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Yams naturally break dormancy and sprout when warmth and humidity rise in storage, because the tuber senses that the season for growing is approaching regardless of whether rain has fallen.
ga: Sweet potatoes baafo shihilɛ mli ni ekwɛ̃ be mli ni hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i yaa hiɛ yɛ nitoohe lɛ. Ejaakɛ yitso lɛ baale akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ miibɛŋkɛ, nugbɔ nɛ loo enɛɛɛ jio.

english: Curled, wrinkled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids hiding under the leaves and sucking out the plant juices.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa.

english: Why do my full-grown plantain trees fall over easily when light wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain ni eda lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ fioo ko tswa lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and can be destroyed underground by microscopic worms or root borers, destroying the tree's anchor in the soil under heavy bunches.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni ŋmeii bibii loo shishifãi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baanyɛ afite amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Enɛ fiteɔ tso lɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ sũ ni yɔɔ jwɛi ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ shishi lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do the pods on my cowpea plants get tiny holes in them before they dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Dani ebaagbi?

english: Holes in cowpea pods are made by pod borer caterpillars that hatch from eggs laid inside the flowers and eat their way through the fresh pods.
ga: Pod borer ŋmeii ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ amɛ gbɛ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii heei lɛ amli lɛ ji mɛi ni feɔ bu yɛ tsina ŋmeii amli.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full, harsh sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and have large leaves that provide living shade and keep the soil moist while the cocoa trees grow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Maize leaves usually turn yellow when there is not enough nitrogen in the soil or when too much water stays around the roots. Adding poultry manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo kɛ́ nu babaoo ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi ashishifã loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I avoid burning the bush on my land after clearing it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ brɔshi ni ashãa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni ajie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Burning destroys rich topsoil nutrients and kills useful soil organisms like earthworms. Leaving the cleared plants to rot into the ground turns them into natural manure that feeds your crops.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ mli lɛ. ni amɛfiteɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii. Tsei ni ajie lɛ ni oooŋmɛ gbɛ ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa onibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do agricultural officers instruct us not to plant cocoa trees too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he onukpai lɛ gu kookoo dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When trees are planted too close, their roots struggle against each other for food and water. The thick branches also block air movement, creating damp conditions that allow black pod disease to spread fast.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tso shishifãi kɛ amɛhe yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Niji ni mli tse lɛ hu tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ naa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa, ni no haa black pod hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: What causes small holes in my tomato leaves, and how can I stop it?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ tomato baai anɔ Ni te aaafee tɛŋŋ akpa?

english: Small holes are made by insect pests like caterpillars feeding on the plant. You can protect your crop by spraying neem oil extract or proper organic pesticides early in the morning.
ga: Buji bibii lɛ jɛɔ kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ tsei lɛ amli. Obaanyɛ obu onibii ahe kɛtsɔ neem fɔ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ wala mli lɛ ni oooshwie nɔ leebi lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I know if my cassava leaves are dry because of heat or because of disease?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ hulutsoo loo hela hewɔ ni ŋmei baa lɛ egbi lɛ?

english: In dry heat, cassava leaves drop off cleanly to save water. If a plant is diseased, you will see yellow wavy patterns or curled leaves caused by viral diseases spread by small insects like whiteflies.
ga: Kɛ akɛ la ni mli egbi miitsu nii lɛ Cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ koni ekɛbu nu he. Kɛji hela mɔ tso lɛ, abaana ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo baai ni ebɔle ehe. Virus hela ko ni koolooi bibii tamɔ whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why is it necessary for me to remove weeds early instead of waiting until harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ?

english: Weeds grow quickly and steal fertilizer, sunlight, and water away from your crops. Removing them early gives your crops all the nourishment they need to produce a good yield.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, hulu la, kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Ajieɔ mra Ebaaha onibii lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetable garden in the morning or in the afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooha aduawai abɔɔ lɛ nɔ nu leebi loo shwane?

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the hot afternoon sun evaporates the water before it reaches the roots, while evening watering leaves plants wet overnight and encourages fungal growth.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani eshɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni oooha tso lɛ gbɛkɛ lɛ baaha tso lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ gbɛkɛ muu lɛ fɛɛ, ni ewo ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Can I save seeds from my harvested maize to plant during the next rain season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu nugbɔshiimɔ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: You can, but saved seeds from hybrid maize usually produce smaller, weaker plants with lower yields. Buying fresh certified seeds every season ensures strong growth and high yields.
ga: Obaanyɛ, shi dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa mli lɛ fɔɔ tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo baa shi lɛ woɔ. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli hemɔ daa be lɛ haa amɛdaraa waa ni amɛnáa sɛɛnamɔi babaoo.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting easily when I store them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya kɛ́ akɛto lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly when they are bruised during harvesting or stored in hot, enclosed spaces. Storing undamaged yams on open wooden racks in a shady barn keeps them cool and dry.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli loo akɛto hei ni mli edɔ ni afo he. Atomɔ ni mli ewo muji ni akɛtoɔ tso adekai ni agbele mli yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni yɔɔ shade mli. Ehaa edɔ ni egbiɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning yellow from the tip down the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-corn lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛnajiaŋ kɛmiiba shi kɛmiiya teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves in maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crop plants need to grow green and leafy. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help restore their green color and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná baai. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my groundnut plants look healthy on top, but the pods underground turn out empty when I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli efolo beni mikpa amɛ lɛ.

english: Empty groundnut pods happen when the soil lacks calcium, which the plant needs to form the nut inside the shell. Adding agricultural lime or wood ash to the soil before planting helps the nuts fill out properly.
ga: Peanut ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ baa kɛji akɛ calcium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni tso lɛ ajie ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ lime loo tso sũ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani odu lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. This naturally fertilizes the soil, helping the maize grow stronger while giving you two different harvests from the same piece of land.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa waa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, aduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wither and die when I clear all the big trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei ni edara lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot survive direct, scorching sunlight and dry winds. Keeping larger shade trees or planting plantains alongside young cocoa provides the essential shade and cool soil moisture they need to survive their first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni tswaa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ akwɛmɔ loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ baaha hulutsoo ni he hiaa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa koni anyɛ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves upward toward the sun to produce enough energy to grow tubers. Staking keeps the leaves off the hot ground, reduces fungal diseases, and results in much bigger yams.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã hulu lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha bulbs lɛ akwɛ̃. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa yɛ lɛ, ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ aba shi, ni ebaaha sweet potatoes ni dara babaoo aba.

english: Why should I cut away the extra small shoots growing at the base of my plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Nɔ krɛdɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ yɛ mi plantains lɛ shishi lɛ je kpo.

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and plant food from the main mother plant. Leaving only one or two strong suckers ensures the main tree gets enough nutrition to produce large, heavy bunches of plantain.
ga: Tso krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo tso wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop all their leaves during the dry season, and is my crop dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai fɛɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ? Ni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ miigboi?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry spells to conserve water and protect itself from heat. The plant is not dead; the roots underground stay healthy and fresh leaves will quickly grow back once the rains return.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni akɛbu nu he ni abu he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ baawa ni baai heei baakwɛ̃ oya kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when daytime temperatures get too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Keeping soil moisture steady by mulching around the roots helps the flowers stay on and turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa mli lɛ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be fɛɛ be kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ohe lɛ ni oookɛwo mli lɛ nɔ. Shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni ehiɔ shi ni ewoɔ aduawai.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my corn leaves and small brown dirt inside the central whorl?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa baa lɛ mli buji ni etse kɛ muji bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ? yɛ tsɔne ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which burrows into the center leaf funnel to feed on the plant. Applying approved bio-pesticides or recommended sprays directly into the whorl early in the morning helps protect the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni shwieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli koni amɛye tso lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ wo ŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Curled, twisted pepper leaves are caused by tiny sucking pests like thrips or mites, or a virus transmitted by insects. Spraying the leaves with a mild soapy water solution or neem oil helps manage these pests and prevents further damage.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ pepper baa ni etse ehe lɛ baa ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites. loo helai ni kooloi kɛbaa lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ nu ni mli ejɔ Loo neem fɔ shwie baa lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekwɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ ni ebaatsi nibii krokomɛi ni baafite lɛ anaa.

english: What is the difference between a shade net house and a plastic greenhouse for growing my vegetables?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ shade net shia kɛ plastic greenhouse ni akɛduɔ aduawai lɛ teŋ?

english: A net house uses a mesh net to protect crops from harsh sunlight and pests while allowing air to flow through easily to keep plants cool. A plastic greenhouse completely seals the environment to trap heat and moisture, which can make it too hot for crops in warm areas unless expensive cooling systems are used.
ga: Netting greenhouses kɛ mesh netting tsuɔ nii kɛbuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ mlɛo koni tsei lɛ afee fɛ̃i. Plastic tsũi ni akɛfee hulutsoo be lɛ tsiɔ shihilɛ lɛ naa kwraa koni ekɛmɔmɔ dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i. Enɛ baanyɛ aha edɔ tsɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ. Ja akɛ tsɔne ni haa hulutsoo baa ni jara wa tsu nii.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that easily burn under full sunshine. Plantains grow quickly and produce broad leaves that act as natural umbrellas, shielding the cocoa plants from intense sun and keeping the soil moist while the cocoa roots grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Buu kookoo tsei ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ daraa waa lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize plant lacks enough nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is the main food maize needs to stay green and produce strong stalks, so adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer early in the season prevents this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ehiɛ eŋɔli kɛ ŋmãa ni mli wa lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Why do my cabbage plants remain loose and leafy instead of forming hard, solid heads?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage tsei lɛ hiɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ baai yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee yitsei ni wa ni wa lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to form tight heads when they lack adequate nutrients like nitrogen and potassium, or when the soil gets too hot and dry during the period when the head is supposed to form.
ga: Kaabaji nyɛŋ afee yitsei ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ potassium bɛ mli. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni egbi yɛ be mli ni esa akɛ atswa bulb lɛ ama shi lɛ.

english: Cassava draws a large amount of nutrients out of the soil to build its big roots. Planting it in the same spot continuously wears out the soil, leading to smaller tubers and a buildup of soil-borne pests and diseases over time.
ga: Cassava jieɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛfee shishifãi wuji. Kɛ́ adu nii yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya nɔ afite. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii feɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii kɛ helai ni buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: When pepper plants get too much water, their roots drown from a lack of air, causing the leaves to turn pale green or yellow, droop down, and drop off prematurely despite the wet soil.
ga: Kɛji pepper tsei lɛ ná nu babaoo Amɛshishifãi lɛ baagbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse, amɛshwieɔ shi, ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ po nɔ.

english: What makes my yam tubers rot underground before I get the chance to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani miná hegbɛ makpã amɛ?

english: Yam rot underground is caused by excess water staying in heavy clay soil without proper drainage, which creates an environment where soil fungi and tiny worms called nematodes attack and decay the tuber.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni buaa ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ sũ ni tsii ni nu tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato fitemɔ baa shikpɔŋ shishi. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ko baa ni sũ mli ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ tutuaa ni amɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without producing any tomatoes during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato ko yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When weather temperatures get excessively hot, tomato pollen dries out and becomes sterile. Because the flowers cannot be pollinated, the plant drops them to conserve energy.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ mli latsaa lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ, Tomato pollen lɛ mli egbi ni ebɛ fɔmɔ nii. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, anyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔii amli ŋmɔtɔ. No hewɔ lɛ esa akɛ tsei lɛ ajie fɔfɔii koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Twisted leaves with yellow patches are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, a sickness carried from plant to plant by tiny insects called whiteflies as they feed on the sap.
ga: Baai ni atsɔ mli yɛ hei srɔtoi Yellow ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Enɛ ji hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ woɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ beni amɛyeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ.

english: Why do I get smaller cobs when I plant my maize seeds very close to one another?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmeii bibii anɔ kɛ́ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Planting maize seeds too close together forces the plants to compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, resulting in thin, weak stalks and small or incomplete cobs.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii loo ni eshɛɛɛ he lɛ feɔ mlɛo.

english: Young cocoa trees have sensitive leaves that burn under full sun and heat. They need shade from plants like plantains or leguminous trees in their early years to keep the soil moist and protect them from direct heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa yɛ hulu kɛ dɔlɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei tamɔ plantains loo legumes mli yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli. Koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebu he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he.

english: Yellowing that starts at the lower leaves usually means your maize is hungry for nitrogen. Maize needs nitrogen to stay green and grow heavy cobs, so adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer will fix this.
ga: Yellowing ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃ ŋmãa ni tsii. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaatsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce long, thin roots instead of big, fat tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ shishifãi kakadaji ni yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ shishifãi wuji ni yɔɔ fɔ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots cannot expand if the ground is too hard and packed down. Loosening the soil before planting allows the roots room to swell into large, heavy tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi nyɛŋ alɛɛ mli kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ dani adu lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shishifã tsu lɛ mli alɛɛ ni etsɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when the weather gets too hot or when soil watering is irregular. Giving the plants steady water and mulching the soil helps the flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Kɛ́ afɔ tsei lɛ anɔ nu daa ni awo amɛmli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do I need to raise stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo tsei anɔ koni mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the sunlight to make energy for growing large tubers underground. Staking also keeps the leaves off damp ground, preventing leaf diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã hulu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs wuji ni baakwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Koni akɛtsi baa helai anaa

english: Why do my maize leaves have small holes eaten through them with dirt inside the funnels?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii kɛ muji yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by caterpillars like Fall Armyworm that hide inside the central leaves of the maize plant. Checking plants early and applying correct controls protects the growing stem from destruction.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ. Tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Ni nibii ni sa ni akɛkwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu tsei ni miida lɛ ahe kɛjɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ lɛ he.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips sucking leaf sap. Controlling these pests early helps fresh leaves grow normal and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Eyeɔ ebuaa baai heei ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I leave all the young suckers growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishiɔ ŋmeii bibii komɛi yɛ jɛmɛ? Mi plantain tso titri lɛ

english: Too many suckers compete with the main plantain stem for nutrients, water, and sunlight, leading to tiny bunches. Leaving only two or three strong suckers ensures a big, heavy bunch of plantain.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ tso lɛ yibii titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii, nu kɛ hulu la, ni amɛfeɔ kui bibii. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii agbo ni tsii aba.

english: Rice plants are uniquely adapted to thrive in flooded soil, while most weeds drown in standing water. Keeping water in the field prevents weeds from stealing light and nutrients from your rice.
ga: Afee ŋmãa tsei pɔtɛɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ be mli ni jwɛi lɛ ateŋ babaoo boteɔ nu ni damɔ shi mli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo oŋmɔ mli lɛ, ebaatsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaju la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ mli lɛ.

english: How do my groundnut plants form nuts underground after flowering up in the air?
ga: Te feɔ tɛŋŋ ni mi-peanut tsei lɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii beni amɛwo fɔfɔi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Once groundnut flowers are pollinated, they grow long pegs that push themselves down into the soil. Once inside the dark soil, the tips of these pegs swell up to form the groundnut pods.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ ebɔi ŋmɔtɔ lɛ Ebaato ŋmei kakadaŋŋ ko ni ekɛ ehe awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni eyɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo duŋ nɔ Pin lɛ naagbee lɛ baafu aahu kɛyashi ebaatsɔ ŋmei ŋmei.

english: This is often a sign of cocoa swollen shoot virus disease. It attacks the vascular system of the tree, causing swollen stems and sickly leaves, and eventually stops the tree from producing healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji hela ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa lɛ he okadi: kookoo ŋmeii ni efuu. Etutuaa tso lɛ lá fãji lɛ. Ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni hela mɔɔ baai lɛ. ni yɛ naagbee lɛ, ekpaa tso lɛ koni ekafee kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How can a crop disease spread from a distant town into my own farm?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsei ahe helai agbɛ ashwã kɛjɛ maji ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ amli kɛba miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Diseases travel very easily through insects like mealybugs, infected pod husks, contaminated farm tools, or farmers carrying infected plant cuttings from one village to another.
ga: Hela nɛɛ tsɔɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ mealybugs kɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli oya waa. Okwaafoi adɛŋdadei ni mli ewo muji loo okwaafoi ni hiɛɔ tso ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ shishifãi kɛjɛɔ akrowa kome mli kɛyaa ekroko mli.

english: Why does cutting down a sick cocoa tree completely seem like the only fix when it gets infected?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni cacao tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ni abaafo kwraa lɛ ji tsabaa pɛ kɛji akɛ hela lɛ mɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Some plant viruses, like swollen shoot disease, live deep inside the tree's sap. Since there is no chemical medicine to cure the tree from the inside, cutting it down completely stops the disease from spreading to healthy trees nearby.
ga: Tso mli helai komɛi, tamɔ bud swollen hela lɛ hiɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsofa ko bɛ ni akɛbaatsa tso lɛ kɛjɛ emli. Kɛ́ afo tso muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ eshwa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do my new cocoa seedlings keep dying before they grow into mature trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo dumɔwui heei lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboɔ lɛ? Dani ebaada ni etsɔ tso agbo?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate roots and thin leaves that easily get burnt by strong sunlight or dry winds. They require proper shade from plantains or shade trees and reliable watering during their early growth stage.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ baai bibii ni hulu loo kɔɔyɔɔ haa egbiɔ oya. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo ni sa kɛjɛ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. kɛ nu ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dalɛ be lɛ mli.

english: Why is cocoa so important to our country compared to other crops I can grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo he hiaa wɔmaŋ lɛ waa kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni manyɛ makwɛ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Cocoa is Ghana's main cash crop sold to international markets, bringing in major revenue for the national treasury that supports local infrastructure, community projects, and agricultural development programs.
ga: Kookoo ji Ghana shika ŋmɔshi nii titri ni ahɔ̃ɔ kɛyaa majimaji jarayelihei. Ekɛ shika titri baa maŋ shikatoohe ni fiɔ maŋ lɛ mli nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii, akutsoŋ nitsumɔi kɛ okwaayeli nitsumɔi asɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I plant new food crops at the same time I am starting a new cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ niyenii hee yɛ be kome too mli lɛ? kɛ kookoo ŋmɔ hee ko shishijee

english: Cocoa trees take three to five years to start bearing fruit. Planting food crops like cassava, maize, or plantain gives your family quick food to eat and income to survive on while waiting for the cocoa to mature.
ga: Eheɔ afii etɛ kɛyashi enumɔ dani cacao tsei lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi. Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni ooodu lɛ baaha oweku lɛ aná niyenii oya kɛ shika ni amɛkɛhi shi yɛ be mli ni amɛmɛɔ ni kookoo lɛ akwɛ lɛ.

english: How do government support programs help farmers protect their crops from dying out?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nɔyeli lɛ yelikɛbuamɔ gbɛjianɔtoi yeɔ ebuaa okwaafoi ni amɛbuɔ amɛŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni amɛkafite?

english: Government programs provide farmers with disease-resistant hybrid seedlings, subsidize spraying services, and send officers to teach modern techniques that stop pest and disease outbreaks early.
ga: Nɔyeli gbɛjianɔtoo ko haa okwaafoi dumɔwui ni akɛ tsofai ebɔ he ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ. Ye ebua nitsumɔi ni akɛshwieɔ tsofa nɔ lɛ kɛ onukpai ni atsuɔ koni amɛyatsɔɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋaai ni haa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa mra.

english: Can a crop disease stay in the soil even after I remove all the dead plants from my field?
ga: Ani tsei ahe helai baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mijie tsei ni egboi lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli po sɛɛ?

english: Yes, some plant diseases and insect pests can live in leftover roots, dead leaves, or soil for months. Resting the soil or planting non-host crops before putting down new seedlings prevents the new plants from catching the old disease.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahe helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi baanyɛ ahi shishifãi ni eshwɛ lɛ amli. baai ni egboi loo shikpɔŋ nyɔji babaoo Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ hejɔɔmɔ loo dumɔ tsei ni jeee gbɔi lɛ dani okɛ dumɔwui heei awo mli koni tsei heei akaná helai momo.

english: How can I tell if my crop is dying from a disease or just from a lack of rainfall?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji helai miigbe miŋmɔshi nibii loo nugbɔ ni enɛɛɛ kɛkɛ hewɔ?

english: Lack of rain usually makes all leaves wilt and dry up evenly across the farm. Disease usually causes strange spots, swollen branches, rotting pods, or dying leaves on specific trees even when other plants look normal.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɛɛ lɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli. Bei pii lɛ, hela lɛ haa tsei komɛi feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, tsei niji ni efuu, tsei lɛ amli ŋmeii ni egboi, loo baai ni egboi. Kɛji tsei krokomɛi tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo po.

english: Why do agriculture officers urge us to report disease outbreaks in our area quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi miifee oya kɛmiibɔ helai ni egbɛ eshwa wɔ akutso lɛ mli lɛ he amaniɛ lɛ?

english: Crop diseases multiply very fast across connected farmland. Early reporting lets officers map the problem and isolate the affected farms before the infection spreads to entire districts.
ga: Tsei ahe helai miiya hiɛ oya yɛ okwaayeli hei ni kɛ amɛhe kpaa gbee lɛ amli. Amaniɛbɔɔ ni akɛhaa mra lɛ yeɔ ebuaa onukpai lɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ naagba lɛ he mfoniri ni amɛjieɔ ŋmɔji ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ he dani hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kpokpaa muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ.

english: Mounds loosen the soil so cassava roots can expand and grow large easily, while also preventing rainwater from pooling around the roots and causing them to rot.
ga: Gɔji lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi koni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛdara mlɛo. Ehaa nugbɔ nu hu buaa ehe naa kɛbɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why does putting dried leaves or animal manure on my soil help my crops during hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ baai ni egbi loo ŋmeii fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Organic matter like manure and leaf mulch acts like a sponge, keeping moisture trapped in the soil longer and protecting plant roots from extreme heat.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ. ni ebuɔ tsei shishifãi ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I cut down all the large shade trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ beni mifoɔ tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains protects them until they grow strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaye abua ni abu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, leaving no plant with enough energy to make big cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei komɛi bɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaafee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Wait until the rains become regular and wet the soil deeply for several days in a row, so seeds don't sprout and then dry up during unexpected dry breaks.
ga: Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ anɛ fiofio ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ gbii babaoo ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ akakwɛ̃ ni amɛkagbi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei ni akpaaa gbɛ lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are missing essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or that heavy rain has washed those nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele tsei lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ nakai niyenii lɛ kɛjɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies hiding under the leaves and spreading plant diseases.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe ewoɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛgbɛɔ tsei ahe helai amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the air becomes too hot and dry, or when the plant doesn't get a steady supply of water while it is flowering.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. Aloo kɛ́ tomato tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu nɔ daa be mli ni amɛmiikwɛ fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: Why are my yam vines growing so many thick green leaves, but the tubers underground remain very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ baai ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa lolo?

english: Too much leaf growth happens when the soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer, causing the plant to put all its energy into top growth instead of storing strength in the tuber.
ga: Baai ni yaa hiɛ fe nine lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ. Enɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛdara babaoo. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ hewalɛ ato oyitsoŋ lɛ

english: Why do my stored grains develop small holes and powdery dust after a few weeks in the storage room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni sũ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi ni akɛtoɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Insects like grain weevils eat into the stored grains if the crop was not fully dried in the sun before being bagged, or if the storage space is humid.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmaa ŋmeii baaye ŋmaa ni ato kɛji akɛ agbiko ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwraa yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani akɛwo kotoku mli. aloo kɛji akɛ he ni akɛ nibii lɛ toɔ lɛ mli edɔ

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate strong, direct sunlight because their roots are small and leaf surfaces dry out quickly. Shade trees protect the young plants from extreme heat and moisture loss until they grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ daraaa ni baa lɛ hiɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Tsei ni yɔɔ shade mli lɛ buɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa waa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why is it important to trim or prune the upper branches of mature shade trees on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ loo mafolɔ tsei ni eda ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aniji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Excessive shade creates a dark, damp environment that encourages black pod disease, while controlled pruning lets in enough light and air to help the crops thrive.
ga: Shade babaoo haa shihilɛ ni mli ewo duŋ ni mli edɔ ni woɔ black pod hela lɛ he hewalɛ baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa baaye abua tso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: When maize plants are crowded, they fight for the same sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, which leaves them with tall, thin stems and small or empty cobs.
ga: Beni ŋmãa tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛbaatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Amɛyɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli, ni no haa amɛfeɔ tsei kakadaji ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ tsei bibii loo ni nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning pale yellow during heavy rain periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excessive water in poorly drained soil suffocates root systems and washes away essential nitrogen nutrients, causing the leaves to lose their healthy green color.
ga: Nu babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekɛ nitrogen nibii ni he hiaa lɛ atsu nii. Enɛ haa baa lɛ sɛɛ foɔ amɛ su ni ji eŋɔli ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow small and crooked when planted in hard clay soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need loose, light soil to expand smoothly underground, whereas hard clay physically blocks their path and forces them to deform or stop growing.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni mli tse koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi jogbaŋŋ. yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni wa tsiɔ amɛ gbɛ naa ni enyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛfite loo amɛkpa dalɛ.

english: Why do the flowers drop off my pepper plants without producing any fruit during hot dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni ewooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside the flowers, preventing fertilization and causing the plant to shed the flowers to save its water.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Etsiɔ fɔmɔ nii anaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu he

english: Why do the leaves on my plantain shoots roll inward during the middle of hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa mli yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rolling leaves reduces the surface area exposed to direct heat, helping the plant trap moisture and avoid excessive water loss during peak sunshine.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ haa he ni hulutsoo baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baa shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ nu ni amɛfiteɔ fe nine yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: Why do weeds grow back much faster than my main crops right after the rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii titri lɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds have hardy, natural deep root systems designed to absorb sudden rainfall and nutrients faster than farm crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ, ni ji adebɔɔ mli nibii ni afee koni amɛŋɔ nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei.

english: Why do the pods on my cocoa trees start turning black and rotting during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ diŋ ni egboɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Black pod is a fungal disease that spreads quickly in cool, wet, and humid conditions when water sits on the pod surface for too long.
ga: Black pods ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ, ni mli efɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛji nu hi pod lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: Why do armyworms suddenly appear and destroy young maize leaves right after early season rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ cutworms lɛ jeɔ kpo trukaa ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: The warm, humid air right after early rains triggers dormant moths to lay eggs on fresh green maize shoots, which hatch quickly into hungry caterpillars.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ ni baa mra be mli nugbɔshiimɔi lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ haa ŋmeii ni wɔɔ shi lɛ gboiɔ. Amɛwoɔ wɔji yɛ ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni kpɛɔ lɛ anɔ. ni baatsɔ ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ oya.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily in harsh sunlight. They need shade from plants like plantains or shade trees to shield them and keep the moisture in the soil while their roots develop.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni naa wa shɛ amɛnɔ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Koni abu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he ni ekwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Wait until the rainy season firmly establishes with two or three heavy soaking rains. Planting too early after a light rain leaves seeds stranded in dry soil when the rain stops for days.
ga: Mɛɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baabote mli fiofio. Akɛni nugbɔ nɛ waa aaafee shii 2-3 hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ ba mra tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ fioo lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa gbii babaoo.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the plant is starving for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient that gives plants their deep green color and helps them build strong ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni haa tsei lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa toi ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot inside the ground when heavy rains fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long without draining. Planting your cassava on raised earth mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe. be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu lɛ efooo Shika ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from high heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients, as the plant tries to save energy rather than grow fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli lɛ ye amɛ awui. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei miitao ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato moŋ fe ni amɛaakwɛ aduawai.

english: Is it good for my crop if I plant beans together in the same farm with my maize?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa fata ŋmãa he yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Yes, beans and maize grow well together because beans naturally trap nitrogen from the air and feed the soil, which helps the maize grow bigger while maize stalks support bean vines.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei kɛ ŋmei feɔ ekome kɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛyeɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa tsei lɛ fiɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ asɛɛ

english: What is eating small holes into the fresh middle leaves of my young corn?
ga: Mɛni ye bu bibioo ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baa hee lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide deep inside the growing center of the corn plant to feed on tender young leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ adalɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Weeds have strong, fast-growing roots that steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight meant for your crops, so clearing weeds before fertilizing is necessary.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni wa ni amɛdaraa oya. Enɛ juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛhaa onibii. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni ajie jwɛi lɛ dani awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Saved hybrid seeds lose the strength and high yield of the parent seed, resulting in uneven plant growth, smaller yields, and higher vulnerability to diseases.
ga: Hybrid dumɔwui ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ haa fɔlɔ dumɔwu lɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo lɛ baa shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ daraaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. ekɛ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi ni ehaa mɔ he feɔ shoo

english: Does burning bush on my land before planting destroy the food in the soil?
ga: Ani tsei bibii ni ashãa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani aduɔ lɛ baafite niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yes, while burning gives a quick boost of ash, intense heat destroys useful organic matter, kills helpful soil living organisms, and causes soil to dry out faster.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ be mli ni shãa haa sũ yaa hiɛ oya lɛ. Shi dɔlɛ ni naa wa fiteɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ. Efiteɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive strong, direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or taller forest trees to shield them and keep the soil moist while their roots develop during the first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ tsei bibii loo koo mli tsei kakadaji koni ebu amɛhe ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ.

english: How do I know which direction is the right way up when planting my cassava stem cuttings?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male gbɛ ni ja ni esa akɛ madu mi-cassava tso lɛ?

english: Look closely at the small buds or 'eyes' on the stem where old leaves used to grow. Plant the stem with these buds pointing upwards toward the sky so the shoots can grow properly above ground.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ‘ŋmeii’ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi he ni baai momoi kwɛ̃ɔ be ko ni eho lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Dumɔ tso lɛ yitso lɛ ni fɔfɔii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why will my crops produce a smaller harvest if I plant seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ naa ŋmaa bibioo kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Giving plants proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to grow big and produce well.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ he ni sa ha tsei lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ni ewo yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is essential plant food. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer early in the season keeps leaves green and strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa.

english: Planting maize continuously drains the same nutrients from the soil every year and allows pests to multiply. Alternating maize with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts naturally puts nitrogen back into the soil.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa afi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo yaa hiɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why should I avoid putting fertilizer on my field right before a heavy rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ miŋmɔji amli ŋmɔshi nibii ahe dani nugbɔ anɛ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes the fertilizer off the farm or pushes it too deep into the ground before roots can absorb it, which wastes your effort and money.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji amli loo ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsɔ dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Enɛ baaha ofite hewalɛ kɛ shika.

english: Yam is a climbing vine that needs to lift its leaves toward sunlight to make food. Staking allows the foliage to catch maximum light, which helps build large tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potatoes are creeping vines that need to raise their leaves towards the sunlight in order to cook. Staking haa baai lɛ naa la babaoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni afeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plant without ever producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get extremely hot, when soil moisture swings from too dry to too wet, or when insects fail to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baa shi be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ. When soil moisture changes from too dry to too wet or when insects are unable to pollinate flowers

english: Why do my crops stay healthier during dry weather when I cover the soil around them with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ náa hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ, kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi shwie shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, acts like a blanket. It traps moisture in the dirt, keeps roots cool in hot sunshine, and stops weeds from taking over.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: How do I check my young maize field early enough to see if Fall Armyworms are attacking?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ mi-baby corn ŋmɔ lɛ mli mra bɔ ni sa koni mana kɛji Fall Armyworms lɛ miitutua mi?

english: Look inside the center funnel or 'whorl' of the young maize leaves. If you see small holes in the leaf blades or droppings that look like sawdust, armyworms are present and need treatment before they destroy the crop center.
ga: Kwɛmɔ gbɛ ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ loo ‘ring’ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibioo lɛ baa lɛ mli. Kɛji ona bu bibioo ko yɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii yɛ lolo ni ehe miihia ni atsa amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔhei lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plants lack nitrogen, which is the key nutrient crops use to build green leaves and grow strong. It can happen when heavy rains wash nutrients out of the soil or when the soil lacks organic matter.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfee baai eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa. Ebaanyɛ eba beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ loo kɛ́ sũ lɛ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ bɛ.

english: How do groundnuts help make my soil better for the next crop I plant?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni efee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni madu lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into plant food stored in small bumps on their roots. When the groundnut crop is harvested and its roots decay, that stored nitrogen remains in the soil to feed the next crop.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ tsei aniyenii ni buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ akpa ŋmeii ni amɛshishifãi lɛ fite lɛ, Nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soil because excess water fills all the air spaces in the dirt, suffocating the roots and encouraging rot-causing fungi. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps water drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ hei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ hewalɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my pepper leaves wilt in the hot afternoon sun even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: During the hottest part of the day, leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can draw it up from the soil. The plant wilts temporarily to protect itself from heat, but it usually recovers in the cooler evening.
ga: yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli Baai lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. But they usually recover on cooler evenings.

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking sap from the underside of leaves, or by a plant virus spread by whiteflies. The damaged leaf tissues grow unevenly, causing them to twist and curl.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni ŋmeii yɛji gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli. Baa lɛ mli fãji ni efite lɛ daaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Ebaanyɛ ekɛ ŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ aba.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the tomato fruit cannot get enough calcium while growing, usually caused by irregular watering that disrupts how the plant absorbs minerals from the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛ́ tomato aduawai lɛ enine shɛɛɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni esaaa ni haaa shika tsuru ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aná.

english: Why do my cocoa tree flowers dry up and fall off without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands more flowers than they can support, dropping many on purpose. However, excessive loss occurs if the tree lacks water, faces severe heat, or suffers attack from insects like mirids.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ, ni fa fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ nɔ. And many flowers fall off on purpose. Shi kɛlɛ, nɔ ni baafite babaoo tsɔ baaba kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu. ni hulutsoo be ni naa wa waa yɔɔ mli loo kooloi bibii tamɔ pollen tutuaa lɛ

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily once the heavy fruit bunch forms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ŋmeii ni mli edɔ lɛ fee lɛ?

english: Plantain plants do not have deep taproots like woody trees; their shallow roots spread close to the surface. As the heavy bunch grows at the top, the plant becomes top-heavy and can easily pull its shallow roots out of the ground unless supported with wooden props.
ga: Dumɔwui bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ tamɔ tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo. Amɛshishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ gbɛ eshwa he ko ni bɛŋkɛ nu lɛ hiɛ. Kɛji kuu lɛ da yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ Tso lɛ baafee tsiimɔ ni ebaanyɛ egbala shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ oooshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ja tso nibii fiɔ sɛɛ

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with neighboring plants for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. The stalks stretch upward rapidly to reach light, leaving the plant with little energy to produce thick stems and large cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. The stem extends quickly to reach the light. Enɛ haa tso lɛ náaa hewalɛ fioo ko ni ekɛbaawo tsei bibii ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my harvested seed yams start sprouting in the storage barn before the planting season reaches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani ekwɛ̃mɔ be lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Yam tubers naturally rest in a state called dormancy after harvest, but warm temperatures and high air moisture signal to the tuber that it is time to wake up and grow shoots, even if they are stored inside a barn.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ jɔɔ amɛhe yɛ shihilɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Shi hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo lɛ tsɔɔ sweet potato tsei lɛ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ amɛte shi ni amɛdu tsei lɛ. Even if they are kept in a barn.

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in small bumps on their roots. When the crop is harvested and the roots decay, this free food is left behind in the soil for future crops.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ amli kɛ́ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ egbo. Ashiɔ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko nɛɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli koni akɛdu nii wɔsɛɛ.

english: Why is it better to leave cleared weeds on top of my soil instead of burning them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaashi jwɛi ni ajie lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ moŋ fe ni aaashã lɛ?

english: Leaving cleared weeds on the field creates mulch that protects the soil from hot sunlight, stops water from evaporating quickly, and rots into plant food that enriches your farm.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi jwɛi ni he tse yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekaho oya Ni efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ tsei aniyenii ni kɛ sɛɛnamɔ baa oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do the leaves of my cassava drop off completely during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves in dry weather to save water and stay alive. The underground tubers remain fine, and fresh green leaves will sprout as soon as the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni nu egbi lɛ koni ekɛbu nu he ni ehi wala mli. Tubers lɛ hi lolo. Ni baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni kpɛɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ pɛ.

english: Yam vines climb upward so their leaves can catch direct sunlight, which gives the plant energy to build big tubers underground. Lifting leaves off the wet ground also protects them from rot.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ ashɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛfeɔ bulb agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Baai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa amɛfite.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen food. Rain often washes this nutrient out of the soil, so adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer will turn the leaves dark green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Nugbɔ fɔɔ nɛkɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my young cocoa pods turning dark brown and drying up on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is black pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in wet, shaded areas. Pruning high branches to let sunlight and breeze into your farm dries out the moisture and stops the rot.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni efɔ kɛ shade yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni kwɔlɔ lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Fɛ̃i lɛ baagbi ni ekpa fitemɔ.

english: This is blossom-end rot, which happens when tomato plants do not get enough calcium or when soil moisture changes rapidly. Watering regularly and adding wood ash or lime to the soil prevents it.
ga: Enɛ ji fɔfɔii lɛ anaagbee fitemɔ he okadi. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tomato tsei lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ oya Nu ni oooha daa ni okɛ tso sũ loo lime awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the plant juices. Spraying the leaves with neem water or soapy water helps clear them away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii, tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies, ni miinu tso lɛ mli nu lɛ kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem nu loo samla nu shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni afɔ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are small caterpillars hiding inside the center leaf funnel of my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-abele lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are fall armyworms that feed on soft young leaves inside the plant heart. Dropping a pinch of clean dry sand or neem powder right into the leaf center smothers and deters them.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji baai amli ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ tsui lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋã ni egbi ni he tse loo neem powda wo baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛtsi amɛnaa ni ekɛtsi amɛnaa.

english: Why is it better for me to plant my maize in straight lines rather than scattering the seeds across the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting in straight lines ensures every seed gets equal space, sunlight, and nutrients. It also makes daily tasks like weeding, applying fertilizer, and harvesting much easier and faster.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui fɛɛ dumɔwui náa he ko, hulu la kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni fa bɔ ni sa. Eyeɔ ebuaa yɛ daa gbi nitsumɔi tamɔ jwɛi shwiemɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ hu mli. Eyɛ mlɛo ni eyaa oya hu.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to keep specific distances between my cassava cuttings when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ esa akɛ mikɛ tsei ni afo lɛ ahi shi yɛ he ko kɛ́ midu nii lɛ?

english: Proper spacing prevents crop roots from fighting each other for water and nutrients in the soil. Giving each cassava plant enough space allows the tubers to grow larger and healthier.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaatsi tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkawu amɛshi amɛhe koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ aha yucca tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ adara ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Is it good for me to plant cowpea together on the same land with my maize?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mafee ekome kɛdu tsina ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Yes, planting cowpeas with maize is beneficial because cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which helps the maize grow stronger while protecting the soil from drying out.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛnamɔ yɛ tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he ejaakɛ tsina ŋmãa lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa abele lɛ ni edaraa waa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekagbi.

english: How often should I clear weeds from my young vegetable farm to prevent them from choking my crops?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ majie jwɛi kɛjɛ mi-aduawai ŋmɔ bibioo lɛ mli koni amɛkatsi miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa?

english: Weeding should be done early and regularly, especially during the first 4 to 6 weeks of planting, so weeds do not steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients from your young crops.
ga: Esa akɛ ajie jwɛi lɛ mra ni afeɔ daa, titri lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii 4 kɛyashi 6 ni akɛduɔ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ jwɛi lɛ juŋ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛjɛ otsei bibii lɛ amli.

english: What simple signs should I look out for every morning when checking my crop leaves for pests?
ga: Ani esa akɛ makwɛ okadii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ? Mɛni ofeɔ daa leebi kɛ́ ookwɛ tsei ahe baai lɛ amli kɛji ŋmeii yɛ mli?

english: Check under the leaves and along the stems for small holes, yellow patches, insect eggs, or sticky residues. Catching these early allows you to deal with pests before they destroy the whole crop.
ga: Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ ashishi kɛ tso lɛ shishi kɛji ŋmeii bibii yɛ mli. Ani amɛji ŋmɔtɔi, kooloi bibii, loo ŋmɔtɔi ni shwieɔ shi? Amɔmɔ mra Ehaa onyɛɔ otsuɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe nii dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ.

english: Why do my tomato seedlings droop and dry up when I move them from the nursery to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seedlings suffer from transplant shock when moved abruptly. You can prevent this by exposing them to direct sunlight gradually in the nursery and transplanting them during cool late afternoons.
ga: Dumɔwui naa amanehulu kɛjɛɔ transplant shock mli kɛji ajie amɛ trukaa. Obaanyɛ otsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ blɛoo ni oooye lɛ nɔ. Ha hulu la aba tɛ̃ɛ yɛ gbekɛbii akwɛmɔhe lɛ. ni aduɔ yɛ shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ lɛ.

english: Should I strictly follow traditional planting dates every year even if the rains arrive late?
ga: Ani esa akɛ makwɛ kusum naa be ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ nɔ daa afi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ba sɛɛ po?

english: No, planting calendars are flexible guides rather than strict rules. You should always adjust your planting daily routines based on when moisture actually becomes reliable in your local soil.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui kalanda lɛ ji gbɛtsɔɔmɔ ni anyɛɔ atsakeɔ moŋ fe mlai ni mli wa. Esa akɛ otsake bɔ ni oduɔ nii ohaa daa gbi lɛ mli koni osusu be ni abaanyɛ akɛ he afɔ̃ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he.

english: If the sun is very hot this season, what can I do daily to keep moisture in the soil for my crops?
ga: Kɛji akɛ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ hulu lɛ mli edɔ waa Mɛni mifeɔ daa gbi koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Covering the soil around your crops with dried grass or leaves (mulching) acts as a shield that slows down water evaporation and keeps the root area cool.
ga: Mulching around Okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi aha onibii ahe (mulching) tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo ni ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants turning yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is lacking essential nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, or the roots are sitting in waterlogged soil and cannot breathe.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo shishifãi lɛ eta shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu.

english: How can I tell when my yam tubers are fully grown and ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ edara jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Yams indicate full maturity when the vines and leaves naturally start yellowing and drying up at the end of the rainy season, showing the plant has finished feeding the tuber.
ga: Atomɔ tsɔɔ akɛ edara beni wain tsei kɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee. Etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe ŋmeii lɛ niyenii egbe naa.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn brown and fall off when there is too much sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ hulu la shɛ mihe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains protects them until they grow strong enough to withstand direct heat.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo fioo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tso lɛ he kɛyashi ebaada ni enyɛ edamɔ hulutsoo tɛ̃ɛ naa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is essential food for plants. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure will help the corn plants recover and stay healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei lɛ bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmei loo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ŋmei tsei lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: How does cassava manage to stay alive during the dry season when there is no rain?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei ahi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry spells to conserve water and stores energy deep underground in its tubers, allowing it to survive harsh heat until rains return.
ga: Akɛ ŋmeii baa shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni akɛbu nu he ni akɛ hewalɛ ato shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Ha eŋmɛ etsui shi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ mli kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet too quickly. Keeping soil moisture steady with mulching helps flowers stay on and produce fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ oya tsɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: How do I know the exact right time to sow my seeds when the rains start?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ?

english: It is best to wait for two or three heavy, steady rains that thoroughly soak deep into the soil before planting, rather than sowing after the very first drizzle which might be followed by a long hot spell.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni baabote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ dani odu. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ, ni ekolɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ baanyiɛ sɛɛ.

english: Lifting yam vines on stakes exposes more leaves to sunlight, which allows the plant to produce more energy and feed bigger yam tubers underground.
ga: Kɛ́ owó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ebaaha hulu la babaoo ashɛ etso lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ hewalɛ babaoo. ni amɛyeɔ yam tsei wuji lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips hiding underneath the leaves and sucking out the plant sap, which damages normal leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. ni fiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni sa lɛ

english: Why do my corn plants fall over easily when strong winds blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa lɛ?

english: Maize plants fall over if their roots are close to the surface or if the soil around them is loose. Heap fresh soil around the base of the stems to help the brace roots lock firmly into the ground.
ga: Abɛi baagbee shi kɛji shishifãi lɛ bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ loo shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli etse. Okɛ shikpɔŋ hee ato tso lɛ shishi koni eye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shiŋŋ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and lets specific pests build up. Alternating with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts refills nitrogen into the soil naturally.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii atsake. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ nitrogen afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do I need to cut off some of the small stems growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ Mi plantain tso titri lɛ he lɛ ajie
