english: Leaving too many young shoots makes them compete with the main tree for food and water, resulting in smaller plantains. Removing extra suckers leaves only the strongest shoots to produce large, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii bibii babaoo lɛ, ebaaha amɛkɛ tso titri lɛ abɔi niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ bibii. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ feɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Yellowing leaves at the bottom usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient in the soil. When nitrogen is low, the plant moves what little it has from older lower leaves up to support new leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ nitrogen faaa Tso lɛ tsiɔ nɔ fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni etsɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni baa lɛ adalɛ.

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the earth, but groundnuts and beans do the opposite by taking nitrogen from the air and storing it in the ground, naturally feeding your soil for the next planting season.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi kɛ ŋmeii feɔ nɔ ni tamɔɔɔ nakai, ni amɛjieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa saplings burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act like umbrellas, giving young cocoa trees the shade and moist air they need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: When plants are crowded together, their roots fight underground for water and soil nutrients, and their leaves fight for sunlight, causing them to grow thin and produce small harvests.
ga: Kɛ́ abua tsei anaa yɛ kui amli lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni amɛbaai lɛ baawuu koni amɛná hulu la. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm pest. The mother moths lay eggs on the leaves, and when the tiny caterpillars hatch, they crawl into the heart of the maize plant where the leaves are softest to eat.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Fall Armyworm lɛ. Nyɛ lɛ fɔ̃ɔ wɔji yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Ni kɛ́ ŋmeii bibii lɛ fɔ lɛ, amɛkpãa kɛboteɔ ŋmei tso lɛ mli, he ni baai ni mli tse fe fɛɛ lɛ yɔɔ ni ayeɔ lɛ.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by a plant virus spread by tiny white insects called whiteflies, or it happens when the soil gets too dry during hot weather.
ga: Tso mli hela ko ni koolooi bibii eyɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Aloo ebaa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: The first rain is often followed by a long hot dry spell before the real rainy season begins, which can dry out and kill young sprouted seedlings in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ diɛŋtsɛ jeɔ shishi. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting in the soil before I can dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani abaanyɛ atsa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when there is too much standing water in the field from heavy rains. Soil that stays soaked suffocates the roots and allows water rot diseases to spread.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ni damɔ shi babaoo yɛ ŋmɔji amli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa nu ni egbo lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do I have to place tall wooden sticks for my yam plants to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ okɛ tsei kakadaji ama shi lɛ? Ha sweet potato tso lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi?

english: Yam plants are vines that need to lift their leaves up toward the sun to make food, which feeds the tuber underground. Lifting the vines off the ground also prevents ground rot.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ ji wain tso ni esa akɛ ewo ebaa lɛ nɔ kɛya hulu la lɛ he koni ekɛfee niyenii. ni yeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii Wein tsei lɛ ni awóɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmeii anaa.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when the weather gets extremely hot, when the soil lacks water, or if you use too much nitrogen fertilizer which makes the plant grow leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Beni nu bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Aloo kɛji akɛ okɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii, ni no haa tso lɛ baa yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Why should I plant Bambara beans or cowpeas on my land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu bambara ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikpa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Beans and Bambara groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil through their roots. Planting them naturally restores fertility to tired soil, making it richer for the next crop you plant.
ga: Bambara ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Tsei nɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni etɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni woɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ.

english: Why do my bean plants produce plenty of green leaves but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pea tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or when plants get excessive water early on, they put all their energy into growing leaves instead of fruits. Giving them balanced nutrients and avoiding over-watering during flowering helps them produce full pods.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo be mli ni tsei lɛ náa nu babaoo mra Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai ni miida lɛ mli yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Niyenii ni sa ni akɛhaa amɛ kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ fe nine yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why are my young crops weak and falling over instead of standing strong in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaadamɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Plants grow weak stems when they lack vital soil nutrients like potassium or when they are planted too closely together and have to fight for sunlight. Giving them proper spacing and the right soil nutrients builds strong stalks that can handle heavy winds.
ga: Tsei daa ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ amɛbɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium, loo kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ni amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii ni sa ha lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ afee tsei ni wa ni baanyɛ adamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa.

english: Why do crop leaves turn yellow and stop growing even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves mean the plant is starving for nitrogen nutrients in the soil, or the ground is so flooded that the roots cannot breathe. Adding compost or fertilizer helps the leaves turn deep green and resume healthy growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aahu akɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua baa lɛ ni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ebɔi dalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does fertilizer fail to work on my crops when the ground is dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuuu nii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi lɛ?

english: Crop roots cannot eat dry fertilizer directly; they can only drink nutrients dissolved in water. Applying fertilizer to dry soil leaves it useless and can even burn the roots until rainfall or watering melts it into the soil.
ga: Tso shishifãi nyɛŋ aye ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛnu niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni akɛwo nu mli pɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha efee nɔ ni he ehiaaa, ni ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ po kɛyashi nugbɔ loo nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaha etsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: How do I know if my soil is completely exhausted and needs food before I plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ ni ehe miihia ni aha lɛ niyenii dani madu nii?

english: Exhausted soil looks dry, pale, and dusty, and weeds or crops planted in it grow slowly with yellowish leaves. Adding animal manure or well-rotted plant waste feeds the soil so it can feed your crops again.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbi, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni eyɛ sũ, ni jwɛi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni adu yɛ mli lɛ baakwɛ̃ fiofio. kɛ baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ Kooloo ŋmɔtɔ loo tsei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ bɔni afee ni enyɛ eye ebua onibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do small holes appear in my stored maize and bean seeds after a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bu bibioo ko yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ejie ehe kpo yɛ mi-ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ mli yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ.

english: Tiny insects called weevils lay invisible eggs inside the seeds while in the field or during drying, which hatch and eat the seeds from the inside out. Drying seeds properly and storing them in sealed, airtight containers keeps these insects out.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ weevils lɛ woɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli ni anaaa amɛ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli loo be mli ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. ni baafo ni eye dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛ mli kɛya kpo nɔ Dumɔwui ni agbi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛto tsɛnsii ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akabote mli.

english: What causes tiny holes in the leaves of my pepper and vegetable plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi pepper baai kɛ aduawai anɔ

english: Tiny holes are made by small beetles and caterpillars that chew on leaves to feed themselves. Spraying neem leaf extract or safe botanical insecticides protects the leaves so the plant can feed itself and produce fruit.
ga: Buji bibii lɛ ji ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni ŋmɔɔ baai lɛ koni amɛna amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ niyenii. Neem tso lɛ mli nu ni ajieɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ tso ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baabu tso lɛ he koni tso lɛ anyɛ aye niyenii ni ewo yibii.

english: Why do tomato processing factories reject fruits that are soft or watery?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni nitsumɔhei ni feɔ tomato lɛ kpooɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ loo nu mli lɛ?

english: Processing factories need firm tomatoes with low water content so they can turn them into thick paste efficiently. Watery or damaged tomatoes spoil too quickly and reduce the quality of the final processed product.
ga: Tsoi ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ biɔ tomato ni loo yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni nu faaa yɛ mli. bɔni afee ni enyɛ etsake lɛ jogbaŋŋ efee tomato concentrate Tomato ni nu yɔɔ mli loo ni efite lɛ baafite oya tsɔ ni ebaaha naagbee nibii ni afee lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ aba shi.

english: Cassava roots store starch for a limited time, but if left unharvested past maturity, the plant uses up the soft starch and turns the root into tough wood fiber, making it hard to cook or process.
ga: Cassava shishifãi kɛ starch toɔ be fioo ko. Shi kɛji oshi lɛ kɛyashi be ni eho lɛ, Tso lɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ tsuɔ nii ni etsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli efeɔ tso mli tsɔi ni wa. Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ aaahoo nii loo atsu he nii.

english: Maize leaves can turn yellow if fertilizer is applied when the soil is too dry, preventing plants from absorbing nutrients, or if the soil lacks nitrogen despite applying the wrong type of fertilizer.
ga: Abɛi baai baanyɛ afee ŋmɔŋ kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ Aloo kɛji akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ejaaa wo mli po.

english: Can using too much chemical fertilizer damage my farm soil over time?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ baanyɛ afite shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: Yes, using too much chemical fertilizer over time can make the soil too acidic and destroy beneficial soil organisms, making it harder for crops to absorb nutrients naturally.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ baanyɛ aha sũ lɛ mli afee acid tsɔ ni efite sũ mli nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei akɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛaaŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Should I apply fertilizer before or after clearing weeds from my farm?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo ŋmɔshi nibii dani mijie jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ loo beni majie lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You should always clear weeds before applying fertilizer. If you leave the weeds, they will consume the fertilizer faster than your crops and choke them out.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie jwɛi lɛ be fɛɛ be dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli. Kɛji oshi jwɛi lɛ Amɛbaaye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ oya fe oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛbaagbe amɛ.

english: Leaf curling in cassava is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that spread diseases such as Cassava Mosaic Virus while feeding on the leaves' sap.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii, tamɔ whiteflies, ni gbɛɔ helai tamɔ cassava virus amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. beni eyeɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ

english: How can I tell if armyworms are attacking my maize field early before the leaves are destroyed?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmeii miitutua mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ dani tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ afite?

english: Look for small pinholes on young leaves and moist, sawdust-like droppings tucked inside the central funnel of the maize plant where the worm hides during the day.
ga: Taomɔ buji bibii ni yɔɔ baai bibii amli kɛ ŋmeii ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni mli ewo fɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmei tso lɛ teŋgbɛ he ni ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when exposed to stress, such as sudden hot dry spells, waterlogging from heavy rain, or a lack of nutrients needed to form fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ ko, tamɔ hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa, ni mli edɔ waa lɛ he. Nu ni eyi mli obɔ kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha aduawai afeemɔ ni bɛ

english: Why should I plant plantains or cassava next to my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui loo ŋmei yɛ emasɛi? Mi kookoo tso bibioo lɛ

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn under full sunlight. Fast-growing plants like plantains provide shade and retain soil moisture to help the cocoa survive its early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains haa hulutsoo ni amɛhiɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu mli koni eye ebua kookoo ni ehi shi yɛ eshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why does saved maize seed from my last harvest produce smaller yields than newly bought certified seed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni ato kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ?

english: Saved hybrid seeds lose their vigor and disease resistance after the first harvest, resulting in uneven growth and smaller cobs compared to fresh certified seed.
ga: Hybrid dumɔwui ni ahere lɛ lɛ ahewalɛ kɛ helai ahe hewalɛ baa shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee kɛ ŋmeii bibii kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ ahe.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to plant groundnuts or beans on my land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ midu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, naturally restoring nutrients that heavy-feeding crops like maize took away.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni tsei ni yeɔ niyenii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ ejie lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my harvested corn catch mold while stored in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ batsɔ ŋmãa be mli ni mikɛtoɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Corn develops mold if it is stored before drying completely or placed in warm, damp rooms without proper airflow, which creates ideal conditions for fungi to grow.
ga: Abele baaná ŋmɔtɔ kɛji akɛ akɛto dani egbi kwraa loo akɛwo tsu ko ni mli edɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni sa kɛha ŋmeii adalɛ baa.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sun. Plantains grow quickly with wide leaves that provide living shade and keep the soil moist, protecting young cocoa seedlings during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Does it matter which direction I plant my cassava stems in the ground?
ga: Ani miduɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ yɛ he fɛɛ he yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, planting cassava stems with the leaf buds pointing upward ensures the leaves grow properly toward the sun. Planting stems upside down forces the plant to waste energy reorienting itself, resulting in smaller tubers.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɛ́ adu ŋmei tsei ni ŋmeii lɛ kwɛɔ ŋwɛi lɛ, ebaaye ebua baai lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ. Kɛ́ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ da ni ekɛ ehe shwie shi lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ he waaa yɛ ehe ni ekɛbaatsake ehe lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yitso bibioo.

english: Why should I wait for the major rainy season to settle before planting my main maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be wulu lɛ dani madu ŋmãa titri ni akɛyeɔ niyenii lɛ?

english: Planting after just one early rain can trap seeds in dry soil if the rain stops for a few weeks. Waiting until the soil is consistently moist guarantees proper seed germination and prevents seedlings from scorching.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ amɔmɔ dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ lɛ kpa otsii fioo komɛi. Kɛ́ omɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ, ni ebaatsi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkashã.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient for green growth. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen out of topsoil, so adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Legumes like groundnuts have special root nodules that draw nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the ground. When the crop is harvested, these roots decompose and leave natural fertilizer in the soil for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni akpaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Nɛkɛ shishifãi nɛɛ fiteɔ ni amɛshiɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha wɔsɛɛ tsei.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my maize leaves and small caterpillars hiding inside the central funnels?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii Mine lɛ yɛ bu ni etse. Akɛtee gbɛjegbɛ lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that feeds on young tender leaves inside the plant funnel. Treating them early with suitable insecticides or neem oil prevents them from destroying the growing tip of the plant.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ. Tsofai ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem fɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra. Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni miida lɛ.

english: Leaf curling is commonly caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips feeding on leaf sap and spreading plant viruses. Controlling these insect vectors keeps the leaves flat and allows normal fruit production.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baa mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ tsei ahe helai amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nibii nɛɛ ni akudɔɔ lɛ baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eye ebua nibii ni afeɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam vines grow much bigger yams when I give them tall wooden stakes to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ daa sweet potatoi wuji babaoo beni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ha amɛ koni amɛkwɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves off the ground so they can catch more sunlight. Sunlight allows the leaves to make energy, which the plant transfers underground to grow thicker and heavier tubers.
ga: Staking baajie ŋmeii lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai ni amɛfeɔ hewalɛ. ni tso lɛ tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi koni eha ŋmeii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni etsii

english: Tomato flowers drop off unpollinated when temperatures get extremely hot or when water supply drops suddenly. Keeping soil moisture consistent with regular watering helps the flowers stay attached and form tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni pollination bɛ mli kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ba shi trukaa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛma shi akɛ tomatoi.

english: Why do farmers spread dry grass on top of the soil around their tomato and pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi shwieɔ jwɛi ni egbi amɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛbɔleɔ amɛ tomato kɛ pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Spreading dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a protective blanket over the soil. It traps soil moisture, keeps roots cool during hot afternoons, and prevents weeds from growing and taking nutrients away from your crops.
ga: Hay ni agbɛɔ ashwãa, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛkajie niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: Why are tiny insects constantly attacking the young leaves and shoots of my tree crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi tsei lɛ ahe baai bibii kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Insects like capsids or aphids feed on the soft, nutrient-rich parts of young leaves and shoots to suck their juices, which causes the leaves to curl, dry up, or stop growing.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ capsids loo aphids yeɔ baai bibii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli hei ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ koni amɛkɛnu nu. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛgbiɔ, loo amɛkpaa dalɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my tree curl up or change color after bugs bite them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kooloi emɔ amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When insects bite crop leaves, they suck out essential plant juices and sometimes inject toxins or diseases, which prevents the leaf from making food and causes it to turn yellow or curl.
ga: Kɛji kooloi ŋmɔ tso baai lɛ Ebaaŋɔ tso nu ni he hiaa lɛ. Ni bei komɛi lɛ, amɛwoɔ tsofai fɔji loo helai ni haaa baai lɛ afee niyenii ni ehaa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ loo amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do people call crop spray 'medicine' if it can sometimes damage my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi tsɛɔ crop spray akɛ ‘tsofa’ kɛji akɛ bei komɛi lɛ ebaanyɛ efite miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Chemical sprays work like human medicine to fight off pests and diseases, but applying the wrong dose or using harsh chemicals can burn fragile crop leaves and harm the plant's health.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsofa yɛ adesai amli koni ekɛwu eshi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai. Shi kɛ́ akɛ falɛ ni ejaaa tsu nii loo akɛ tsofai ni mli wa tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ baai ni waaa lɛ ni eye tso lɛ hewalɛnamɔ lɛ awui.

english: How can I tell if my plant leaves are being eaten by pests or burned by crop medicine?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai eye mitso lɛ baai lɛ loo akɛ tso tsofa eshã?

english: Pest damage leaves visible holes, chewed edges, or sticky spots, whereas chemical burn usually causes the edges of the leaves to turn dry, yellow, or brown very quickly after spraying.
ga: Nɔ ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ amli baa ji bu ni anaa, naa ni akumɔ, loo hei ni kpɛtɛɔ he. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, tsofai ni ashãa lɛ haa baai lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ, loo amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ oya kɛji akɛ afɔ amɛ nɔ.

english: Is it helpful for my crops if I spray them with chemical medicine every week?
ga: Ani ebaaye ebua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛji mikɛ tsofa ni akɛ tsofa tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ shwie nɔ daa otsi?

english: No, spraying too frequently can weaken your crops, burn flowers and leaves, kill friendly insects that help your farm, and waste your hard-earned money.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ shii abɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha onibii lɛ agbɔjɔ. Fɔfɔi kɛ baai ni ashãa Gbeɔ naanyobɔɔ kooloi ni yeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔ lɛ. kɛ shika ni akɛtsu nii waa ni anáa lɛ ni afiteɔ

english: Can spraying too much chemical medicine actually cause my farm yield to drop?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ fe nine lɛ baaha miŋmɔ lɛ mli yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, over-spraying puts stress on the plant, damaging its leaves and flowers, which reduces its ability to produce good fruits or cocoa pods.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ tsei lɛ anɔ fe nine lɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná haomɔ. efiteɔ baai kɛ fɔfɔii Enɛ haa nyɛmɔ ni ayɔɔ akɛ aaawo aduawai kpakpai loo kookoo ŋmeii lɛ baa shi.

english: What is the best time of day for me to spray my crops with pest medicine?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: Early morning or late afternoon is best because hot mid-day sunlight can cause the chemical liquid to evaporate too quickly or react with the sun to burn the leaves.
ga: Leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane teŋ lɛ baanyɛ aha tsofai ni akɛwoɔ nu mli lɛ atsɔ oya tsɔ loo ekɛ hulu la lɛ afee ekome ni ekɛshã baai.

english: Why do insect pests keep coming back to my farm even after I spray them with chemical medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yaa nɔ amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofai shwie amɛnɔ moŋ.

english: Pests return if the chemical spray misses their hidden eggs, if neighboring farms have untreated pests, or if the insects build up resistance to the chemical from frequent use.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba kɛji tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ shɛɛɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ ahe. Kɛji ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ yɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni asaaa amɛ Aloo kɛji kooloi bibii lɛ ná tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii shii abɔ lɛ ahe hewalɛ.

english: What happens to my farm soil when chemical spray drips onto the ground?
ga: Mɛni baa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Heavy chemical dripping can kill useful soil organisms and earthworms that break down leaves to make natural food for your crop's roots.
ga: Tsofai ni tsii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baanyɛ agbe shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ baai lɛ koni amɛfee adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Are there ways I can protect my tree crops from pests without using heavy chemicals every time?
ga: Ani gbɛ ko yɛ ni matsɔ nɔ mabu mitsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe ni mikɛ tsofai ni tsii tsuuu nii be fɛɛ be?

english: Yes, simple farm practices like pruning excess branches to let in sunlight, clearing weeds regularly, removing diseased fruits, and using natural neem extracts can keep pest numbers down safely.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔ mli nifeemɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ koni hulu la aba mli lɛ yɛ. Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ kɛjɛ ohe daa. Jiemɔ aduawai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Ni kɛ akɛ adebɔɔ mli neem mli nu tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eba tsɛŋemɔ helai ayibɔ shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to build strong stems and green leaves. When food in the soil runs low, the plant moves what little nitrogen it has to the top leaves to keep growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná ŋmeii ni wa kɛ baai eŋɔli. Kɛ niyenii fioo pɛ eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen fioo ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara.

english: Why does my farm yield less harvest every year even when I use the same seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii moŋ?

english: Soil gets tired and loses its nutrients when the same crop is planted year after year without rest. Adding organic manure, compost, or rotating crops puts goodness back into the ground so it can feed your plants again.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nijiaŋ jeɔ wui ni niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ kɛji akɛ adu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi ni hejɔɔmɔ bɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaha kpakpafeemɔ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ koni enyɛ eye ebua otsei lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: What causes my small cocoa pods to turn black and dry up on the tree?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ? Minɔ lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbi yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly during cold, rainy periods. Clearing heavy weeds and pruning dead branches lets sunlight into your farm to dry out the moisture that the fungus needs to grow.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Fɛ̃i ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ fɛ̃i kɛ nugbɔnɛmɔ bei amli lɛ kɛbaa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ waa kɛ tsei niji ni egboi lɛ ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ baaha hulu la ashɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ejie ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa ŋmei lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants are like small babies that cannot handle full sunlight. Without shade trees like plantains or forest trees to shield them, the intense sun burns their young leaves and dries out their shallow roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ abifabii bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Kɛji tsei ni baaha hulutsoo, tamɔ tsei bibii loo koo mli tsei bɛ lɛ, Hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã baai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ agbi.

english: Leaf curling and pale patches are signs of Cassava Mosaic Disease. Tiny whiteflies spread this sickness from sick plants to healthy ones when they suck juices from the leaves.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. small whitefly Hela nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli kɛ́ amɛmu nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Cassava roots stay thin when the soil is packed too hard for the roots to expand, or if the farm was weeded too late while the roots were forming.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã. Aloo kɛji akɛ ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ miifee lɛ.

english: Flowers fall off when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, lack of soil moisture, or a lack of visiting insects like bees to help fertilize the blossoms.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni bɛ loo kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni bɛ.

english: Why do my tomato fruits split open on top right before they get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes split when they get a sudden large amount of rain or water after a dry period. The inside of the fruit grows faster than the skin can stretch, causing it to crack.
ga: Tomato tswaa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ loo nu babaoo ba trukaa yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Yibii lɛ amli lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. kɛ mligbalamɔ baa

english: Why are tiny holes appearing across my young maize leaves like small windows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bu lɛ ji bibioo lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, eje kpo yɛ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ anɔ tamɔ samflɛ bibioo ko.

english: Small holes in maize leaves are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars eating the soft inner leaves while hiding inside the central leaf funnel.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fall armyworm caterpillars, ni yeɔ baa bibii lɛ amli niyenii yɛ be mli ni amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋshɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji mɛi ni feɔ bu bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Plantain roots are shallow and do not grip deep into the soil. When heavy fruit grows on top, the plant becomes top-heavy and soft, wet soil loses its hold on the roots.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛshɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji aduawai ni tsii kwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni eyɛ blɛoo. Shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ baafee nɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ akpɛtɛ he.

english: Cassava plants drop their lower leaves during long dry spells to save water and protect themselves from dying. It is a natural survival trick to hold energy in the roots until the rains return.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛshishigbɛ baai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ gbele he. Eji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ ŋaa akɛ ekɛ hewalɛ ato shishifãi lɛ amli kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baa.

english: When maize seeds are planted too close to each other, the plants fight for sunlight, soil food, and water. This forces them to waste energy growing tall to reach light instead of building fat cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli. Enɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛfite hewalɛ ni amɛdaraa koni amɛyashɛ la lɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaama ŋmeii ni yɔɔ fɔ.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the farm after harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of food out of the soil. Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts put nitrogen—a vital soil nutrient—back into the earth through their roots, helping to restore the land for the next season.
ga: Abele heɔ eniyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts kɛ nitrogen, ni ji shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ kuɔ sɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Koni eye ebua ni asaa jɛmɛ ekoŋŋ kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up like thin tubes during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Rolling leaves is the plant's way of protecting itself. By curling up, the leaves expose less surface area to the burning sun and dry wind, which stops water from evaporating out of the plant too quickly.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ kome ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe he. Curling baai lɛ baa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa egbiɔ lɛ shɛɛɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Enɛ baatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekajɛ tso lɛ mli oya tsɔ.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly when there is too much shade, high humidity, and poor airflow around the cocoa trees during heavy rainy periods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ hulutsoo be babaoo yɛ. Fɛ̃i yɛ jɛmɛ waa, ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɔleɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe lɛ ehiii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Is it good to splash water over the leaves of my pepper plants in the middle of a hot day?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooshɛrɛ nu ashwie pepper tsei ahe yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: No, watering leaves in the full afternoon sun can scorch the foliage and creates a warm, wet environment that allows fungal diseases to attack the plant easily. It is better to water early in the morning near the soil.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ okɛ nu wo baai lɛ anɔ yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã amɛ ni eha shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baatutua tsei. Ehi akɛ ooofɔ nu lɛ leebi yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the plant experiences extreme dry spells. High heat damages the pollen, causing the plant to shed unfertilized flowers to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na hɔmɔ ni naa wa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa fiteɔ pollen. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni awooo amɛ fɔ lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers start sprouting even while stored in a dark barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ kɛji akɛ akɛto ŋmɔ ko ni mli ewo duŋ mli po lɛ?

english: Yams have an internal clock. After a few months of rest after harvest, rising heat levels signal to the tuber that a new planting season is near, causing it to push out sprouts using its stored energy.
ga: Sweet potato yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswaa ko ni yɔɔ mli. Beni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe nyɔji fioo komɛi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, dɔlɛ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ tsɔɔ bulbs lɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei miiba. Ehaa ŋmeii lɛ daa kɛtsɔ hewalɛ ni ato lɛ nɔ.

english: Cutting off unnecessary branches and vertical sucker shoots (chupons) opens up the tree canopy to allow light and fresh air in, while directing food energy into making healthy cocoa pods instead of extra wood.
ga: Niji ni he ehiaaa kɛ tsei ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ (chupons) lɛ ni aaafo lɛ baaye abua ni agbele tso lɛ ŋwɛitsu lɛ naa koni la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa abote mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, akɛ niyenii lɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ moŋ fe ni akɛ tsei krokomɛi baafata he.

english: Why do weeds cause young oil palm seedlings to grow so slowly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa oil palm dumɔwui lɛ daraa blɛoo nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal fertilizer, water, and space directly from young oil palm roots. Clearing a wide circle around the base of the palm ensures the seedling gets all the nutrients it needs.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu kɛ he ko tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛɔ mu tso bibii lɛ amli. Afee kooloo ni mli kwɔ ni bɔleɔ Tso lɛ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to grow green and strong. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients away or when weeds are stealing the plant's food.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ loo jwɛi ju tsei aniyenii.

english: Cassava is usually ready 9 to 12 months after planting when the lower leaves dry up and fall off, and the soil around the base of the main stem begins to crack as the tubers expand underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni ŋmei lɛ mli shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly during the rainy season when there is too much shade, high humidity, and poor air movement around the cocoa trees.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela Fungal helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli Kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ fa babaoo, hulutsoo be lɛ fa babaoo, ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle he lɛ eyaaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Bad cocoa tree.

english: Why is it harmful to burn the bush on my land before I plant my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mashã jwɛi yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani adu nii lɛ?

english: Burning destroys the topsoil's natural organic matter and beneficial organisms that feed your crops. Over time, burning makes the soil hard, dry, and less able to hold water.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa onibii lɛ niyenii lɛ. Beni be hoɔ lɛ Shãa haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ, egbiɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ehiɛ nu.

english: Tomato blossoms drop when temperatures become too hot, when watering is inconsistent, or when sucking insects damage the delicate stems that hold the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu ni akɛhaa lɛ bɛ daa Aloo be mli ni kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ fiteɔ tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hiɛ fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips, aphids, or mites feeding on the undersides of leaves, or by a virus transmitted by those insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips, aphids, loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ kɛbaa lɛ nɔ

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow well even when I do not apply chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fataaa he lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that work with helpful bacteria in the soil to capture nitrogen directly from the air, feeding themselves naturally and improving the soil for future crops.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ helatsɛmɛi ahe nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my maize seeds rot in the ground when I plant right after the very first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The very first rainfall often only wet the surface. If heat returns immediately after, the seeds absorb just enough water to start sprouting but then die and rot in the hot, dry soil before steady rains begin.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu pɛ. Kɛji latsaa lɛ ku esɛɛ eba amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baaŋɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛje shishi amɛkwɛ̃. Shi ebaagbo ni ebaagbo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi nɔ dani nugbɔ anɛ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why are my yam tubers small even though the vines on top are long and leafy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tsei lɛ bibii eyɛ mli akɛ wain tso ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ baai moŋ lɛ?

english: When yam plants are planted too close together or receive too much nitrogen, the plant spends all its energy growing leafy green vines above ground instead of storing food in the tubers below.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu sweet potatoes ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo enine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛdu wain tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato tuber ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli lɛ

english: Why do my young plantain suckers dry up and die when planted in open sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ lɛ?

english: Young plantain suckers have underdeveloped root systems that cannot pull enough water from dry soil. They need partial shade and organic mulch around their bases to stay cool while establishing roots.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni eyako hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ni nyɛɛɛ ajie nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo fã ko kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni bɔleɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he koni eha amɛhe ajɔ be mli ni amɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants are fragile and burn easily in full sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains provides shelter from the hot sun and keeps the soil moist while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to reach up to sunlight to produce energy. Raising the leaves off the ground allows them to catch maximum sunlight, which feeds the tubers growing under the ground to make them large.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ awó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ. ni haa bulb ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara.

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the crops fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in thin plants and very small corn cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii nibii ni yɔɔ sũ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ bibii kwraa.

english: Too many shoots (suckers) take away food and water from the main tree. Leaving only one or two strong suckers allows the main tree to produce larger and healthier fruit bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ shishi (tso lɛ) babaoo tsɔ miihe niyenii kɛ nu kɛmiijɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo yibii akui wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves at the base usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need for green growth. Adding organic manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni tsei he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ Kɛ́ akɛ organic fertilizer loo nitrogen fertilizer fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha eŋɔli lɛ su kɛ hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Empty groundnut pods, often called 'pops,' happen when the soil lacks calcium. Groundnuts need calcium in the soil while the pods are developing underground to fill the shells.
ga: Peanut pods ni bɛ nɔ ko, ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ lɛ ‘pops’ lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ calcium. Calcium he miihia ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ miiya hiɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛwo amɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli ekoŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why is it good for me to cover the wet soil around my crop roots with dried leaves or grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mikɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi baawo shikpɔŋ ni efɔ ni bɔle tsei shishifãi ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with organic matter, called mulching, blocks direct sunlight, keeps the ground moist longer, and prevents weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli woɔ mli lɛ akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni etsi hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ. ni otsi jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ naa.

english: Cassava drops its leaves during hot, dry spells to save water and survive drought. The plant is not dead; once the rains return, it will grow fresh leaves and continue growing underground.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaai lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ, ni egbi koni ekɛbu nu he ni ehi wala mli yɛ hɔmɔ mli. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ, baai heei baaje kpo ni amɛbaaya nɔ amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Flowers fall off when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, hot dry winds, or irregular watering. Giving plants steady moisture during dry periods helps flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ, loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ hao tsei lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha tso lɛ be fɛɛ be yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehaa fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai hiɔ shi.

english: Why are there small jagged holes in the leaves and dirt inside the central funnel of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai kɛ muji yɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛ lɛ nɔ

english: This damage is caused by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm feeding inside the leaves. Catching it early and treating the funnels with neem extract or appropriate controls stops them from destroying the growing tip.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm ni yeɔ tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ. Ni ooomɔ lɛ mra ni okɛ neem mli nu loo nɔ ni sa ni akɛyeɔ nɔ lɛ atsa ŋmeii lɛ. Ehaa efiteɔ ŋmei ni miida lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings need shade because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves. Plantain trees grow quickly and provide broad leaves that protect young cocoa plants while keeping the soil cool and moist during their early years.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui taoɔ shade ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ baanyɛ ashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in wet conditions. Clearing heavy weeds around the tree base and pruning extra branches helps air flow through the farm, which stops the fungus from staying wet and spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ amli. Jwɛi ni tsii ni yɔɔ Tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛ tsei krokomɛi ni afoɔ lɛ baaye abua ni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ baatsi ŋmɔtɔ lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbɛ eshwa.

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a pest that attacks the growing heart of maize. Checking your field early and spraying recommended insecticides or a mild neem seed solution direct into the funnel of the plant controls them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa tsui ni miida lɛ. Kwɛmɔ he ni oduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mra. ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ loo neem dumɔwui ni mli ejɔ waa lɛ afɔ nɔ. tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa tsei lɛ agbɛi lɛ amli koni eye amɛnɔ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn pale yellow instead of staying bright green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which maize relies on to make food and leaves. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the maize regain its green color and build large cobs.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ŋmãa kɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ nɔ koni ekɛfee niyenii kɛ baai Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmãa, ŋmãa, loo nitrogen ŋmãa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ŋmãa lɛ ni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ewo ŋmãa wuji.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants twisting up and developing yellow patterns?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni efee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: This is Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried from plant to plant by small insects called whiteflies. Using disease-resistant cassava stem cuttings recommended by extension officers prevents the disease from reducing your tuber size.
ga: Hela nɛɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ woɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa ekroko nɔ lɛ. Kɛ akɛ ŋmei niji ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni extension nitsulɔi lɛ wo he ŋaa lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ helai anaa ni ebaaha ŋmei ŋmeii lɛ ayibɔ aba shi.

english: Why do my yam tubers turn out short and bent instead of straight and large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji kukuji ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee tɛ̃ɛ ni eyɛ agbo lɛ?

english: Yam roots bend when the soil inside your mounds is compact, hard, or full of rocks. Creating high, loose mounds free of stones gives the tuber space to push down easily and grow long and straight.
ga: Sweet potato shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ gɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli edɔ, ewa, loo eyɛ tɛi. Tɛi ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni tɛi bɛ mli lɛ ni afee lɛ haa he ko kakadaŋŋ ni ja ni yitso lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ shi mlɛo.

english: Tomatoes drop flowers when the soil fluctuates between being too dry and too wet, or when it gets excessively hot. Watering regularly and covering the soil around the base with dried grass helps maintain even moisture so flowers stay on.
ga: Tomato fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi tsɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni edɔ tsɔ teŋ. Aloo kɛ́ edɔ tsɔ Nu ni oooha daa ni okɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishi lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ hiɔ shi koni fɔfɔi lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Leaf curl in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking pests like thrips or mites feeding under the leaves. Spraying early with appropriate pest control solutions clears the insects so new leaves can expand normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa lɛ baa. Ni akɛ tsofai ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ baashwie nɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni ajie kooloi lɛ koni baai heei lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã bɔ ni sa.

english: Why does planting groundnuts on my field first make the maize I plant next grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ haa ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans take nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in their roots in the soil. When the groundnut crop is finished, that left-over nitrogen feeds the following maize crop like natural fertilizer.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei agbe naa lɛ, akɛ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ haa ŋmei tsei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ nɛɛ akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmei.

english: Why does my crop yield get smaller every year if I keep planting on the exact same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛji mitee nɔ midu shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop year after year uses up the specific soil nutrients that crop needs while letting pests build up in the ground. Rotating with different crops or leaving the land to rest allows the soil to rebuild its natural fertility.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tso lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ be mli ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi amli ni atsakeɔ Loo ni ahaa shikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔ ehe, ni ahaa shikpɔŋ lɛ etswaa bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, a key plant nutrient. Adding well-rotted manure or the right fertilizer gives the maize the food it needs to grow green and strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso lɛ mli niyenii titri ko bɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ ni efee ŋmɔŋ ni ehe wa.

english: People tell me that planting beans or cowpeas makes the soil better for future crops, how does that work?
ga: Akɛɛ mi akɛ, kɛ́ adu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Te etsuɔ ​​nii ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Beans and cowpeas have special root nodules that take nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into natural fertilizer in the soil. When the plant dies, that food stays in the ground for the next crop to use.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni heɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai niyenii lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛtsu nii.

english: Why is it harmful to plant my crop seeds very close to each other in the row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the grown plants end up competing with each other for light, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to produce large, healthy yields.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my mature plantain plants easily fall over whenever a heavy wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain ni eda lɛ gbeeɔ shi mlɛo be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baatswa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that can struggle to hold the weight of heavy fruit bunches. Supporting the stems with sturdy wooden or bamboo props helps keep the plants standing until harvesting time.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni baanyɛ akwɛ aduawai ni tsii ni abua naa lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei loo ŋmeii ni wa fĩ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni edamɔɔ shi kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Frequent rains and excess humidity encourage a fungal attack known as Black Pod disease. Clearing extra tree branches to let sunlight in and removing infected pods quickly stops the moisture buildup that spreads the disease.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shii abɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine woɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela lɛ he hewalɛ. Tso lɛ niji amli gbalamɔ kroko koni hulu la abote mli ni ejie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni buaa ehe naa ni gbɛɔ helai oya lɛ kpaa.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from new leaves. Spraying with neem oil or targeted pest controls stops the insects and allows new leaves to grow normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai heei amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Neem fɔ loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ Ehaa kooloi bibii lɛ kpaa ni ehaa baa heei daa bɔ ni sa.

english: Tomatoes drop flowers when they suffer from high heat, erratic watering, or a lack of nutrients like calcium. Keeping soil moisture consistent and mulching around the roots helps flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Tomatoi baajie fɔfɔii kɛji hulutsoo ni naa wa kpe amɛ. nu ni bɛ shiŋŋ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ calcium ni bɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: How do I know when my cassava underground tubers are mature enough to harvest?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting, depending on the variety. You can carefully dig up the soil near the base of one plant to check if the tubers have grown thick enough before harvesting the entire farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Edamɔ tso lɛ henɔi lɛ anɔ Obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsu shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ tso kome shishi lɛ he nii koni okwɛ kɛji ŋmeii lɛ mli eyi obɔ bɔ ni sa dani okpa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my seed yams start sprouting shoots inside the barn long before I am ready to plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ dani mifee klalo akɛ madu amɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers naturally wake up from dormancy when warmth and humidity build up inside the storage area. Keeping your yam barn well-ventilated, cool, and shaded delays sprouting until the planting season begins.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ teɔ shi kɛjɛɔ wɔɔhe mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa beni hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ bua amɛhe naa yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ oha o-sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa, ni eyɛ fɛ̃i, ni eyɛ hulutsoo lɛ, ehaa ekwɛ̃ɔ sɛɛ tsɛɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: Does my swamp rice need to be completely covered in deep water all through its growth?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni akɛ mi-swamp ŋmãa lɛ awo nu ni mli kwɔ mli yɛ be fɛɛ mli ni edaa lɛ?

english: While swamp rice loves water, keeping the water too deep when plants are young can drown them. Maintaining shallow water levels allows roots to breathe while still preventing unwanted weeds from growing.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋshɔ mli ŋmãa sumɔɔ nu moŋ Shi kɛ́ okɛ nu lɛ wo mli tsɔ beni tso lɛ ji gbekɛ lolo lɛ, ebaanyɛ egbo. Kɛ́ aha nu lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ muɔ yɛ be mli ni ehaa jwɛi ni ataooo lɛ hu kwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen food in the soil, or the soil is too waterlogged. Adding fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure gives the maize the food it needs to stay green and build big ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele lɛ bɛ nitrogen niyenii yɛ sũ lɛ mli. aloo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ, ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ baaha ŋmãa lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekɛ toi wuji aba.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny pests like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from under the leaf, or a disease spread by them. Clearing surrounding weeds and spraying organic or recommended neem oil mixtures helps protect the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ni akɛ neem fɔ ni akɛfutuɔ nii loo ni akɛwo ŋaa lɛ afɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu baai lɛ ahe.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot, when the plant lacks water, or if pests attack the blossoms. Regular watering at the root level and protecting plants from harsh midday heat helps the flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ nu loo kɛji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutua fɔfɔi lɛ Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ shishifã lɛ he daa kɛ tso lɛ he ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ gbi lɛ mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under strong sunlight because their leaves are tender. Plantains or fast-growing shade trees should be planted alongside them first to act as living umbrellas that give young cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi yɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ ahewɔ. Esa akɛ okɛ dumɔwui loo shade tsei ni daa oya lɛ afee ekome klɛŋklɛŋ. Bɔni afee ni etsu nii akɛ umbrella aha kookooi bibii lɛ koni amɛná hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to reach high into the sunlight to make food for the tubers growing underground. Staking keeps the leaves open to the sun and holds them off the damp ground where rotting diseases spread.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ shɛɔ hulu la nɔ ni ehaa amɛyaaa hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni helai ni fiteɔ nii baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin without yielding well if I plant seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo ni ekɛ yibiiwoo kpakpa baaa kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, plants fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil food. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to grow strong stems and produce heavy harvests.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa ni ekɛ ŋmaa babaoo baa.

english: Cassava roots rot when left in standing water because flat soil holds excess rain. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows water to drain away freely so the roots stay healthy underground.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ nu ni damɔ shi mli ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ hiɛɔ nugbɔ nu babaoo. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya. No hewɔ lɛ shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans take natural plant food from the air and store it in their roots. When the crop is harvested and roots decay, that extra nitrogen fertilizes the soil for future crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei lɛ jieɔ tsei aniyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni shishifãi lɛ egbo Nakai nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Should I apply my fertilizer to the soil before it rains or immediately after it rains?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani nugbɔ anɛ loo beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Fertilizer works best when placed on moist soil after a light rain or right before a gentle shower. If applied right before heavy downpours, the strong water flow washes the expensive fertilizer away before the roots can drink it.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. aloo dani okɛ ohe awo nu mli fioo Kɛji akɛwo mli dani nugbɔ nɛ waa Nu ni naa wa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa lɛ dani shishifãi lɛ nuɔ.

english: How do I know which plantain shoots to cut away and which ones to leave on the main plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male plantains ni esa akɛ mafo? Ni mɛɛ niji esa akɛ ashi yɛ tso titri lɛ nɔ?

english: Keep only one or two strong shoots with narrow leaves called sword suckers alongside the main plant. Cutting away extra shoots prevents them from stealing food and water, allowing the main plant to produce larger plantain bunches.
ga: Kpãa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni baai bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ 1-2 pɛ. Dumɔ nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ klante ŋmeii lɛ yɛ tso titri lɛ masɛi. Kɛ́ ofolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛ nu. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ woɔ plantain tsei wuji.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because intense direct sunlight burns their foliage and dries out the soil moisture fast. Planting shade crops like plantains provides shelter and creates the cool environment young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa mɔ náa wɔɔhe ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa kookoo bibii lɛ koni amɛhi shi lɛ baa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves indicate a nitrogen deficiency in the soil. The maize plant moves available nitrogen from older lower leaves to feed newer upper leaves, signaling that your crop needs fertilizer or compost application.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi tsei tsiɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ niyenii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ otso lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why shouldn't I save and replant the seeds from my high-yielding hybrid maize harvest next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ni ji hybrid dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ toɔ ni mikɛduɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for one generation. Replanting saved hybrid seeds results in low yields, uneven crop heights, and weak plants because the offspring lose the vigor of their parent seeds.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛhaa yinɔ kome. Hybrid dumɔwui heei ni aŋmala ashwie shi lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi. Tsei lɛ abɔlemɔ lɛ jeee ekome ni tsei lɛ hu bɛ hewalɛ ejaakɛ seshibii lɛ ahewalɛ ni yɔɔ nyɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ baa shi.

english: Cassava roots rot in wet soils that drain poorly, creating conditions for fungal diseases to thrive. Poorly drained soil deprives roots of oxygen, causing them to decay underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ ni nu shwieee nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛi ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ aya hiɛ yɛ mli lɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ aye hɔmɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my yam vines grow plenty of leafy foliage but only give me tiny tubers at harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ baai babaoo shi ŋmeii bibii pɛ yɔɔ mli yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Excessive leaf growth with small tubers often happens when there is too much nitrogen in the soil. High nitrogen encourages the plant to put energy into growing leaves rather than swelling its underground roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yaa hiɛ fe nine ni bulbs bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ baa kɛji nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo lɛ woɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ awo baai ni miida lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up tightly and look stunted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe waa ni etamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in peppers is usually caused by sap-sucking insects like thrips, aphids, or whiteflies that transmit viruses or physically damage the young tissue as the leaves expand.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, aphids loo whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai loo amɛfiteɔ fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baai lɛ baa.

english: Tomato flowers fall off without fruiting due to heat stress or irregular watering. Extremely high temperatures dry out the pollen, preventing pollination and causing the plant to shed the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ hewɔ. He ni mli edɔ waa lɛ haa pollen lɛ gĩɔ. Tsi pollination naa ni oha tsei lɛ agbo

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during mild winds even when the stems look thick and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli wa waa mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ

english: Plantain trees fall over easily when microscopic worms called nematodes or banana weevils eat away the roots underground, leaving the heavy upper stem without a solid foundation.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo banana ŋmeii lɛ ye shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ. Ashi ŋwɛi tso ni tsii lɛ ni shishitoo ni ma shi shiŋŋ bɛ he.

english: Why does the top of my soil turn into a hard crust after rain, making it hard for seedlings to shoot out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni wa beni nugbɔ enɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ? Ani ehaa ewaa kɛhaa dumɔwui lɛ akɛ amɛakwɛ̃?

english: Soil crusting happens when land lacks organic matter like decomposed leaves or manure. Without organic matter to bind soil particles together, heavy rain breaks down soil texture and hot sunshine bakes it hard.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, tamɔ baai loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ. Kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni baaha sũ mli nibii bibii lɛ afee ekome lɛ bɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaha sũ lɛ mli agbala. ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why is it harmful to place chemical fertilizer directly against the stem of my young crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baawo mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Concentrated fertilizer draws moisture out of plant tissues through salt burn. Putting fertilizer directly against stems or fresh roots burns the plant tissue, causing it to wither or die.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ jieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei amli kɛtsɔɔ ŋmei ni shãa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tsei loo shishifãi heei amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ mli fãji lɛ ashã. Enɛ baanyɛ aha egbi loo egbo.

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct, intense sunlight and high heat. They need temporary shade from nurse crops like plantains to maintain soil moisture and cool temperatures while their roots establish.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Amɛmiitao be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛɔ helatsɛmɛi anɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ fɛ̃i ahi shi yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: When too many shoots (suckers) grow together, they compete with the mother plant for soil nutrients and water. Removing extra suckers leaves energy for the main plant to produce large, heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii (ŋmeii) babaoo ni miida yɛ he kome lɛ Amɛkɛ tso nyɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ náa hewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ aduawai wuji ni tsii.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is essential for green foliage growth, so adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps restore healthy leaf color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he hiaa waa kɛha baa eŋɔli lɛ dalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha baai lɛ ahe afee fɛo ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell from above the ground if my cassava is ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ akɛ mi-cassava lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is typically mature when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack open as the tubers swell underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ eda beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. Ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni tuber lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds away from my young cassava stalks during the first three months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kakadaji kɛjɛ yucca tsei bibii lɛ amli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji etɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Young cassava grows slowly at first, so tall weeds easily steal light, water, and soil nutrients. Keeping the field clean early on lets the cassava roots build strong tubers before the canopy closes.
ga: Kasava bibioo lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli. No hewɔ lɛ, jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ juɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli oya. He lɛ he tsemɔ nɔkwɛmɔ kɛjɛ shishijee Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ bulbs ni mli wa dani ŋmei lɛ ŋmɛɔ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves upward to catch sunlight for food production. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, reducing fungal diseases and helping the tubers grow much larger.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hulu la bɔni afee ni amɛná niyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Ehaa ŋmeii helai baa shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ daraa babaoo.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves roll up tightly and stop the fruits from growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe waa ni amɛtsiɔ aduawai lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that feed on plant juices and spread viruses. Controlling these pests with mild soap sprays or neem extract helps protect the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni yeɔ tsei amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ samla ni mli ejɔ loo neem mli nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ ye nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu baai lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly droop and die during the daytime even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ? Ani nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lolo?

english: This sudden wilting is often caused by soil-borne fungi or bacteria that block the flow of water inside the stem. Rotating tomato crops with maize or cassava helps clear these disease organisms from the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii loo helatsɛmɛi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni tsiɔ nu ni hoɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ naa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ shwiemɔ trukaa nɛɛ baa. Tomato ni akɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ helai nɛɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the central growing tips of my young maize look chewed up with dark dust inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tips lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛyɛ sũ ni mli edɔ yɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the fall armyworm caterpillar, which feeds inside the leaf funnel and leaves behind its waste. Checking fields early and applying targeted natural or approved controls stops them from destroying the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmeii ni egbee shi, ni amɛyeɔ nii yɛ baai amli ni amɛshiɔ amɛjwɛi lɛ. Gbɛjegbɛ nɔ kwɛmɔ mra kɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ loo nɔkwɛmɔnii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii. Etsiɔ nakai ŋmɔji lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why does planting groundnuts in my field make the maize I plant next season grow stronger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ daa waa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that have friendly bacteria in their roots capable of taking nitrogen from the air and trapping it in the soil. When the roots decay, they leave behind free natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ naanyobɔɔ bacteria yɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni baanyɛ agbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ fite lɛ, amɛshiɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha dumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops produce so much more harvest during the main rainy season compared to the minor season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ shishijee nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli kɛ akɛto nɔ ni ji enyɔ nɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: During the main rainy season, crops receive consistent moisture, optimal sunlight, and favorable ground temperatures, allowing plants to flower heavily and produce full yields. In the minor season, irregular rain causes plant stress, leading to fewer flowers and lower harvest yields.
ga: Yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ mli lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baaná ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa. hulu la ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa ni sa Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi babaoo ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni fa. Yɛ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni ekɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔii fioo pɛ baa, ni ŋmaa lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Is it possible to produce a good harvest during the dry off-season, and how can I keep my crops alive?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ ana ŋmaa kpakpa yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ sɛɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ahi shi?

english: Yes, off-season crop production is possible using artificial watering like drip irrigation, conserving soil moisture with organic mulch, and growing shade trees. Off-season harvests often command higher market prices because crop supply in the market is low.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ aná ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ be mli lɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛfee tamɔ drip irrigation nɔ. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ organic mulch. kɛ tsei ni aduɔ koni akɛha hulutsoo Bei pii lɛ, ŋmaakpamɔ ni bɛ be mli lɛ haa jarayeli jara yaa hiɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni faaa yɛ jara nɔ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why does so much of the money I make from selling my crop harvest go toward paying hired farm labor?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ shika ni minine shɛɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛhɔ̃ɔ lɛ mli lɛ babaoo woɔ nitsumɔ he nyɔmɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni akɛ kpaŋmɔ woɔ mli lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Farming operations like land clearing, weeding, chemical spraying, and harvesting require heavy physical work. Relying fully on hired labor quickly drains farm earnings, which is why many farmers use community labor-sharing groups or simple machines to reduce costs.
ga: Okwaayeli, tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ Eheɔ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ babaoo. Hiɛ ni akɛfɔ̃ɔ nitsulɔi ni awoɔ amɛ nyɔmɔ lɛ nɔ kwraa lɛ eha ŋmɔ mli shika ni anáa lɛ eba shi waa. Enɛ hewɔ ni okwaafoi babaoo kɛ akutsoŋ nitsumɔ mlijaa kui loo tsɔnei ni yɔɔ mlɛo tsuɔ nii lɛ. koni akɛba shika ni afiteɔ lɛ shi

english: How do I calculate whether my farm made a true financial profit after selling all my crop bags?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu he akɔntaa kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ diɛŋtsɛ beni mihɔ̃ɔ mi-grow bags lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ?

english: To calculate your profit, add up all the money earned from selling every bag of produce, then subtract all your total expenses—including seeds, fertilizers, farm chemicals, land rent, and labor fees. If the money left over is positive, your farm made a profit.
