ga: Bɔni afee ni obu sɛɛnamɔ ni oná lɛ he akɔntaa Kɛ shika fɛɛ ni onine shɛ nɔ kɛjɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ kotoku fɛɛ kotoku mli lɛ jaramɔ mli lɛ afata he. No sɛɛ lɛ, jiemɔ shika fɛɛ ni ofiteɔ lɛ kɛjɛ mli. Dumɔwui, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofai fata he. shikpɔŋ nyɔmɔwoo kɛ nyɔmɔwoo kɛji shika ni eshwɛ lɛ ji positive Oŋmɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ.

english: How does the traditional harvest-sharing agreement work between a farmer and a landowner in Ghana?
ga: Te kusum mli ŋmaakpamɔ mlijaa he kpaŋmɔi ni yɔɔ okwaafoi kɛ shikpɔŋtsɛmɛi ateŋ yɛ Ghana lɛ tsuɔ nii ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Under traditional agreements like Abusa or Abunu, the final harvested crop or sales proceeds are divided into portions—Abusa splits the yield into three parts (two for the farmer, one for the landowner), while Abunu splits it equally in two. This allows farmers to work land without paying upfront cash rent.
ga: Yɛ kusum gbɛjianɔtoi tamɔ Abusa loo Abunu shishi lɛ, ajaa naagbee ŋmaa loo jarayeli mli nyɔmɔwoo lɛ mli awoɔ fãi amli, ni Abusa jaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli etɛ. (Fãi enyɔ kɛha okwaafoi eko kɛha shikpɔŋtsɛ lɛ), yɛ be mli ni Abunu jaa nibii ni adu lɛ mli enyɔ ni yeɔ egbɔ, ni ehaa okwaafoi lɛ tsuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nii ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛwo shika kɛha shĩa nyɔmɔ kɛtsɔ hiɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop many of their young flowers and pods before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii bibii babaoo dani eshɛɔ shweremɔ he lɛ?

english: Young pod drop, known as cherelle wilt, happens when the crop lacks sufficient water, soil nutrients, or light, or when pests attack. The plant naturally sheds excess pods it cannot support, so adequate fertilization and pest management help save the harvest.
ga: Pods bibii, ni ale amɛ hu akɛ Cherelle Wilt lɛ baa kɛji nu bɛ tso lɛ mli. niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli loo la ni fa bɔ ni sa loo be mli ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutua lɛ Tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli jogbaŋŋ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do my young crops wither and die when planted in direct, open sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings have delicate leaves and tender roots that dry out quickly under intense heat. Planting fast-growing nurse crops like plantain or cassava provides living shade that keeps the soil cool and moist until the young plants grow strong.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii ni gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ la ni naa wa waa shishi. Nurse tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni yaa hiɛ Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná ŋmɔlɔ ni baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi tso bibioo lɛ baadara waa.

english: Crops remove nutrients from the soil every time they grow and produce fruit. If you do not replenish the soil using organic manure, compost, or fertilizers, the soil becomes exhausted, leading to declining yields season after season.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ ni amɛwo yibii. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii haaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, ebaafite, ni no baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ aba shi yɛ be kɛ bei amli.

english: Why do insects and crop diseases cause more damage to my farm during the minor rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii kɛ tsei ahe helai fiteɔ miŋmɔ lɛ babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Warm and humid conditions during the minor season create ideal breeding environments for insects and fungal spores. Because crops are often stressed by erratic rainfall during this period, they are weaker and less able to fight off diseases.
ga: Shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ yɛ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ fɔɔ yɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii haoɔ. Tso lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ekɛ helai awuu.

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally adapted to local soils, making them faster at absorbing water, fertilizer, and sunlight than domesticated crops. Clearing weeds early prevents them from stealing critical resources from your main crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni kɛ amɛhe ewo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa amɛnyɛɔ amɛheɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ shia lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju nibii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ onibii titrii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for water, sunlight, and nutrients in the soil. This competition makes the plants grow tall and thin with tiny, poorly filled cobs instead of strong stalks with large yields.
ga: Kɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii bibii. poorly packaged Mohu ɔ, a ngɛ tsohi nɛ a he wa, nɛ a woɔ yiblii fuu.

english: Why does planting beans or cowpeas alongside my maize make the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ midu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ masɛi lɛ, ehaa edaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas belong to a family of plants called legumes that take nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil through their roots. Maize needs a lot of nitrogen to grow strong and green, so it feeds on the soil nutrients improved by the beans.
ga: Peas kɛ cowpeas fata tsei akuu ko ni atsɛɔ amɛ legumes lɛ he. ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ Abɛi he miihia nitrogen babaoo koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni efee ŋmɔŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, eyeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni ŋmeii lɛ haa ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: How can I know if my land is ready and healthy enough for planting tomatoes without using chemical fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo ni eyɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu tomato ni mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Healthy soil is usually dark in color, crumbly to touch, holds moisture well without staying waterlogged, and contains living creatures like earthworms. If previous weeds grew thick and dark green on the plot, the soil usually has good natural fertility.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Efoɔ kɛji akɛ ata he Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni nu bɛ mli Ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli, tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii yɛ, kɛji akɛ tsutsu lɛ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why do my pepper leaves roll up and twist even when I give them water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu moŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids, thrips, or mites feeding on the underside of leaves, or by a virus transmitted by whiteflies. The insects suck out the plant sap, causing leaves to distort and stunt the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Kplukai shwieɔ tsei amli nu lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsĩɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ naa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off instead of turning into fruits during hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high during the day or night, tomato pollen becomes sticky or sterile, preventing proper pollination. The plant recognizes it cannot produce a healthy fruit and drops the flower to save its energy.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ yɛ shwane loo gbɛkɛ mli lɛ Tomato pollen lɛ shwieɔ shi loo ebɛ fɔmɔ nii. Etsiɔ pollination ni sa naa. Tso lɛ yɔseɔ akɛ enyɛŋ ewo yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛshɛrɛ fɔfɔi lɛ amɛshwie koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When heavy rains waterlog the ground for too long, oxygen is cut off from the roots, causing underground fungal diseases to attack and rot the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Afoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ji oxygen lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii helai tutuaa amɛ ni amɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: During Harmattan, dry winds and hot sun cause water to evaporate rapidly from leaves. Cocoa trees drop their leaves naturally to reduce water loss and protect their main stem from drying out completely until the rains return.
ga: Yɛ harmattan beaŋ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ haa nu shwieɔ oya kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli. Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi, ni ebu tso titri lɛ he koni ekagbi kwraa kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating small holes in the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu bibii lɛ? Yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that hides inside the central growing shoot (whorl) of young maize to feed on tender leaves. They must be sprayed early in the morning or late evening when they come out to feed.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ (ring) lɛ amli koni eye baai bibii lɛ. Esa akɛ ashwie nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ beni ajeɔ kpo koni ayatao niyenii.

english: Why do my harvested yams start growing roots and shoots in the barn before I sell them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ bɔi shishifãi shwiemɔ ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani manyɛ mahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Yams are living tubers that enter a natural resting phase after harvest. Once warm temperatures and air moisture signal that a new season is near, the tuber breaks dormancy and uses its stored food to sprout fresh shoots.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka ni boteɔ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Beni hulutsoo kɛ latsaa ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ be hee ko ebɛŋkɛ. Bulbs lɛ fiteɔ dormance ni amɛkɛ niyenii ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ ŋmeii heei.

english: Hybrid maize seeds are created by crossing specific parent plants to produce high yield in the first generation. If you plant seeds saved from that harvest, the second-generation plants lose their uniform strength, resulting in lower yields and uneven growth.
ga: Afeɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni akɛfee ŋmãa kɛtsɔ fɔlɔ tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni akɛfoɔ mli koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ Yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli tsei lɛ laajeɔ amɛhewalɛ ni tamɔ amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi ni eyaaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some cocoa varieties grow very well on my neighbor's land but fail on my own farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo henɔi komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ akutsoŋbii ashikpɔji anɔ shi amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛŋmɔji amli lɛ amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: Different cocoa varieties require specific soil types, rainfall levels, and shade conditions. If your land has poorer soil or gets less water, a high-yielding variety meant for rich, moist land will not perform well without extra organic fertilizer and shade.
ga: Kokoo henɔ fɛɛ henɔ biɔ shikpɔŋ henɔi pɔtɛɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, kɛ hulutsoo shihilɛ. Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii loo nu fioo pɛ yɔɔ lɛ Tsoi srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo kɛha hei ni baa nii, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ efeŋ jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ hulutsoo be fataaa he.

english: What is the main difference between traditional local cocoa seeds and the new hybrid seedlings from extension officers?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔi titrii ni yɔɔ blema maŋ lɛ mli kookoo ŋmeii kɛ dumɔwui heei ni akɛfee ekome ni jɛ extension nitsulɔi adɛŋ lɛ ateŋ?

english: Traditional local cocoa trees take 3 to 5 years to bear fruit and grow very tall, while hybrid cocoa seedlings produce pods much faster—in 2 to 3 years—and stay shorter, making harvesting easier and yields much higher if well maintained.
ga: Kusum mli cacao tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ heɔ afii 3 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛwoɔ yibii ni amɛdaraa waa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kookoo dumɔwui ni akɛ tsofai ebɔ he lɛ woɔ ŋmeii mra kwraa, yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, ni amɛkwɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ be kukuoo ko. Enɛ haa ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo, ni ehaa yibii babaoo baa kɛji akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I attach a better cocoa branch to my old, weak cocoa tree so it produces bigger pods?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ cacao niji ni hi jogbaŋŋ akpɛtɛ cacao tsei ni egbɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ ahe koni amɛha ŋmeii lɛ afee wuji?

english: You can use a technique called grafting or budding. By taking a fresh shoot from a high-producing cocoa tree and attaching it to the trunk of your existing tree, the new branch will grow and produce the large pods of the improved variety.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋaa ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ grafting loo budding atsu nii. Afeɔ enɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmeii heei ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ kookoo tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ amli ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ tsei ni yɔɔ momo lɛ ashishifãi ahe lɛ nɔ. Niji heei baakwɛ̃ ni amɛbaawo ŋmeii wuji kɛjɛ tso ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli.

english: Is it safe for me to plant two different cocoa varieties right next to each other on the same plot?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu kookoo henɔi enyɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting multiple varieties on the same plot can actually protect your farm. If a disease attacks one variety, the other variety may be resistant to it, ensuring you still get a harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ odu tsei srɔtoi babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ ebu oŋmɔ lɛ he diɛŋtsɛ. Kɛji hela lɛ ba yɛ kooloi akuu kome mli lɛ Kooloi akuu kroko baanyɛ afee nɔ ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ hela lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okpa ŋmaa lɛ lolo.

english: Can I plant food crops like cassava or plantain inside my cocoa farm, or will they ruin my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli? Aloo tsei nɛɛ baafite mi-cacao tsei lɛ?

english: Planting plantains alongside young cocoa is helpful because plantain leaves provide crucial shade. However, cassava should be kept slightly farther away because its heavy root system can steal water and nutrients from young cocoa plants.
ga: Sɛɛnamɔi yɛ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ cocoa tsei bibii ahe lɛ he ejaakɛ baai lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa waa. Shi kɛlɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha amɛhi he ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ fioo ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi ni tsii lɛ baanyɛ aju nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ amli.

english: How do I know if my land is suitable for growing cocoa or if I should plant another crop instead?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha kookoo ŋmɔ loo esa akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi moŋ?

english: Cocoa prefers deep, rich soil that holds moisture but drains well after heavy rain. If your land is very rocky, sandy, or gets flooded easily, crops like cashew, oil palm, or rice will perform much better than cocoa.
ga: Cocoa sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni baa nii ni hiɛɔ nu mli. Shi nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛi, ŋã, loo nu shwieɔ nɔ oya lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ cashew nuts, palm oil, loo ŋmãa baatsu nii jogbaŋŋ kwraa fe kookoo.

english: Why do cocoa trees planted under big shade trees stay green during the dry season while cocoa in full sun turns yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ ashishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni kookoo kɛji akɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shɛ ehe lɛ ebaatsɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Big shade trees reduce ground temperature and preserve water in the soil, protecting young cocoa from drying out. Full-sun cocoa grows faster in rainy months but suffers severe leaf burn during dry, hot harmattan seasons unless well irrigated.
ga: Tsei wuji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dɔlɛ baa shi, ni amɛhaa nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ebuɔ kookoo bibii ahe koni amɛkagbi. Cocoa ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ daa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ nyɔji amli. Shi tsɛŋemɔ hela ni naa wa yeɔ lɛ yɛ harmattan be ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ mli. ja enine shɛ nu kpakpa nɔ

english: Why do foreign hybrid cocoa trees seem to catch diseases faster than our older local cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni maŋsɛɛ cacao tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yeɔ helai oya fe cacao tsei ni etsɛ, ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid varieties put most of their energy into producing lots of pods quickly, which can make them weak against diseases if they lack fertilizer or pruning. Older local trees grow slower and have naturally tough bark, but produce fewer pods.
ga: Hybrid henɔi lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfee ŋmeii babaoo oya. Enɛ haa helai yeɔ amɛ oya kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni afolɔ mli lɛ faaa. Maŋ tsei ni edara lɛ daa blɛoo ni amɛyɛ tsitsii ni mli wa fe tsutsu lɛ. Shi ha pods fioo.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce many flowers during the rainy season, but most of them fall off before forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ? Shi amɛteŋ mɛi babaoo gbeeɔ shi dani amɛjeɔ kpo akɛ pods?

english: Cocoa flowers drop when heavy rains wash away pollen, when insects attack them, or when the tree lacks soil nutrients. Pruning extra branches and feeding the soil helps the tree retain flowers so they turn into pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ. Beni kooloi bibii batutua tso lɛ loo be mli ni tso lɛ bɛ niyenii yɛ sũ lɛ mli Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ niyenii ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli bɔni afee ni enyɛ efee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are my young cocoa trees producing smaller pods compared to the trees on older farms in my village?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ akɛto tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ momo ni yɔɔ mi akrowa lɛ mli lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees use a lot of energy building strong roots and stems during their early years, leading to smaller pods initially. As the tree matures and its root system expands, the pods will naturally grow larger.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii kɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii koni amɛwo shishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi ni wa yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli, ni no haa amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shishijee mli. Beni tso lɛ daa ni eshishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ. Pods lɛ baafee wuji yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How long does a rubber tree take from the time I plant it before I can start harvesting the sap?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ ni rɔbɔt tso ko feɔ dani rɔbɔt kpamɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi?

english: Rubber trees usually take about 5 to 7 years to mature before they are ready for tapping. During this waiting period, the trunk needs to reach a proper thickness (around 50 cm circumference) to ensure tapping does not stunt or harm the tree.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, rɔbɔt tsei heɔ afii 5 kɛyashi 7 dani amɛfeɔ klalo kɛha ŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ mɛmɔ be nɛɛ mli lɛ Esa akɛ tso lɛ mli tsɔne lɛ afee nɔ ni sa. (ebɔleɔ he aaafee 50 cm) koni ana akɛ tsɔne ni akɛtswaa lɛ lɛ haŋ tso lɛ agbɔjɔ loo eyeee awui.

english: Can I plant cassava or maize between my young rubber trees while waiting for them to grow?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ rɔbɔt tsei bibii ateŋ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Yes, during the first 2 to 3 years when young trees are still small, you can intercrop with food crops like maize, cassava, or legumes. This helps you earn income and feed your family before the tree canopy closes and blocks sunlight.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 lɛ mli beni dumɔwui lɛ darako lolo lɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ niyenii nibii tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, loo ŋmãa adu amɛ. Enɛ baaye abua bo ni oná shika ni okwɛ oweku lɛ dani tso lɛ ŋwɛitsu lɛ aŋmɛ ni etsi hulu lɛ naa.

english: If I plant long-term tree crops like rubber on my land, will it ruin the soil for future crops?
ga: Kɛji midu tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo tamɔ rɔbɔt tsei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ani ebaafite shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Rubber trees actually protect soil from heavy rain erosion with their deep roots and fallen leaves that decay into rich organic matter. However, because they draw deep soil nutrients over many years, the soil will need fertilizer replenishment if you clear them later for seasonal crops.
ga: Rɔba tsei buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he kɛtsɔ amɛshishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ baai ni egbee shi lɛ anɔ, ni amɛgbalaa amɛfeɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo. Shi, akɛni amɛgbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ afii babaoo mli hewɔ lɛ, No hewɔ lɛ ehe baahia ni awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji ojie mli sɛɛ mli kɛha tsei ni baa be mli lɛ.

english: How do I know if my land is better suited for long-term tree crops rather than seasonal food crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ fe niyenii ni aduɔ yɛ be mli lɛ?

english: Tree crops like rubber prefer deep, well-drained soils in areas with high, consistent rainfall. If your land gets flooded easily or has shallow, rocky soil, it is better for food crops like rice or vegetables rather than deep-rooted tree crops.
ga: Tsoi ni yɔɔ jwɛi mli tamɔ rɔbɔt tsei sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa ni eyaa nɔ daa lɛ. Kɛji akɛ nu shwieɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya loo eyɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛha niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai moŋ fe tsei ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my farm trees turn yellow and drop off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Many tree crops, including rubber, shed their leaves during the dry season as a natural defense to conserve water. This seasonal leaf drop helps the tree survive moisture stress, and fresh green leaves will sprout once the rains return.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi babaoo ni Rɔba fata he Eshwieɔ ebaa lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ nu he. Nɛkɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Ni baai eŋɔli heei baakwɛ̃ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Why is correct spacing so important when planting young tree seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɛ ni sa ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ he hiaa waa kɛ́ adu dumɔwui bibii lɛ?

english: Proper spacing ensures each tree receives enough sunlight, air, water, and soil nutrients. Planting trees too close together causes them to fight for resources, leading to thin trunks, low yields, and easy spread of fungal diseases.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ nibii ni he hiaa lɛ ahe tawuu baa, tsei lɛ ahe tsei bibii, yibiiwoo ni baa shi, kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: Does harvesting sap from a rubber tree every week shorten the tree's lifespan?
ga: Ani nu ni jɛɔ rɔbɔt tsei amli lɛ ni abua naa daa otsi lɛ baaha tso lɛ wala afee kuku?

english: If tapping is done correctly with the right depth and cut angle, it will not harm the tree. Properly managed rubber trees can continue producing latex safely for 25 to 30 years without dying.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afo lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni sa lɛ, eyeŋ tso lɛ awui. Rɔba tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aya nɔ afee latɛs shweshweeshwe afii 25 kɛyashi 30 ni amɛgbooo.

english: Why do weeds grow faster and choke my young crop saplings during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛtsiɔ tsei bibii anaa yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that absorb rainwater and nutrients much faster than young crop saplings. Regular clearing around the base of your young saplings is necessary so weeds do not steal the water and light your crops need.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni shwieɔ nugbɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii oya fe dumɔwui bibii. clearing around Odumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi daa he miihia. Bɔni afee ni jwɛi akaju nu kɛ la kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: Why are my food crops growing poorly when I plant them close to large shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi niyenii tsei lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Large trees have wide canopies that block essential sunlight needed for crop growth. Their big root systems also pull water and nutrients out of the ground before smaller crops can reach them.
ga: Tsei ni eda lɛ yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni da ni tsiɔ hulu la ni he hiaa koni tsei lɛ adalɛ naa lɛ naa. Amɛ shishifãi wuji lɛ hu gbalaa nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe.

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist at the start or mid-point of the rainy season, but avoid applying it right before a heavy downpour. This allows the soil to absorb the fertilizer so the roots can take up nutrients efficiently.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee loo teŋgbɛ. Shi tsi ohe kɛjɛ he ni ooowo amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ anɛ waa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli nibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, an essential plant food, or that the soil is waterlogged and the roots cannot breathe properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa. Aloo nu eyi sũ lɛ mli obɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves roll up and curl during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl during hot and dry weather to reduce water loss from their surface, acting as a natural shield to survive heat stress.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ ni egbiɔ koni nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛi lɛ aba shi. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko ni tsiɔ mɔ naa koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ dɔlɛ mli haomɔ mli.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the plants before setting any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani ewoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures become too high or when there is extreme wetness or dryness, causing heat stress that prevents pollination.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ. Enɛ kɛ dɔlɛ haomɔ ni tsiɔ pollination naa lɛ baa.

english: Why do my crops wilt in the hot sun even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ miigbo yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji mikɛ nu wo nɔ leebi po.

english: In intense midday sun, water evaporates from leaves faster than roots can draw water up from the soil, causing temporary wilting until the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli yɛ shwane mli Nu lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Egboɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why does my cassava yield smaller tubers when I plant it too close to maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa bibii kwɛ̃ɔ kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmãa tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely together, they compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, and faster-growing crops like maize shade out the cassava.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Ni tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ ŋmãa, haa ŋmãa haa ŋmãa.

english: How do I know that my cassava roots under the soil are fully matured for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei shishifãi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava plants signal maturity when lower leaves naturally turn yellow and shed, and small cracks appear on the soil surface around the base of the stem.
ga: Cassava tsei tsɔɔ akɛ amɛmiida kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbee shi. ni ŋmeii bibii yɛ Ejeɔ kpo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ebɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ he.

english: Why do seeds saved from my previous harvest yield less than certified seeds from the agrodealer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui ni mibua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii ni faaa fe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ okwaayeli mli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ?

english: Saved seeds lose their vigor over successive generations and can carry seed-borne diseases, while certified seeds are specially bred for high purity, disease resistance, and yield.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ ahewalɛ baaje amɛdɛŋ yɛ yinɔi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ helai ni jɛɔ dumɔwui amli baa lɛ aba. Yɛ be mli ni akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛhe atse waa, helai nyɛŋ amɔ amɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo lɛ.

english: Why is clearing weeds early in the growth stage so important for my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ he hiaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young crop seedlings and steal the nutrients, water, and light that young plants need to build strong root systems.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe dumɔwui bibii ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ la ni he hiaa tsei bibii koni amɛma shishifãi ni wa lɛ.

english: Why does adding dried cow dung or poultry manure help my sandy soil stay moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo kooloi ashishifã ni egbi ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa mishikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ mli fũuɔ lɛ?

english: Animal manure adds organic matter that acts like a sponge, helping sandy soils bind together and hold moisture around root zones longer.
ga: Manure kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji fataa he. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ he ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shishifãi lɛ amli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do young cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni amɛkã tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Cocoa pods turn black primarily due to Black Pod disease caused by excessive humidity and damp shade, or naturally when the tree sheds surplus pods it cannot feed.
ga: Nɔ titri ni kɛ cocoa pods ni feɔ ediŋŋ lɛ baa ji black pods hela ni jɛɔ hulutsoo ni fa fe nine kɛ hulutsoo ni mli edɔ mli baa lɛ. Aloo yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, beni tso ko shwieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni enyɛŋ eye lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow strong. This happens when the soil lacks organic matter or when heavy rains wash away the nutrients from around the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ bɛ loo kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I plant them in an open field without trees or plantains around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei loo plantains bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and shallow roots that burn easily in full sunlight. Planting plantain trees alongside cocoa provides temporary shade and holds soil moisture, acting like an umbrella to protect the young trees during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni akɛ kookoo duɔ lɛ haa be kukuoo mli hɔɔŋ ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ akpɔlɔ ni buɔ tso bibioo lɛ he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: What is eating small holes in the middle leaves of my maize, and why do I see little green caterpillars inside?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ nɔ Ni mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Those caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that hides inside the growing center of maize plants during the day to feed on soft leaves. If left untreated early, they damage the growing point and stop the maize from producing healthy cobs.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii lɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ naa yɛ ŋmei tsei ni miida lɛ ateŋ yɛ gbi mli koni eye baai bibii lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ashi lɛ ni atsaaa lɛ mra Efiteɔ he ni ŋmãa lɛ daa lɛ ni ehaaa ŋmãa lɛ afee ŋmãa ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops produce very thin stems and small fruits when I plant many seeds close together in one spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa kɛ aduawai bibii yɛ be mli ni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing crops fight with each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Spacing plants properly gives each plant enough room to spread its roots and leaves to grow big and healthy.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaagbɛ eshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ eshwa koni tso lɛ aya nɔ agbo ni efee hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground before I am even ready to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani mifee klalo po akɛ makpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot mostly when water sits in the soil for too long during heavy rains, causing the roots to suffocate and decay. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ babaoo kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off onto the ground without growing into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress, such as very high heat, dry soil, or sudden irregular watering. When the plant feels stressed, it drops its flowers to conserve energy.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛna haomɔi, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ trukaa ni bɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ tso lɛ nu he akɛ eyɛ haomɔ mli lɛ Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why shouldn't I spread fertilizer on my farm right before a big rain comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes fertilizer away off the surface of the soil before the plant roots can drink it, wasting your money. Fertilizer works best when applied to moist soil when rain is light or after heavy rain has passed.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ nuɔ. Enɛ baaha ofite oshika. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ beni nugbɔ enɛ fioo loo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ.

english: Why do yam plants grow bigger tubers when I give the leaves sticks to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tsei lɛ woɔ bulbs wuji beni mihaa niji lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yam vines produce tubers using energy from sunlight collected by their leaves. Staking allows the leaves to spread out higher in the air to catch maximum sunlight, which results in larger yam tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ hulu la ni amɛbaai lɛ toɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ ŋmeii. Staking haa baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ mli koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: How do short weeds reduce my crop yield even if my crops are taller than the weeds?
ga: Te shortweed baanyɛ aha mi yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi eha tɛŋŋ? Eyɛ mli akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ fe jwɛi lɛ moŋ

english: Weeds have aggressive roots underground that steal water and fertilizer away from your main crop before it can reach them. They also harbor insects and plant diseases that can spread to your crops.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ onibii titrii lɛ amli dani amɛshɛɔ amɛhe. Amɛhiɛɔ kooloi bibii kɛ tsei ahe helai ni baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã onibii amli lɛ hu.

english: Why do my young tomato seedlings grow very long, thin, and weak in the nursery bed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato dumɔwui bibii lɛ daraa, amɛfeɔ mlɛo, ni amɛhe waaa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seedlings stretch out and become tall and weak (leggy) when they are not receiving enough light and are searching for the sun. Giving nursery beds moderate sunlight and enough space between seeds builds strong stems.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baagbala amɛhe ni amɛbaafee mɛi ni kwɔlɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ (naji) beni amɛnáaa la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛmiitao hulu la lɛ. Ha hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ. Ebaaha tso lɛ mli awa.

english: Why should I leave some big trees standing on my farm when I am planting cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi tsei wuji yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ́ midu kookoo?

english: Cocoa trees thrive best under partial shade because intense direct sunlight burns young cocoa leaves and dries out the soil quickly. Shade trees shield cocoa from high heat, retain soil moisture, and help cocoa plants stay healthy and produce longer.
ga: Kokoo tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni hulutsoo be fioo yɔɔ lɛ ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa kookoo baai bibii lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ Ni eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my plantain stems with dry leaves and grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai ni egbi kɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle plantain tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves (known as mulching) traps moisture in the ground during hot weather, stops weeds from growing, and slowly rots into natural plant food that makes the soil richer.
ga: Mulching kɛ baai ni egbi Enɛ (ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching) mɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves at the base of maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which the crop needs for green growth. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-decomposed animal manure will help bring back their green color and strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni he hiaa tso lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔŋ kɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Maize feeds heavily on soil nitrogen, leaving the land tired. Legumes like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil, naturally restoring soil nutrients for the next crop.
ga: Abele haa nitrogen babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shãa. Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Koni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: When maize is planted too close, the roots and leaves compete fiercely for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak plants with small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni ŋmeii bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Yes, planting cassava and maize together is a great strategy. Maize grows rapidly and is harvested early, while cassava grows slowly at first and takes over the space after the maize is cleared, giving you two harvests from one land.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ ji gbɛ kpakpa. Abɛi daa oya ni akpaa lɛ mra. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ni eŋɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni ajie ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ. Ehaa okpaa nii shii 2 kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: What is causing small, round holes in the leaves of my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ baa? Mi-pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ

english: Small holes are usually caused by tiny leaf-eating insects like beetles or caterpillars. You can manage them by spraying natural neem seed extract solution or an approved mild insecticide early in the morning.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni yeɔ baai tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii kɛ bu bibii baa. Obaanyɛ otsa amɛ kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli neem dumɔwui amli nu loo tsofa ko ni gbeɔ kooloi ni bɛ mlɛo ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni oookɛshwie nɔ leebi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my yam stems rotting at the base where they touch the soil after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato tsei lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shishigbɛ ni taa shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam stem rot occurs when excessive water stays around the plant base, creating conditions for fungal diseases to grow. Creating higher earth mounds or ridges helps rain drain away safely from the stems.
ga: Sweet potato stem rot lɛ baa kɛji nu babaoo bɔle tso lɛ shishi, ni enɛ haa shihilɛi ni haa tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ adara yɛ mli lɛ baa. Gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ ni aaafee lɛ baaha nugbɔ lɛ atsɔ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi.

english: Why do my tomato blossoms drop off without turning into fruit during very hot weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai yɛ otsii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing them from producing fruit so they drop off. Watering regularly around the base and providing light shade during peak heat helps save the blossoms.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ. Enɛ haaa enyɛ ewo yibii ni no hewɔ lɛ egbeeɔ shi. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akafite.

english: Why is it better for me to buy certified seeds instead of planting saved seeds from last year's harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ nyɛsɛɛ afi nikpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specifically bred to give high yields, uniform crop growth, and strong resistance to local diseases. Saved seeds lose these strong qualities over time, leading to lower yields.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. tso lɛ dalɛ ni yɔɔ ekomefeemɔ mli ni eyɛ hewalɛ kpakpa ni ekɛteɔ shi ewoɔ helai ni baa jɛmɛ lɛ Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ laajeɔ sui ni mli wa nɛɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ ni baa shi.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the necessary shade and soil moisture cocoa needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa ni kookoo baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Is it good for my soil if I plant cowpeas in between my rows of maize?
ga: Ani ebaafee nɔ ni hi aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ?

english: Yes, cowpeas belong to the legume family, which naturally takes nitrogen from the air and feeds it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for your maize.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, cowpeas yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ejieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha o-corn lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient it uses to stay green and grow strong. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps bring back the green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni akɛkwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Local weeds are naturally tougher and better adapted to the soil, so they can absorb water and soil nutrients faster than cultivated crops unless you clear them early.
ga: Jwɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli wa yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛnyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛ baanyɛ amɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni aduɔ. Ja ojie amɛ mra.

english: What happens if I plant my cassava stem cuttings too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When cassava plants are crowded, their roots fight each other for water and nutrients, which leaves you with thin stems and very small tubers instead of thick, healthy cassava roots.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii. Enɛ baaha oná tsitsi bibioo kɛ yitso bibioo waa. Mohu ɔ, kasava sisifã ɔmɛ a mi wa nɛ a he wa.

english: Tomatoes shed their flowers when the weather gets too hot or when they don't get enough water, because heat and drought stress prevent the flowers from successfully forming fruit.
ga: Tomatoi shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo amɛnáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Yɛ nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hɔmɔ mli baa lɛ hewɔ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ awo yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my pepper plants are getting too much water or not enough?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-pepper tsei lɛ miiná nu babaoo loo amɛmiiná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa?

english: If leaves wilt under midday heat but bounce back at night, they need water; if leaves turn pale yellow and stems feel soft, the roots are drowning in too much water.
ga: Kɛji baai lɛ gboi yɛ gbi mli shi amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba gbɛkɛ mli lɛ, Etsɔɔ akɛ nu he miihia bo Kɛji baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tso lɛ shishi lɛ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ blɛoo Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ ebote nu babaoo mli.

english: What is eating small holes in my cassava leaves, and will it ruin my harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi-cassava baai lɛ anɔ Ni ani ebaafite mi-nitsumɔ mli nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ?

english: Small leaf holes are usually caused by insects like beetles or grasshoppers feeding. Mild leaf damage won't kill cassava since the main food grows underground, but severe damage requires pest treatment.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ladybugs loo ŋmeii ni taoɔ niyenii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa. Baai bibii ni efite lɛ nyɛŋ agbe ŋmei ejaakɛ niyenii titri lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Shi nɔ ni efite waa lɛ biɔ ni atsa tsɛŋemɔ helai.

english: What is that white powdery dust on the leaves of my okra plants?
ga: Mɛni ji sũ yɛŋ ni yɔɔ mi okra baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: That dust is a common fungal disease called powdery mildew, which develops in humid weather when air cannot flow freely between tightly packed plants.
ga: Muji lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew. Enɛ baa mli yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe waa lɛ ateŋ lɛ.

english: Can I save seeds from my maize harvest to plant again next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni akpaa lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: You can, but saved seeds from hybrid varieties often yield much smaller harvests than fresh, certified seeds from registered agro-dealers, which are bred to resist diseases and heat.
ga: Obaanyɛ, shi dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔi ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo wolo nɔ lɛ adɛŋ. ni atsɔse amɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛte shi amɛwo helai kɛ dɔlɛ

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize plants are running out of nitrogen in the soil or getting too much water around their roots. Adding nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn deep green again so the plant can make food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu babaoo yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe. Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ekoŋŋ bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ awo niyenii.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows soil pests to build up. Rotating your crop with legumes like beans or groundnuts puts vital nitrogen back into the dirt.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa Tsɔɔmɔ oŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii. Enɛ baaha nitrogen ni he hiaa lɛ aku esɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot when too much water collects around them in heavy rain. Planting your cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows extra water to drain away, keeping the tubers dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu babaoo bua ehe naa yɛ hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu babaoo atsɔ mli. Ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Yams need soft, loose soil to push down and expand easily. If the ground is hard or full of stones, the yam gets blocked and bends, so creating deep, soft soil mounds lets them grow long and thick.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse koni ekɛtsi kɛya ŋwɛi ni egbɛ eshwa mlɛo. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ wa loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ, Sweet potatoes lɛ baatswa ni ebɔle ehe. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ afee gɔŋ ko ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ, ebaaha sweet potato lɛ atsɔ kakadaŋŋ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that hide under the leaves and spread plant viruses. Spraying neem oil or appropriate organic remedies helps clear these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ekɛ ehe teeɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni egbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni sa ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the branches without growing into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbee shi kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they suffer from extreme heat or irregular watering to save their own energy. Giving your plants steady water at the root level during flowering helps fruits set properly.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo otsei lɛ amli yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni amɛwoɔ aduawai lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees shed all their leaves during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ fɛɛ yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves dry out fast under hot winds, so the tree drops leaves to conserve precious water inside its stems. Planting fast-growing shade trees like plantain nearby protects young cocoa from dry wind and direct sun.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ shishi. No sɛɛ lɛ, tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛto nu ni jara wa yɛ amɛtsei lɛ amli. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa egbiɔ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he.

english: Why are my sweet orange trees dropping young green fruits off the branches early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso ni ŋɔɔ lɛ miiho aduawai bibii ni ji eŋɔli kɛmiijɛ eniji lɛ anɔ oya nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Citrus trees shed young fruit when they don't have enough water and nutrients to feed all of them, or when attacked by fruit flies. Clearing weeds, watering during dry spells, and keeping pests away helps the tree retain its fruit.
ga: Citrus tsei lɛ baawo yibii kɛ́ nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua amɛ fɛɛ lɛ bɛ. aloo kɛ́ aduawai amli ŋmeii ni shwieɔ jwɛi lɛ tutua amɛ Nu ni ashwieɔ amɛnɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli Ni ŋmeii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛyibii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize plants produce very small cobs when I put four or five seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmeii ejwɛ loo enumɔ wo bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for limited sunlight, soil food, and water. Planting one or two seeds per hole with proper spacing gives each plant enough space to make full cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ baawu koni amɛná hulu la ni faaa, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ nu. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui kome loo enyɔ yɛ bu kome mli ni gbɛ ni sa yɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaaha tso fɛɛ tso aná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee pod ni eyi obɔ.

english: Weeds are wild plants with very strong, aggressive roots that grab water and soil nutrients much faster than farm crops. Clearing weeds early gives your young crops a fair chance to grow without being choked.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni shishifãi ni mli wa, ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha otsei bibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛdara ni nɔ ko nɔ ko akatsi amɛnaa.

english: How do I know when my maize is fully ripe and ready to harvest from the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When maize is mature, the husks turn papery and brown, and a small black spot appears at the base of each kernel. Harvesting at this exact stage prevents mold from excess farm moisture and protects the grain from field pests.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ŋmãa lɛ baatsɔ wolo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Ni ŋmeii bibii diji yɛ jɛmɛ. Ejeɔ kpo yɛ dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko shishi. Nikpamɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli pɛpɛɛpɛ tsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekafee ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. ni ebuɔ dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting just two or three days after I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ bɔi fitemɔ beni mikɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ tsu nii lɛ?

english: Cassava roots are living tissue that react very rapidly with oxygen once removed from the moist soil, causing internal decay within 48 hours. It is best to harvest only the amount of cassava you can sell or process into gari immediately.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ji fãji ni hiɛ ka ni tsuɔ nii oya kɛji ajie amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Enɛ haa mligbɛ fitemɔ baa yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 mli. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookpa ŋmei babaoo pɛ ni obaanyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ loo okɛtsu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ofee ŋmei.

english: Why do cocoa pods change color from green to bright yellow when they mature on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli nɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse nɔ beni amɛdaraa yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: The color change in cocoa pods is a natural signal that the beans inside have fully developed their fats and sugars. Harvesting pods when they turn completely yellow ensures the beans will ferment properly to give good quality chocolate.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo ŋmɔŋ ko su tsake lɛ, eji adebɔɔ mli okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kookoo ŋmɔŋ lɛ etsɔ emli fɔ kɛ sugars lɛ nɔ kwraa. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmeii lɛ beni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ kwraa lɛ, ehaa kɔfi ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ koni amɛná tsokolate ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves in intense afternoon sun to shrink the surface area exposed to heat and slow down water loss. As long as the leaves uncurl by evening, it is a normal defense behavior to survive dry heat.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni ekɛba he ni hulutsoo lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ shi ni nu ni hoɔ oya lɛ aba shi. Shii abɔ ni baai lɛ baatse amɛhe yɛ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ, hulutsoo be ni mli egbi lɛ mlihilɛ hi.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the plants without producing any tomato fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Extremely high temperatures can cause tomato pollen to dry out and fail to fertilize the blossoms. When flowers are unfertilized, the plant sheds them to preserve its water and energy for survival.
ga: Kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tomato mli ŋmɔtɔ lɛ agbi ni ekɛtsi enaa koni ekawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ. Beni afɔɔɔ fɔfɔii lɛ Tsei jieɔ nu koni amɛkɛto nu kɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi.

english: Why do my yam tubers crack open under the soil before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miigba yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani mikpa amɛ po lɛ?

english: Yam tubers crack when sudden heavy rains follow a long dry period. The inside of the tuber absorbs water rapidly and expands faster than the outer skin can stretch.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ tswaa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa trukaa ni nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Yitso lɛ mligbɛ lɛ shwieɔ nu oya ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛre.

english: Why do the outer leaves of my plantains turn yellow and drop off during the harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have large leaves that lose water very fast. During dry harmattan weather, the plant intentionally sacrifices its older outer leaves to keep water inside the central stem so the main plant survives.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ baai wuji ni nu fiteɔ oya waa. Yɛ Harmattan kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli lɛ Tso lɛ jwɛŋɔ ekɛ esɛɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ shaa afɔle koni ekɛ nu ato tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tso lɛ mli bɔni afee ni tso titri lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why is my cowpea crop growing lots of dark green leaves but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil makes cowpea plants put all their energy into growing vines and leaves rather than flowers. Since cowpeas make their own nitrogen, extra fertilizer stops them from producing pods.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa cowpea tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛduɔ wain tsei kɛ baai yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsina ŋmei feɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ e-nitrogen. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi fata he lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why should I use a sharp tool to cut cocoa pods instead of pulling or twisting them off with my hands?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ dɛŋdade ni mli wa afo kookoo ŋmɔtɔ lɛ moŋ fe ni mikɛ minine baagbala loo matsɔ mli?

english: Twisting cocoa pods tears the flower cushion on the tree branch, which is the exact spot where future flowers and pods grow. Using a sharp blade leaves the cushion healthy for next season's crop.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii ni atsɔ mli lɛ gbálaa fɔfɔii akutsei ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ lɛ amli. Biɛ ji he ni wɔsɛɛ fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ. Kɛ akɛ tsɔne ni mli wa tsuɔ nii Enɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Does working in group harvesting teams and singing while harvesting harm the mature crops?
ga: Ani kuu mli nitsumɔ, kuu mli nikpamɔ kɛ lala ni alaɔ yɛ be mli ni akpaa nii lɛ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni edara lɛ awui?

english: Singing and working together keeps farm workers energetic and focused. High worker morale leads to faster, more careful crop handling, reducing accidental damage to crops while clearing the field before heat sets in.
ga: Lala kɛ nitsumɔ ni akɛ he woɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔ mli nitsulɔi lɛ náa hewalɛ ni amɛjwɛŋmɔ hiɔ nɔ. Nitsulɔi ajwɛŋmɔ ni nɔ kwɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ oya kɛ hiɛdɔɔ baa. Ha ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ yɛ oshara mli lɛ aba shi be mli ni ojieɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ dani latsaa lɛ aba.
